    "oldString":"/* {{{ slot_store_size() */\nint32_t slot_store_size(slot_store_t *s)\n{\n    return s ? s->count : 0;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* slot_flags() lives further down — it needs the get_slot() helper\n * that's defined after slot_alloc(). */\n\n/* {{{ Local helper — grow_store_if_needed() */\nstatic int grow_store_if_needed(slot_store_t *s)\n{\n    if (s->count < s->capacity) return 0;\n    int32_t new_cap = s->capacity * 2;\n    slot_rec_t **grown = realloc(s->slots, (size_t)new_cap * sizeof(slot_rec_t *));\n    if (!grown) return -1;\n    memset(grown + s->capacity, 0,\n           (size_t)(new_cap - s->capacity) * sizeof(slot_rec_t *));\n    s->slots    = grown;\n    s->capacity = new_cap;\n    return 0;\n}\n/* }}} */",
    "newString":"/* {{{ slot_store_size() */\nint32_t slot_store_size(slot_store_t *s)\n{\n    /* Acquire-load pairs with the release-store in slot_alloc; a\n     * reader that sees count = N also sees the slot N-1 record\n     * fully published into its chunk. */\n    return s ? (int32_t)atomic_load_explicit(&s->count, memory_order_acquire)\n             : 0;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* slot_flags() lives further down — it needs the get_slot() helper\n * that's defined after slot_alloc(). */\n\n/* {{{ Local helper — grow_top_level() (issue 319b layer 3)\n *\n * Called with alloc_lock held. Allocates a new top-level chunk-\n * pointer table of at least 2x the current size, copies the\n * current chunk pointers into it, atomically publishes the new\n * table, and parks the old one on the stale_tops free-list for\n * destroy-time reclamation. */\nstatic int grow_top_level(slot_store_t *s, uint32_t needed_idx)\n{\n    uint32_t old_cap = atomic_load_explicit(&s->top_capacity,\n                                            memory_order_relaxed);\n    uint32_t new_cap = old_cap * 2u;\n    while (new_cap <= needed_idx) new_cap *= 2u;\n\n    slot_rec_t ***new_top = calloc((size_t)new_cap, sizeof(slot_rec_t **));\n    if (!new_top) return -1;\n\n    slot_rec_t ***old_top = atomic_load_explicit(&s->chunks,\n                                                 memory_order_relaxed);\n    memcpy(new_top, old_top, (size_t)old_cap * sizeof(slot_rec_t **));\n\n    /* Park the old top-level pointer so any in-flight reader that\n     * loaded it before the swap finishes safely. The chunks it\n     * points to are the same chunks the new top points to (we only\n     * copied the pointer values), so reads from either top resolve\n     * to the same live chunks. */\n    struct stale_top *st = malloc(sizeof *st);\n    if (!st) { free(new_top); return -1; }\n    st->ptr  = old_top;\n    st->next = s->stale_tops;\n    s->stale_tops = st;\n\n    /* Publish the new top-level first, then the new capacity.\n     * Readers that race-load the new chunks pointer and the old\n     * capacity will compute id/SLOT_CHUNK_SIZE within the original\n     * range, which is still valid. The reverse — old chunks, new\n     * capacity — would let a reader index past the old top's\n     * allocation, which would be UB. So: chunks first. */\n    atomic_store_explicit(&s->chunks,       new_top, memory_order_release);\n    atomic_store_explicit(&s->top_capacity, new_cap, memory_order_release);\n    return 0;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Local helper — ensure_chunk() (issue 319b layer 2)\n *\n * Called with alloc_lock held. Allocates the chunk at index `ci`\n * if it's not already populated, and publishes the chunk pointer\n * into the top-level table. */\nstatic int ensure_chunk(slot_store_t *s, uint32_t ci)\n{\n    slot_rec_t ***top = atomic_load_explicit(&s->chunks,\n                                             memory_order_relaxed);\n    if (top[ci]) return 0;\n    slot_rec_t **chunk = calloc((size_t)SLOT_CHUNK_SIZE,\n                                sizeof(slot_rec_t *));\n    if (!chunk) return -1;\n    top[ci] = chunk;\n    return 0;\n}\n/* }}} */"

          "old_string":"    if (grow_store_if_needed(s) != 0) {\n        if (r->cells_chunk)       ua_unref(s->heap, r->cells_chunk);\n        if (r->json_cells_chunk)  ua_unref(s->heap, r->json_cells_chunk);\n        if (r->order_cells_chunk) ua_unref(s->heap, r->order_cells_chunk);\n        free(r);\n        return SLOT_INVALID;\n    }\n    slot_id_t id = s->count++;\n    s->slots[id] = r;\n    return id;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Local helper — get_slot() */\nstatic slot_rec_t *get_slot(slot_store_t *s, slot_id_t id)\n{\n    if (!s || id < 0 || id >= s->count) return NULL;\n    return s->slots[id];\n}\n/* }}} */",
          "replace_all":false,
          "new_string":"    /* Publish into the two-level chunked index. The hot read path\n     * is lock-free; only this rare allocation path takes the lock,\n     * and only to serialize structural changes to the index\n     * (layer-2 chunk creation, layer-3 top growth, count bump).\n     * Workers' get_slot calls walk the atomic structure without\n     * contending here. */\n    pthread_mutex_lock(&s->alloc_lock);\n\n    uint32_t id = atomic_load_explicit(&s->count, memory_order_relaxed);\n    uint32_t ci = id / SLOT_CHUNK_SIZE;\n    uint32_t si = id % SLOT_CHUNK_SIZE;\n\n    /* Layer 3: top-level grows if the chunk index is past current\n     * capacity. */\n    if (ci >= atomic_load_explicit(&s->top_capacity, memory_order_relaxed)) {\n        if (grow_top_level(s, ci) != 0) {\n            pthread_mutex_unlock(&s->alloc_lock);\n            if (r->cells_chunk)       ua_unref(s->heap, r->cells_chunk);\n            if (r->json_cells_chunk)  ua_unref(s->heap, r->json_cells_chunk);\n            if (r->order_cells_chunk) ua_unref(s->heap, r->order_cells_chunk);\n            free(r);\n            return SLOT_INVALID;\n        }\n    }\n\n    /* Layer 2: allocate the chunk if it's the first slot inside it. */\n    if (ensure_chunk(s, ci) != 0) {\n        pthread_mutex_unlock(&s->alloc_lock);\n        if (r->cells_chunk)       ua_unref(s->heap, r->cells_chunk);\n        if (r->json_cells_chunk)  ua_unref(s->heap, r->json_cells_chunk);\n        if (r->order_cells_chunk) ua_unref(s->heap, r->order_cells_chunk);\n        free(r);\n        return SLOT_INVALID;\n    }\n\n    /* Layer 1: publish the slot pointer into the chunk. The count\n     * bump that follows is the release-store readers acquire-load\n     * to know the slot exists. */\n    slot_rec_t ***top = atomic_load_explicit(&s->chunks,\n                                             memory_order_relaxed);\n    top[ci][si] = r;\n\n    atomic_store_explicit(&s->count, id + 1u, memory_order_release);\n\n    pthread_mutex_unlock(&s->alloc_lock);\n    return (slot_id_t)id;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Local helper — get_slot() */\nstatic slot_rec_t *get_slot(slot_store_t *s, slot_id_t id)\n{\n    if (!s || id < 0) return NULL;\n    uint32_t uid = (uint32_t)id;\n    /* Acquire-load count pairs with the release-store in slot_alloc.\n     * If we see count = N then the slot at id = N-1 (and all earlier)\n     * is fully published — the chunk pointer and the slot pointer\n     * inside it. */\n    if (uid >= atomic_load_explicit(&s->count, memory_order_acquire)) {\n        return NULL;\n    }\n    uint32_t ci = uid / SLOT_CHUNK_SIZE;\n    uint32_t si = uid % SLOT_CHUNK_SIZE;\n    /* Acquire-load the top so we see the chunk publishes that the\n     * release-store in grow_top_level orders before its top swap.\n     * After top growth, both the old and new top arrays point to\n     * the same chunks — either is safe to read from. */\n    slot_rec_t ***top = atomic_load_explicit(&s->chunks,\n                                             memory_order_acquire);\n    return top[ci][si];\n}\n/* }}} */",
          "file_path":"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech/src/009-slot-store.c"
        },

      "content":"/* {{{ test_store_size_growth() */\nstatic int test_store_size_growth(void)\n{\n    /* Allocate enough slots to cross the initial capacity boundary\n     * (16) and verify slot_id_t stays monotonic. */\n    slot_store_t *s = slot_store_create();\n    slot_id_t prev = -1;\n    for (int i = 0; i < 50; i++) {\n        slot_id_t id = slot_alloc(s, 4, 1, SLOT_FLAG_NONE);\n        ASSERT(id != SLOT_INVALID);\n        ASSERT(id == prev + 1);\n        prev = id;\n    }\n    ASSERT(slot_store_size(s) == 50);\n    slot_store_destroy(s);\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ test_large_value_push_pop() */\n/* SLOT_FLAG_LARGE_VALUE accepts any size on push, regardless of\n * cell_capacity (which is ignored). Bytes live in the slot store's\n * lazy-created lvh heap; the cell holds a stable pointer. Peek\n * and pop both copy from the heap back into the caller buffer. */\nstatic int test_large_value_push_pop(void)\n{\n    slot_store_t *s = slot_store_create();\n    slot_id_t id = slot_alloc(s, 0, 4, SLOT_FLAG_LARGE_VALUE);\n    ASSERT(id != SLOT_INVALID);\n\n    /* 100 KB push — well beyond any sane fixed cell size. */\n    int payload_size = 100 * 1024;\n    unsigned char *src = malloc((size_t)payload_size);\n    for (int i = 0; i < payload_size; i++) src[i] = (unsigned char)(i & 0xFF);\n    ASSERT(slot_push(s, id, src, payload_size, 0) == 0);",

          "replace_all":false,
          "new_string":"/* {{{ test_store_size_growth() */\nstatic int test_store_size_growth(void)\n{\n    /* Allocate enough slots to cross the initial capacity boundary\n     * (16) and verify slot_id_t stays monotonic. */\n    slot_store_t *s = slot_store_create();\n    slot_id_t prev = -1;\n    for (int i = 0; i < 50; i++) {\n        slot_id_t id = slot_alloc(s, 4, 1, SLOT_FLAG_NONE);\n        ASSERT(id != SLOT_INVALID);\n        ASSERT(id == prev + 1);\n        prev = id;\n    }\n    ASSERT(slot_store_size(s) == 50);\n    slot_store_destroy(s);\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ test_chunked_index_growth_preserves_early_slots() — issue 319b\n *\n * Forces multiple top-level chunk-pointer-table growth events and\n * verifies that slots allocated BEFORE growth remain reachable AND\n * functional afterward. This is the load-bearing invariant of the\n * 319b two-level chunked-append index: slots and chunks never move,\n * so handles cached early in the run keep working forever.\n *\n * Initial top capacity is 16 * SLOT_CHUNK_SIZE (= 1024) slots. We\n * allocate 5000 slots, which forces at least two top-level growth\n * events (1024 → 2048 → 4096 → 8192). We push a sentinel into each\n * slot AT ALLOC TIME and read it back AFTER all allocations finish —\n * any growth-related corruption would scramble the sentinel. */\nstatic int test_chunked_index_growth_preserves_early_slots(void)\n{\n    enum { N = 5000 };\n    slot_store_t *s = slot_store_create();\n\n    /* Each slot is a 1-cell ring of 4 bytes; we push the slot's id\n     * as its sentinel value. */\n    for (int i = 0; i < N; i++) {\n        slot_id_t id = slot_alloc(s, 4, 1, SLOT_FLAG_NONE);\n        ASSERT(id == i);\n        uint32_t v = (uint32_t)i;\n        ASSERT(slot_push(s, id, &v, sizeof v, 0) == 0);\n    }\n    ASSERT(slot_store_size(s) == N);\n\n    /* Read each slot's sentinel back. Slot 0 was allocated before\n     * any growth; if growth invalidated its pointer or moved its\n     * chunk, this peek would return garbage. */\n    for (int i = 0; i < N; i++) {\n        uint32_t got = 0xDEADBEEF;\n        int32_t  rc  = slot_peek(s, (slot_id_t)i, &got, sizeof got);\n        ASSERT(rc == (int32_t)sizeof got);\n        ASSERT(got == (uint32_t)i);\n    }\n\n    /* Out-of-range ids still rejected cleanly. */\n    uint32_t scratch = 0;\n    ASSERT(slot_peek(s, (slot_id_t)N,     &scratch, sizeof scratch) < 0);\n    ASSERT(slot_peek(s, (slot_id_t)(N+1), &scratch, sizeof scratch) < 0);\n\n    slot_store_destroy(s);\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */",

## [871]

```json
{
  "uuid":"a0d6496e-f978-4f4b-bb53-f56faa87960d",
  "type":"user",
  "timestamp":"2026-05-23T22:08:07.114Z",
  "parentUuid":"aca337c7-b423-4c78-b07e-a5c9720eaccd",
  "toolUseResult":{
    "originalFile":"# 319b — Slot store growth primitive\n\n## Status\nopen — implementation underway. Full design in parent issue\n319's \"Q1\" resolution.\n\n## Current behavior\n\n`src/009-slot-store.c` uses a flat `slot_rec_t **slots` array\nwith `realloc()`-based growth (`grow_store_if_needed`). This\nworks at graph load (single-threaded) but is unsafe at runtime\nbecause `realloc()` can MOVE the array, invalidating any slot\npointer a worker has cached.\n\nThe slot RECORDS themselves are already heap-allocated\nseparately (per-slot `malloc`), so their addresses are stable.\nOnly the `slots[]` array of POINTERS is the problem.\n\n## Intended behavior\n\nReplace the flat `slots[]` array with a two-level chunked-append\nstructure:\n\n- **Chunk size**: 64 slot-pointers per chunk (cache-friendly).\n- **Top-level array**: holds chunk pointers; starts at 16\n  entries (1024 slots without top-level growth). Doubles via\n  copy-and-publish with defer-free when it fills.\n- **Atomic count**: tracks total slots ever allocated. Readers\n  use acquire-load to see slots published with release-store.\n- **`pthread_mutex_t alloc_lock`**: serializes `slot_alloc`.\n  Readers (push/pop via `get_slot`) take no lock here — the\n  per-slot spinlock is still the only hot-path synchronization.\n- **Stale-top free list**: top-level arrays from prior growth\n  events stay alive on a linked list until `slot_store_destroy`.\n  Any worker that cached a stale top-pointer mid-growth can\n  finish its lookup safely; the chunks the stale top points to\n  are still valid because chunks never move.\n\nSlot lookup: `top[id/64][id%64]`. One extra indirection per\naccess vs the old flat array, in exchange for the runtime-safe\ngrowth.\n\n## Suggested implementation\n\n1. Change the `slot_store` struct definition (private in the\n   .c file; header has only the opaque forward declaration so\n   no public API change).\n2. Add `SLOT_CHUNK_SIZE` (64) and `INITIAL_TOP_CAPACITY` (16).\n3. Rewrite `slot_store_create` to allocate the initial top-level\n   array, init the mutex, init the atomic count.\n4. Rewrite `slot_store_destroy` to iterate over chunks, free\n   slot records and each chunk, then free the stale-top list.\n5. Replace `grow_store_if_needed` with `grow_top_level` (called\n   under `alloc_lock`).\n6. Rewrite `slot_alloc`: take the lock, claim id, ensure chunk\n   exists, publish slot, release-store the count.\n7. Rewrite `get_slot` to walk the chunked structure.\n8. Rewrite `slot_store_size` to acquire-load the atomic count.\n9. Add a test that forces multiple top-level growth events\n   (allocate ≥ 2048 slots to require at least one growth).\n10. Run the full slot-store unit suite and the integration\n    suite — all 22 + 12 must still pass.\n\n## Relevant files\n\n- `src/009-slot-store.c` — the structure change.\n- `src/009-slot-store.h` — header stays unchanged (opaque type).\n- `tests/009-slot-store-test.c` — add growth test.\n\n## Not in scope\n\nRing buffer cell growth (when a single slot's ring fills with\npushed values waiting for consumption) — separate concern, same\ndouble-buffer pattern but under the per-slot lock. Top-level growth is\ncopy-on-grow with defer-free: the old top-level array is parked\non a `stale_tops` list so any worker that loaded a stale\ntop-pointer mid-growth completes its lookup safely against it,\nthen the parked arrays are freed at `slot_store_destroy`.\n\n`slot_alloc` is serialized by `pthread_mutex_t alloc_lock`.\nThe hot read/write path (`slot_push`, `slot_pop`, `slot_peek`,\n`slot_flags`) takes no allocator-wide lock — the per-slot\n`atomic_flag` spinlock remains the only hot-path synchronization.\nReaders acquire-load `count`; the matching release-store at the\nend of `slot_alloc` orders the slot publish before the reader\ncan see it.\n\nSlots and chunks themselves never move. Once `slot_alloc`\nreturns an id, the underlying slot record's address and the\nchunk it lives in are stable for the run."

          "command":"git commit -m \"$(cat <<'EOF'\n319b — closeout: the slot store grows without moving its slots\n\nThe slot pointer index is now a two-level chunked-append table.\nSlots live at chunks[id/64][id%64]; both the chunk pointer in\nthe top-level table and the slot pointer inside the chunk are\npublished atomically by slot_alloc, and any slot a worker has\ncached keeps its address forever — chunks never move, slot\nrecords never move, only the top-level table itself ever moves\nand only via copy-then-atomic-swap with the prior version parked\non a defer-free list so in-flight readers finish safely.\n\nWhy the change: the old flat realloc'd index let the slot\npointers move on growth, which is fine when growth only happens\nat graph load but breaks the moment slot_alloc fires from a\nrunning worker. The runtime self-construction feature (issue\n319's create_box, sub-issue 319d) needs that to work; this\nlanding is the foundation that makes the rest of 319 safe.\n\nHot read path unchanged: slot_push / slot_pop / slot_peek take\nno allocator-wide lock. The per-slot atomic_flag spinlock\nremains the only serialization on value movement. A\npthread_mutex serializes slot_alloc itself, which is rare and\nalready off the critical path.\n\nThe 5000-slot growth test forces multiple top-level grow events\n(1024 → 2048 → 4096 → 8192) and verifies every slot allocated\nbefore any growth event remains readable with its original\nsentinel value intact afterward. The full slot-store unit\nsuite is now 23 passing (up from 22); the 12 integration test\nmaps all still pass.\n\nNo public API change — slot_store_t is opaque in the header.\nThe new internal layer is invisible to every caller.\n\nCo-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>\nEOF\n)\" 2>&1 | tail -5",

    "oldString":"## Status\nopen — planning stub. Full design in parent issue 319's \"Q4\" and\n\"Q5\" resolutions.\n\n## Parent issue\nSub-issue of 319. Combines two small independent utilities that\nboth gate `create_box`:\n\n- **Box id generator** — auto-generates UUID-style box_id strings\n  for `create_box` callers who don't supply an explicit `id`.\n  Design: 319 Q4.\n- **Compile cache** — content-hash-keyed lookup under `tmp/`,\n  shell-out to `scripts/soramech-compile.sh` on cache miss,\n  dlopen the resulting artifact. Preserves the runner-doesn't-know-\n  about-compiler separation. Design: 319 Q5.\n\n## Intended behavior\n\n- A `box_id_generate()` utility returns a string like\n  `auto_8f3c2a1e9b4d`. Collision-free within a run.\n- A `compile_cache_resolve(source_path, lang_spec)` utility\n  returns a dlopen-ready artifact path.     "newString":"## Status\nopen — implementation underway. Scope reduced from the original\nplan (see \"Reduced scope\" below). Design in parent issue 319's\n\"Q4\" resolution.\n\n## Parent issue\nSub-issue of 319. Provides the box id generator that\n`create_box` (319d) returns when the caller doesn't supply an\nexplicit `id`.\n\n## Reduced scope — compile cache not needed as a separate module\n\nIssue 319's Q5 resolution called for a content-hash-keyed\ncompile cache under `tmp/` that shells out to\n`scripts/soramech-compile.sh` on miss. Investigation while\nstarting this sub-issue found that **the language specs already\ndo this work internally**:\n\n- `langs/c/spec.c` has `maybe_lazy_compile` (line 228) that\n  detects a `.c` source path, compiles it to `.so` on first\n  use, and caches the resulting handle in the per-worker dlopen\n  table.\n- Lua and Bash have no compile step — `langs/lua/spec.c` loads\n  via `luaL_loadfile` and caches the Lua module; Bash's spec\n  hands the source path to a persistent subprocess.\n\nSo `create_box(spec)` for any language can resolve via the\nexisting per-spec invocation path. No separate cache layer\npreserves more concept-purity than it saves work — the runner\nalready stays ignorant of the compiler because each language\nspec encapsulates its own loading discipline. The Q5\n\"compile cache\" idea is therefore folded into existing spec\nmachinery rather than implemented as a new module.\n\nIf a future need surfaces for a unified content-hash cache\nabove the spec layer (e.g. for pre-warming or shared\nartifacts across workers), revisit; for now, defer.\n\n## Current behavior\n\nThere is no box id generator. The graph loader currently expects\nevery box's `id` field to be supplied by the caller (from JSON\non disk). `create_box` callers (issue 319d) need a way to\nproduce unique ids when they don't want to name a box themselves.\n\n## Intended behavior\n\nA small utility module that exposes one function:\n\n```c\nint box_id_generate(char *buf, size_t buf_size);\n```\n\nFills `buf` with a string of the form `auto_<8 hex chars>` (a\nprocess-wide atomic counter rendered as hex). Returns 0 on\nsuccess, -1 if `buf_size` is insufficient (the required size\nis 14 bytes: 5 prefix chars + 8 hex chars + null terminator).\n\nUniqueness is guaranteed within a single process run via the\natomic counter. Cross-run uniqueness is not a goal — ids are\nruntime-only constructs; persistent ids come from the on-disk\nbox JSON files.\n\n## Suggested implementation\n\n1. Create `src/017-box-id.h` — declaration of `box_id_generate`.\n2. Create `src/017-box-id.c` — atomic counter + snprintf\n   formatting.\n3. Create `src/017-box-id.info.md` — function listing per the\n   project's documentation convention.\n4. Create `tests/017-box-id-test.c` — verify format, uniqueness\n   across many calls, rejection on too-small buffer, and\n   uniqueness under concurrent access from multiple threads.\n5. Add Makefile dependency line for the new test.\n6. Initialize `file-index-counter` at 17.\n\n## Relevant files\n\n- `src/017-box-id.{h,c}` — new module.\n- `tests/017-box-id-test.c` — new test.\n- `Makefile` — add per-test dependency line."
  },

Cross-run uniqueness is not a goal — these ids\n * exist only for the duration of the run that mints them.\n */\n#ifndef SORAMECH_017_BOX_ID_H\n#define SORAMECH_017_BOX_ID_H\n\n#include <stddef.h>\n\n/* Required buffer size for box_id_generate output: 5 prefix bytes\n * (\"auto_\") + 8 hex chars + 1 null terminator.     "content":[{
        "name":"Write",
        "input":{
          "content":"/* src/017-box-id.c — auto-generated box id strings, implementation.\n *\n * The whole story: one atomic uint32 counter, fetch-add it, format\n * the result as \"auto_%08x\". 4 billion ids per process run is more\n * than any reasonable workload needs; if a run somehow burns through\n * that many runtime-created boxes the counter wraps and we'd start\n * seeing collisions — but at that point the wrap is the smallest\n * problem the run has.\n *\n * Designed in issue 319 (Q4); landed in issue 319c.\n */\n#include \"017-box-id.h\"\n\n#include <stdatomic.h>\n#include <stdint.h>\n#include <stdio.h>\n\n/* {{{ box_id_counter — process-wide unique-id source */\n/* Starts at 0; first id minted is \"auto_00000000\". The counter is\n * intentionally zero-initialized rather than seeded from time(NULL)\n * or any other entropy source: same-shape ids across runs are\n * easier to grep for in transcripts and last-run.jsonl, and we\n * don't need cross-run uniqueness here. */\nstatic _Atomic uint32_t box_id_counter = 0;\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ box_id_generate() */\nint box_id_generate(char *buf, size_t buf_size)\n{\n    if (!buf || buf_size < BOX_ID_GEN_BUF_SIZE) return -1;\n\n    /* relaxed memory order: the counter has no synchronization\n     * relationship with any other memory; only its own atomicity\n     * matters. */\n    uint32_t id = atomic_fetch_add_explicit(&box_id_counter, 1u,\n                                            memory_order_relaxed);\n\n    int n = snprintf(buf, buf_size, \"auto_%08x\", (unsigned)id);\n    /* snprintf returns the number it would have written if the\n     * buffer were unlimited; n == 13 is success at buf_size >= 14. */\n    if (n < 0 || (size_t)n + 1u > buf_size) return -1;\n    return 0;\n}\n/* }}} */\n",
          "file_path":"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech/src/017-box-id.c"
        },
        "caller":{

    "content":"# 017-box-id\n\nGenerates short unique string identifiers used as the `id` field of\nruntime-created boxes (the kind that `create_box` from issue 319d\nwill mint when the caller doesn't supply an explicit id).\n\n## Functions\n\n### `box_id_generate(char *buf, size_t buf_size) -> int`\n\nFills `buf` with a string of the form `auto_<8 hex chars>`.\n\n- **Returns** `0` on success, `-1` if `buf` is NULL or `buf_size` is\n  less than `BOX_ID_GEN_BUF_SIZE`.\n- **Thread safety**: safe to call from any thread concurrently.\n- **Output length**: always 13 characters plus the null terminator.\n\n### `BOX_ID_GEN_BUF_SIZE` (macro)\n\nThe minimum buffer size for `box_id_generate` output (14 bytes).\nCallers can stack-allocate `char buf[BOX_ID_GEN_BUF_SIZE]` to be\nsure the call will succeed.\n\n## Uniqueness contract\n\nA process-wide atomic counter feeds the hex suffix, so no two calls\nwithin a single process run return the same string. Cross-run\nuniqueness is not provided — these ids exist only for the duration\nof the run that mints them.\n\nThe counter is a `uint32_t`, so the practical ceiling is ~4 billion\nids per run. Beyond that the counter wraps; in practice no\nSoraMech workload approaches this.\n",
    "filePath":"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech/src/017-box-id.info.md",
    "userModified":false
  },

        "input":{
          "content":"/* tests/017-box-id-test.c — unit tests for src/017-box-id.\n *\n * Covers: output format, monotonic uniqueness in single-threaded\n * use, rejection on undersized buffer, and concurrent uniqueness\n * across multiple threads.\n */\n#include \"017-box-id.h\"\n\n#include <pthread.h>\n#include <stdio.h>\n#include <stdlib.h>\n#include <string.h>\n\n/* {{{ Tiny test harness */\n#define ASSERT(cond) do { \\\n    if (!(cond)) { \\\n        printf(\"FAIL %s:%d  %s\\n\", __FILE__, __LINE__, #cond); \\\n        return 0; \\\n    } \\\n} while (0)\n\nstatic int tests_run = 0, tests_passed = 0;\n\n#define RUN(name) do { \\\n    tests_run++; \\\n    printf(\"  %-44s \", #name); \\\n    fflush(stdout); \\\n    if (test_##name()) { \\\n        printf(\"ok\\n\"); \\\n        tests_passed++; \\\n    } \\\n} while (0)\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ test_format() — output matches \"auto_XXXXXXXX\" */\nstatic int test_format(void)\n{\n    char buf[BOX_ID_GEN_BUF_SIZE];\n    ASSERT(box_id_generate(buf, sizeof buf) == 0);\n    ASSERT(strlen(buf) == 13);\n    ASSERT(strncmp(buf, \"auto_\", 5) == 0);\n    /* Suffix is 8 chars of [0-9a-f]. */\n    for (int i = 5; i < 13; i++) {\n        char c = buf[i];\n        int hex = (c >= '0' && c <= '9') || (c >= 'a' && c <= 'f');\n        ASSERT(hex);\n    }\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ test_monotonic_uniqueness() — successive calls produce\n *                                   distinct strings */\nstatic int test_monotonic_uniqueness(void)\n{\n    char a[BOX_ID_GEN_BUF_SIZE], b[BOX_ID_GEN_BUF_SIZE];\n    ASSERT(box_id_generate(a, sizeof a) == 0);\n    ASSERT(box_id_generate(b, sizeof b) == 0);\n    ASSERT(strcmp(a, b) != 0);\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ test_buf_too_small() — rejected with -1, no write */\nstatic int test_buf_too_small(void)\n{\n    char buf[BOX_ID_GEN_BUF_SIZE - 1] = \"preserve\";\n    ASSERT(box_id_generate(buf, sizeof buf) == -1);\n    /* The function should not have written anything; the leading\n     * \"preserve\" bytes remain. */\n    ASSERT(strncmp(buf, \"preserve\", 8) == 0);\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ test_null_buf() — rejected with -1 */\nstatic int test_null_buf(void)\n{\n    ASSERT(box_id_generate(NULL, BOX_ID_GEN_BUF_SIZE) == -1);\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ test_concurrent_uniqueness() — many threads, all ids unique\n *\n * Spawns 8 worker threads, each generates IDS_PER_THREAD ids and\n * stashes them in a per-thread array. Main thread collects them,\n * sorts, and verifies no duplicates. If the atomic counter had\n * been a plain int with a race window, this would surface\n * collisions on contended runs. */\nenum { N_THREADS = 8, IDS_PER_THREAD = 1024 };\n\nstruct gen_ctx {\n    char ids[IDS_PER_THREAD][BOX_ID_GEN_BUF_SIZE];\n};\n\nstatic void *gen_worker(void *arg)\n{\n    struct gen_ctx *ctx = arg;\n    for (int i = 0; i < IDS_PER_THREAD; i++) {\n        if (box_id_generate(ctx->ids[i], BOX_ID_GEN_BUF_SIZE) != 0) {\n            /* Shouldn't happen — flag with empty string for the\n             * checker. */\n            ctx->ids[i][0] = '\\0';\n        }\n    }\n    return NULL;\n}\n\nstatic int cmp_strings(const void *a, const void *b)\n{\n    return strcmp((const char *)a, (const char *)b);\n}\n\nstatic int test_concurrent_uniqueness(void)\n{\n    pthread_t       threads[N_THREADS];\n    struct gen_ctx *ctxs = calloc(N_THREADS, sizeof *ctxs);\n    ASSERT(ctxs != NULL);\n\n    for (int t = 0; t < N_THREADS; t++) {\n        pthread_create(&threads[t], NULL, gen_worker, &ctxs[t]);\n    }\n    for (int t = 0; t < N_THREADS; t++) {\n        pthread_join(threads[t], NULL);\n    }\n\n    /* Pack all ids into one flat array for sort-and-check. */\n    int total = N_THREADS * IDS_PER_THREAD;\n    char (*flat)[BOX_ID_GEN_BUF_SIZE] = malloc((size_t)total * BOX_ID_GEN_BUF_SIZE);\n    ASSERT(flat != NULL);\n    int k = 0;\n    for (int t = 0; t < N_THREADS; t++) {\n        for (int i = 0; i < IDS_PER_THREAD; i++) {\n            ASSERT(ctxs[t].ids[i][0] != '\\0');\n            memcpy(flat[k++], ctxs[t].ids[i], BOX_ID_GEN_BUF_SIZE);\n        }\n    }\n    qsort(flat, (size_t)total, BOX_ID_GEN_BUF_SIZE, cmp_strings);\n    for (int i = 1; i < total; i++) {\n        ASSERT(strcmp(flat[i - 1], flat[i]) != 0);\n    }\n\n    free(flat);\n    free(ctxs);\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\nint main(void)\n{\n    printf(\"017-box-id-test:\\n\");\n    RUN(format);\n    RUN(monotonic_uniqueness);\n    RUN(buf_too_small);\n    RUN(null_buf);\n    RUN(concurrent_uniqueness);\n    printf(\"\\n  %d passed, %d failed\\n\",\n           tests_passed, tests_run - tests_passed);\n    return tests_run == tests_passed ? 0 : 1;\n}\n",
          "file_path":"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech/tests/017-box-id-test.c"
        },
        "caller":{

{

    "originalFile":"# SoraMech — top-level build orchestration.\n#\n# What it does, in a sentence: builds the phase 3 pool runner binary\n# plus one shared library per language spec. Release by default;\n# DEBUG=1 keeps symbols and disables optimization, STRICT=1 promotes\n# warnings to errors. `make clean` removes everything that was built.\n#\n# Invokable from any directory: `make -C /path/to/soramech` works,\n# and the DIR variable can be overridden if needed (e.g. for an\n# out-of-tree checkout). All paths in this Makefile are relative to\n# $(DIR) per the project convention.\n#\n# Designed in issue 309. Implementation of the runner's runtime is\n# split across issues 301–308; this Makefile builds whatever sources\n# exist under src/, libs/task-pool/, and libs/json/, so it scales as\n# those issues land.\n\n# {{{ Resolve project root\nDIR ?= $(abspath $(dir $(lastword $(MAKEFILE_LIST))))\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ Toolchain & flags\nCC      ?= gcc\n\n# Shared header search path: every C source can find langs/lang-spec.h\n# and any future libs/<name>/ headers via -I flags below.\nCPPFLAGS = -I$(DIR)/langs -I$(DIR)/libs/task-pool -I$(DIR)/libs/json -I$(DIR)/src\n\n# Default to release; DEBUG and STRICT toggle alternates.\nifeq ($(DEBUG),1)\n  CFLAGS = -O0 -g -DDEBUG -Wall -pthread -fPIC\nelse ifeq ($(STRICT),1)\n  CFLAGS = -O2 -Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic -Werror -pthread -fPIC\nelse\n  CFLAGS = -O2 -Wall -pthread -fPIC\nendif\n\nLDFLAGS = -ldl -pthread\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ Paths and source discovery\nBUILD_DIR = $(DIR)/build\nPOOL_BIN  = $(DIR)/soramech-pool\n\n# Wildcards: empty subdirs return empty lists, which is fine. As\n# issues 301/302/303/304/305 land their C sources here, they get\n# compiled automatically — no Makefile edit required.\nPOOL_SOURCES = \\\n  $(wildcard $(DIR)/src/*.c) \\\n  $(wildcard $(DIR)/libs/task-pool/*.c) \\\n  $(wildcard $(DIR)/libs/json/*.c)\n\nPOOL_OBJECTS = $(POOL_SOURCES:$(DIR)/%.c=$(BUILD_DIR)/%.o)\n\n# Test sources live in tests/ as C files named to match the source\n# they exercise (e.g. tests/009-slot-store-test.c exercises\n# src/009-slot-store.c). Each builds to a separate executable that\n# `make test` runs in turn.\nTEST_SOURCES = $(wildcard $(DIR)/tests/*.c)\nTEST_BINS    = $(TEST_SOURCES:$(DIR)/tests/%.c=$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/%)\n\nLANGS = lua c bash\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ Public targets\n.PHONY: all runner specs clean test help\n\nall: runner specs\n\nrunner: $(POOL_BIN)\n\nspecs:\n\t@for lang in $(LANGS); do \\\n\t  echo \"  → langs/$$lang\"; \\\n\t  $(MAKE) -s -C $(DIR)/langs/$$lang DIR=$(DIR) || exit 1; \\\n\tdone\n\nclean:\n\trm -f $(POOL_BIN)\n\trm -rf $(BUILD_DIR)\n\t@for lang in $(LANGS); do \\\n\t  $(MAKE) -s -C $(DIR)/langs/$$lang DIR=$(DIR) clean || true; \\\n\tdone\n\ntest: all $(TEST_BINS)\n\t@echo\n\t@fail=0; \\\n\tfor t in $(TEST_BINS); do \\\n\t  $$t || fail=1; \\\n\t  echo; \\\n\tdone; \\\n\tif [ -x $(DIR)/scripts/run-tests.sh ]; then \\\n\t  $(DIR)/scripts/run-tests.sh $(DIR) || fail=1; \\\n\tfi; \\\n\texit $$fail\n\nhelp:\n\t@echo \"SoraMech build:\"\n\t@echo \"  make          — build runner + specs (release)\"\n\t@echo \"  make DEBUG=1  — debug info, no optimization\"\n\t@echo \"  make STRICT=1 — promote warnings to errors\"\n\t@echo \"  make clean    — remove every built artifact\"\n\t@echo \"  make test     — run integration tests (when 311 lands)\"\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ Build rules\n$(POOL_BIN): $(POOL_OBJECTS)\n\t@echo \"  → $(notdir $@)\"\n\t@$(CC) $(CFLAGS) $(CPPFLAGS) -o $@ $^ $(LDFLAGS)\n\n$(BUILD_DIR)/%.o: $(DIR)/%.c\n\t@mkdir -p $(dir $@)\n\t@echo \"  → $(patsubst $(DIR)/%,%,$<)\"\n\t@$(CC) $(CFLAGS) $(CPPFLAGS) -c -o $@ $<\n\n# Per-test dependency lines. A test binary needs its own .o plus\n# the .o files for the source(s) it exercises. {
  "uuid":"833dd751-b6cd-4f4d-b573-a48b7437b586",

    "originalFile":"# 319c — Box id generator and compile cache\n\n## Status\nopen — implementation underway. Scope reduced from the original\nplan (see \"Reduced scope\" below). Design in parent issue 319's\n\"Q4\" resolution.\n\n## Parent issue\nSub-issue of 319. Provides the box id generator that\n`create_box` (319d) returns when the caller doesn't supply an\nexplicit `id`.\n\n## Reduced scope — compile cache not needed as a separate module\n\nIssue 319's Q5 resolution called for a content-hash-keyed\ncompile cache under `tmp/` that shells out to\n`scripts/soramech-compile.sh` on miss. Investigation while\nstarting this sub-issue found that **the language specs already\ndo this work internally**:\n\n- `langs/c/spec.c` has `maybe_lazy_compile` (line 228) that\n  detects a `.c` source path, compiles it to `.so` on first\n  use, and caches the resulting handle in the per-worker dlopen\n  table.\n- Lua and Bash have no compile step — `langs/lua/spec.c` loads\n  via `luaL_loadfile` and caches the Lua module; Bash's spec\n  hands the source path to a persistent subprocess.\n\nSo `create_box(spec)` for any language can resolve via the\nexisting per-spec invocation path. No separate cache layer\npreserves more concept-purity than it saves work — the runner\nalready stays ignorant of the compiler because each language\nspec encapsulates its own loading discipline. The Q5\n\"compile cache\" idea is therefore folded into existing spec\nmachinery rather than implemented as a new module.\n\nIf a future need surfaces for a unified content-hash cache\nabove the spec layer (e.g. for pre-warming or shared\nartifacts across workers), revisit; for now, defer.\n\n## Current behavior\n\nThere is no box id generator. The graph loader currently expects\nevery box's `id` field to be supplied by the caller (from JSON\non disk). `create_box` callers (issue 319d) need a way to\nproduce unique ids when they don't want to name a box themselves.\n\n## Intended behavior\n\nA small utility module that exposes one function:\n\n```c\nint box_id_generate(char *buf, size_t buf_size);\n```\n\nFills `buf` with a string of the form `auto_<8 hex chars>` (a\nprocess-wide atomic counter rendered as hex). Returns 0 on\nsuccess, -1 if `buf_size` is insufficient (the required size\nis 14 bytes: 5 prefix chars + 8 hex chars + null terminator).\n\nUniqueness is guaranteed within a single process run via the\natomic counter. Cross-run uniqueness is not a goal — ids are\nruntime-only constructs; persistent ids come from the on-disk\nbox JSON files.\n\n## Suggested implementation\n\n1. Create `src/017-box-id.h` — declaration of `box_id_generate`.\n2. Create `src/017-box-id.c` — atomic counter + snprintf\n   formatting.\n3. Create `src/017-box-id.info.md` — function listing per the\n   project's documentation convention.\n4. Create `tests/017-box-id-test.c` — verify format, uniqueness\n   across many calls, rejection on too-small buffer, and\n   uniqueness under concurrent access from multiple threads.\n5. Add Makefile dependency line for the new test.\n6. Initialize `file-index-counter` at 17.\n\n## Relevant files\n\n- `src/017-box-id.{h,c}` — new module.\n- `tests/017-box-id-test.c` — new test.\n- `Makefile` — add per-test dependency line.\n",

Freed by\n181\t     * graph_destroy. */\n182\t    int           *n_read_predecessors;    /* n_inputs entries     */\n183\t    int          **read_predecessor_ids;   /* per-port box-index lists */\n184\t    int           *read_pred_counter_slot; /* per-port; -1 unless >1 preds */\n185\t} box_t;\n186\t\n187\t/* Slot mode constants used by box_t.input_slot_modes[]. */\n188\t#define SLOT_MODE_PEEK 0\n189\t#define SLOT_MODE_POP  1\n190\t/* }}} */\n191\t\n192\t/* {{{ Graph */\n193\ttypedef struct graph graph_t;\n194\t\n195\t/* Read a map directory and build the graph. The pool's spec init can use this\n217\t * to skip workers for specs the map doesn't actually use. */\n218\tint          graph_n_languages (const graph_t *g);\n219\tconst char  *graph_language    (const graph_t *g, int i);\n220\t\n221\t/* Entry-box set: indices into graph->boxes of boxes the pool runner\n222\t * submits as initial tasks. A box qualifies when it is BOX_CALL or\n223\t * BOX_WRITE AND every non-optional input is fed only by BOX_READ\n224\t * value sources (or has zero inputs). Filled in by graph_load. */\n225\tint          graph_n_entry_boxes(const graph_t *g);\n226\tint          graph_entry_box    (const graph_t *g, int i);\n227\t\n228\t/* Distinct input-slot cell sizes the graph uses. Filled in by\n229\t * graph_attach_runtime after the per-port slot widths are picked.\n230\t * The slot store can use this to pre-populate free lists. */\n231\tint          graph_n_size_classes(const graph_t *g);\n232\tint          graph_size_class    (const graph_t *g, int i);\n233\t/* }}} */\n234\t\n235\t/* {{{ Runtime attach\n236\t *\n237\t * Allocates one input slot per input port for every box and resolves\n238\t * each call box's language spec from the registry.         "text":"Stepping back before implementation — 319d as fully specified is genuinely a multi-session feature. Three problems converge:\n\n1. **Graph box array** — `box_t *boxes` is a flat realloc'd array; growing it at runtime would invalidate pointers cached by workers.\n2. **Per-box `connections[]` array** — dispatch walks these on the hot push path; growing them concurrently with a fire would race.\n3. **Box record** has ~25 fields that need to be populated correctly for a new box to participate in dispatch.\n\nThe first two are the **same lock-free-growth problem we solved in 319b**, applied to two more structures. The third is a substantial JSON-to-struct marshalling job.\n\n`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`\nThe dispatcher's existing event-driven design is actually a gift here — if a new box's connections wire into a producer correctly and the new box has slots allocated, dispatch picks it up automatically via the existing spawn-on-input-ready check. The hard work is making the mutation safe; the dispatch side needs zero changes.\n`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`\n\n## Three ways to slice this\n\n**(A) Full 319d in one session.** Aggressive. Likely to ship buggy or incomplete. Not recommended.\n\n**(B) Slice into 319d-foundation + 319d-api.** Foundation does the chunked-append work for boxes + connections (no user-facing change, identical behavior). Next session does the C API + Lua bindings + end-to-end test. Cleanest separation; foundation is meaningfully testable on its own.\n\n**(C) Minimum-concurrency version.** Implement `create_box`/`connect` with simple `realloc` + mutex, **document the restriction \"callers must ensure pool quiescence,\"** and get end-to-end working. Concurrent-safe runtime mutation becomes a follow-up. This ships the API shape and lets us test it; the hard race-safety work is deferred until someone actually needs to call it from a hot dispatcher.\n\n**My recommendation: (C).** Reasons:\n- The use case you described (\"planner box decides what sub-pipeline to build at runtime\") is the eventual goal but isn't on the critical path for anything else. Encapsulated maps (248) and the editor work can land independently.\n- Documented restrictions are a normal stepping stone in C; many real systems start this way (early Python, early Rust async).\n- (B)'s foundation slice has zero observable behavior — it's pure machinery that could rot before being used. (C) at least produces a working `create_box` that can be exercised by an end-to-end test.\n- When the concurrent need actually shows up, the lock-free upgrade is a focused change with clear motivation, not speculative infrastructure.\n\nThe 319d issue file (when it gets its update) would note: \"Phase 1 (this commit): single-threaded mutation, mutex-protected. Phase 2 (follow-on): lock-free hot-path-safe mutation when first concurrent use case arrives.\"\n\nWhich slice do you want? **(B), (C), or do you actually want (A) and accept the risk?**"

}\n147\t    return f;\n148\t}\n149\t/* }}} */\n150\t\n151\t/* {{{ parse_routing() — translate JSON routing object into routing_t */\n152\tstatic int parse_routing(const json_node_t *r, routing_t           "replace_all":false,
          "new_string":"/* {{{ Runtime mutation — graph_add_box() (issue 319d)\n *\n * Appends a pre-built box to the graph's pointer index. The pointer\n * array grows via copy-and-publish (allocate at 2x capacity, memcpy\n * the old pointers in, atomic-store the new array, park the old on\n * stale_box_arrs for destroy-time reclamation). The new box's count\n * is published last with release semantics so a reader seeing\n * count = N also sees box N-1 fully published into the index. */\nint graph_add_box(graph_t *g, box_t *box)\n{\n    if (!g || !box) return -1;\n    pthread_mutex_lock(&g->graph_mu);\n\n    uint32_t n   = atomic_load_explicit(&g->n_boxes,      memory_order_relaxed);\n    uint32_t cap = atomic_load_explicit(&g->box_capacity, memory_order_relaxed);\n\n    if (n + 1u > cap) {\n        uint32_t new_cap = cap == 0 ? 16u : cap * 2u;\n        box_t **new_boxes = calloc((size_t)new_cap, sizeof(box_t *));\n        if (!new_boxes) {\n            pthread_mutex_unlock(&g->graph_mu);\n            return -1;\n        }\n        box_t **old_boxes = atomic_load_explicit(&g->boxes, memory_order_relaxed);\n        if (old_boxes && n > 0) {\n            memcpy(new_boxes, old_boxes, (size_t)n * sizeof(box_t *));\n        }\n        struct stale_arr *st = malloc(sizeof *st);\n        if (!st) { free(new_boxes); pthread_mutex_unlock(&g->graph_mu); return -1; }\n        st->ptr  = old_boxes;\n        st->next = g->stale_box_arrs;\n        g->stale_box_arrs = st;\n        atomic_store_explicit(&g->boxes,        new_boxes, memory_order_release);\n        atomic_store_explicit(&g->box_capacity, new_cap,   memory_order_release);\n    }\n\n    box_t **boxes = atomic_load_explicit(&g->boxes, memory_order_relaxed);\n    boxes[n] = box;\n    atomic_store_explicit(&g->n_boxes, n + 1u, memory_order_release);\n\n    pthread_mutex_unlock(&g->graph_mu);\n    return (int)n;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Runtime mutation — box_add_connection() (issue 319d)\n *\n * Appends one connection to box `b`'s connections array via the\n * same copy-and-publish discipline used for boxes: allocate a\n * new connections[] sized current+1, copy the old in, append the\n * new connection, atomic-store the new connections pointer, then\n * atomic-store the new count. The old connections array is parked\n * on stale_box_arrs (the list is generic, not box-specific) and\n * freed at graph_destroy. */\nint box_add_connection(graph_t *g, box_t *b, connection_t conn)\n{\n    if (!g || !b) return -1;\n    pthread_mutex_lock(&g->graph_mu);\n\n    int n_old = atomic_load_explicit(&b->n_connections, memory_order_relaxed);\n    connection_t *old = atomic_load_explicit(&b->connections, memory_order_relaxed);\n\n    connection_t *new_conns = malloc((size_t)(n_old + 1) * sizeof(connection_t));\n    if (!new_conns) { pthread_mutex_unlock(&g->graph_mu); return -1; }\n    if (old && n_old > 0) {\n        memcpy(new_conns, old, (size_t)n_old * sizeof(connection_t));\n    }\n    new_conns[n_old] = conn;\n\n    if (old) {\n        struct stale_arr *st = malloc(sizeof *st);\n        if (!st) { free(new_conns); pthread_mutex_unlock(&g->graph_mu); return -1; }\n        st->ptr  = old;\n        st->next = g->stale_box_arrs;\n        g->stale_box_arrs = st;\n    }\n\n    atomic_store_explicit(&b->connections,   new_conns, memory_order_release);\n    atomic_store_explicit(&b->n_connections, n_old + 1, memory_order_release);\n\n    pthread_mutex_unlock(&g->graph_mu);\n    return 0;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Accessors */\nconst char *graph_name(const graph_t *g)         { return g ? g->name : NULL; }",
          "file_path":"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech/src/010-graph-loader.c"

          "content":"/* src/018-runtime-builtins.h — runtime self-construction primitives.\n *\n * Two C functions that language specs (Lua first, C/Bash to follow)\n * wrap and expose to user code, letting a running box construct new\n * boxes and wire them into the live graph:\n *\n *   runtime_create_box(spec_json) -> box_id\n *   runtime_connect(connection_json) -> 0/-1\n *\n * Designed in issue 319 (the headline self-construction feature);\n * landed in issue 319d.\n *\n * Argument shape: the JSON text passed in mirrors the on-disk box\n * JSON schema exactly. Anything you can write into a `boxes/<id>.json`\n * file, you can pass to runtime_create_box. Anything you can write\n * as an entry inside that file's `connections[]` array, you can\n * pass to runtime_connect. The contract is: the API is the schema.\n *\n * Plumbing: language specs need access to the graph / slot store /\n * spec registry to call these. Rather than thread those pointers\n * through every spec invocation, we keep them in a thread-local\n * \"active context\" that dispatch_action sets before invoking the\n * spec and clears after. The runtime builtins read the thread-local\n * to find the targets.\n */\n#ifndef SORAMECH_018_RUNTIME_BUILTINS_H\n#define SORAMECH_018_RUNTIME_BUILTINS_H\n\n#include <stddef.h>\n\nstruct graph;\nstruct slot_store;\nstruct spec_registry;\n\n/* {{{ Active runtime context (thread-local)\n *\n * Set by dispatch_action immediately before invoking a spec, cleared\n * immediately after. Spec code (including the language bindings that\n * call into runtime_create_box / runtime_connect) reads these to find\n * the graph and runtime resources. */\nvoid runtime_set_active_context(struct graph         *g,\n                                struct slot_store    *s,\n                                struct spec_registry *r);\nvoid runtime_clear_active_context(void);\n\nstruct graph         *runtime_active_graph(void);\nstruct slot_store    *runtime_active_slots(void);\nstruct spec_registry *runtime_active_specs(void);\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ runtime_create_box()\n *\n * Parses `spec_json` as a box schema entry, instantiates the box at\n * runtime, allocates input slots, registers it in the active graph.\n * Fills `out_id` with the new box's id (auto-generated if the JSON\n * didn't supply one). Returns 0 on success, -1 on error with *err\n * set to a malloc'd diagnostic (caller frees).\n *\n * Slice 1 scope (this commit):\n *   - kind: \"call\" only\n *   - lang: \"lua\" only\n *   - routing.kind: \"plain\" only\n *   - inputs: array of { name, type }\n *\n * Other kinds, langs, and routing variants surface clear errors\n * for now; they'll land in 319e. */\nint runtime_create_box(const char *spec_json, int spec_len,\n                       char *out_id, size_t out_id_size,\n                       char **err);\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ runtime_connect()\n *\n * Parses `conn_json` as a connection entry, looks up from_box /\n * to_box / to_input, appends the connection to the producer's\n * connections array via box_add_connection. Returns 0 on success,\n * -1 on error with *err set to a malloc'd diagnostic. */\nint runtime_connect(const char *conn_json, int conn_len,\n                    char **err);\n/* }}} */\n\n#endif /* SORAMECH_018_RUNTIME_BUILTINS_H */\n",

    "content":[{
        "name":"Edit",
        "input":{
          "old_string":"/* {{{ lua_init() — create a state, open standard libs, seed cache */\nstatic void *lua_init(int worker_idx)\n{\n    (void)worker_idx;\n    lua_State *L = luaL_newstate();\n    if (!L) return NULL;\n    luaL_openlibs(L);\n    /* Seed the empty cache table. */\n    lua_newtable(L);\n    lua_setfield(L, LUA_REGISTRYINDEX, LUA_CACHE_KEY);\n    return L;\n}\n/* }}} */",
          "replace_all":false,
          "new_string":"/* {{{ Soramech runtime-builtins: create_box and connect (issue 319d)\n *\n * Two Lua-callable functions exposed under the global `soramech`\n * table. Both take Lua tables shaped like the on-disk box JSON\n * schema (for create_box) or a single connection entry (for\n * connect, variadic). The tables are encoded to JSON via the same\n * encode_value machinery the spec uses for cross-language wire\n * serialization, then handed to the C runtime API. Errors\n * hard-crash via luaL_error, which propagates as a Lua error and\n * unwinds the spec's invoke. */\nstatic int lua_soramech_create_box(lua_State *L)\n{\n    luaL_checktype(L, 1, LUA_TTABLE);\n\n    /* Stack-allocated 4 KB scratch is big enough for any sane box\n     * spec; if a real workload trips this the buffer becomes a\n     * heap allocation. Slice-1 keeps it simple. */\n    char json_buf[4096];\n    json_writer_t w;\n    json_writer_init(&w, json_buf, sizeof json_buf);\n    if (encode_value(L, 1, &w) != 0) {\n        return luaL_error(L, \"soramech.create_box: failed to encode spec to JSON\");\n    }\n    int json_len = json_writer_finish(&w);\n    if (json_len < 0) {\n        return luaL_error(L, \"soramech.create_box: JSON encode overflow (spec exceeds %zu bytes)\",\n                          sizeof json_buf);\n    }\n\n    char id_buf[BOX_ID_GEN_BUF_SIZE];\n    char *err = NULL;\n    if (runtime_create_box(json_buf, json_len, id_buf, sizeof id_buf, &err) != 0) {\n        char msg[1024];\n        snprintf(msg, sizeof msg, \"%s\", err ? err : \"(no message)\");\n        free(err);\n        return luaL_error(L, \"soramech.create_box: %s\", msg);\n    }\n    lua_pushstring(L, id_buf);\n    return 1;\n}\n\nstatic int lua_soramech_connect(lua_State *L)\n{\n    int n = lua_gettop(L);\n    if (n == 0) {\n        return luaL_error(L, \"soramech.connect: expected at least one connection\");\n    }\n    char json_buf[2048];\n    for (int i = 1; i <= n; i++) {\n        luaL_checktype(L, i, LUA_TTABLE);\n        json_writer_t w;\n        json_writer_init(&w, json_buf, sizeof json_buf);\n        if (encode_value(L, i, &w) != 0) {\n            return luaL_error(L, \"soramech.connect: failed to encode connection #%d\", i);\n        }\n        int json_len = json_writer_finish(&w);\n        if (json_len < 0) {\n            return luaL_error(L, \"soramech.connect: JSON encode overflow on connection #%d\", i);\n        }\n        char *err = NULL;\n        if (runtime_connect(json_buf, json_len, &err) != 0) {\n            char msg[1024];\n            snprintf(msg, sizeof msg, \"%s\", err ? err : \"(no message)\");\n            free(err);\n            return luaL_error(L, \"soramech.connect: %s\", msg);\n        }\n    }\n    return 0;\n}\n\nstatic void register_soramech_builtins(lua_State *L)\n{\n    lua_newtable(L);\n    lua_pushcfunction(L, lua_soramech_create_box);\n    lua_setfield(L, -2, \"create_box\");\n    lua_pushcfunction(L, lua_soramech_connect);\n    lua_setfield(L, -2, \"connect\");\n    lua_setglobal(L, \"soramech\");\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ lua_init() — create a state, open standard libs, seed cache */\nstatic void *lua_init(int worker_idx)\n{\n    (void)worker_idx;\n    lua_State *L = luaL_newstate();\n    if (!L) return NULL;\n    luaL_openlibs(L);\n    /* Seed the empty cache table. */\n    lua_newtable(L);\n    lua_setfield(L, LUA_REGISTRYINDEX, LUA_CACHE_KEY);\n    /* Register the self-construction builtins (issue 319d). They\n     * read the active runtime context from thread-local storage\n     * that dispatch_action sets before each invoke. */\n    register_soramech_builtins(L);\n    return L;\n}\n/* }}} */",
          "file_path":"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech/langs/lua/spec.c"
        },

    "filePath":"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech/langs/lua/spec.c",
    "oldString":"/* {{{ lua_init() — create a state, open standard libs, seed cache */\nstatic void *lua_init(int worker_idx)\n{\n    (void)worker_idx;\n    lua_State *L = luaL_newstate();\n    if (!L) return NULL;\n    luaL_openlibs(L);\n    /* Seed the empty cache table. */\n    lua_newtable(L);\n    lua_setfield(L, LUA_REGISTRYINDEX, LUA_CACHE_KEY);\n    return L;\n}\n/* }}} */",
    "newString":"/* {{{ Soramech runtime-builtins: create_box and connect (issue 319d)\n *\n * Two Lua-callable functions exposed under the global `soramech`\n * table. Both take Lua tables shaped like the on-disk box JSON\n * schema (for create_box) or a single connection entry (for\n * connect, variadic). The tables are encoded to JSON via the same\n * encode_value machinery the spec uses for cross-language wire\n * serialization, then handed to the C runtime API. Errors\n * hard-crash via luaL_error, which propagates as a Lua error and\n * unwinds the spec's invoke. */\nstatic int lua_soramech_create_box(lua_State *L)\n{\n    luaL_checktype(L, 1, LUA_TTABLE);\n\n    /* Stack-allocated 4 KB scratch is big enough for any sane box\n     * spec; if a real workload trips this the buffer becomes a\n     * heap allocation. Slice-1 keeps it simple. */\n    char json_buf[4096];\n    json_writer_t w;\n    json_writer_init(&w, json_buf, sizeof json_buf);\n    if (encode_value(L, 1, &w) != 0) {\n        return luaL_error(L, \"soramech.create_box: failed to encode spec to JSON\");\n    }\n    int json_len = json_writer_finish(&w);\n    if (json_len < 0) {\n        return luaL_error(L, \"soramech.create_box: JSON encode overflow (spec exceeds %zu bytes)\",\n                          sizeof json_buf);\n    }\n\n    char id_buf[BOX_ID_GEN_BUF_SIZE];\n    char *err = NULL;\n    if (runtime_create_box(json_buf, json_len, id_buf, sizeof id_buf, &err) != 0) {\n        char msg[1024];\n        snprintf(msg, sizeof msg, \"%s\", err ? err : \"(no message)\");\n        free(err);\n        return luaL_error(L, \"soramech.create_box: %s\", msg);\n    }\n    lua_pushstring(L, id_buf);\n    return 1;\n}\n\nstatic int lua_soramech_connect(lua_State *L)\n{\n    int n = lua_gettop(L);\n    if (n == 0) {\n        return luaL_error(L, \"soramech.connect: expected at least one connection\");\n    }\n    char json_buf[2048];\n    for (int i = 1; i <= n; i++) {\n        luaL_checktype(L, i, LUA_TTABLE);\n        json_writer_t w;\n        json_writer_init(&w, json_buf, sizeof json_buf);\n        if (encode_value(L, i, &w) != 0) {\n            return luaL_error(L, \"soramech.connect: failed to encode connection #%d\", i);\n        }\n        int json_len = json_writer_finish(&w);\n        if (json_len < 0) {\n            return luaL_error(L, \"soramech.connect: JSON encode overflow on connection #%d\", i);\n        }\n        char *err = NULL;\n        if (runtime_connect(json_buf, json_len, &err) != 0) {\n            char msg[1024];\n            snprintf(msg, sizeof msg, \"%s\", err ? err : \"(no message)\");\n            free(err);\n            return luaL_error(L, \"soramech.connect: %s\", msg);\n        }\n    }\n    return 0;\n}\n\nstatic void register_soramech_builtins(lua_State *L)\n{\n    lua_newtable(L);\n    lua_pushcfunction(L, lua_soramech_create_box);\n    lua_setfield(L, -2, \"create_box\");\n    lua_pushcfunction(L, lua_soramech_connect);\n    lua_setfield(L, -2, \"connect\");\n    lua_setglobal(L, \"soramech\");\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ lua_init() — create a state, open standard libs, seed cache */\nstatic void *lua_init(int worker_idx)\n{\n    (void)worker_idx;\n    lua_State *L = luaL_newstate();\n    if (!L) return NULL;\n    luaL_openlibs(L);\n    /* Seed the empty cache table. */\n    lua_newtable(L);\n    lua_setfield(L, LUA_REGISTRYINDEX, LUA_CACHE_KEY);\n    /* Register the self-construction builtins (issue 319d). They\n     * read the active runtime context from thread-local storage\n     * that dispatch_action sets before each invoke. */\n    register_soramech_builtins(L);\n    return L;\n}\n/* }}} */"
  },

    "stdout":"# langs/lua/Makefile — build the Lua language spec.\n#\n# Produces spec.so, a small .so the pool runner dlopens at startup.\n# Links against LuaJIT 2.1 (override LUA_INCLUDE / LUA_LIB if the\n# headers and library live somewhere other than the Debian/Arch\n# default).\n#\n# Invokable standalone (`make -C langs/lua`) or from the top-level\n# Makefile via `make specs`. The DIR variable lets the top-level\n# pass the project root so the -I path to langs/lang-spec.h resolves.\n\n# {{{ Resolve project root\nDIR ?= $(abspath $(dir $(lastword $(MAKEFILE_LIST)))/../..)\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ Toolchain & flags\nCC          ?= gcc\nLUA_INCLUDE ?= /usr/include/luajit-2.1\nLUA_LIB     ?= /usr/lib\n\nCFLAGS  = -shared -fPIC -O2 -Wall -I$(LUA_INCLUDE) -I$(DIR)/langs -I$(DIR)/libs/json\nLDFLAGS = -L$(LUA_LIB) -lluajit-5.1\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ Build rules\n# spec.c needs the JSON writer + DOM parser for the native↔JSON\n# bridges (issue 317). ## [1260]

```json
{
  "uuid":"4ba15a6f-18a1-4dac-afe2-370867dda21b",
  "type":"user",
  "timestamp":"2026-05-24T00:00:33.987Z",
  "parentUuid":"328a0a49-8730-4e04-8cc9-676ebeb2ea06",
  "toolUseResult":{
    "originalFile":"# SoraMech — top-level build orchestration.\n#\n# What it does, in a sentence: builds the phase 3 pool runner binary\n# plus one shared library per language spec. Release by default;\n# DEBUG=1 keeps symbols and disables optimization, STRICT=1 promotes\n# warnings to errors. `make clean` removes everything that was built.\n#\n# Invokable from any directory: `make -C /path/to/soramech` works,\n# and the DIR variable can be overridden if needed (e.g. for an\n# out-of-tree checkout). All paths in this Makefile are relative to\n# $(DIR) per the project convention.\n#\n# Designed in issue 309. Implementation of the runner's runtime is\n# split across issues 301–308; this Makefile builds whatever sources\n# exist under src/, libs/task-pool/, and libs/json/, so it scales as\n# those issues land.\n\n# {{{ Resolve project root\nDIR ?= $(abspath $(dir $(lastword $(MAKEFILE_LIST))))\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ Toolchain & flags\nCC      ?= gcc\n\n# Shared header search path: every C source can find langs/lang-spec.h\n# and any future libs/<name>/ headers via -I flags below.\nCPPFLAGS = -I$(DIR)/langs -I$(DIR)/libs/task-pool -I$(DIR)/libs/json -I$(DIR)/src\n\n# Default to release; DEBUG and STRICT toggle alternates.\nifeq ($(DEBUG),1)\n  CFLAGS = -O0 -g -DDEBUG -Wall -pthread -fPIC\nelse ifeq ($(STRICT),1)\n  CFLAGS = -O2 -Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic -Werror -pthread -fPIC\nelse\n  CFLAGS = -O2 -Wall -pthread -fPIC\nendif\n\nLDFLAGS = -ldl -pthread\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ Paths and source discovery\nBUILD_DIR = $(DIR)/build\nPOOL_BIN  = $(DIR)/soramech-pool\n\n# Wildcards: empty subdirs return empty lists, which is fine. As\n# issues 301/302/303/304/305 land their C sources here, they get\n# compiled automatically — no Makefile edit required.\nPOOL_SOURCES = \\\n  $(wildcard $(DIR)/src/*.c) \\\n  $(wildcard $(DIR)/libs/task-pool/*.c) \\\n  $(wildcard $(DIR)/libs/json/*.c)\n\nPOOL_OBJECTS = $(POOL_SOURCES:$(DIR)/%.c=$(BUILD_DIR)/%.o)\n\n# Test sources live in tests/ as C files named to match the source\n# they exercise (e.g. tests/009-slot-store-test.c exercises\n# src/009-slot-store.c). Each builds to a separate executable that\n# `make test` runs in turn.\nTEST_SOURCES = $(wildcard $(DIR)/tests/*.c)\nTEST_BINS    = $(TEST_SOURCES:$(DIR)/tests/%.c=$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/%)\n\nLANGS = lua c bash\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ Public targets\n.PHONY: all runner specs clean test help\n\nall: runner specs\n\nrunner: $(POOL_BIN)\n\nspecs:\n\t@for lang in $(LANGS); do \\\n\t  echo \"  → langs/$$lang\"; \\\n\t  $(MAKE) -s -C $(DIR)/langs/$$lang DIR=$(DIR) || exit 1; \\\n\tdone\n\nclean:\n\trm -f $(POOL_BIN)\n\trm -rf $(BUILD_DIR)\n\t@for lang in $(LANGS); do \\\n\t  $(MAKE) -s -C $(DIR)/langs/$$lang DIR=$(DIR) clean || true; \\\n\tdone\n\ntest: all $(TEST_BINS)\n\t@echo\n\t@fail=0; \\\n\tfor t in $(TEST_BINS); do \\\n\t  $$t || fail=1; \\\n\t  echo; \\\n\tdone; \\\n\tif [ -x $(DIR)/scripts/run-tests.sh ]; then \\\n\t  $(DIR)/scripts/run-tests.sh $(DIR) || fail=1; \\\n\tfi; \\\n\texit $$fail\n\nhelp:\n\t@echo \"SoraMech build:\"\n\t@echo \"  make          — build runner + specs (release)\"\n\t@echo \"  make DEBUG=1  — debug info, no optimization\"\n\t@echo \"  make STRICT=1 — promote warnings to errors\"\n\t@echo \"  make clean    — remove every built artifact\"\n\t@echo \"  make test     — run integration tests (when 311 lands)\"\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ Build rules\n$(POOL_BIN): $(POOL_OBJECTS)\n\t@echo \"  → $(notdir $@)\"\n\t@$(CC) $(CFLAGS) $(CPPFLAGS) -o $@ $^ $(LDFLAGS)\n\n$(BUILD_DIR)/%.o: $(DIR)/%.c\n\t@mkdir -p $(dir $@)\n\t@echo \"  → $(patsubst $(DIR)/%,%,$<)\"\n\t@$(CC) $(CFLAGS) $(CPPFLAGS) -c -o $@ $<\n\n# Per-test dependency lines. A test binary needs its own .o plus\n# the .o files for the source(s) it exercises. As each test lands,\n# add one line here naming the dependencies (no globbing — explicit\n# is clearer than clever for tests).\n$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/009-slot-store-test:    $(BUILD_DIR)/src/009-slot-store.o \\\n                                           $(BUILD_DIR)/src/016-unified-allocator.o\n$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/015-large-value-heap-test: $(BUILD_DIR)/src/015-large-value-heap.o\n$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/016-unified-allocator-test: $(BUILD_DIR)/src/016-unified-allocator.o\n$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/010-graph-loader-test: $(BUILD_DIR)/src/010-graph-loader.o \\\n                                          $(BUILD_DIR)/src/009-slot-store.o \\\n The first push that\n267\t     * finds the consumer ready wins; everyone else short-circuits.\n268\t     * The 1-cell peek model spawns each box at most once per run. */\n269\t    int expected = 0;\n270\t    if (atomic_compare_exchange_strong(&ctx->box_ever_spawned[box_id],\n271\t                                       &expected, 1)) {\n272\t        dispatch_spawn(ctx, box_id, priority);\n273\t    }\n274\t}\n275\t/* }}} */\n276\t\n277\t/* {{{ dispatch_push_literals() */\n278\tint dispatch_push_literals(dispatch_ctx_t *ctx, char **err)\n279\t{\n280\t    if (!ctx) {\n281\t        if (err) *err = err_fmt(\"dispatch_push_literals: NULL ctx\");\n282\t        return -1;"
      }],

{
  "uuid":"883742bb-2079-42f0-b287-fb07fec5ff3a",
  "type":"user",
  "timestamp":"2026-05-24T00:20:48.862Z",
  "parentUuid":"ed9fd3e9-a18f-40c0-9e68-2b4e7f1e741c",
  "toolUseResult":{
    "originalFile":"#!/bin/bash\n# scripts/run-tests.sh — phase 3 integration tests.\n#\n# Runs every fixture map under tests/maps/ through `soramech-pool`\n# and asserts that the captured outputs match a hardcoded\n# expectation per map. The point is to catch regressions\n# end-to-end — past the spec interface, past the dispatch action,\n# past JSONL writing — rather than via the in-process unit tests.\n#\n# Per the project convention: scripts run from any directory via a\n# hard-coded ${DIR} path with an override argument; all paths are\n# relative to ${DIR}.\n\nset -u\n\nDIR=\"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech\"\nif [[ $# -ge 1 ]]; then\n    DIR=\"$1\"\nfi\n\ncd \"$DIR\"\n\npass=0\nfail=0\nfailures=()\n\n# {{{ check_map() — run one fixture, verify expected substrings\ncheck_map() {\n    local map=\"$1\"\n    shift\n    local expected=(\"$@\")\n\n    printf \"  %-44s \" \"$map\"\n\n    local output\n    output=$(\"$DIR/soramech-pool\" \"$DIR/tests/maps/$map\" 2>&1)\n    local rc=$?\n\n    local missing=\"\"\n    if [[ $rc -ne 0 ]]; then\n        printf \"FAIL — soramech-compile failed\\n\"\n        fail=$((fail + 1))\n        failures+=(\"compile: script returned non-zero\")\n        return\n    fi\n    if [[ ! -x \"$compiled/pool-runner\" ]]; then\n        printf \"ok\\n\"\n        pass=$((pass + 1))\n    else\n        printf \"FAIL — output='%s' file='%s'\\n\" \"$output\" \"$content\"\n        fail=$((fail + 1))\n        failures+=(\"compile: bad output\")\n    fi\n}\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ run all fixtures\necho \"integration tests (fixture maps):\"\n\ncheck_map \"calc\" \\\n    \"add → 42\"\n\ncheck_map \"hello\" \\\n    \"greet → Hello, World!\"\n\ncheck_map \"comparator\" \\\n    \"classify → 8\" \\\n    \"high → HIGH:8\" \\\n    \"low → (no output)\" \\\n    \"mid → (no output)\"\n\ncheck_map \"iter-route\" \\\n    \"iter → hi\" \\\n    \"a → A:hi\" \\\n    \"b → (no output)\" \\\n    \"c → (no output)\"\n\ncheck_map \"pipeline\" \\\n    \"double → 10\" \\\n    \"addone → 11\" \\\n    \"shout → 11!\"\n\ncheck_map \"read-literal\" \\\n    \"echo → hello, world!\"\n\ncheck_map \"319a-many-inputs\" \\\n    \"combine → count=20 sum=210\"\n\npipeline_output_check\ncompile_pipeline_check\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ parser_tests() — issue 232: unit tests for langs/<lang>/parser.js\n# Run Node's built-in test runner over each per-language parser test\n# file and fold the result into the surrounding pass/fail counters.\n# Each .mjs file is one logical \"test\" from this script's perspective;\n# Node prints its own subtest breakdown on failure for the diagnostic.\nparser_tests() {\n    if ! command -v node >/dev/null 2>&1; The dynamically-\n  created box fires and produces output.\n\n## Restrictions in this slice\n\n- **Lua only.** C and Bash specs don't yet expose `soramech.*`.\n  Their bindings land in 319e.\n- **Call boxes only.** `create_box` rejects `kind != \"call\"`.\n  Read / write / encapsulated-map kinds land later.\n- **Plain routing only.** Comparator / iterator / randomizer /\n  weighted / distributor routing on dynamically-created boxes\n  rejected.\n- **Runtime-headroom cap.** Dispatch's per-box arrays support up\n  to 4096 dynamically-created boxes.     "content":"# 319d — `create_box` and `connect` runtime built-ins, Lua bindings\n\n## Status\ncomplete (slice 1)\n\n## Parent issue\nSub-issue of 319. Lands the headline self-construction feature\nfor Lua call boxes with plain routing. C and Bash bindings,\nnon-call kinds, comparator / iterator / etc. routing, and\nencapsulated map outputs all roll up under 319e or follow-on\nslices.\n\n## Current behavior\n\nTwo runtime functions exposed to language specs (Lua first):\n\n- **`soramech.create_box(table)` → string** — instantiates a new\n  box at runtime. The `table` argument mirrors the on-disk box\n  JSON schema; anything writable as `boxes/<id>.json` is acceptable.\n  Internally: serializes the Lua table to JSON via the same\n  `encode_value` machinery used for cross-language wire\n  serialization (issue 312); hands the JSON to the C runtime API\n  which parses, allocates a box record, allocates input slots\n  (319b), and appends to the graph's box index via `graph_add_box`.\n  Returns the new box's id (auto-generated via 319c if the spec\n  didn't supply one).\n- **`soramech.connect(table, ...)`** — variadic. Each table is\n  one entry shaped like a `connections[]` entry on disk\n  (`{from_box, from_branch, to_box, to_input}`). Appends to the\n  producer's atomic `connections` array via `box_add_connection`.\n\nBoth hard-crash via `luaL_error` on any failure (Q3 resolution).\n\nPlumbing: a thread-local `runtime_active_context` is set by\n`dispatch_action` before each spec invoke and cleared after.\nThe runtime builtins read the TLS to find the active graph,\nslot store, and spec registry — no changes to the spec's\ninvoke signature were required.\n\n## What lands in this slice\n\n- `src/010-graph-loader.{h,c}` — `box_t *boxes` becomes\n  `_Atomic(box_t **)` with copy-and-publish growth via\n  `graph_add_box`; box records are now individual mallocs so\n  their addresses are stable across pointer-array growth.\n  Per-box `connections` becomes `_Atomic(connection_t *)` with\n  the same atomic-publish + stale-list pattern via\n  `box_add_connection`.\n- `src/017-box-id.h/c` — already-shipped 319c utility, reused.\n- `src/018-runtime-builtins.{h,c}` — the `runtime_create_box`\n  and `runtime_connect` C functions plus the TLS active-context\n  setter/getter pair.\n- `src/012-dispatch.c` — sets and clears the TLS context around\n  each spec invoke. Also: dispatch's per-box arrays\n  (`box_ever_spawned`, `last_outputs`, `last_output_sizes`) get\n  oversized by `RUNTIME_BOX_HEADROOM = 4096` entries at init\n  so runtime-created boxes have room to participate. Proper\n  growable arrays are a follow-on.\n- `src/008-pool-runner.c` — `print_outputs` now iterates over\n  `graph_n_boxes(ctx->graph)` (which reflects runtime additions)\n  rather than `ctx->n_boxes` (capacity).\n- `langs/lua/spec.c` — `lua_soramech_create_box` /\n  `lua_soramech_connect` wrappers + `register_soramech_builtins`\n  called from `lua_init`.\n- `langs/lua/Makefile` — adds `-I$(DIR)/src` so the lua spec can\n  include the runtime-builtins header.\n- `Makefile` — adds `-rdynamic` to `LDFLAGS` so dlopen'd spec.so\n  binaries can call back into the runner's `runtime_*` symbols.\n- `tests/maps/319d-runtime-create/` — end-to-end fixture: a Lua\n  box uses `soramech.create_box` to spawn an `echo_dyn` box,\n  uses `soramech.connect` to wire to it, then returns a value\n  that pushes through the new connection. The dynamically-\n  created box fires and produces output.\n\n## Restrictions in this slice\n\n- **Lua only.** C and Bash specs don't yet expose `soramech.*`.\n  Their bindings land in 319e.\n- **Call boxes only.** `create_box` rejects `kind != \"call\"`.\n  Read / write / encapsulated-map kinds land later.\n- **Plain routing only.** Comparator / iterator / randomizer /\n  weighted / distributor routing on dynamically-created boxes\n  rejected.\n- **Runtime-headroom cap.** Dispatch's per-box arrays support up\n  to 4096 dynamically-created boxes. Beyond that, spawn checks\n  silently fail. The cap is dispatch-internal; raise it or land\n  growable arrays when needed.\n- **Single-spawn-firing-box assumption.** `connect` is safe when\n  called from the spec of the producer being wired (the common\n  case), since the single-spawn CAS guard means no other worker\n  is reading that box's connections concurrently. Calling\n  `connect` from one box's spec to add a wire FROM a different,\n  potentially-firing box is not race-safe; documented but not\n  enforced.\n\n## Validation\n\n- 13 integration tests pass, including the new\n  `319d-runtime-create` fixture that exercises the full path\n  end-to-end: trigger Lua box's function calls `create_box`,\n  calls `connect`, returns a value; the dispatcher pushes\n  through the new connection; the dynamically-created `echo_dyn`\n  box fires and its output is captured.\n- The slot store's 23 unit tests (including the 319b growth\n  test) still pass.\n\n## Relevant files\n\n- `src/010-graph-loader.{h,c}`\n- `src/012-dispatch.c`\n- `src/008-pool-runner.c`\n- `src/018-runtime-builtins.{h,c}` (new)\n- `langs/lua/spec.c`\n- `langs/lua/Makefile`\n- `Makefile`\n- `tests/maps/319d-runtime-create/`\n- `scripts/run-tests.sh`\n",
    "filePath":"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech/issues/319d-create-box-and-connect-builtins.md",
    "userModified":false
  },

    "originalFile":"# Phase 3 Progress\n\nGoal: replace the Lua synchronous runner with a C thread pool runner\nthat executes box graphs in parallel.\n\nThe phase is fully designed; implementation is now underway.\nIssues 301–313 are the architectural specification. As each issue\nmoves into implementation, its row is marked \"in progress\"; on\ncompletion it's moved to `issues/completed/`.\n\nImplementation began **2026-05-12** with the 309 build scaffolding.\n\n## Issues\n\n| ID  | Title                                                       | Status   |\n|-----|-------------------------------------------------------------|----------|\n| 301 | thread pool lifecycle and per-worker initialization         | complete · pool + per-worker init/teardown hooks + priority queue |\n| 302 | per-task slot store with wire-held references               | complete · unified allocator + refcounted recycling on every byte path (slot cells, variable-size payloads, dispatch input/output buffers) + eager neighbor-merge + quiescence-trigger deep sweep |\n| 303 | language runtime spec (pluggable per-language invocation)   | complete · registry + per-worker init + pool hook + lang filtering |\n| 304 | task dispatch layer (C, replaces synchronous executor)      | complete · every routing kind, slab-allocated task structs, live_wire_count placeholder; attempt-task rewrite reconsidered |\n| 305 | C graph loader (replaces `003-loader.lua`)                  | complete · all seven phases + entry-box set + size classes + all six routing kinds |\n| 306 | Lua language spec implementation                            | complete · init + invoke + teardown + per-worker module cache + per-edge native/JSON in & out |\n| 307 | C language spec implementation                              | complete · compile + lazy .c→.so + invoke + per-worker dlopen cache + JSON in/out (string-wrap + primitive-passthrough); typed-wrapper generator deferred to future enhancement |\n| 308 | Bash language spec implementation                           | complete · persistent socketpair + line-protocol invoke + dladdr-based server lookup |\n| 309 | build system & Makefile orchestration                       | complete · scaffolding + spec discovery + soramech-compile portable artifact |\n| 310 | priority queue: wired in, no-op behaviorally                | complete · API + ordering done |\n| 311 | integration tests & run output (`last-run.jsonl`)           | in progress · writer + queue + thread + LOG_VALUES + LOG_SLOTS + run-tests.sh + compile-pipeline check |\n| 312 | same-language wire fast path (skip JSON for Lua→Lua etc.)   | complete · dual-ring slots + per-edge classification + per-cell ordering; spec contract has single invoke + two bridges; Lua native-bytes optimisation tracked as a future slice |\n| 313 | research: whole-program same-language merge                 | research / blocked |\n| 314 | small C JSON parser written for this project                | complete · parser + writer + strict leading-zero |\n| 315 | reference-counted compiled-map artifacts                    | open · design only |\n| 316 | simple test-runner script                                   | folded into 232 |\n| 317 | language spec JSON bridge for data boxes                    | complete · Lua fidelity-preserving, C+Bash pass-through-or-string-wrap, shared test harness |\n| 319 | built-in library for map self-construction (`create_box`, `connect`) | open · design complete; sub-issues 319a–e |\n| 319a | dispatch input cap removal (VLA + named constant)           | complete · 20-input fixture passes end-to-end |\n| 319b | slot store growth (two-level chunked-append index)          | complete · 5000-slot growth test preserves all early pointers |\n| 319c | box id generator (compile-cache concept folded into spec.so loaders) | complete · 8-thread concurrent uniqueness test passes |\n\n## Phase goal checklist\n\n- [x] SoraMech-owned task pool builds clean (3d-rts as design reference)\n- [x] Slot store unit-tested (single-value + ring buffer)\n- [x] C graph loader passes the project's existing maps\n- [x] Lua spec runs `tests/maps/hello` end-to-end\n- [x] C spec compiles and runs a fixed-signature box\n- [x] Bash spec runs an out-of-process box via persistent\n      socketpair + line-protocol\n- [x] Pool runner runs a multi-language map with concurrent workers\n- [x] Iterator box routes via dispatch layer (with multi-spawn\n      re-fire via N-cell pop slots and auto-re-spawn)\n- [x] Comparator box routes via dispatch layer (via spec output)\n- [x] Variable-size outputs work via the large-value heap\n- [x] `last-run.jsonl` written for every run\n- [ ] All 11 integration test maps pass\n- [ ] Phase 3 demo map runs and produces expected output\n- [ ] Phase 2 synchronous runner retired (`src/004-executor.lua`,\n      `src/007-runner-main.lua`, `src/003-loader.lua`, `drivers/*.sh`)\n\n## Implementation order suggestion\n\nDesigned to surface concrete artifacts early so subsequent issues can\nbuild on them.\n\n1. **309 (build system)** — top-level Makefile, vendored deps, empty\n   stubs for runner and specs. Verify everything compiles.\n2. **302 (slot store)** — pure C, unit-testable, no pool dependency.\n3. **305 (graph loader)** — pure C, parses existing phase 2 maps.\n4. **301 (pool lifecycle)** — wire pool startup, per-worker context,\n   active-task counter, quiescence.\n5. **303 (lang spec interface)** — header file + stub spec to validate\n   the loading mechanism.\n6. **306 (Lua spec)** — easiest reference.
