The producer is free as\n  soon as it's done writing raw bytes to the ring.\n- Each consumer eats its own translation cost; mixed fan-in\n  consumers translate cell-by-cell as they pop.\n- The custom shim is in the same language as the box's main\n  function, so it has full access to that language's runtime\n  (Lua tables, C structs, etc.) without crossing another\n  language boundary first.\n\n## Where it sits relative to the dual-ring (issue 312)\n\nThe dual-ring routing still applies. The producer chooses a ring\nper `output_edge_native[j]` as today. The consumer's per-port\ncustom shim sees the raw bytes plus the `which_ring` tag — so it\ncan distinguish \"these bytes are my own language's native format\"\nfrom \"these bytes are JSON from a cross-language producer\" and act\naccordingly.\n\nIn the easy cases (same-language same-shape), no custom shim is\nneeded; the default native pass-through still works. The custom\nshim earns its keep on the cells where the default\n`json_to_native` would error or produce something useless — that's\nwhere the user-written code takes over.\n\n## File layout\n\n```\nmaps/<name>/\n    boxes/\n        <box_id>.json                ← per-input port may reference translations/\n    translations/\n        <box_id>__<port_name>.<lang_ext>     ← per-port shim\n    src/\n        <box_id>.<lang_ext>                  ← box's main function\n```\n\nThe box JSON's `inputs` array grows an optional per-port field:\n\n```json\n{\n    \"id\": \"consume_class\",\n    \"lang\": \"c\",\n    \"ref\": \"consume.c\",\n    \"fn\": \"consume\",\n    \"inputs\": [\n        { \"name\": \"instance\", \"type\": \"bytes\",\n          \"custom_translation\": \"translations/consume_class__instance.c\" },\n        { \"name\": \"weight\",   \"type\": \"int\" }\n    ],\n    \"...\": \"...\"\n}\n```\n\nIf a port omits `custom_translation`, the default-spec decode runs\nfor that port as today. The `translations/` directory may contain\nshims with no attached port (orphaned, kept on disk by the\ndelete-doesn't-delete-file rule).\n\n## Custom translation function signature\n\nPer-port shims take one input's raw bytes and the `which_ring`\nflag, return one translated value in the consumer's native form.\nWorking draft for C:\n\n```c\nint sm_translate(const void *input_raw, int input_size,\n                 int input_native,\n                 void *output_native, int output_capacity,\n                 int *output_size);\n```\n\nLua's shape is analogous but in Lua-native terms — the function\ntakes a Lua string (the raw bytes) and a boolean (the native\nflag), returns the translated Lua value.\n\nOne signature per port keeps each shim's surface area exactly\nmatched to the port's job. A shim that needs to consult other\nports has a problem this design doesn't try to solve (per-port\nisolation is the principled choice); the user can fall back to\nplain decode-then-validate inside the box's main function for\ncross-port logic.\n\n## Default content of a freshly-created shim\n\nThe \"New\" button writes a file containing a literal copy of what\nthe default spec would do for that port's declared type. For C,\nthat's the small generated wrapper that parses `input_raw` per\nthe port's declared type and writes the result. For Lua, it's a\nfew lines that decode via the existing JSON / native helpers\nbased on `input_native`.\n\nThe user can run the shim without edits and behaviour matches the\nno-shim default. Edits typically replace one branch (the\nspecific weird case) and leave the rest alone. The \"starts as\ndefault, edits in place\" shape matches the project's preference\nfor upgrade paths over from-scratch authoring.\n\n## Compile pipeline (issue 309)\n\nThe compile pipeline already walks every box's `ref` to copy\nsource into `compiled/src/`. The same walk inspects each input\nport's `custom_translation` field and copies referenced files\ninto `compiled/translations/`. For C, each translation file\ncompiles to a `.so` alongside the box's main function. For Lua,\nfiles load into the worker's `lua_State` like any other Lua\nsource.\n\nWhen issue 313 (same-language source merge) lands, translation\nfiles get concatenated into the per-language bundle the same way\nbox main functions do — a translation file is just another\nfunction in the merged module.\n\n## Why this is the right escape hatch\n\nThe default spec contract is \"JSON is the universal interop, each\nspec handles its own native form, sentinels carry the in-process\nexotic cases on the producer side.\" That's enough for the\noverwhelming majority of data flow. The cases where it fails are\nexactly the cases where the user has knowledge the system can't\never infer — what a `void *` points to, how a serialized object\nis structured, which port is a discriminator for which other port.\n\nPushing those back to the user via a per-port shim is honest\nabout where the knowledge has to come from. It also lets the\ndefault spec contract stay narrow and predictable — the spec\nauthors don't have to chase every possible ambiguous receive-side\ntype with new special cases.\n\n## Relevant files\n\n- `assets/js/002-boxes.js` — box state; per-input\n  `custom_translation` field read/write.\n- `assets/index.html` — inspector UI (New / View / Delete buttons\n  on each input-port row).\n- `src/006-server-main.lua` — HTTP backend for translation file\n  CRUD (path validation against `maps/<name>/translations/`).\n- `src/010-graph-loader.{c,h}` — load each input port's\n  `custom_translation` onto `box_t->inputs[i]`.\n- `src/012-dispatch.c` — input-read branch on\n  `box->inputs[i].custom_translation`.\n- `scripts/soramech-compile.sh` — package translation files into\n  the compiled map (issue 309).\n- `issues/245-wire-color-by-cross-language-classification.md` —\n  goldenrod-cheddar wires for ports with custom translations.\n- `issues/312-same-language-wire-fast-path.md` — dual-ring shape\n  the translation slots into.\n- `issues/313-research-whole-program-same-language-merge.md` —\n  custom translations get merged alongside box source.\n\n## Suggested implementation sequence\n\n1. **Box JSON schema**: add the optional per-input\n   `custom_translation` field. Graph loader reads it; absence\n   means default path for that port.\n2. **HTTP backend**: CRUD routes for translation files. Path\n   validation against `maps/<name>/translations/`.\n3. **Editor inspector**: New / View / Delete affordances on each\n   input-port row. \"New\" generates the file with\n   default-spec-equivalent contents parameterized on the port's\n   declared type. The 245 wire-coloring change activates\n   automatically once the field exists.\n4. **Box-delete confirmation**: detect any ports with attached\n   translations; prompt before deletion; preserve the files on\n   disk regardless.\n5. **Dispatch**: input-read per-port branch on\n   `custom_translation`; route bytes through the shim instead of\n   the default decode for that port.\n6. **Compile pipeline**: walk each input port's\n   `custom_translation`; package files into\n   `compiled/translations/` and the per-language source bundle.\n\n## Open questions\n\n- **Shared translations across multiple ports.** Two ports on\n  different boxes that need the same shim can both reference the\n  same file path — the system supports it implicitly. The\n  editor's \"New\" button always creates a fresh file with the\n  default naming so users don't accidentally share by default.\n  Library imports inside translation files (for shared helpers\n  inside a shim) are out of scope here — the user can do that via\n  the language's normal import mechanism.\n- **Compile-time validation.** Should the compile button check\n  that every `custom_translation` path exists and parses? Easy\n  add to the existing compile validation; do once translations\n  exist as a feature.\n- **Shim author seeing cross-port context.** Per-port isolation\n  means a shim only sees its own input. A union whose\n  discriminator is in another port has to validate inside the\n  box's main function rather than in the shim. If a real\n  cross-port case shows up, the workaround is a follow-on\n  ticket — not a reason to abandon per-port isolation."
      }],
    "role":"user"
  },
  "entrypoint":"cli",
  "userType":"external",
  "sessionId":"1228a221-1c09-4c26-94f3-172d7777b2b9"
}

      "content":"/* langs/lang-spec.h — public interface for SoraMech language specs.\n *\n * What it is, in a sentence: the C contract that every language\n * spec (Lua, C, Bash, anything user-added) implements. The pool\n * runner discovers specs by dlopen()ing langs/<name>/spec.so at\n * startup and reading the exported soramech_lang_spec symbol.\n *\n * Designed in issue 303. The init barrier (issue 301) calls init()\n * for every spec on every worker before unblocking task dispatch;\n * the dispatch action (issue 304) calls invoke() per task; the\n * compile-button pipeline (issue 309) calls compile() per source\n * file for languages whose compile pointer is non-NULL.\n *\n * Errors: a nonzero return from any callback is fatal. The dispatch\n * layer prints the error context and aborts. There is no recovery,\n * no retry, no per-task failed state. This is intentional.\n *\n * Issue 312 adds per-input / per-output format flags to `invoke`\n * (so a spec can decode each cell as native or JSON based on the\n * per-edge classification the loader assigned) and a pair of\n * bridges, `native_to_json` / `json_to_native`, used by the\n * dispatch's push path at language boundaries and by data boxes\n * (issue 317) that author values in their language's native\n * idioms. There is one invoke entry point per spec; the\n * format-branch lives inside that single function.\n */\n\n#ifndef SORAMECH_LANG_SPEC_H\n#define SORAMECH_LANG_SPEC_H\n\n#include <stddef.h>\n\n#ifdef __cplusplus\nextern \"C\" {\n#endif\n\n/* Forward declaration. `box_t` lives in src/010-graph-loader.h and\n * carries the full per-box record (input declarations, language,\n * compile-time hints like `cflags` / `link_libs` / `headers`).\n * Spec implementations include the loader header when they want to\n * read those fields; the bare forward declaration here keeps the\n * spec interface stand-alone for callers that only need the typedef\n * names. */\ntypedef struct box box_t;\n\n/* {{{ Invoke signature\n *\n * One entry point per spec. The dispatch layer hands the spec a\n * per-input format flag and a per-output format flag that the\n * spec consults internally — no separate native / JSON variants.\n *\n * Per-input format flag (`input_native[i]`): non-zero iff the\n * bytes in `input_data[i]` are this spec's native form; zero iff\n * they are JSON from a cross-language producer. The spec\n * dispatches internally — its decoder for that input picks the\n * native or JSON path based on the flag.\n *\n * Per-output format flag (`output_native`): non-zero iff the\n * dispatch wants the spec to write native bytes to `out_buf`,\n * zero iff it wants JSON. The spec produces one form per call;\n * cross-language fan-out is handled by the dispatch layer, which\n * converts via `native_to_json` once and pushes the JSON to every\n * cross-language consumer.\n *\n * On non-dual-ring slots (single-language inputs or single-language\n * outputs only), the dispatch passes NULL for `input_native` and\n * 0 for `output_native`; the spec falls back to its default\n * decode (typically JSON, which Lua's existing bridge handles).\n * `input_native` may be NULL even when `n_inputs > 0` — specs\n * must check before dereferencing. */\ntypedef int (*lang_invoke_fn)(void *handle,\n                              const box_t *box,\n                              const char *file_path,\n                              const char *fn_name,\n                              const void **input_data,\n                              const int   *input_sizes,\n                              const int   *input_native,\n                              int          n_inputs,\n                              int          output_native,\n                              void        *out_buf,\n                              int          out_buf_capacity,\n                              int         *out_size);\n\n/* `box` is the box record being invoked, or NULL when the caller has\n * no box context (e.g. test fixtures driving the spec directly).\n * Specs that need declared return type, compile hints, or future\n * sentinel-emission decisions read fields off `box`. Specs that\n * don't need it ignore the parameter. The pointer is valid only for\n * the duration of the call. */\n\n/* Wire-format bridge: convert one direction of native ↔ JSON.\n * Used when a value crosses a language boundary. Spec sets one\n * or both; if NULL, the dispatch layer treats native and JSON as\n * identical byte streams (the current uniform-byte default).\n *\n * `handle` is the worker's per-language handle (the same one\n * `invoke` receives) — bridges may need it to reach a runtime-side\n * scratch area: Lua reads/writes via the lua_State stack, C may\n * keep a typed-pointer table, Bash may need its sub-process. Specs\n * that don't need it ignore the argument.\n *\n * Stack-protocol convention for `native_to_json`: the producer\n * leaves its native value on top of its runtime's working store\n * (Lua: top of stack); the bridge consumes it. For `json_to_native`:\n * the bridge pushes the reconstructed value onto the same store.\n * `src` / `dst` carry only the JSON side. */\ntypedef int (*lang_bridge_fn)(void *handle,\n                              const void *src, int src_size,\n                              void *dst, int dst_capacity, int *dst_size);\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ lang_spec_t */\ntypedef struct lang_spec {\n    const char *name;       /* \"lua\", \"bash\", \"c\", \"python\", ... */\n    const char *file_ext;   /* \".lua\", \".sh\", \".c\", \".py\"        */\n\n    /* init: once per worker thread at pool startup. Returns an\n     * opaque handle stored in the worker context; the dispatch\n     * layer passes this handle back to invoke() for every call. */\n    void *(*init)(int worker_idx);\n\n    /* teardown: once per worker at pool shutdown. Frees the handle\n     * and any per-worker resources (e.g. lua_State, dlopen caches,\n     * persistent socket connections). */\n    void  (*teardown)(void *handle);\n\n    /* compile: optional. Called once per source file at map-load\n     * (or at editor compile-button time). For languages that don't\n     * compile (Lua, Bash), leave this NULL. For C, it runs\n     * gcc -shared -fPIC -o out_path src_path, plus any per-box\n     * compile flags / link libraries / headers the box declared.\n     *\n     * `box` is the box record for the box being compiled, or NULL\n     * if the caller is compiling a source file with no box context\n     * (e.g. the C spec's internal lazy-compile path that maps a raw\n     * `.c` ref to a `/tmp/<hash>.so` on the fly). When non-NULL,\n     * the spec may read box->cflags / box->link_libs / box->headers\n     * to customise the compile. Returns 0 on success, nonzero on\n     * failure. */\n    int   (*compile)(const char *src_path, const char *out_path,\n                     const box_t *box);\n\n    /* invoke: per box call. Inputs are arrays of (bytes, size) pairs,\n     * already read from slots by the dispatch layer. The per-input\n     * `input_native[i]` flag tells the spec whether each cell is in\n     * the spec's native byte form (cell came from a same-language\n     * producer via `ring_native`) or in JSON (came from a\n     * cross-language producer via `ring_json`). The `output_native`\n     * flag tells the spec which form to write; cross-language\n     * fan-out is materialised by the dispatch via `native_to_json`\n     * before pushing the JSON ring. Returns 0 on success, nonzero\n     * (fatal) on error. Issue 312. */\n    lang_invoke_fn invoke;\n\n    /* Bridges between this spec's native byte form and JSON. Used\n     * by the dispatch's push path when a producer writes a\n     * cross-language wire (call `native_to_json` once on the\n     * producer side, push JSON to the consumer's `ring_json`) and\n     * by data boxes that author values in their language's native\n     * idioms (issue 317). `native_to_json` reads from the\n     * producer's runtime working store (e.g. lua_State stack);\n     * `json_to_native` writes into the consumer's runtime working\n     * store. The buffer-oriented signature accommodates stateless\n     * specs (C, Bash) that treat the value form as bytes; stateful\n     * specs (Lua, future Python / Ruby) ignore the unused half. */\n    lang_bridge_fn native_to_json;\n    lang_bridge_fn json_to_native;\n} lang_spec_t;\n/* }}} */\n\n#ifdef __cplusplus\n}\n#endif\n\n#endif /* SORAMECH_LANG_SPEC_H */\n",

The spec produces one form per call;\n61\t * cross-language fan-out is handled by the dispatch layer, which\n62\t * converts via `native_to_json` once and pushes the JSON to every\n63\t * cross-language consumer.\n64\t *\n65\t * On non-dual-ring slots (single-language inputs or single-language\n66\t * outputs only), the dispatch passes NULL for `input_native` and\n67\t * 0 for `output_native`; the spec falls back to its default\n68\t * decode (typically JSON, which Lua's existing bridge handles).\n69\t * `input_native` may be NULL even when `n_inputs > 0` — specs\n70\t * must check before dereferencing. */\n71\ttypedef int (*lang_invoke_fn)(void *handle,\n72\t                              const box_t *box,\n73\t                              const char *file_path,\n74\t                              const char *fn_name,\n75\t                              const void **input_data,\n76\t                              const int   *input_sizes,\n77\t                              const int   *input_native,\n78\t                              int          n_inputs,\n79\t                              int          output_native,\n80\t                              void        *out_buf,\n81\t                              int          out_buf_capacity,\n82\t                              int         *out_size);\n83\t\n84\t/* `box` is the box record being invoked, or NULL when the caller has\n85\t * no box context (e.g. test fixtures driving the spec directly).\n86\t * Specs that need declared return type, compile hints, or future\n87\t * sentinel-emission decisions read fields off `box`. Specs that\n88\t * don't need it ignore the parameter. The pointer is valid only for\n89\t * the duration of the call. */\n90\t\n91\t/* Wire-format bridge: convert one direction of native ↔ JSON.\n92\t * Used when a value crosses a language boundary. Spec sets one\n93\t * or both; if NULL, the dispatch layer treats native and JSON as\n94\t * identical byte streams (the current uniform-byte default).\n95\t *\n96\t * `handle` is the worker's per-language handle (the same one\n97\t * `invoke` receives) — bridges may need it to reach a runtime-side\n98\t * scratch area: Lua reads/writes via the lua_State stack, C may\n99\t * keep a typed-pointer table, Bash may need its sub-process. Specs\n100\t * that don't need it ignore the argument.\n101\t *\n102\t * Stack-protocol convention for `native_to_json`: the producer\n103\t * leaves its native value on top of its runtime's working store\n104\t * (Lua: top of stack); the bridge consumes it. For `json_to_native`:\n105\t * the bridge pushes the reconstructed value onto the same store.\n106\t * `src` / `dst` carry only the JSON side. */\n107\ttypedef int (*lang_bridge_fn)(void *handle,\n108\t                              const void *src, int src_size,\n109\t                              void *dst, int dst_capacity, int *dst_size);\n110\t/* }}} */\n111\t\n112\t/* {{{ lang_spec_t */\n113\ttypedef struct lang_spec {\n114\t    const char *name;       /* \"lua\", \"bash\", \"c\", \"python\", ... */\n115\t    const char *file_ext;   /* \".lua\", \".sh\", \".c\", \".py\"        */\n116\t\n117\t    /* init: once per worker thread at pool startup. Returns an\n118\t     * opaque handle stored in the worker context; the dispatch\n119\t     * layer passes this handle back to invoke() for every call. */\n120\t    void *(*init)(int worker_idx);\n121\t\n122\t    /* teardown: once per worker at pool shutdown. Frees the handle\n123\t     * and any per-worker resources (e.g. lua_State, dlopen caches,\n124\t     * persistent socket connections). */\n125\t    void  (*teardown)(void *handle);\n126\t\n127\t    /* compile: optional. Called once per source file at map-load\n128\t     * (or at editor compile-button time). For languages that don't\n129\t     * compile (Lua, Bash), leave this NULL. For C, it runs\n130\t     * gcc -shared -fPIC -o out_path src_path, plus any per-box\n131\t     * compile flags / link libraries / headers the box declared.\n132\t     *\n133\t     * `box` is the box record for the box being compiled, or NULL\n134\t     * if the caller is compiling a source file with no box context\n135\t     * (e.g. the C spec's internal lazy-compile path that maps a raw\n136\t     * `.c` ref to a `/tmp/<hash>.so` on the fly). When non-NULL,\n137\t     * the spec may read box->cflags / box->link_libs / box->headers\n138\t     * to customise the compile. Returns 0 on success, nonzero on\n139\t     * failure. */\n140\t    int   (*compile)(const char *src_path, const char *out_path,\n141\t                     const box_t *box);\n142\t\n143\t    /* invoke: per box call. Inputs are arrays of (bytes, size) pairs,\n144\t     * already read from slots by the dispatch layer. The per-input\n145\t     * `input_native[i]` flag tells the spec whether each cell is in\n146\t     * the spec's native byte form (cell came from a same-language\n147\t     * producer via `ring_native`) or in JSON (came from a\n148\t     * cross-language producer via `ring_json`). The `output_native`\n149\t     * flag tells the spec which form to write; cross-language\n150\t     * fan-out is materialised by the dispatch via `native_to_json`\n151\t     * before pushing the JSON ring. Returns 0 on success, nonzero\n152\t     * (fatal) on error. Issue 312. */\n153\t    lang_invoke_fn invoke;\n154\t\n155\t    /* Bridges between this spec's native byte form and JSON. Used\n156\t     * by the dispatch's push path when a producer writes a\n157\t     * cross-language wire (call `native_to_json` once on the\n158\t     * producer side, push JSON to the consumer's `ring_json`) and\n159\t     * by data boxes that author values in their language's native\n160\t     * idioms (issue 317). `native_to_json` reads from the\n161\t     * producer's runtime working store (e.g. lua_State stack);\n162\t     * `json_to_native` writes into the consumer's runtime working\n163\t     * store. The buffer-oriented signature accommodates stateless\n164\t     * specs (C, Bash) that treat the value form as bytes; stateful\n165\t     * specs (Lua, future Python / Ruby) ignore the unused half. */\n166\t    lang_bridge_fn native_to_json;\n167\t    lang_bridge_fn json_to_native;\n168\t} lang_spec_t;\n169\t/* }}} */\n170\t\n171\t#ifdef __cplusplus\n172\t}\n173\t#endif\n174\t\n175\t#endif /* SORAMECH_LANG_SPEC_H */\n176\t"

    "originalFile":"/* langs/lang-spec.h — public interface for SoraMech language specs.\n *\n * What it is, in a sentence: the C contract that every language\n * spec (Lua, C, Bash, anything user-added) implements. The dispatch\n * layer prints the error context and aborts. There is no recovery,\n * no retry, no per-task failed state. This is intentional.\n *\n * Issue 312 adds per-input / per-output format flags to `invoke`\n * (so a spec can decode each cell as native or JSON based on the\n * per-edge classification the loader assigned) and a pair of\n * bridges, `native_to_json` / `json_to_native`, used by the\n * dispatch's push path at language boundaries and by data boxes\n * (issue 317) that author values in their language's native\n * idioms. Specs\n * that don't need it ignore the argument.\n *\n * Stack-protocol convention for `native_to_json`: the producer\n * leaves its native value on top of its runtime's working store\n * (Lua: top of stack); the bridge consumes it. For `json_to_native`:\n * the bridge pushes the reconstructed value onto the same store.\n * `src` / `dst` carry only the JSON side. */\ntypedef int (*lang_bridge_fn)(void *handle,\n                              const void *src, int src_size,\n                              void *dst, int dst_capacity, int *dst_size);\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ lang_spec_t */\ntypedef struct lang_spec {\n    const char *name;       /* \"lua\", \"bash\", \"c\", \"python\", ... */\n    const char *file_ext;   /* \".lua\", \".sh\", \".c\", \".py\"        */\n\n    /* init: once per worker thread at pool startup. Frees the handle\n     * and any per-worker resources (e.g. lua_State, dlopen caches,\n     * persistent socket connections). */\n    void  (*teardown)(void *handle);\n\n    /* compile: optional. Called once per source file at map-load\n     * (or at editor compile-button time). For languages that don't\n     * compile (Lua, Bash), leave this NULL.           "replace_all":false,
          "new_string":"/* {{{ lua_translate() — per-port custom translation shim (issue 246)\n *\n * The shim is a .lua file the user wrote. It is expected to return\n * a single function with the signature\n *\n *   function(raw_bytes, raw_native) -> translated_bytes\n *\n * Cached per-worker in a registry table keyed by shim path so\n * repeat invocations skip the load. The cache table is created\n * lazily on first use. */\n#define LUA_SHIM_CACHE_KEY \"soramech.shim_cache\"\n\nstatic int lua_translate(void *handle,\n                         const char *shim_path,\n                         const void *raw, int raw_size, int raw_native,\n                         void *out_buf, int out_capacity, int *out_size)\n{\n    lua_State *L = (lua_State *)handle;\n    if (!L || !shim_path) return -1;\n    int baseline = lua_gettop(L);\n\n    /* Find or create the cache table. */\n    lua_getfield(L, LUA_REGISTRYINDEX, LUA_SHIM_CACHE_KEY);\n    if (lua_isnil(L, -1)) {\n        lua_pop(L, 1);\n        lua_newtable(L);\n        lua_pushvalue(L, -1);\n        lua_setfield(L, LUA_REGISTRYINDEX, LUA_SHIM_CACHE_KEY);\n    }\n    /* Stack: ..., cache */\n\n    /* Cache miss → load. */\n    lua_getfield(L, -1, shim_path);\n    if (lua_isnil(L, -1)) {\n        lua_pop(L, 1);\n        if (luaL_loadfile(L, shim_path) != 0) {\n            fprintf(stderr, \"lua spec: shim loadfile('%s'): %s\\n\",\n                    shim_path, lua_tostring(L, -1));\n            lua_settop(L, baseline);\n            return -1;\n        }\n        if (lua_pcall(L, 0, 1, 0) != 0) {\n            fprintf(stderr, \"lua spec: shim chunk exec '%s': %s\\n\",\n                    shim_path, lua_tostring(L, -1));\n            lua_settop(L, baseline);\n            return -1;\n        }\n        if (!lua_isfunction(L, -1)) {\n            fprintf(stderr, \"lua spec: shim '%s' did not return a function\\n\",\n                    shim_path);\n            lua_settop(L, baseline);\n            return -1;\n        }\n        /* Cache: store function under the path. */\n        lua_pushvalue(L, -1);\n        lua_setfield(L, -3, shim_path);\n    }\n    /* Stack: ..., cache, fn */\n\n    /* Call fn(raw_bytes, raw_native) → translated string. */\n    lua_pushlstring(L, (const char *)raw, (size_t)raw_size);\n    lua_pushboolean(L, raw_native ? 1 : 0);\n    if (lua_pcall(L, 2, 1, 0) != 0) {\n        fprintf(stderr, \"lua spec: shim '%s' call: %s\\n\",\n                shim_path, lua_tostring(L, -1));\n        lua_settop(L, baseline);\n        return -1;\n    }\n    /* Stack: ..., cache, result */\n\n    size_t out_len = 0;\n    const char *out_ptr = NULL;\n    if (lua_isstring(L, -1)) {\n        out_ptr = lua_tolstring(L, -1, &out_len);\n    } else if (lua_isnumber(L, -1)) {\n        out_ptr = lua_tolstring(L, -1, &out_len);  /* coerces */\n    } else if (lua_isnil(L, -1)) {\n        out_len = 0;\n        out_ptr = \"\";\n    } else {\n        fprintf(stderr, \"lua spec: shim '%s' returned non-string\\n\", shim_path);\n        lua_settop(L, baseline);\n        return -1;\n    }\n    if ((int)out_len > out_capacity) {\n        fprintf(stderr, \"lua spec: shim '%s' output %zu > capacity %d\\n\",\n                shim_path, out_len, out_capacity);\n        lua_settop(L, baseline);\n        return -1;\n    }\n    if (out_len > 0) memcpy(out_buf, out_ptr, out_len);\n    if (out_size) *out_size = (int)out_len;\n    lua_settop(L, baseline);\n    return 0;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ soramech_lang_spec */\nlang_spec_t soramech_lang_spec = {\n    .name           = \"lua\",\n    .file_ext       = \".lua\",\n    .init           = lua_init,\n    .teardown       = lua_teardown,\n    .compile        = 0,\n    .invoke         = lua_invoke,\n    .native_to_json = lua_native_to_json,\n    .json_to_native = lua_json_to_native,\n    .translate      = lua_translate,\n};\n/* }}} */",

          "new_string":"    /* Verbose: emit the input payloads now, before the spec runs. */\n    emit_input_events(ctx, task_id, bufs, sizes, n_present);\n\n    /* Issue 246: per-port custom translation shims. For each input\n     * port that carries a `custom_translation` file path, route the\n     * raw bytes through the spec's translate callback and replace\n     * the per-port data + size with the shim's output. The shim's\n     * output is always native bytes (the spec's invoke sees it that\n     * way regardless of what raw_native was). Skip silently for\n     * ports without a shim — the default decode path inside invoke\n     * runs as before. */\n    ua_t *xlate_heap = slot_store_allocator(ctx->slots);\n    ua_chunk_t *xlate_chunks[n_arr]; memset(xlate_chunks, 0, sizeof xlate_chunks);\n    for (int i = 0; i < n_present; i++) {\n        const char *shim_rel = b->inputs[i].custom_translation;\n        if (!shim_rel) continue;\n        if (!spec->translate) {\n            fprintf(stderr,\n                \"dispatch: box '%s' port '%s' has custom_translation but \"\n                \"spec '%s' doesn't support shims\\n\",\n                b->id, b->inputs[i].name, spec->name ? spec->name : \"?\");\n            for (int k = 0; k <= i; k++) {\n                if (xlate_chunks[k]) ua_unref(xlate_heap, xlate_chunks[k]);\n            }\n            release_inputs(ctx, n, bufs, buf_chunks);\n            return -1;\n        }\n        int xlate_cap = ctx->default_out_capacity;\n        ua_chunk_t *xc = ua_alloc(xlate_heap, (size_t)xlate_cap);\n        if (!xc) {\n            fprintf(stderr, \"dispatch: '%s' port '%s' shim out-of-memory\\n\",\n                    b->id, b->inputs[i].name);\n            release_inputs(ctx, n, bufs, buf_chunks);\n            return -1;\n        }\n        xlate_chunks[i] = xc;\n        char *xbuf = ua_data(xc);\n        int xsize = 0;\n        char *shim_path = resolve_path(ctx, shim_rel);\n        int rc_xlate = spec->translate(handle,\n                                       shim_path ? shim_path : shim_rel,\n                                       datas[i], sizes[i],\n                                       input_native[i],\n                                       xbuf, xlate_cap, &xsize);\n        free(shim_path);\n        if (rc_xlate != 0) {\n            fprintf(stderr, \"dispatch: '%s' port '%s' shim failed (rc=%d)\\n\",\n                    b->id, b->inputs[i].name, rc_xlate);\n            for (int k = 0; k <= i; k++) {\n                if (xlate_chunks[k]) ua_unref(xlate_heap, xlate_chunks[k]);\n            }\n            release_inputs(ctx, n, bufs, buf_chunks);\n            return -1;\n        }\n        datas[i]        = xbuf;\n        sizes[i]        = xsize;\n        input_native[i] = 1;\n    }\n\n    /* Resolve the box's source file relative to map_dir. */\n    char *ref_path = b->ref ? resolve_path(ctx, b->ref) : NULL;",

The contract: sm_translate is the entry\n * symbol; output goes in out_buf (native bytes); raw_native tells\n * us whether the input was already this language's native form\n * (1) or JSON from a cross-language producer (0). For this\n * fixture we treat both identically — uppercase regardless. */\n\n#include <string.h>\n\n/* {{{ sm_translate */\nint sm_translate(const void *raw, int raw_size, int raw_native,\n                 void *out_buf, int out_capacity, int *out_size)\n{\n    (void)raw_native;\n    if (raw_size > out_capacity) return -1;\n    const unsigned char *in  = (const unsigned char *)raw;\n    unsigned char       *out = (unsigned char *)out_buf;\n    for (int i = 0; i < raw_size; i++) {\n        unsigned char c = in[i];\n        if (c >= 'a' && c <= 'z') c = (unsigned char)(c - 'a' + 'A');\n        out[i] = c;\n    }\n    *out_size = raw_size;\n    return 0;\n}\n/* }}} */\n",

{
  "uuid":"31972049-e4d0-41c6-8a22-6575ecbb4ddc",
  "type":"user",
  "timestamp":"2026-05-24T00:52:07.648Z",
  "parentUuid":"104c5ccc-3a5f-444a-978c-36b2f1551d9f",
  "toolUseResult":{
    "originalFile":"#!/bin/bash\n# scripts/run-tests.sh — phase 3 integration tests.\n#\n# Runs every fixture map under tests/maps/ through `soramech-pool`\n# and asserts that the captured outputs match a hardcoded\n# expectation per map. The point is to catch regressions\n# end-to-end — past the spec interface, past the dispatch action,\n# past JSONL writing — rather than via the in-process unit tests.\n#\n# Per the project convention: scripts run from any directory via a\n# hard-coded ${DIR} path with an override argument; all paths are\n# relative to ${DIR}.\n\nset -u\n\nDIR=\"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech\"\nif [[ $# -ge 1 ]]; then\n    DIR=\"$1\"\nfi\n\ncd \"$DIR\"\n\npass=0\nfail=0\nfailures=()\n\n# {{{ check_map() — run one fixture, verify expected substrings\ncheck_map() {\n    local map=\"$1\"\n    shift\n    local expected=(\"$@\")\n\n    printf \"  %-44s \" \"$map\"\n\n    local output\n    output=$(\"$DIR/soramech-pool\" \"$DIR/tests/maps/$map\" 2>&1)\n    local rc=$?\n\n    local missing=\"\"\n    if [[ $rc -ne 0 ]]; then\n        missing=\"exit=$rc\"\n    fi\n    for e in \"${expected[@]}\"; do\n        if [[ \"$output\" != *\"$e\"* ]]; then\n            missing+=\"${missing:+; }missing '$e'\"\n        fi\n    done\n\n    if [[ -z \"$missing\" ]]; then\n        printf \"ok\\n\"\n        pass=$((pass + 1))\n    else\n        printf \"FAIL — %s\\n\" \"$missing\"\n        fail=$((fail + 1))\n        failures+=(\"$map: $missing\")\n    fi\n}\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ pipeline_output_check() — additional: the pipeline writes to disk\npipeline_output_check() {\n    local file=\"/tmp/soramech-pipeline-out.txt\"\n    rm -f \"$file\"\n    \"$DIR/soramech-pool\" \"$DIR/tests/maps/pipeline\" > /dev/null 2>&1\n    printf \"  %-44s \" \"pipeline write output\"\n    if [[ -f \"$file\" ]]; then\n        local content\n        content=$(cat \"$file\")\n        if [[ \"$content\" == \"11!\" ]]; then\n            printf \"ok\\n\"\n            pass=$((pass + 1))\n        else\n            printf \"FAIL — expected '11!', got '%s'\\n\" \"$content\"\n            fail=$((fail + 1))\n            failures+=(\"pipeline file: $content\")\n        fi\n    else\n        printf \"FAIL — output file missing\\n\"\n        fail=$((fail + 1))\n        failures+=(\"pipeline: $file missing\")\n    fi\n}\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ compile_pipeline_check() — soramech-compile produces a portable artifact\n# Verifies issue 309's compile pipeline: bundles all spec.so + sources\n# into compiled/, then runs the artifact from /tmp (i.e. with no\n# dependency on the project's cwd) and verifies it produces the same\n# output as the source map.\ncompile_pipeline_check() {\n    local map=\"$DIR/tests/maps/pipeline\"\n    local compiled=\"$map/compiled\"\n    local file=\"/tmp/soramech-pipeline-out.txt\"\n\n    printf \"  %-44s \" \"compile pipeline (portable run)\"\n\n    rm -rf \"$compiled\"\n    if ! \"$DIR/scripts/soramech-compile.sh\" \"$map\" --dir \"$DIR\" >/dev/null 2>&1; then\n        printf \"FAIL — soramech-compile failed\\n\"\n        fail=$((fail + 1))\n        failures+=(\"compile: script returned non-zero\")\n        return\n    fi\n    if [[ ! -x \"$compiled/pool-runner\" ]]; then\n        printf \"FAIL — compiled/pool-runner missing or not executable\\n\"\n        fail=$((fail + 1))\n        failures+=(\"compile: pool-runner missing\")\n        return\n    fi\n\n    rm -f \"$file\"\n    local output\n    output=$(cd /tmp && \"$compiled/pool-runner\" \"$compiled\" 2>&1)\n\n    local content=\"\"\n    [[ -f \"$file\" ]] && content=$(cat \"$file\")\n\n    if [[ \"$output\" == *\"addone → 11\"* ]] && [[ \"$content\" == \"11!\" ]];           "replace_all":false,
          "new_string":"-- {{{ handle_get_src\nlocal function handle_get_src(client, req, maps_root)\n    local map_name  = req.parts[2]\n    local file_name = req.parts[4]\n    local path = safe_path(maps_root, map_name, \"src\", file_name)\n    if not path then return json_err(client, \"400 Bad Request\", \"invalid path\") end\n\n    local raw, err = read_file(path)\n    if not raw then return json_err(client, \"404 Not Found\", tostring(err)) end\n    respond(client, \"200 OK\", raw, \"text/plain\")\nend\n-- }}}\n\n-- {{{ Translation file CRUD — issue 246\n-- Per-port custom translation shims live at\n--   maps/<name>/translations/<box_id>__<port_name>.<lang_ext>\n-- The handlers below read / write / list those files. Box JSON\n-- references them by relative path in the per-input\n-- `custom_translation` field; the editor uses these endpoints to\n-- create / inspect / replace the shim file contents.\n\n-- List translation files under maps/<name>/translations/.\n-- Returns an array of plain filenames; empty array if the dir\n-- doesn't exist yet (a brand-new map hasn't been forced to create\n-- the directory).\nlocal function handle_list_translations(client, req, maps_root)\n    local map_name = req.parts[2]\n    local dir = safe_path(maps_root, map_name, \"translations\")\n    if not dir then return json_err(client, \"400 Bad Request\", \"invalid path\") end\n    local handle = io.popen(\"ls \" .. dir .. \"/ 2>/dev/null\")\n    local files = {}\n    if handle then\n        local listing = handle:read(\"*a\")\n        handle:close()\n        for name in listing:gmatch(\"[^\\n]+\") do\n            if name ~= \"\" then files[#files + 1] = name end\n        end\n    end\n    json_ok(client, files)\nend\n\n-- Read one translation file as plain text.\nlocal function handle_get_translation(client, req, maps_root)\n    local map_name  = req.parts[2]\n    local file_name = req.parts[4]\n    if file_name:find(\"%.%.\", 1, true) or file_name:find(\"/\", 1, true) then\n        return json_err(client, \"400 Bad Request\", \"invalid filename\")\n    end\n    local path = safe_path(maps_root, map_name, \"translations\", file_name)\n    if not path then return json_err(client, \"400 Bad Request\", \"invalid path\") end\n    local raw, err = read_file(path)\n    if not raw then return json_err(client, \"404 Not Found\", tostring(err)) end\n    respond(client, \"200 OK\", raw, \"text/plain\")\nend\n\n-- Write (create or overwrite) one translation file. Creates the\n-- translations/ directory on demand.\nlocal function handle_put_translation(client, req, maps_root)\n    local map_name  = req.parts[2]\n    local file_name = req.parts[4]\n    if file_name:find(\"%.%.\", 1, true) or file_name:find(\"/\", 1, true) then\n        return json_err(client, \"400 Bad Request\", \"invalid filename\")\n    end\n    local dir = safe_path(maps_root, map_name, \"translations\")\n    if not dir then return json_err(client, \"400 Bad Request\", \"invalid path\") end\n    -- Make the directory; mkdir -p is idempotent so existing dirs\n    -- don't error.\n    os.execute(\"mkdir -p \" .. dir)\n    local path = dir .. \"/\" .. file_name\n    local ok, werr = write_file_atomic(path, req.body or \"\")\n    if not ok then return json_err(client, \"500 Internal Server Error\", tostring(werr)) end\n    json_ok(client, { ok = true, path = path })\nend\n\n-- Delete a translation file outright. Distinct from the inspector's\n-- \"Delete\" affordance which only clears the box's reference — this\n-- is the file-browser-side hard delete.\nlocal function handle_delete_translation(client, req, maps_root)\n    local map_name  = req.parts[2]\n    local file_name = req.parts[4]\n    if file_name:find(\"%.%.\", 1, true) or file_name:find(\"/\", 1, true) then\n        return json_err(client, \"400 Bad Request\", \"invalid filename\")\n    end\n    local path = safe_path(maps_root, map_name, \"translations\", file_name)\n    if not path then return json_err(client, \"400 Bad Request\", \"invalid path\") end\n    if not file_exists(path) then\n        return json_err(client, \"404 Not Found\", \"no such translation file\")\n    end\n    local ok, err = os.remove(path)\n    if not ok then return json_err(client, \"500 Internal Server Error\", tostring(err)) end\n    json_ok(client, { ok = true })\nend\n-- }}}",

    "filePath":"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech/src/005-http-server.lua",
    "oldString":"-- {{{ handle_get_src\nlocal function handle_get_src(client, req, maps_root)\n    local map_name  = req.parts[2]\n    local file_name = req.parts[4]\n    local path = safe_path(maps_root, map_name, \"src\", file_name)\n    if not path then return json_err(client, \"400 Bad Request\", \"invalid path\") end\n\n    local raw, err = read_file(path)\n    if not raw then return json_err(client, \"404 Not Found\", tostring(err)) end\n    respond(client, \"200 OK\", raw, \"text/plain\")\nend\n-- }}}",
    "newString":"-- {{{ handle_get_src\nlocal function handle_get_src(client, req, maps_root)\n    local map_name  = req.parts[2]\n    local file_name = req.parts[4]\n    local path = safe_path(maps_root, map_name, \"src\", file_name)\n    if not path then return json_err(client, \"400 Bad Request\", \"invalid path\") end\n\n    local raw, err = read_file(path)\n    if not raw then return json_err(client, \"404 Not Found\", tostring(err)) end\n    respond(client, \"200 OK\", raw, \"text/plain\")\nend\n-- }}}\n\n-- {{{ Translation file CRUD — issue 246\n-- Per-port custom translation shims live at\n--   maps/<name>/translations/<box_id>__<port_name>.<lang_ext>\n-- The handlers below read / write / list those files. Box JSON\n-- references them by relative path in the per-input\n-- `custom_translation` field; the editor uses these endpoints to\n-- create / inspect / replace the shim file contents.\n\n-- List translation files under maps/<name>/translations/.\n-- Returns an array of plain filenames; empty array if the dir\n-- doesn't exist yet (a brand-new map hasn't been forced to create\n-- the directory).\nlocal function handle_list_translations(client, req, maps_root)\n    local map_name = req.parts[2]\n    local dir = safe_path(maps_root, map_name, \"translations\")\n    if not dir then return json_err(client, \"400 Bad Request\", \"invalid path\") end\n    local handle = io.popen(\"ls \" .. dir .. \"/ 2>/dev/null\")\n    local files = {}\n    if handle then\n        local listing = handle:read(\"*a\")\n        handle:close()\n        for name in listing:gmatch(\"[^\\n]+\") do\n            if name ~= \"\" then files[#files + 1] = name end\n        end\n    end\n    json_ok(client, files)\nend\n\n-- Read one translation file as plain text.\nlocal function handle_get_translation(client, req, maps_root)\n    local map_name  = req.parts[2]\n    local file_name = req.parts[4]\n    if file_name:find(\"%.%.\", 1, true) or file_name:find(\"/\", 1, true) then\n        return json_err(client, \"400 Bad Request\", \"invalid filename\")\n    end\n    local path = safe_path(maps_root, map_name, \"translations\", file_name)\n    if not path then return json_err(client, \"400 Bad Request\", \"invalid path\") end\n    local raw, err = read_file(path)\n    if not raw then return json_err(client, \"404 Not Found\", tostring(err)) end\n    respond(client, \"200 OK\", raw, \"text/plain\")\nend\n\n-- Write (create or overwrite) one translation file. Creates the\n-- translations/ directory on demand.\nlocal function handle_put_translation(client, req, maps_root)\n    local map_name  = req.parts[2]\n    local file_name = req.parts[4]\n    if file_name:find(\"%.%.\", 1, true) or file_name:find(\"/\", 1, true) then\n        return json_err(client, \"400 Bad Request\", \"invalid filename\")\n    end\n    local dir = safe_path(maps_root, map_name, \"translations\")\n    if not dir then return json_err(client, \"400 Bad Request\", \"invalid path\") end\n    -- Make the directory; mkdir -p is idempotent so existing dirs\n    -- don't error.\n    os.execute(\"mkdir -p \" .. dir)\n    local path = dir .. \"/\" .. file_name\n    local ok, werr = write_file_atomic(path, req.body or \"\")\n    if not ok then return json_err(client, \"500 Internal Server Error\", tostring(werr)) end\n    json_ok(client, { ok = true, path = path })\nend\n\n-- Delete a translation file outright. Distinct from the inspector's\n-- \"Delete\" affordance which only clears the box's reference — this\n-- is the file-browser-side hard delete.\nlocal function handle_delete_translation(client, req, maps_root)\n    local map_name  = req.parts[2]\n    local file_name = req.parts[4]\n    if file_name:find(\"%.%.\", 1, true) or file_name:find(\"/\", 1, true) then\n        return json_err(client, \"400 Bad Request\", \"invalid filename\")\n    end\n    local path = safe_path(maps_root, map_name, \"translations\", file_name)\n    if not path then return json_err(client, \"400 Bad Request\", \"invalid path\") end\n    if not file_exists(path) then\n        return json_err(client, \"404 Not Found\", \"no such translation file\")\n    end\n    local ok, err = os.remove(path)\n    if not ok then return json_err(client, \"500 Internal Server Error\", tostring(err)) end\n    json_ok(client, { ok = true })\nend\n-- }}}"
  },

      "numLines":85,

      "totalLines":1028,
      "content":"  // {{{ mk_port_display\n  // Renders input ports as a two-row block per port: name field +\n  // variadic toggle on the top row, value field on the bottom row.\n  // Layout chosen so the value (often the longest entry) gets the\n  // full sidebar width instead of competing for space with the name\n  // (issue 224 reverted: name editing comes back to the inspector\n  // because the canvas <input> overlay was eating drag attempts).\n  function mk_port_display(ports) {\n    const wrap = document.createElement('div');\n    wrap.className = 'port-display';\n    if (!ports || ports.length === 0) {\n      const empty = document.createElement('span');\n      empty.className   = 'port-display-empty';\n      empty.textContent = '(none)';\n      wrap.appendChild(empty);\n    } else {\n      ports.forEach((p, i) => {\n        const block = document.createElement('div');\n        block.className = 'port-display-block';\n\n        const top_row = document.createElement('div');\n        top_row.className = 'port-display-row';\n\n        // Variadic context (issue 217 part B):\n        //   in_var_group = is part of a variadic group (one of multiple slots)\n        //   pv           = { base, index } parsed from the slot name\n        const pv           = current_box ? parse_variadic_name(p.name) : null;\n        const in_var_group = current_box && is_variadic_slot(current_box, p.name);\n\n        // Read-only name label. Port names come from the parsed\n        // function signature (file browser populates them); editing\n        // them in the inspector is gone — the original 208 rationale\n        // (prevent typo drift between source and box JSON) holds, and\n        // post-fact rename was just a user tag anyway.\n        const name_el = document.createElement('span');\n        name_el.className   = 'port-name-display';\n        name_el.textContent = p.name || '';\n        top_row.appendChild(name_el);\n\n        if (p.type && p.type !== 'any') {\n          const type_el = document.createElement('span');\n          type_el.className   = 'port-type';\n          type_el.textContent = ':' + p.type;\n          top_row.appendChild(type_el);\n        }\n\n        // Variadic control button. Three states:\n        //   1. Plain port — \"var\" toggle turns it on\n        //   2. First slot of a variadic group — \"var ×\" collapses back\n        //   3. Non-first slot — \"×\" removes that slot\n        const btn_style = 'background:none;border:1px solid #2a2f45;border-radius:3px;' +\n          'color:#6c72a0;cursor:pointer;font-family:monospace;font-size:9px;' +\n          'padding:1px 5px;line-height:1.4;';\n\n        if (!in_var_group) {\n          // Issue 217 part C: the var toggle is offered when the box's\n          // language declares `variadic_shape: 'positional'`. Until\n          // the spec is loaded we default to \"offered\" (every shipped\n          // language is positional) so the first render of a box\n          // doesn't lose the button. Already-variadic groups keep\n          // their collapse + remove controls regardless, so flipping\n          // a language to 'none' later can't trap an existing group.\n          const spec          = spec_for_box(current_box);\n          const var_supported = !spec || spec.variadic_shape === 'positional';\n          if (var_supported) {\n            const var_btn = document.createElement('button');\n            var_btn.style.cssText = btn_style;\n            var_btn.textContent   = 'var';\n            var_btn.title         = 'mark this input as variadic (grows to N slots)';\n            var_btn.onclick       = () => make_variadic(p.name);\n            top_row.appendChild(var_btn);\n          }\n        } else if (pv.index === 0) {\n          const var_btn = document.createElement('button');\n          var_btn.style.cssText = btn_style + 'border-color:#4a9eff;color:#4a9eff;';\n          var_btn.textContent   = 'var ×';\n          var_btn.title         = 'collapse back to a single non-variadic input';\n          var_btn.onclick       = () => unmake_variadic(pv.base);\n          top_row.appendChild(var_btn);\n        } else {\n          const x_btn = document.createElement('button');\n          x_btn.style.cssText = btn_style;\n          x_btn.textContent   = '×';\n          x_btn.title         = 'remove this slot';\n          x_btn.onclick       = () => remove_variadic_slot(p.name);",
      "filePath":"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech/assets/js/004-inspector.js"
    }
  },
  "cwd":"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech",
  "isSidechain":false,
  "promptId":"bcdc53d4-bb1b-4307-8409-29be1ad7dca9",

  "gitBranch":"master",
  "message":{
    "content":[{

If `anchor_box` is given, the window is centered over that\n  // box's screen position; otherwise it's centered on the canvas.\n  async function open_source_view(ref, anchor_box) {\n    let text;\n    try {\n      text = await fetch_source(ref);\n    } catch (e) {\n      status_msg('view source: ' + e.message, 'error');\n      return;\n    }\n\n    const win  = make_window(ref, text);\n    const size = default_size(text);\n\n    document.body.appendChild(win);\n    win.style.width  = size.w + 'px';\n    win.style.height = size.h + 'px';\n\n    // Default position: centered over anchor_box (if provided) or canvas.\n    const cr = canvas_rect();\n    let cand_left, cand_top;\n    if (anchor_box && anchor_box.ui) {\n      const s = Canvas.world_to_screen(anchor_box.ui.x + Boxes.BOX_W / 2,\n                                       anchor_box.ui.y + Boxes.box_height(anchor_box) / 2);\n      cand_left = cr.left + s.x - size.w / 2;\n      cand_top  = cr.top  + s.y - size.h / 2;\n    } else {\n      cand_left = cr.left + cr.width  / 2 - size.w / 2;\n      cand_top  = cr.top  + cr.height / 2 - size.h / 2;\n    }\n    const clamped = clamp_position(cand_left, cand_top, size.w, size.h);\n    win.style.left = clamped.left + 'px';\n    win.style.top  = clamped.top  + 'px';\n\n    bring_to_front(win);\n    open_windows.push(win);\n  }\n  // }}}",

Amber styling so it reads as a\n        // different category from the blue `var` family.\n        const opt_btn = document.createElement('button');\n        const opt_on  = ports[i].optional === true;\n        opt_btn.style.cssText = btn_style + (opt_on\n          ? 'border-color:#d4762a;color:#d4762a;'\n          : '');\n        opt_btn.textContent = 'opt';\n        opt_btn.title       = 'mark this input as optional — the box runs even if unwired';\n        opt_btn.onclick     = () => {\n          ports[i].optional = opt_on ? undefined : true;\n          save();\n          show(current_box, on_change_cb, on_delete_cb);\n        };\n        top_row.appendChild(opt_btn);\n\n        block.appendChild(top_row);",
          "replace_all":false,
          "new_string":"        // `opt` toggle (issue 230). Flips port.optional between true\n        // and undefined (absent = false). An optional port doesn't\n        // require a wire or literal — the compile-time check from\n        // 230 allows it through. Amber styling so it reads as a\n        // different category from the blue `var` family.\n        const opt_btn = document.createElement('button');\n        const opt_on  = ports[i].optional === true;\n        opt_btn.style.cssText = btn_style + (opt_on\n          ? 'border-color:#d4762a;color:#d4762a;'\n          : '');\n        opt_btn.textContent = 'opt';\n        opt_btn.title       = 'mark this input as optional — the box runs even if unwired';\n        opt_btn.onclick     = () => {\n          ports[i].optional = opt_on ? undefined : true;\n          save();\n          show(current_box, on_change_cb, on_delete_cb);\n        };\n        top_row.appendChild(opt_btn);\n\n        // {{{ Custom translation shim affordance (issue 246)\n        // Three states:\n        //   - no custom_translation: \"+xlate\" button — creates a\n        //     default shim file matching the box's language and\n        //     sets the port's custom_translation field.\n        //   - custom_translation set: \"xlate\" button opens the shim\n        //     in the source-view window; small \"×\" clears the field\n        //     (file stays on disk per the issue's delete rule).\n        // Suppressed entirely when the box has no language (read /\n        // data / write boxes — shims only make sense on call boxes\n        // whose spec runs the translate callback). */\n        if (current_box && current_box.kind === 'call' && current_box.lang) {\n          const has_shim = !!ports[i].custom_translation;\n          if (!has_shim) {\n            const new_btn = document.createElement('button');\n            new_btn.style.cssText = btn_style;\n            new_btn.textContent   = '+xlate';\n            new_btn.title         = 'add a per-port custom translation shim (issue 246)';\n            new_btn.onclick       = () => create_shim_for(ports[i]);\n            top_row.appendChild(new_btn);\n          } else {\n            const view_btn = document.createElement('button');\n            view_btn.style.cssText = btn_style + 'border-color:#e8a317;color:#e8a317;';\n            view_btn.textContent   = 'xlate';\n            view_btn.title         = 'view shim: ' + ports[i].custom_translation;\n            view_btn.onclick       = () =>\n              SourceView.open_source_view(ports[i].custom_translation, current_box);\n            top_row.appendChild(view_btn);\n\n            const clr_btn = document.createElement('button');\n            clr_btn.style.cssText = btn_style + 'border-color:#e8a317;color:#e8a317;';\n            clr_btn.textContent   = '×';\n            clr_btn.title         = 'clear shim reference (file stays on disk)';\n            clr_btn.onclick       = () => {\n              ports[i].custom_translation = undefined;\n              save();\n              show(current_box, on_change_cb, on_delete_cb);\n            };\n            top_row.appendChild(clr_btn);\n          }\n        }\n        // }}}\n\n        block.appendChild(top_row);",
          "file_path":"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech/assets/js/004-inspector.js"
        },

Amber styling so it reads as a\n        // different category from the blue `var` family.\n        const opt_btn = document.createElement('button');\n        const opt_on  = ports[i].optional === true;\n        opt_btn.style.cssText = btn_style + (opt_on\n          ? 'border-color:#d4762a;color:#d4762a;'\n          : '');\n        opt_btn.textContent = 'opt';\n        opt_btn.title       = 'mark this input as optional — the box runs even if unwired';\n        opt_btn.onclick     = () => {\n          ports[i].optional = opt_on ? undefined : true;\n          save();\n          show(current_box, on_change_cb, on_delete_cb);\n        };\n        top_row.appendChild(opt_btn);\n\n        block.appendChild(top_row);",
    "newString":"        // `opt` toggle (issue 230). Flips port.optional between true\n        // and undefined (absent = false). An optional port doesn't\n        // require a wire or literal — the compile-time check from\n        // 230 allows it through. Amber styling so it reads as a\n        // different category from the blue `var` family.\n        const opt_btn = document.createElement('button');\n        const opt_on  = ports[i].optional === true;\n        opt_btn.style.cssText = btn_style + (opt_on\n          ? 'border-color:#d4762a;color:#d4762a;'\n          : '');\n        opt_btn.textContent = 'opt';\n        opt_btn.title       = 'mark this input as optional — the box runs even if unwired';\n        opt_btn.onclick     = () => {\n          ports[i].optional = opt_on ? undefined : true;\n          save();\n          show(current_box, on_change_cb, on_delete_cb);\n        };\n        top_row.appendChild(opt_btn);\n\n        // {{{ Custom translation shim affordance (issue 246)\n        // Three states:\n        //   - no custom_translation: \"+xlate\" button — creates a\n        //     default shim file matching the box's language and\n        //     sets the port's custom_translation field.\n        //   - custom_translation set: \"xlate\" button opens the shim\n        //     in the source-view window; small \"×\" clears the field\n        //     (file stays on disk per the issue's delete rule).\n        // Suppressed entirely when the box has no language (read /\n        // data / write boxes — shims only make sense on call boxes\n        // whose spec runs the translate callback). */\n        if (current_box && current_box.kind === 'call' && current_box.lang) {\n          const has_shim = !!ports[i].custom_translation;\n          if (!has_shim) {\n            const new_btn = document.createElement('button');\n            new_btn.style.cssText = btn_style;\n            new_btn.textContent   = '+xlate';\n            new_btn.title         = 'add a per-port custom translation shim (issue 246)';\n            new_btn.onclick       = () => create_shim_for(ports[i]);\n            top_row.appendChild(new_btn);\n          } else {\n            const view_btn = document.createElement('button');\n            view_btn.style.cssText = btn_style + 'border-color:#e8a317;color:#e8a317;';\n            view_btn.textContent   = 'xlate';\n            view_btn.title         = 'view shim: ' + ports[i].custom_translation;\n            view_btn.onclick       = () =>\n              SourceView.open_source_view(ports[i].custom_translation, current_box);\n            top_row.appendChild(view_btn);\n\n            const clr_btn = document.createElement('button');\n            clr_btn.style.cssText = btn_style + 'border-color:#e8a317;color:#e8a317;';\n            clr_btn.textContent   = '×';\n            clr_btn.title         = 'clear shim reference (file stays on disk)';\n            clr_btn.onclick       = () => {\n              ports[i].custom_translation = undefined;\n              save();\n              show(current_box, on_change_cb, on_delete_cb);\n            };\n            top_row.appendChild(clr_btn);\n          }\n        }\n        // }}}\n\n        block.appendChild(top_row);"

The filename\n  // convention matches issue 246: <box_id>__<port_name>.<lang_ext>.\n  function shim_default_content(lang) {\n    if (lang === 'lua') {\n      return [\n        '-- Per-port custom translation shim (issue 246).',\n        '-- The file returns a single function taking the raw bytes',\n        '-- and a \"raw_native\" flag (true if the bytes came from a',\n        '-- same-language producer, false if from a cross-language',\n        '-- producer via JSON). Default is identity',\n        ' * pass-through — edit to add decode / coerce / validate */',\n        '#include <string.h>',\n        '',\n        'int sm_translate(const void *raw, int raw_size, int raw_native,',\n        '                 void *out_buf, int out_capacity, int *out_size)',\n        '{',\n        '    (void)raw_native;',\n        '    if (raw_size > out_capacity) return -1;',\n        '    memcpy(out_buf, raw, (size_t)raw_size);',\n        '    *out_size = raw_size;',\n        '    return 0;',\n        '}',\n        '',\n      ].join('\\n');\n    }\n    // Unknown language — give the user an empty file so they can\n    // author whatever's right; the spec will error at task time if\n    // the shape doesn't match its translate callback's expectations.\n    return '-- Custom translation shim — author for lang: ' + lang + '\\n';\n  }\n\n  function shim_ext_for(lang) {\n    if (lang === 'lua') return 'lua';\n    if (lang === 'c')   return 'c';\n    if (lang === 'bash')return 'sh';\n    return 'txt';\n  }\n\n  async function create_shim_for(port) {\n    if (!current_box || !current_box.id || !port || !port.name) return;\n    const lang = current_box.lang || 'lua';\n    const ext  = shim_ext_for(lang);\n    const fname = current_box.id + '__' + port.name + '.' + ext;\n    const content = shim_default_content(lang);\n    try {\n      await API.put_translation(fname, content);\n    } catch (e) {\n      status_msg('shim create failed: ' + e.message, 'error');\n      return;\n    }\n    port.custom_translation = 'translations/' + fname;\n    await save();\n    status_msg('created shim: translations/' + fname);\n    show(current_box, on_change_cb, on_delete_cb);\n    Canvas.mark_dirty();\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ mk_port_display"

## [2007]

```json
{
  "uuid":"bf72133c-08ba-490e-98a0-828131151469",
  "type":"user",
  "timestamp":"2026-05-24T01:02:04.446Z",
  "parentUuid":"8c3e6092-8908-4d2b-9174-7d4ea23add43",
  "toolUseResult":{
    "originalFile":"#!/bin/bash\n# scripts/soramech-compile.sh — produce a self-contained compiled map.\n#\n# What it does, in CEO terms: takes a SoraMech map directory, walks\n# every box file to find the languages and source files it uses,\n# copies everything into a `compiled/` subdirectory alongside the\n# language spec.so plugins and the pool runner binary, and stamps a\n# manifest. The resulting directory is portable — copy or symlink it\n# anywhere on the same machine and it runs the map standalone.\n#\n# Layout produced under <map>/compiled/:\n#   meta.json, boxes/, src/, data/  — verbatim copies from the map\n#   langs/<lang>/spec.so            — copies of the language plugins\n#                                     that the map actually uses\n#   langs/bash/bash-server.sh       — only if bash boxes are present\n#   bin/<box>.so                    — pre-compiled C boxes (informational;\n#                                     the runner still lazy-compiles\n#                                     from src/ but having them here\n#                                     means you can verify the compile\n#                                     step worked without running)\n#   pool-runner                     — symlink to soramech-pool\n#   manifest.json                   — summary stats\n#\n# Run as:\n#   scripts/soramech-compile.sh <map-dir>\n#   scripts/soramech-compile.sh <map-dir> --dir <project-root>\n#\n# Convention: scripts run from any directory via a hard-coded ${DIR}\n# path with an override argument; all paths relative to ${DIR}.\n\nset -u\n\n# {{{ defaults\nDIR=\"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech\"\nMAP=\"\"\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ argv parse — map first, --dir <path> optional\nwhile [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do\n    case \"$1\" in\n        --dir)\n            DIR=\"$2\"\n            shift 2\n            ;;\n        --help|-h)\n            grep '^#' \"$0\" | sed 's/^# \\?//'\n            exit 0\n            ;;\n        *)\n            if [[ -z \"$MAP\" ]]; then\n                MAP=\"$1\"\n            else\n                echo \"soramech-compile: unexpected argument '$1'\" >&2\n                exit 2\n            fi\n            shift\n            ;;\n    esac\ndone\n\nif [[ -z \"$MAP\" ]]; then\n    echo \"usage: soramech-compile <map-dir> [--dir <project-root>]\" >&2\n    exit 2\nfi\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ resolve paths & sanity-check\nif [[ ! -d \"$MAP\" ]]; then\n    echo \"soramech-compile: not a directory: $MAP\" >&2\n    exit 1\nfi\nMAP=$(cd \"$MAP\" && pwd)\nif [[ ! -f \"$MAP/meta.json\" ]]; then\n    echo \"soramech-compile: missing meta.json in $MAP\" >&2\n    exit 1\nfi\nif [[ ! -d \"$MAP/boxes\" ]]; then\n    echo \"soramech-compile: missing boxes/ in $MAP\" >&2\n    exit 1\nfi\nif [[ ! -x \"$DIR/soramech-pool\" ]]; then\n    echo \"soramech-compile: pool runner not built at $DIR/soramech-pool\" >&2\n    echo \"  run 'make' in $DIR first\" >&2\n    exit 1\nfi\n\nCOMPILED=\"$MAP/compiled\"\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ box_field — pull a top-level string field from a box JSON file\n# Tolerant of whitespace; returns empty string if the field is missing.\n# We don't have jq in-tree, so a regex over the small box files is\n# fine. Box JSON is hand-written and shallow.\nbox_field() {\n    local file=\"$1\"\n    local field=\"$2\"\n    grep -o \"\\\"$field\\\"[[:space:]]*:[[:space:]]*\\\"[^\\\"]*\\\"\" \"$file\" \\\n        | head -n1 \\\n        | sed 's/.*\"\\([^\"]*\\)\"$/\\1/'\n}\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ wipe & lay out the compiled directory\nrm -rf \"$COMPILED\"\nmkdir -p \"$COMPILED\" \"$COMPILED/boxes\" \"$COMPILED/src\" \"$COMPILED/bin\" \"$COMPILED/langs\"\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ copy verbatim assets (meta, boxes, src, data, *.txt)\ncp \"$MAP/meta.json\" \"$COMPILED/meta.json\"\ncp -r \"$MAP/boxes/.\" \"$COMPILED/boxes/\"\n\nif [[ -d \"$MAP/src\" ]]; then\n    cp -r \"$MAP/src/.\" \"$COMPILED/src/\"\nfi\n\nif [[ -d \"$MAP/data\" ]]; then\n    mkdir -p \"$COMPILED/data\"\n    cp -r \"$MAP/data/.\" \"$COMPILED/data/\"\nfi\n\n# Top-level data files (input.txt, names.txt, etc) — the runner\n# resolves file_write/data refs relative to the map root.\nshopt -s nullglob\nfor f in \"$MAP\"/*.txt; do\n    cp \"$f\" \"$COMPILED/\"\ndone\nshopt -u nullglob\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ enumerate the set of languages the map actually uses\n# A box file is in compiled/boxes/. We read `lang` from each.\nLANGS=()\nfor box in \"$COMPILED\"/boxes/*.json; do\n    lang=$(box_field \"$box\" lang)\n    if [[ -z \"$lang\" ]]; then continue; fi\n    seen=0\n    for known in \"${LANGS[@]+\"${LANGS[@]}\"}\"; do\n        if [[ \"$known\" == \"$lang\" ]]; then seen=1; break; fi\n    done\n    if [[ $seen -eq 0 ]]; then\n        LANGS+=(\"$lang\")\n    fi\ndone\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ copy spec.so for each used language\nfor lang in \"${LANGS[@]+\"${LANGS[@]}\"}\"; do\n    src_spec=\"$DIR/langs/$lang/spec.so\"\n    if [[ ! -f \"$src_spec\" ]]; then\n        echo \"soramech-compile: missing spec.so for language '$lang'\" >&2\n        echo \"  expected at $src_spec — run 'make' in $DIR\" >&2\n        exit 1\n    fi\n    mkdir -p \"$COMPILED/langs/$lang\"\n    cp \"$src_spec\" \"$COMPILED/langs/$lang/spec.so\"\n    # Bash spec needs its companion server script for runtime.\n    if [[ \"$lang\" == \"bash\" ]] && [[ -f \"$DIR/langs/bash/bash-server.sh\" ]]; then\n        cp \"$DIR/langs/bash/bash-server.sh\" \"$COMPILED/langs/bash/\"\n    fi\ndone\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ merge_lua_sources — concatenate all Lua source files into one\n# merged module (issue 313). Each per-file module is wrapped in its\n# own closure so the file's `local` declarations stay file-scoped,\n# and exported under the source file's basename. The Lua spec\n# detects the merged file at init and loads it once per worker\n# instead of per-file lazy-loading every box's ref. The original\n# files stay in src/ unchanged so the existing per-file path still\n# works for callers that haven't been told about the merge.\nmerge_lua_sources() {\n    local out=\"$COMPILED/src/__merged__.lua\"\n    shopt -s nullglob\n    local files=(\"$COMPILED/src\"/*.lua)\n    shopt -u nullglob\n    if [[ ${#files[@]} -eq 0 ]]; then return; fi\n\n    {\n        echo \"-- soramech merged Lua module (issue 313)\"\n        echo \"-- Generated by soramech-compile.sh; do not hand-edit.\"\n        echo \"-- Each per-file module wraps in its own closure and is\"\n        echo \"-- exported under the source file's basename, so two\"\n        echo \"-- files can both define a local M without colliding.\"\n        echo \"\"\n        echo \"local merged = {}\"\n        echo \"\"\n        local f base\n        for f in \"${files[@]}\"; do\n            base=$(basename \"$f\" .lua)\n            if [[ \"$base\" == \"__merged__\" ]]; then continue; fi\n            echo \"-- {{{ from $(basename \"$f\")\"\n            echo \"merged[\\\"$base\\\"] = (function()\"\n            cat \"$f\"\n            echo \"\"\n            echo \"end)()\"\n            echo \"-- }}}\"\n            echo \"\"\n        done\n        echo \"return merged\"\n    } > \"$out\"\n}\nmerge_lua_sources\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ pre-compile C boxes into compiled/bin/\n# The runner already lazy-compiles .c → .so on first invoke, so this\n# step is purely informational: it surfaces compile errors at compile\n# time rather than at run time, and produces artifacts the user can\n# inspect or distribute alongside the source.\nn_c_compiled=0\nn_c_failed=0\nfor box in \"$COMPILED\"/boxes/*.json; do\n    box_lang=$(box_field \"$box\" lang)\n    if [[ \"$box_lang\" != \"c\" ]]; then continue; fi\n    ref=$(box_field \"$box\" ref)\n    if [[ -z \"$ref\" ]]; then continue; fi\n    src_path=\"$COMPILED/$ref\"\n    if [[ ! -f \"$src_path\" ]]; then\n        echo \"soramech-compile: C box source missing: $ref\" >&2\n        n_c_failed=$((n_c_failed + 1))\n        continue\n    fi\n    base=$(basename \"$ref\" .c)\n    out=\"$COMPILED/bin/$base.so\"\n    if ! gcc -shared -fPIC -O2 -Wall -o \"$out\" \"$src_path\" 2>/tmp/soramech-compile-cc.log; then\n        echo \"soramech-compile: gcc failed for $ref:\" >&2\n        cat /tmp/soramech-compile-cc.log >&2\n        n_c_failed=$((n_c_failed + 1))\n        continue\n    fi\n    n_c_compiled=$((n_c_compiled + 1))\ndone\n\nif [[ $n_c_failed -gt 0 ]]; then\n    echo \"soramech-compile: $n_c_failed C box(es) failed to compile\" >&2\n    exit 1\nfi\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ copy the pool runner into the compiled directory\n# A real copy (not a symlink) is intentional: the runner discovers\n# its sibling langs/ via /proc/self/exe, which follows symlinks to\n# their canonical target. A symlinked pool-runner would resolve back\n# to the project tree and pick up the project's langs/ instead of\n# the bundled compiled/langs/. Copying keeps the compiled artifact\n# self-describing and portable.\ncp \"$DIR/soramech-pool\" \"$COMPILED/pool-runner\"\nchmod +x \"$COMPILED/pool-runner\"\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ write manifest.json\n# Hand-rolled JSON (no jq) keeps the script self-contained. The\n# fields are stable enough to grep against in tests.\nn_boxes=$(ls -1 \"$COMPILED\"/boxes/*.json 2>/dev/null | wc -l)\nn_langs=${#LANGS[@]}\nlangs_json=\"\"\nfirst=1\nfor lang in \"${LANGS[@]+\"${LANGS[@]}\"}\"; do\n    if [[ $first -eq 1 ]]; then\n        langs_json=\"\\\"$lang\\\"\"\n        first=0\n    else\n        langs_json+=\",\\\"$lang\\\"\"\n    fi\ndone\ncompiled_at=$(date -Iseconds 2>/dev/null || date)\nmap_name=$(basename \"$MAP\")\n\ncat > \"$COMPILED/manifest.json\" <<EOF\n{\n    \"name\": \"$map_name\",\n    \"compiled_at\": \"$compiled_at\",\n    \"n_boxes\": $n_boxes,\n    \"n_languages\": $n_langs,\n    \"languages\": [$langs_json],\n    \"c_boxes_precompiled\": $n_c_compiled,\n    \"source_map_dir\": \"$MAP\"\n}\nEOF\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ summary line\necho \"compiled $map_name → $COMPILED\"\necho \"  boxes:       $n_boxes\"\necho \"  languages:   $n_langs (${LANGS[*]+${LANGS[*]}})\"\necho \"  c precompiled: $n_c_compiled\"\necho\necho \"run with:\"\necho \"  $COMPILED/pool-runner $COMPILED\"\n# }}}\n",

          "replace_all":false,
          "new_string":"# 246 — Custom translation specs per input port\n\n## Status\ncomplete\n\n## Current behavior\n\nPer-port custom translation shims are live for Lua and C boxes:\n\n- The box JSON schema gains an optional per-input\n  `custom_translation` field that names a file under\n  `translations/<file>` relative to the map dir. Absence means\n  \"use the default decode for this port.\"\n- The graph loader (`src/010-graph-loader.{h,c}`) reads the\n  field onto `input_decl_t->custom_translation`.\n- The language spec interface (`langs/lang-spec.h`) grows a\n  `translate` callback that takes `(handle, shim_path, raw,\n  raw_size, raw_native, out_buf, out_capacity, out_size)`.\n- Lua's spec (`langs/lua/spec.c`) implements `lua_translate`:\n  loads the shim file expecting it to return a function, caches\n  the function reference per-worker in the Lua registry under\n  `LUA_SHIM_CACHE_KEY`, calls it with `(raw, raw_native)` and\n  returns the result.\n- C's spec (`langs/c/spec.c`) implements `c_translate`:\n  lazy-compiles the shim .c to .so via the existing\n  `maybe_lazy_compile` + `get_or_load` infrastructure, dlsym's\n  `sm_translate`, and calls it.\n- Bash's spec doesn't implement `translate` (its protocol needs\n  extension; deferred per the 319e/Bash pattern).\n- Dispatch (`src/012-dispatch.c`) walks each box's inputs after\n  `read_inputs`; for any port with a `custom_translation` it\n  routes the raw bytes through `spec->translate`, allocates an\n  output buffer from the unified allocator, replaces the per-port\n  data/size, and sets `input_native[i] = 1` so the spec's invoke\n  sees the translated bytes as native.\n- The HTTP backend (`src/005-http-server.lua`) gains four routes:\n  `GET /maps/<name>/translations` (list),\n  `GET /maps/<name>/translations/<file>` (read),\n  `PUT /maps/<name>/translations/<file>` (write — used by the\n  inspector's \"+xlate\" affordance to create with default content),\n  `DELETE /maps/<name>/translations/<file>` (hard delete — used\n  by the file browser, not by the inspector).\n- The editor's `API` module (`assets/js/003-api.js`) exposes\n  `list_translations` / `get_translation` / `put_translation` /\n  `delete_translation`.\n- The inspector (`assets/js/004-inspector.js`) grows three button\n  states per input port row on call boxes:\n  - **`+xlate`** (no shim) — creates a default shim file with\n    identity pass-through content matching the box's language\n    and sets `port.custom_translation`.\n  - **`xlate`** (shim present) — opens the shim in the\n    source-view window.\n  - **`×`** (shim present) — clears the box's reference to the\n    shim (file stays on disk per the issue's delete rule).\n- The source-view (`assets/js/008-source-view.js`) detects\n  `translations/` paths and routes to `API.get_translation` so\n  the `xlate` view button works.\n- The wire-color module (`assets/js/006-wires.js`, from issue\n  245) already paints shim-port wires in goldenrod because it\n  detects `port.custom_translation`.\n- The compile pipeline (`scripts/soramech-compile.sh`) copies\n  `translations/` from the map into the compiled artifact so\n  shims survive packaging.\n- The runtime self-construction path (`src/018-runtime-builtins.c`)\n  reads `custom_translation` from spec JSON in\n  `runtime_create_box`, so dynamically-created boxes can carry\n  shims too.\n\n## Validation\n\nTwo integration test fixtures pass end-to-end:\n\n- `tests/maps/246-c-shim/` — a C box whose `msg` port has a\n  shim that uppercases the input. Expected output\n  `seen:HELLO-FROM-SEED` confirms the shim ran before the\n  box's `echo` function.\n- `tests/maps/246-lua-shim/` — a Lua box whose `msg` port has\n  a shim that reverses the input and prepends `REV-`. Expected\n  output `seen:REV-fedcba` confirms the same on the Lua side.\n\nAll 16 integration tests pass. The slot store's 23 unit tests\nstill pass.\n\n## Deferred\n\n- **Bash spec `translate`** — the bash server's line protocol\n  needs extension to route shim invocation back to the C\n  runtime. Same shape of follow-on as the 319e Bash deferral.\n- **Compile-time validation** of `custom_translation` paths —\n  per the issue's open questions, easy add when the feature\n  matures.\n- **Default-content generators that match the port's declared\n  type more closely** — the current default is identity\n  pass-through. Type-aware decoders (e.g. JSON-parse for\n  `type: \"json\"` inputs) are an enhancement.\n- **Box-delete confirmation when ports have shims** — the\n  current delete path doesn't warn. Easy add when needed; the\n  files staying on disk regardless means data isn't lost,\n  the user just loses the reference.\n\n## Concept",
          "file_path":"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech/issues/246-custom-translation-specs-per-port.md"
        },
