masks\n */\n#include \"020-sentinels.h\"\n#include \"json.h\"\n\n#include <stdio.h>\n#include <stdlib.h>\n#include <string.h>\n\n/* {{{ Tiny test harness */\n#define ASSERT(cond) do { \\\n    if (!(cond)) { \\\n        printf(\"FAIL %s:%d  %s\\n\", __FILE__, __LINE__, #cond); \\\n        return 0; \\\n    } \\\n} while (0)\n\nstatic int tests_run = 0, tests_passed = 0;\n#define RUN(name) do { \\\n    tests_run++; \\\n    printf(\"  %-44s \", #name); \\\n    fflush(stdout); \\\n    if (test_##name()) { \\\n        printf(\"ok\\n\"); \\\n        tests_passed++; \\\n    } \\\n} while (0)\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ detect_round_trip — emit then re-detect */\nstatic int test_detect_round_trip_ref(void)\n{\n    char buf[256];\n    json_writer_t w;\n    json_writer_init(&w, buf, sizeof buf);\n    sentinel_write_ref(&w, 0xCAFEBABE, 1024);\n    int n = json_writer_finish(&w);\n    ASSERT(n > 0);\n\n    json_arena_t *a = json_arena_create();\n    int eo; const char *em;\n    json_node_t *root = json_parse(a, buf, &eo, &em);\n    ASSERT(root != NULL);\n    ASSERT(sentinel_detect(root) == SENTINEL_REF);\n    json_arena_destroy(a);\n    return 1;\n}\n\nstatic int test_detect_round_trip_lang_opaque(void)\n{\n    char buf[256];\n    json_writer_t w;\n    json_writer_init(&w, buf, sizeof buf);\n    sentinel_write_lang_opaque(&w, \"lua\", 42, \"function\");\n    int n = json_writer_finish(&w);\n    ASSERT(n > 0);\n\n    json_arena_t *a = json_arena_create();\n    int eo; const char *em;\n    json_node_t *root = json_parse(a, buf, &eo, &em);\n    ASSERT(root != NULL);\n    ASSERT(sentinel_detect(root) == SENTINEL_LANG_OPAQUE);\n    json_arena_destroy(a);\n    return 1;\n}\n\nstatic int test_detect_round_trip_function_pointer_stub(void)\n{\n    char buf[256];\n    json_writer_t w;\n    json_writer_init(&w, buf, sizeof buf);\n    sentinel_write_function_pointer_stub(&w, \"int(int,int)\");\n    int n = json_writer_finish(&w);\n    ASSERT(n > 0);\n\n    json_arena_t *a = json_arena_create();\n    int eo; const char *em;\n    json_node_t *root = json_parse(a, buf, &eo, &em);\n    ASSERT(root != NULL);\n    ASSERT(sentinel_detect(root) == SENTINEL_FUNCTION_POINTER);\n    json_arena_destroy(a);\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Non-sentinel objects don't false-positive */\nstatic int test_detect_skips_plain_objects(void)\n{\n    json_arena_t *a = json_arena_create();\n    int eo; const char *em;\n\n    /* Plain object — multiple keys. */\n    json_node_t *n1 = json_parse(a, \"{\\\"a\\\":1,\\\"b\\\":2}\", &eo, &em);\n    ASSERT(sentinel_detect(n1) == SENTINEL_NONE);\n\n    /* Single-key object whose key isn't a sentinel name. */\n    json_node_t *n2 = json_parse(a, \"{\\\"foo\\\":1}\", &eo, &em);\n    ASSERT(sentinel_detect(n2) == SENTINEL_NONE);\n\n    /* Arrays / scalars / null. */\n    json_node_t *n3 = json_parse(a, \"[1,2,3]\", &eo, &em);\n    ASSERT(sentinel_detect(n3) == SENTINEL_NONE);\n    json_node_t *n4 = json_parse(a, \"42\", &eo, &em);\n    ASSERT(sentinel_detect(n4) == SENTINEL_NONE);\n    json_node_t *n5 = json_parse(a, \"null\", &eo, &em);\n    ASSERT(sentinel_detect(n5) == SENTINEL_NONE);\n\n    json_arena_destroy(a);\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ $ref store round-trip */\nstatic int test_ref_store(void)\n{\n    sentinel_ref_store_clear();\n    const char *payload = \"0123456789ABCDEF\";\n    int len = (int)strlen(payload);\n    uintptr_t p = sentinel_ref_alloc(payload, len);\n    ASSERT(p != 0);\n    int got_len = 0;\n    const void *got = sentinel_ref_lookup(p, &got_len);\n    ASSERT(got != NULL);\n    ASSERT(got_len == len);\n    ASSERT(memcmp(got, payload, (size_t)len) == 0);\n\n    /* Lookup with a wrong pointer returns NULL. */\n    int dummy = 0;\n    ASSERT(sentinel_ref_lookup(p + 1, &dummy) == NULL);\n\n    sentinel_ref_store_clear();\n    /* After clear, the pointer is no longer valid (and may be freed\n     * memory — we only assert lookup miss, not dereferencing). */\n    ASSERT(sentinel_ref_lookup(p, &dummy) == NULL);\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Capability validation */\nstatic int test_validate(void)\n{\n    /* No emission → no gap. */\n    ASSERT(sentinel_validate(0, 0) == 0);\n\n    /* Identical capabilities → no gap. */\n    ASSERT(sentinel_validate(\n        SENTINEL_MASK_REF | SENTINEL_MASK_LANG_OPAQUE,\n        SENTINEL_MASK_REF | SENTINEL_MASK_LANG_OPAQUE) == 0);\n\n    /* Consumer covers producer's emit set → no gap. */\n    ASSERT(sentinel_validate(\n        SENTINEL_MASK_REF,\n        SENTINEL_MASK_REF | SENTINEL_MASK_LANG_OPAQUE) == 0);\n\n    /* Producer emits something consumer can't reconstruct → gap. */\n    unsigned int gap = sentinel_validate(\n        SENTINEL_MASK_REF | SENTINEL_MASK_LANG_OPAQUE,\n        SENTINEL_MASK_REF);\n    ASSERT(gap == SENTINEL_MASK_LANG_OPAQUE);\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Kind names */\nstatic int test_kind_names(void)\n{\n    ASSERT(strcmp(sentinel_kind_name(SENTINEL_NONE),             \"(none)\") == 0);\n    ASSERT(strcmp(sentinel_kind_name(SENTINEL_REF),              \"$ref\") == 0);\n    ASSERT(strcmp(sentinel_kind_name(SENTINEL_LANG_OPAQUE),      \"$lang_opaque\") == 0);\n    ASSERT(strcmp(sentinel_kind_name(SENTINEL_FUNCTION_POINTER), \"$function_pointer\") == 0);\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\nint main(void)\n{\n    printf(\"020-sentinels-test:\\n\");\n    RUN(detect_round_trip_ref);\n    RUN(detect_round_trip_lang_opaque);\n    RUN(detect_round_trip_function_pointer_stub);\n    RUN(detect_skips_plain_objects);\n    RUN(ref_store);\n    RUN(validate);\n    RUN(kind_names);\n    printf(\"\\n  %d passed, %d failed\\n\",\n           tests_passed, tests_run - tests_passed);\n    return tests_run == tests_passed ? 0 : 1;\n}\n",

Release by default;\n# DEBUG=1 keeps symbols and disables optimization, STRICT=1 promotes\n# warnings to errors. `make clean` removes everything that was built.\n#\n# Invokable from any directory: `make -C /path/to/soramech` works,\n# and the DIR variable can be overridden if needed (e.g. for an\n# out-of-tree checkout). ## [2240]

```json
{
  "uuid":"a820b8dc-8fa0-4e54-98d2-011ffce2920e",
  "type":"user",
  "timestamp":"2026-05-24T01:39:53.869Z",
  "parentUuid":"582fc87e-d8e1-4e46-8873-dc19593aa947",
  "toolUseResult":{
    "originalFile":"# SoraMech — top-level build orchestration.\n#\n# What it does, in a sentence: builds the phase 3 pool runner binary\n# plus one shared library per language spec. Release by default;\n# DEBUG=1 keeps symbols and disables optimization, STRICT=1 promotes\n# warnings to errors. `make clean` removes everything that was built.\n#\n# Invokable from any directory: `make -C /path/to/soramech` works,\n# and the DIR variable can be overridden if needed (e.g. for an\n# out-of-tree checkout). All paths in this Makefile are relative to\n# $(DIR) per the project convention.\n#\n# Designed in issue 309. Implementation of the runner's runtime is\n# split across issues 301–308; this Makefile builds whatever sources\n# exist under src/, libs/task-pool/, and libs/json/, so it scales as\n# those issues land.\n\n# {{{ Resolve project root\nDIR ?= $(abspath $(dir $(lastword $(MAKEFILE_LIST))))\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ Toolchain & flags\nCC      ?= gcc\n\n# Shared header search path: every C source can find langs/lang-spec.h\n# and any future libs/<name>/ headers via -I flags below.\nCPPFLAGS = -I$(DIR)/langs -I$(DIR)/libs/task-pool -I$(DIR)/libs/json -I$(DIR)/src\n\n# Default to release; DEBUG and STRICT toggle alternates.\nifeq ($(DEBUG),1)\n  CFLAGS = -O0 -g -DDEBUG -Wall -pthread -fPIC\nelse ifeq ($(STRICT),1)\n  CFLAGS = -O2 -Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic -Werror -pthread -fPIC\nelse\n  CFLAGS = -O2 -Wall -pthread -fPIC\nendif\n\nLDFLAGS = -ldl -pthread -rdynamic\n# -rdynamic exports the runner's symbols to dlopen'd spec.so\n# plugins. Specs need this for the issue-319d self-construction\n# builtins (runtime_create_box / runtime_connect) — those live in\n# src/018-runtime-builtins.c, owned by the runner, and the Lua /\n# C / Bash spec.so binaries call back into them at runtime.\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ Paths and source discovery\nBUILD_DIR = $(DIR)/build\nPOOL_BIN  = $(DIR)/soramech-pool\n\n# Wildcards: empty subdirs return empty lists, which is fine.     "originalFile":"# SoraMech — top-level build orchestration.\n#\n# What it does, in a sentence: builds the phase 3 pool runner binary\n# plus one shared library per language spec. Release by default;\n# DEBUG=1 keeps symbols and disables optimization, STRICT=1 promotes\n# warnings to errors. `make clean` removes everything that was built.\n#\n# Invokable from any directory: `make -C /path/to/soramech` works,\n# and the DIR variable can be overridden if needed (e.g. for an\n# out-of-tree checkout). All paths in this Makefile are relative to\n# $(DIR) per the project convention.\n#\n# Designed in issue 309. Implementation of the runner's runtime is\n# split across issues 301–308; this Makefile builds whatever sources\n# exist under src/, libs/task-pool/, and libs/json/, so it scales as\n# those issues land.\n\n# {{{ Resolve project root\nDIR ?= $(abspath $(dir $(lastword $(MAKEFILE_LIST))))\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ Toolchain & flags\nCC      ?= gcc\n\n# Shared header search path: every C source can find langs/lang-spec.h\n# and any future libs/<name>/ headers via -I flags below.\nCPPFLAGS = -I$(DIR)/langs -I$(DIR)/libs/task-pool -I$(DIR)/libs/json -I$(DIR)/src\n\n# Default to release; DEBUG and STRICT toggle alternates.\nifeq ($(DEBUG),1)\n  CFLAGS = -O0 -g -DDEBUG -Wall -pthread -fPIC\nelse ifeq ($(STRICT),1)\n  CFLAGS = -O2 -Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic -Werror -pthread -fPIC\nelse\n  CFLAGS = -O2 -Wall -pthread -fPIC\nendif\n\nLDFLAGS = -ldl -pthread -rdynamic\n# -rdynamic exports the runner's symbols to dlopen'd spec.so\n# plugins. Specs need this for the issue-319d self-construction\n# builtins (runtime_create_box / runtime_connect) — those live in\n# src/018-runtime-builtins.c, owned by the runner, and the Lua /\n# C / Bash spec.so binaries call back into them at runtime.\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ Paths and source discovery\nBUILD_DIR = $(DIR)/build\nPOOL_BIN  = $(DIR)/soramech-pool\n\n# Wildcards: empty subdirs return empty lists, which is fine. As\n# issues 301/302/303/304/305 land their C sources here, they get\n# compiled automatically — no Makefile edit required.\nPOOL_SOURCES = \\\n  $(wildcard $(DIR)/src/*.c) \\\n  $(wildcard $(DIR)/libs/task-pool/*.c) \\\n  $(wildcard $(DIR)/libs/json/*.c)\n\nPOOL_OBJECTS = $(POOL_SOURCES:$(DIR)/%.c=$(BUILD_DIR)/%.o)\n\n# Test sources live in tests/ as C files named to match the source\n# they exercise (e.g. tests/009-slot-store-test.c exercises\n# src/009-slot-store.c). Each builds to a separate executable that\n# `make test` runs in turn.\nTEST_SOURCES = $(wildcard $(DIR)/tests/*.c)\nTEST_BINS    = $(TEST_SOURCES:$(DIR)/tests/%.c=$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/%)\n\nLANGS = lua c bash\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ Public targets\n.PHONY: all runner specs clean test help\n\nall: runner specs\n\nrunner: $(POOL_BIN)\n\nspecs:\n\t@for lang in $(LANGS); do \\\n\t  echo \"  → langs/$$lang\"; \\\n\t  $(MAKE) -s -C $(DIR)/langs/$$lang DIR=$(DIR) || exit 1; \\\n\tdone\n\nclean:\n\trm -f $(POOL_BIN)\n\trm -rf $(BUILD_DIR)\n\t@for lang in $(LANGS); do \\\n\t  $(MAKE) -s -C $(DIR)/langs/$$lang DIR=$(DIR) clean || true; \\\n\tdone\n\ntest: all $(TEST_BINS)\n\t@echo\n\t@fail=0; \\\n\tfor t in $(TEST_BINS); do \\\n\t  $$t || fail=1; \\\n\t  echo; \\\n\tdone; \\\n\tif [ -x $(DIR)/scripts/run-tests.sh ]; then \\\n\t  $(DIR)/scripts/run-tests.sh $(DIR) || fail=1; \\\n\tfi; \\\n\texit $$fail\n\nhelp:\n\t@echo \"SoraMech build:\"\n\t@echo \"  make          — build runner + specs (release)\"\n\t@echo \"  make DEBUG=1  — debug info, no optimization\"\n\t@echo \"  make STRICT=1 — promote warnings to errors\"\n\t@echo \"  make clean    — remove every built artifact\"\n\t@echo \"  make test     — run integration tests (when 311 lands)\"\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ Build rules\n$(POOL_BIN): $(POOL_OBJECTS)\n\t@echo \"  → $(notdir $@)\"\n\t@$(CC) $(CFLAGS) $(CPPFLAGS) -o $@ $^ $(LDFLAGS)\n\n$(BUILD_DIR)/%.o: $(DIR)/%.c\n\t@mkdir -p $(dir $@)\n\t@echo \"  → $(patsubst $(DIR)/%,%,$<)\"\n\t@$(CC) $(CFLAGS) $(CPPFLAGS) -c -o $@ $<\n\n# Per-test dependency lines. Release by default;\n# DEBUG=1 keeps symbols and disables optimization, STRICT=1 promotes\n# warnings to errors. `make clean` removes everything that was built.\n#\n# Invokable from any directory: `make -C /path/to/soramech` works,\n# and the DIR variable can be overridden if needed (e.g. for an\n# out-of-tree checkout). All paths in this Makefile are relative to\n# $(DIR) per the project convention.\n#\n# Designed in issue 309. Implementation of the runner's runtime is\n# split across issues 301–308; this Makefile builds whatever sources\n# exist under src/, libs/task-pool/, and libs/json/, so it scales as\n# those issues land.\n\n# {{{ Resolve project root\nDIR ?= $(abspath $(dir $(lastword $(MAKEFILE_LIST))))\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ Toolchain & flags\nCC      ?= gcc\n\n# Shared header search path: every C source can find langs/lang-spec.h\n# and any future libs/<name>/ headers via -I flags below.\nCPPFLAGS = -I$(DIR)/langs -I$(DIR)/libs/task-pool -I$(DIR)/libs/json -I$(DIR)/src\n\n# Default to release; DEBUG and STRICT toggle alternates.\nifeq ($(DEBUG),1)\n  CFLAGS = -O0 -g -DDEBUG -Wall -pthread -fPIC\nelse ifeq ($(STRICT),1)\n  CFLAGS = -O2 -Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic -Werror -pthread -fPIC\nelse\n  CFLAGS = -O2 -Wall -pthread -fPIC\nendif\n\nLDFLAGS = -ldl -pthread -rdynamic\n# -rdynamic exports the runner's symbols to dlopen'd spec.so\n# plugins. Specs need this for the issue-319d self-construction\n# builtins (runtime_create_box / runtime_connect) — those live in\n# src/018-runtime-builtins.c, owned by the runner, and the Lua /\n# C / Bash spec.so binaries call back into them at runtime.\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ Paths and source discovery\nBUILD_DIR = $(DIR)/build\nPOOL_BIN  = $(DIR)/soramech-pool\n\n# Wildcards: empty subdirs return empty lists, which is fine. As\n# issues 301/302/303/304/305 land their C sources here, they get\n# compiled automatically — no Makefile edit required.\nPOOL_SOURCES = \\\n  $(wildcard $(DIR)/src/*.c) \\\n  $(wildcard $(DIR)/libs/task-pool/*.c) \\\n  $(wildcard $(DIR)/libs/json/*.c)\n\nPOOL_OBJECTS = $(POOL_SOURCES:$(DIR)/%.c=$(BUILD_DIR)/%.o)\n\n# Test sources live in tests/ as C files named to match the source\n# they exercise (e.g. tests/009-slot-store-test.c exercises\n# src/009-slot-store.c). Each builds to a separate executable that\n# `make test` runs in turn.\nTEST_SOURCES = $(wildcard $(DIR)/tests/*.c)\nTEST_BINS    = $(TEST_SOURCES:$(DIR)/tests/%.c=$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/%)\n\nLANGS = lua c bash\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ Public targets\n.PHONY: all runner specs clean test help\n\nall: runner specs\n\nrunner: $(POOL_BIN)\n\nspecs:\n\t@for lang in $(LANGS); do \\\n\t  echo \"  → langs/$$lang\"; \\\n\t  $(MAKE) -s -C $(DIR)/langs/$$lang DIR=$(DIR) || exit 1; \\\n\tdone\n\nclean:\n\trm -f $(POOL_BIN)\n\trm -rf $(BUILD_DIR)\n\t@for lang in $(LANGS); do \\\n\t  $(MAKE) -s -C $(DIR)/langs/$$lang DIR=$(DIR) clean || true; \\\n\tdone\n\ntest: all $(TEST_BINS)\n\t@echo\n\t@fail=0; \\\n\tfor t in $(TEST_BINS); do \\\n\t  $$t || fail=1; \\\n\t  echo; \\\n\tdone; \\\n\tif [ -x $(DIR)/scripts/run-tests.sh ]; then \\\n\t  $(DIR)/scripts/run-tests.sh $(DIR) || fail=1; \\\n\tfi; \\\n\texit $$fail\n\nhelp:\n\t@echo \"SoraMech build:\"\n\t@echo \"  make          — build runner + specs (release)\"\n\t@echo \"  make DEBUG=1  — debug info, no optimization\"\n\t@echo \"  make STRICT=1 — promote warnings to errors\"\n\t@echo \"  make clean    — remove every built artifact\"\n\t@echo \"  make test     — run integration tests (when 311 lands)\"\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ Build rules\n$(POOL_BIN): $(POOL_OBJECTS)\n\t@echo \"  → $(notdir $@)\"\n\t@$(CC) $(CFLAGS) $(CPPFLAGS) -o $@ $^ $(LDFLAGS)\n\n$(BUILD_DIR)/%.o: $(DIR)/%.c\n\t@mkdir -p $(dir $@)\n\t@echo \"  → $(patsubst $(DIR)/%,%,$<)\"\n\t@$(CC) $(CFLAGS) $(CPPFLAGS) -c -o $@ $<\n\n# Per-test dependency lines.     "originalFile":"# SoraMech — top-level build orchestration.\n#\n# What it does, in a sentence: builds the phase 3 pool runner binary\n# plus one shared library per language spec. Release by default;\n# DEBUG=1 keeps symbols and disables optimization, STRICT=1 promotes\n# warnings to errors. `make clean` removes everything that was built.\n#\n# Invokable from any directory: `make -C /path/to/soramech` works,\n# and the DIR variable can be overridden if needed (e.g. for an\n# out-of-tree checkout). All paths in this Makefile are relative to\n# $(DIR) per the project convention.\n#\n# Designed in issue 309. Implementation of the runner's runtime is\n# split across issues 301–308; this Makefile builds whatever sources\n# exist under src/, libs/task-pool/, and libs/json/, so it scales as\n# those issues land.\n\n# {{{ Resolve project root\nDIR ?= $(abspath $(dir $(lastword $(MAKEFILE_LIST))))\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ Toolchain & flags\nCC      ?= gcc\n\n# Shared header search path: every C source can find langs/lang-spec.h\n# and any future libs/<name>/ headers via -I flags below.\nCPPFLAGS = -I$(DIR)/langs -I$(DIR)/libs/task-pool -I$(DIR)/libs/json -I$(DIR)/src\n\n# Default to release; DEBUG and STRICT toggle alternates.\nifeq ($(DEBUG),1)\n  CFLAGS = -O0 -g -DDEBUG -Wall -pthread -fPIC\nelse ifeq ($(STRICT),1)\n  CFLAGS = -O2 -Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic -Werror -pthread -fPIC\nelse\n  CFLAGS = -O2 -Wall -pthread -fPIC\nendif\n\nLDFLAGS = -ldl -pthread -rdynamic\n# -rdynamic exports the runner's symbols to dlopen'd spec.so\n# plugins. Specs need this for the issue-319d self-construction\n# builtins (runtime_create_box / runtime_connect) — those live in\n# src/018-runtime-builtins.c, owned by the runner, and the Lua /\n# C / Bash spec.so binaries call back into them at runtime.\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ Paths and source discovery\nBUILD_DIR = $(DIR)/build\nPOOL_BIN  = $(DIR)/soramech-pool\n\n# Wildcards: empty subdirs return empty lists, which is fine. As\n# issues 301/302/303/304/305 land their C sources here, they get\n# compiled automatically — no Makefile edit required.\nPOOL_SOURCES = \\\n  $(wildcard $(DIR)/src/*.c) \\\n  $(wildcard $(DIR)/libs/task-pool/*.c) \\\n  $(wildcard $(DIR)/libs/json/*.c)\n\nPOOL_OBJECTS = $(POOL_SOURCES:$(DIR)/%.c=$(BUILD_DIR)/%.o)\n\n# Test sources live in tests/ as C files named to match the source\n# they exercise (e.g. tests/009-slot-store-test.c exercises\n# src/009-slot-store.c). Each builds to a separate executable that\n# `make test` runs in turn.\nTEST_SOURCES = $(wildcard $(DIR)/tests/*.c)\nTEST_BINS    = $(TEST_SOURCES:$(DIR)/tests/%.c=$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/%)\n\nLANGS = lua c bash\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ Public targets\n.PHONY: all runner specs clean test help\n\nall: runner specs\n\nrunner: $(POOL_BIN)\n\nspecs:\n\t@for lang in $(LANGS); do \\\n\t  echo \"  → langs/$$lang\"; \\\n\t  $(MAKE) -s -C $(DIR)/langs/$$lang DIR=$(DIR) || exit 1; \\\n\tdone\n\nclean:\n\trm -f $(POOL_BIN)\n\trm -rf $(BUILD_DIR)\n\t@for lang in $(LANGS); do \\\n\t  $(MAKE) -s -C $(DIR)/langs/$$lang DIR=$(DIR) clean || true; \\\n\tdone\n\ntest: all $(TEST_BINS)\n\t@echo\n\t@fail=0; \\\n\tfor t in $(TEST_BINS); do \\\n\t  $$t || fail=1; \\\n\t  echo; \\\n\tdone; \\\n\tif [ -x $(DIR)/scripts/run-tests.sh ]; then \\\n\t  $(DIR)/scripts/run-tests.sh $(DIR) || fail=1; \\\n\tfi; \\\n\texit $$fail\n\nhelp:\n\t@echo \"SoraMech build:\"\n\t@echo \"  make          — build runner + specs (release)\"\n\t@echo \"  make DEBUG=1  — debug info, no optimization\"\n\t@echo \"  make STRICT=1 — promote warnings to errors\"\n\t@echo \"  make clean    — remove every built artifact\"\n\t@echo \"  make test     — run integration tests (when 311 lands)\"\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ Build rules\n$(POOL_BIN): $(POOL_OBJECTS)\n\t@echo \"  → $(notdir $@)\"\n\t@$(CC) $(CFLAGS) $(CPPFLAGS) -o $@ $^ $(LDFLAGS)\n\n$(BUILD_DIR)/%.o: $(DIR)/%.c\n\t@mkdir -p $(dir $@)\n\t@echo \"  → $(patsubst $(DIR)/%,%,$<)\"\n\t@$(CC) $(CFLAGS) $(CPPFLAGS) -c -o $@ $<\n\n# Per-test dependency lines. A test binary needs its own .o plus\n# the .o files for the source(s) it exercises. As each test lands,\n# add one line here naming the dependencies (no globbing — explicit\n# is clearer than clever for tests).\n$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/009-slot-store-test:    $(BUILD_DIR)/src/009-slot-store.o \\\n                                           $(BUILD_DIR)/src/016-unified-allocator.o\n$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/015-large-value-heap-test: $(BUILD_DIR)/src/015-large-value-heap.o\n$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/016-unified-allocator-test: $(BUILD_DIR)/src/016-unified-allocator.o\n$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/010-graph-loader-test: $(BUILD_DIR)/src/010-graph-loader.o \\\n                                          $(BUILD_DIR)/src/009-slot-store.o \\\n                                          $(BUILD_DIR)/src/016-unified-allocator.o \\\n                                          $(BUILD_DIR)/src/011-spec-registry.o \\\n                                          $(BUILD_DIR)/libs/json/json.o\n# Every test binary that loads a language spec via dlopen needs the\n# runner-side symbols the specs call back into (issue 318's\n# sentinel_*, issue 319d's runtime_set_active_context, etc.). The\n# pool runner pulls them in through POOL_SOURCES' wildcard; tests\n# name them explicitly.\nSPEC_LOADER_DEPS = $(BUILD_DIR)/src/020-sentinels.o \\\n $(BUILD_DIR)/src/014-event-queue.o \\\n                                           $(BUILD_DIR)/src/017-box-id.o \\\n                                           $(BUILD_DIR)/src/018-runtime-builtins.o \\\n                                           $(BUILD_DIR)/libs/json/json.o \\\n $(BUILD_DIR)/libs/json/json.o\n$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/014-event-queue-test:   $(BUILD_DIR)/src/014-event-queue.o \\\n                                           $(BUILD_DIR)/src/013-jsonl-events.o \\\n                                           $(BUILD_DIR)/libs/json/json.o\n$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/301-pool-test:         $(BUILD_DIR)/libs/task-pool/pool.o\n$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/303-pool-spec-init-test: $(BUILD_DIR)/libs/task-pool/pool.o \\\n                                            $(BUILD_DIR)/src/011-spec-registry.o \\\n                                            $(SPEC_LOADER_DEPS)\n$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/306-lua-spec-test:     $(BUILD_DIR)/src/011-spec-registry.o \\\n         $(BUILD_DIR)/libs/json/json.o\n$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/017-box-id-test:       $(BUILD_DIR)/src/017-box-id.o\n$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/020-sentinels-test:    $(BUILD_DIR)/src/020-sentinels.o \\\n All paths in this Makefile are relative to\n# $(DIR) per the project convention.\n#\n# Designed in issue 309. Implementation of the runner's runtime is\n# split across issues 301–308; this Makefile builds whatever sources\n# exist under src/, libs/task-pool/, and libs/json/, so it scales as\n# those issues land.\n\n# {{{ Resolve project root\nDIR ?= $(abspath $(dir $(lastword $(MAKEFILE_LIST))))\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ Toolchain & flags\nCC      ?= gcc\n\n# Shared header search path: every C source can find langs/lang-spec.h\n# and any future libs/<name>/ headers via -I flags below.\nCPPFLAGS = -I$(DIR)/langs -I$(DIR)/libs/task-pool -I$(DIR)/libs/json -I$(DIR)/src\n\n# Default to release; DEBUG and STRICT toggle alternates.\nifeq ($(DEBUG),1)\n  CFLAGS = -O0 -g -DDEBUG -Wall -pthread -fPIC\nelse ifeq ($(STRICT),1)\n  CFLAGS = -O2 -Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic -Werror -pthread -fPIC\nelse\n  CFLAGS = -O2 -Wall -pthread -fPIC\nendif\n\nLDFLAGS = -ldl -pthread -rdynamic\n# -rdynamic exports the runner's symbols to dlopen'd spec.so\n# plugins. ## [2314]

```json
{
  "uuid":"c0aa07a8-9a24-4894-9379-3a724791404f",
  "type":"user",
  "timestamp":"2026-05-24T01:48:09.393Z",
  "parentUuid":"473e569c-ae43-48e5-b168-305eeb698ce0",
  "toolUseResult":{
    "originalFile":"# SoraMech — top-level build orchestration.\n#\n# What it does, in a sentence: builds the phase 3 pool runner binary\n# plus one shared library per language spec. Release by default;\n# DEBUG=1 keeps symbols and disables optimization, STRICT=1 promotes\n# warnings to errors. `make clean` removes everything that was built.\n#\n# Invokable from any directory: `make -C /path/to/soramech` works,\n# and the DIR variable can be overridden if needed (e.g. for an\n# out-of-tree checkout). All paths in this Makefile are relative to\n# $(DIR) per the project convention.\n#\n# Designed in issue 309. Implementation of the runner's runtime is\n# split across issues 301–308; this Makefile builds whatever sources\n# exist under src/, libs/task-pool/, and libs/json/, so it scales as\n# those issues land.\n\n# {{{ Resolve project root\nDIR ?= $(abspath $(dir $(lastword $(MAKEFILE_LIST))))\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ Toolchain & flags\nCC      ?= gcc\n\n# Shared header search path: every C source can find langs/lang-spec.h\n# and any future libs/<name>/ headers via -I flags below.\nCPPFLAGS = -I$(DIR)/langs -I$(DIR)/libs/task-pool -I$(DIR)/libs/json -I$(DIR)/src\n\n# Default to release; DEBUG and STRICT toggle alternates.\nifeq ($(DEBUG),1)\n  CFLAGS = -O0 -g -DDEBUG -Wall -pthread -fPIC\nelse ifeq ($(STRICT),1)\n  CFLAGS = -O2 -Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic -Werror -pthread -fPIC\nelse\n  CFLAGS = -O2 -Wall -pthread -fPIC\nendif\n\nLDFLAGS = -ldl -pthread -rdynamic\n# -rdynamic exports the runner's symbols to dlopen'd spec.so\n# plugins. Specs need this for the issue-319d self-construction\n# builtins (runtime_create_box / runtime_connect) — those live in\n# src/018-runtime-builtins.c, owned by the runner, and the Lua /\n# C / Bash spec.so binaries call back into them at runtime.\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ Paths and source discovery\nBUILD_DIR = $(DIR)/build\nPOOL_BIN  = $(DIR)/soramech-pool\n\n# Wildcards: empty subdirs return empty lists, which is fine. As\n# issues 301/302/303/304/305 land their C sources here, they get\n# compiled automatically — no Makefile edit required.\nPOOL_SOURCES = \\\n  $(wildcard $(DIR)/src/*.c) \\\n  $(wildcard $(DIR)/libs/task-pool/*.c) \\\n  $(wildcard $(DIR)/libs/json/*.c)\n\nPOOL_OBJECTS = $(POOL_SOURCES:$(DIR)/%.c=$(BUILD_DIR)/%.o)\n\n# Test sources live in tests/ as C files named to match the source\n# they exercise (e.g. tests/009-slot-store-test.c exercises\n# src/009-slot-store.c). ```json
{
  "uuid":"26f5af56-eeca-433c-8c1e-aded76a45e65",
  "type":"user",
  "timestamp":"2026-05-24T01:52:46.920Z",
  "parentUuid":"953622ca-69da-4477-af0a-33c58f96a21a",
  "toolUseResult":{
    "originalFile":"# SoraMech — top-level build orchestration.\n#\n# What it does, in a sentence: builds the phase 3 pool runner binary\n# plus one shared library per language spec. Release by default;\n# DEBUG=1 keeps symbols and disables optimization, STRICT=1 promotes\n# warnings to errors. `make clean` removes everything that was built.\n#\n# Invokable from any directory: `make -C /path/to/soramech` works,\n# and the DIR variable can be overridden if needed (e.g. for an\n# out-of-tree checkout). All paths in this Makefile are relative to\n# $(DIR) per the project convention.\n#\n# Designed in issue 309. Implementation of the runner's runtime is\n# split across issues 301–308; this Makefile builds whatever sources\n# exist under src/, libs/task-pool/, and libs/json/, so it scales as\n# those issues land.\n\n# {{{ Resolve project root\nDIR ?= $(abspath $(dir $(lastword $(MAKEFILE_LIST))))\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ Toolchain & flags\nCC      ?= gcc\n\n# Shared header search path: every C source can find langs/lang-spec.h\n# and any future libs/<name>/ headers via -I flags below.\nCPPFLAGS = -I$(DIR)/langs -I$(DIR)/libs/task-pool -I$(DIR)/libs/json -I$(DIR)/src\n\n# Default to release; DEBUG and STRICT toggle alternates.\nifeq ($(DEBUG),1)\n  CFLAGS = -O0 -g -DDEBUG -Wall -pthread -fPIC\nelse ifeq ($(STRICT),1)\n  CFLAGS = -O2 -Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic -Werror -pthread -fPIC\nelse\n  CFLAGS = -O2 -Wall -pthread -fPIC\nendif\n\nLDFLAGS = -ldl -pthread -rdynamic\n# -rdynamic exports the runner's symbols to dlopen'd spec.so\n# plugins. Specs need this for the issue-319d self-construction\n# builtins (runtime_create_box / runtime_connect) — those live in\n# src/018-runtime-builtins.c, owned by the runner, and the Lua /\n# C / Bash spec.so binaries call back into them at runtime.\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ Paths and source discovery\nBUILD_DIR = $(DIR)/build\nPOOL_BIN  = $(DIR)/soramech-pool\n\n# Wildcards: empty subdirs return empty lists, which is fine. As\n# issues 301/302/303/304/305 land their C sources here, they get\n# compiled automatically — no Makefile edit required.\nPOOL_SOURCES = \\\n  $(wildcard $(DIR)/src/*.c) \\\n  $(wildcard $(DIR)/libs/task-pool/*.c) \\\n  $(wildcard $(DIR)/libs/json/*.c)\n\nPOOL_OBJECTS = $(POOL_SOURCES:$(DIR)/%.c=$(BUILD_DIR)/%.o)\n\n# Test sources live in tests/ as C files named to match the source\n# they exercise (e.g. tests/009-slot-store-test.c exercises\n# src/009-slot-store.c). Each builds to a separate executable that\n# `make test` runs in turn.\nTEST_SOURCES = $(wildcard $(DIR)/tests/*.c)\nTEST_BINS    = $(TEST_SOURCES:$(DIR)/tests/%.c=$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/%)\n\nLANGS = lua c bash\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ Public targets\n.PHONY: all runner specs clean test help\n\nall: runner specs\n\nrunner: $(POOL_BIN)\n\nspecs:\n\t@for lang in $(LANGS); do \\\n\t  echo \"  → langs/$$lang\"; \\\n\t  $(MAKE) -s -C $(DIR)/langs/$$lang DIR=$(DIR) || exit 1; \\\n\tdone\n\nclean:\n\trm -f $(POOL_BIN)\n\trm -rf $(BUILD_DIR)\n\t@for lang in $(LANGS); do \\\n\t  $(MAKE) -s -C $(DIR)/langs/$$lang DIR=$(DIR) clean || true; \\\n\tdone\n\ntest: all $(TEST_BINS)\n\t@echo\n\t@fail=0; \\\n\tfor t in $(TEST_BINS); do \\\n\t  $$t || fail=1; \\\n\t  echo; \\\n\tdone; \\\n\tif [ -x $(DIR)/scripts/run-tests.sh ]; then \\\n\t  $(DIR)/scripts/run-tests.sh $(DIR) || fail=1; \\\n\tfi; \\\n\texit $$fail\n\nhelp:\n\t@echo \"SoraMech build:\"\n\t@echo \"  make          — build runner + specs (release)\"\n\t@echo \"  make DEBUG=1  — debug info, no optimization\"\n\t@echo \"  make STRICT=1 — promote warnings to errors\"\n\t@echo \"  make clean    — remove every built artifact\"\n\t@echo \"  make test     — run integration tests (when 311 lands)\"\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ Build rules\n$(POOL_BIN): $(POOL_OBJECTS)\n\t@echo \"  → $(notdir $@)\"\n\t@$(CC) $(CFLAGS) $(CPPFLAGS) -o $@ $^ $(LDFLAGS)\n\n$(BUILD_DIR)/%.o: $(DIR)/%.c\n\t@mkdir -p $(dir $@)\n\t@echo \"  → $(patsubst $(DIR)/%,%,$<)\"\n\t@$(CC) $(CFLAGS) $(CPPFLAGS) -c -o $@ $<\n\n# Per-test dependency lines. A test binary needs its own .o plus\n# the .o files for the source(s) it exercises. As each test lands,\n# add one line here naming the dependencies (no globbing — explicit\n# is clearer than clever for tests).\n$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/009-slot-store-test:    $(BUILD_DIR)/src/009-slot-store.o \\\n                                           $(BUILD_DIR)/src/016-unified-allocator.o\n$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/015-large-value-heap-test: $(BUILD_DIR)/src/015-large-value-heap.o\n$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/016-unified-allocator-test: $(BUILD_DIR)/src/016-unified-allocator.o\n$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/010-graph-loader-test: $(BUILD_DIR)/src/010-graph-loader.o \\\n                                          $(BUILD_DIR)/src/009-slot-store.o \\\n                                          $(BUILD_DIR)/src/016-unified-allocator.o \\\n                                          $(BUILD_DIR)/src/011-spec-registry.o \\\n                                          $(BUILD_DIR)/src/020-sentinels.o \\\n                                          $(BUILD_DIR)/libs/json/json.o\n# Every test binary that loads a language spec via dlopen needs the\n# runner-side symbols the specs call back into (issue 318's\n# sentinel_*, issue 319d's runtime_set_active_context, etc.). The\n# pool runner pulls them in through POOL_SOURCES' wildcard; tests\n# name them explicitly.\nSPEC_LOADER_DEPS = $(BUILD_DIR)/src/020-sentinels.o \\\n     "content":[{
        "name":"Edit",
        "input":{
          "old_string":"# 318 — Sentinel primitives in the cross-language JSON wire\n\n## Status\nopen — **amended 2026-05-22** to replace the in-process-FFI\n`$function_pointer` reconstruction path with a\nwrapper-binary + persistent-subprocess design. See the\nAmendment section below; the original FFI-based reconstruction\ntext in the body is retained for context but is no longer the\ntarget.",
          "replace_all":false,
          "new_string":"# 318 — Sentinel primitives in the cross-language JSON wire\n\n## Status\ncomplete (slice 1 — $lang_opaque emit + $ref machinery + capabilities)\n\n## Current behavior\n\nThree canonical JSON sentinel shapes are recognized everywhere\nthe wire format runs, with reserved key names that no plain\nobject will accidentally collide with:\n\n```json\n{\"$ref\":              {\"chunk_ptr\": \"0x...\", \"len\": N}}\n{\"$lang_opaque\":      {\"lang\": \"lua\", \"tag\": N, \"shape\": \"...\"}}\n{\"$function_pointer\": {...amendment: wrapper-binary subsystem...}}\n```\n\nA new spec-independent sentinel module\n(`src/020-sentinels.{h,c}`, with unit tests in\n`tests/020-sentinels-test.c` — 7 passing) carries the shared\nmachinery: kind detection on a parsed JSON node, emit-writers for\neach kind, a process-wide `$ref` bytes store (allocate / lookup\n/ clear), and a capability-mask validator.\n\n`lang_spec_t` (`langs/lang-spec.h`) grows two capability fields:\n`sentinel_emit_mask` and `sentinel_reconstruct_mask`. Each spec\ndeclares which kinds its `native_to_json` may write and which\nits `json_to_native` can rebuild. Lua publishes\n`REF | LANG_OPAQUE` on both sides; C publishes `REF` on both\nsides; Bash leaves both at zero. The capability fields are\nconsultable but the compile-time wire validation that uses them\nto gate cross-language wires is itself a follow-on slice.\n\nLua's encoder (`encode_value` in `langs/lua/spec.c`) no longer\nhard-errors on `LUA_TFUNCTION` / `LUA_TUSERDATA` / `LUA_TTHREAD` /\n`LUA_TLIGHTUSERDATA`. Instead it registers the value in the\nworker's `LUA_REGISTRYINDEX` via `luaL_ref` and emits a\n`$lang_opaque` sentinel carrying the registry tag and a `shape`\nhint (`lua_typename(t)`).\n\nLua's decoder (`decode_node`) detects sentinels at the top of\nthe `JSON_OBJECT` case via `sentinel_detect`:\n\n- `$lang_opaque` with `lang: \"lua\"` looks up the tag in the\n  registry and pushes the value back onto the stack.\n- `$lang_opaque` with any other `lang` value hard-errors with a\n  clear message — cross-language opaque values are not\n  reconstructable by the Lua spec.\n- `$ref` reads bytes from the process-wide store and pushes them\n  as a Lua string.\n- `$function_pointer` hard-errors with a \"wrapper-binary\n  subsystem not yet implemented\" message that names the\n  amendment's design as the future target.\n\n## Validation\n\n- **Unit tests** (7 passing under `tests/020-sentinels-test.c`)\n  cover kind detection, emit-then-detect round trips for all\n  three kinds, plain-object false-positive avoidance,\n  `$ref` store alloc/lookup/clear, capability gap detection,\n  and kind-name strings.\n- **End-to-end emit test**\n  (`tests/maps/318-lang-opaque/`) wires a Lua producer to BOTH a\n  Lua consumer and a `write` box. The `write` box's\n  language-agnostic kind forces the producer's output to JSON,\n  and the producer's output table contains a Lua function. The\n  test runner verifies the producer's output JSON carries the\n  expected `$lang_opaque` sentinel shape including `\"lang\":\n  \"lua\"` and `\"shape\": \"function\"`.\n\n## Documented limit on intra-Lua $lang_opaque reconstruction\n\nThe end-to-end reconstruction of `$lang_opaque` even in the\nintra-Lua case has a deeper structural issue worth flagging\nclearly:\n\n- The dual-ring slot's per-edge `input_native` flag for a\n  Lua → Lua wire is 1 (native), because graph-load\n  classification only knows the producer/consumer languages\n  match — it doesn't know the producer DID actually write JSON\n  (which only happens at call time when the producer has at\n  least one cross-language consumer).\n- When the consumer reads, it sees the JSON bytes but is told\n  by `input_native[i] = 1` that they're native, so it skips the\n  JSON-parse path and falls through to raw-string handling.\n- The consumer ends up with the JSON text as a Lua string\n  rather than a parsed value with the sentinel reconstructed.\n\nFixing this requires the dual-ring slot to track per-CELL the\nactual form written (not just per-edge), and the consumer's\nread path to consult that per-cell flag. The dual-ring design\nalready has the machinery (each cell knows which ring it came\nfrom); plumbing it through the input-decode path is the\nfollow-on. Tracked here as \"intra-Lua $lang_opaque round-trip\nneeds per-cell native flag at read time\" — separate from the\namendment's wrapper-binary subsystem.\n\n## What's deferred to follow-on slices\n\n- **`$function_pointer` reconstruction.** The amendment's\n  wrapper-binary + persistent-subprocess design is fully\n  specified but not implemented. Producer emit writes the\n  shape; consumer reconstruct rejects with a clear message.\n- **C / Bash sentinel emit-side wiring.** C and Bash specs\n  declare their capabilities but don't yet emit sentinels from\n  their `native_to_json` — typed-wrapper sentinel emission is a\n  C-spec enhancement, Bash has no native sentinel-emit case\n  since its values are always strings.\n- **Compile-time wire validation.** Capability masks are\n  declared; the compile-step walker that checks each cross-\n  language wire against producer.emit_mask vs\n  consumer.reconstruct_mask and surfaces warnings is a\n  separate slice.\n- **Lifetime-correct `$ref` store.** Current store is leak-\n  per-run (`sentinel_ref_alloc` + `sentinel_ref_lookup`,\n  cleared at process exit or via `sentinel_ref_store_clear`).\n  Refcount-driven release tied to consumer reads is the\n  follow-on.\n- **Per-cell native-flag on the dual-ring slot** so intra-Lua\n  $lang_opaque reconstruction round-trips correctly when the\n  producer was forced to JSON by a cross-language sibling\n  consumer.\n\n## Amendment (2026-05-22) — function pointers via wrapper binaries, not FFI",

    "filePath":"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech/issues/318-sentinel-primitives-in-cross-language-json.md",
    "oldString":"# 318 — Sentinel primitives in the cross-language JSON wire\n\n## Status\nopen — **amended 2026-05-22** to replace the in-process-FFI\n`$function_pointer` reconstruction path with a\nwrapper-binary + persistent-subprocess design. See the\nAmendment section below; the original FFI-based reconstruction\ntext in the body is retained for context but is no longer the\ntarget.",
    "newString":"# 318 — Sentinel primitives in the cross-language JSON wire\n\n## Status\ncomplete (slice 1 — $lang_opaque emit + $ref machinery + capabilities)\n\n## Current behavior\n\nThree canonical JSON sentinel shapes are recognized everywhere\nthe wire format runs, with reserved key names that no plain\nobject will accidentally collide with:\n\n```json\n{\"$ref\":              {\"chunk_ptr\": \"0x...\", \"len\": N}}\n{\"$lang_opaque\":      {\"lang\": \"lua\", \"tag\": N, \"shape\": \"...\"}}\n{\"$function_pointer\": {...amendment: wrapper-binary subsystem...}}\n```\n\nA new spec-independent sentinel module\n(`src/020-sentinels.{h,c}`, with unit tests in\n`tests/020-sentinels-test.c` — 7 passing) carries the shared\nmachinery: kind detection on a parsed JSON node, emit-writers for\neach kind, a process-wide `$ref` bytes store (allocate / lookup\n/ clear), and a capability-mask validator.\n\n`lang_spec_t` (`langs/lang-spec.h`) grows two capability fields:\n`sentinel_emit_mask` and `sentinel_reconstruct_mask`. Each spec\ndeclares which kinds its `native_to_json` may write and which\nits `json_to_native` can rebuild. Lua publishes\n`REF | LANG_OPAQUE` on both sides; C publishes `REF` on both\nsides; Bash leaves both at zero. The capability fields are\nconsultable but the compile-time wire validation that uses them\nto gate cross-language wires is itself a follow-on slice.\n\nLua's encoder (`encode_value` in `langs/lua/spec.c`) no longer\nhard-errors on `LUA_TFUNCTION` / `LUA_TUSERDATA` / `LUA_TTHREAD` /\n`LUA_TLIGHTUSERDATA`. Instead it registers the value in the\nworker's `LUA_REGISTRYINDEX` via `luaL_ref` and emits a\n`$lang_opaque` sentinel carrying the registry tag and a `shape`\nhint (`lua_typename(t)`).\n\nLua's decoder (`decode_node`) detects sentinels at the top of\nthe `JSON_OBJECT` case via `sentinel_detect`:\n\n- `$lang_opaque` with `lang: \"lua\"` looks up the tag in the\n  registry and pushes the value back onto the stack.\n- `$lang_opaque` with any other `lang` value hard-errors with a\n  clear message — cross-language opaque values are not\n  reconstructable by the Lua spec.\n- `$ref` reads bytes from the process-wide store and pushes them\n  as a Lua string.\n- `$function_pointer` hard-errors with a \"wrapper-binary\n  subsystem not yet implemented\" message that names the\n  amendment's design as the future target.\n\n## Validation\n\n- **Unit tests** (7 passing under `tests/020-sentinels-test.c`)\n  cover kind detection, emit-then-detect round trips for all\n  three kinds, plain-object false-positive avoidance,\n  `$ref` store alloc/lookup/clear, capability gap detection,\n  and kind-name strings.\n- **End-to-end emit test**\n  (`tests/maps/318-lang-opaque/`) wires a Lua producer to BOTH a\n  Lua consumer and a `write` box. The `write` box's\n  language-agnostic kind forces the producer's output to JSON,\n  and the producer's output table contains a Lua function. The\n  test runner verifies the producer's output JSON carries the\n  expected `$lang_opaque` sentinel shape including `\"lang\":\n  \"lua\"` and `\"shape\": \"function\"`.\n\n## Documented limit on intra-Lua $lang_opaque reconstruction\n\nThe end-to-end reconstruction of `$lang_opaque` even in the\nintra-Lua case has a deeper structural issue worth flagging\nclearly:\n\n- The dual-ring slot's per-edge `input_native` flag for a\n  Lua → Lua wire is 1 (native), because graph-load\n  classification only knows the producer/consumer languages\n  match — it doesn't know the producer DID actually write JSON\n  (which only happens at call time when the producer has at\n  least one cross-language consumer).\n- When the consumer reads, it sees the JSON bytes but is told\n  by `input_native[i] = 1` that they're native, so it skips the\n  JSON-parse path and falls through to raw-string handling.\n- The consumer ends up with the JSON text as a Lua string\n  rather than a parsed value with the sentinel reconstructed.\n\nFixing this requires the dual-ring slot to track per-CELL the\nactual form written (not just per-edge), and the consumer's\nread path to consult that per-cell flag. The dual-ring design\nalready has the machinery (each cell knows which ring it came\nfrom); plumbing it through the input-decode path is the\nfollow-on. Tracked here as \"intra-Lua $lang_opaque round-trip\nneeds per-cell native flag at read time\" — separate from the\namendment's wrapper-binary subsystem.\n\n## What's deferred to follow-on slices\n\n- **`$function_pointer` reconstruction.** The amendment's\n  wrapper-binary + persistent-subprocess design is fully\n  specified but not implemented. Producer emit writes the\n  shape; consumer reconstruct rejects with a clear message.\n- **C / Bash sentinel emit-side wiring.** C and Bash specs\n  declare their capabilities but don't yet emit sentinels from\n  their `native_to_json` — typed-wrapper sentinel emission is a\n  C-spec enhancement, Bash has no native sentinel-emit case\n  since its values are always strings.\n- **Compile-time wire validation.** Capability masks are\n  declared; the compile-step walker that checks each cross-\n  language wire against producer.emit_mask vs\n  consumer.reconstruct_mask and surfaces warnings is a\n  separate slice.\n- **Lifetime-correct `$ref` store.** Current store is leak-\n  per-run (`sentinel_ref_alloc` + `sentinel_ref_lookup`,\n  cleared at process exit or via `sentinel_ref_store_clear`).\n  Refcount-driven release tied to consumer reads is the\n  follow-on.\n- **Per-cell native-flag on the dual-ring slot** so intra-Lua\n  $lang_opaque reconstruction round-trips correctly when the\n  producer was forced to JSON by a cross-language sibling\n  consumer.\n\n## Amendment (2026-05-22) — function pointers via wrapper binaries, not FFI"
  },

        "type":"text",
        "text":"318 landed at `bf17dac`.\n\n## What shipped\n\n| Layer | Change |\n|-------|--------|\n| Sentinel module | `src/020-sentinels.{h,c}` — kinds, detection, emit writers, $ref store, capability validation |\n| Spec interface | `lang_spec_t` gains `sentinel_emit_mask` + `sentinel_reconstruct_mask` |\n| Lua encoder | non-structural values (functions, userdata, threads) emit `$lang_opaque` via `luaL_ref` instead of erroring |\n| Lua decoder | detects sentinels in `JSON_OBJECT`; reconstructs `$lang_opaque` (lua only), reads `$ref` from store, rejects `$function_pointer` with a clear message |\n| Capability declarations | Lua = REF \\| LANG_OPAQUE both ways; C = REF both ways; Bash = 0 |\n| Unit tests | 7 in `tests/020-sentinels-test.c` covering all sentinel machinery |\n| End-to-end fixture | `tests/maps/318-lang-opaque/` proves the Lua emit side end-to-end |\n| Makefile | tests that dlopen specs now link 020-sentinels + 018-runtime-builtins + 017-box-id so the spec.so's symbol references resolve |\n\n**Final tally: ~193 tests pass across all unit suites + 17 integration fixtures.**\n\n## Documented limits (all in the issue file)\n\n- `$function_pointer` end-to-end reconstruction needs the amendment's wrapper-binary subsystem — multi-session follow-on. Producer emits the shape; consumer rejects cleanly.\n- Intra-Lua `$lang_opaque` round-trip needs a per-cell native flag (the per-edge flag fights back against the producer's actual JSON write).\n- Compile-time wire validation using the capability masks is declared but not yet walked.\n- $ref store is leak-per-run; refcount-driven release is a follow-on.\n- C and Bash sentinel emit-side wiring is declared but not yet implemented in their encoders.\n\n`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`\nThe most striking finding of this slice: **the sentinel mechanism works end-to-end on the emit side, but the reconstruction side hits a per-edge-vs-per-cell mismatch in the dual-ring slot design.** The producer wrote JSON (because of a cross-language sibling), but the consumer's slot's per-edge classification says \"same-language native.\" Two-axis classification (per-edge for the *language* match, per-cell for the *actual* format written) is the deeper fix. The capability masks I added today are the right primitive; the consumer-side decode pathway is the missing wire.\n\nThe Makefile work was surprisingly important — every test binary that dlopens a spec needs to carry the symbols the spec.so calls back into. The pattern of \"runner-owned symbols + spec.so plugins calling back via -rdynamic\" works beautifully for the runner, but each test binary doing the same thing needs the same symbol inventory. Centralizing those into `SPEC_LOADER_DEPS` is the project-level fix.\n`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`\n\nWhat's next? Remaining untracked issues are **247** (debug build + per-box stats lens) and **249** (tap input mode with radial ports). Both are editor-side. The deferred work pile is now substantial: Bash bindings (319e/246), `$function_pointer` wrapper-binary subsystem (318), per-cell native flag (318 sub-issue), exporter rewrite, box-kind refactor for create_box/connect."

Either may carry a static literal supplied\n * via dispatch_push_literals.\n *\n * On success, the box pushes the boolean string `\"true\"` to its\n * outgoing connections. A `write` box with no downstream wire\n * still produces the boolean; the dispatch fans to zero consumers\n * and the value is discarded (unwired-output rule). */\nstatic int do_write_box(dispatch_ctx_t *ctx, const box_t *b, int task_id,\n                        char *out_buf, int out_capacity, int *out_size)\n{\n    /* Same VLA pattern as invoke_box_impl — sized to the box's\n     * actual input count, capped at DISPATCH_MAX_INPUTS_PER_BOX\n     * for stack-frame sanity. Write boxes only ever need two\n     * inputs (path, value) under issue 229's convention, so n\n     * is typically 1 or 2, but no reason to special-case the\n     * sizing here when the same machinery applies. */\n    int n = b->n_inputs;\n    if (n < 0 || n > DISPATCH_MAX_INPUTS_PER_BOX) {\n        fprintf(stderr, \"dispatch: write box '%s' has %d inputs (sanity cap = %d)\\n\",\n                b->id, n, DISPATCH_MAX_INPUTS_PER_BOX);\n        return -1;\n    }\n    size_t n_arr = (n > 0) ? (size_t)n : 1;\n    char        *bufs[n_arr];        memset(bufs,       0, sizeof bufs);\n    ua_chunk_t  *buf_chunks[n_arr];  memset(buf_chunks, 0, sizeof buf_chunks);\n    const void  *datas[n_arr];       memset(datas,      0, sizeof datas);\n    int          sizes[n_arr];       memset(sizes,      0, sizeof sizes);\n    int failed = 0;\n    /* do_write_box doesn't invoke a language spec — it's a dispatch\n     * primitive that writes a file. The per-input native flag isn't\n     * meaningful here, so pass NULL. */\n    int n_present = read_inputs(ctx, b, bufs, buf_chunks, datas, sizes,\n                                /*input_native=*/NULL,\n                                ctx->default_out_capacity, &failed);\n    emit_input_events(ctx, task_id, bufs, sizes, n_present);\n    int path_idx = -1, value_idx = -1;\n    for (int i = 0; i < b->n_inputs; i++) {\n        if (strcmp(b->inputs[i].name, \"path\")  == 0) path_idx  = i;\n        if (strcmp(b->inputs[i].name, \"value\") == 0) value_idx = i;\n    }\n    if (failed || path_idx < 0 || value_idx < 0\n            || path_idx >= n_present || value_idx >= n_present) {\n        release_inputs(ctx, b->n_inputs, bufs, buf_chunks);\n        return -1;\n    }\n    /* Make NUL-terminated copy of the path. */\n    char *path = malloc((size_t)sizes[path_idx] + 1);\n    if (!path) {\n        release_inputs(ctx, b->n_inputs, bufs, buf_chunks);\n        return -1;\n    }\n    memcpy(path, datas[path_idx], (size_t)sizes[path_idx]);\n    path[sizes[path_idx]] = '\\0';\n\n    char *full = resolve_path(ctx, path);\n    free(path);\n    if (!full) {\n        release_inputs(ctx, b->n_inputs, bufs, buf_chunks);",

      "content":"/* {{{ dispatch_action() — the pool action body */\nvoid dispatch_action(void *arg)\n{\n    dispatch_task_t *t = (dispatch_task_t *)arg;\n    if (!t) return;\n    dispatch_ctx_t *ctx = (dispatch_ctx_t *)t->ctx;\n    const box_t *b = graph_box(ctx->graph, t->box_id);\n\n    /* Issue 319d: publish the active runtime context to thread-local\n     * storage so any spec that calls runtime_create_box /\n     * runtime_connect during its invoke can reach the graph + slot\n     * store + spec registry. Cleared at the end of this task. */\n    runtime_set_active_context((struct graph *)ctx->graph,\n                               ctx->slots,\n                               ctx->specs);\n\n    atomic_fetch_add_explicit(&ctx->tasks_dispatched, 1, memory_order_relaxed);\n\n    int task_id    = t->task_id;\n    int worker_idx = pool_current_worker ? pool_current_worker->thread_idx : -1;\n\n    long start_us = mono_us();\n    if (ctx->events)\n        event_queue_task_start(ctx->events, now_secs(), task_id, worker_idx);\n\n    int out_size = 0;\n    int out_capacity = ctx->default_out_capacity > 0\n                        ? ctx->default_out_capacity : 4096;\n    /* The output buffer comes from the slot store's unified\n     * allocator so it participates in the same refcount-driven\n     * recycling as input buffers and slot cells — every byte that\n     * carries a value through the dispatch runs through one heap. */\n    ua_t *heap = slot_store_allocator(ctx->slots);\n    ua_chunk_t *out_chunk = ua_alloc(heap, (size_t)out_capacity);\n    char *out_buf = out_chunk ? ua_data(out_chunk) : NULL;\n    int rc = -1;\n    if (out_buf && b) {\n        switch (b->kind) {\n            case BOX_CALL:\n                rc = do_call_box(ctx, b, task_id, out_buf, out_capacity, &out_size);\n                break;\n            case BOX_WRITE:\n                rc = do_write_box(ctx, b, task_id,\n                                  out_buf, out_capacity, &out_size);\n                break;",

          "old_string":"/* {{{ dispatch_action() — the pool action body */",
          "replace_all":false,
          "new_string":"/* {{{ do_create_box_box() — runtime self-construction box kind\n *\n * Issue 319 / 246 design-correction follow-on: instead of (or\n * alongside) the per-language `soramech.create_box` wrappers from\n * 319d/319e, a box of kind \"create_box\" performs the same operation\n * driven by data on its `spec` input wire. This is the\n * language-agnostic shape — the same way `write` boxes are the\n * file-sink primitive available to every language.\n *\n * The single input port is named `spec`. Its value carries the box\n * JSON schema text. Same-language fast-path producers might have\n * sent native bytes that aren't yet JSON-shaped, but in practice\n * create_box boxes have no `lang` of their own, so producers'\n * output_edge_native bit is 0 and the JSON form is what arrives.\n *\n * On success the new box's id is written to out_buf so downstream\n * consumers (typically a `connect` kind box) can wire the new box\n * up. */\nstatic int do_create_box_box(dispatch_ctx_t *ctx, const box_t *b, int task_id,\n                             char *out_buf, int out_capacity, int *out_size)\n{\n    int n = b->n_inputs;\n    if (n < 0 || n > DISPATCH_MAX_INPUTS_PER_BOX) return -1;\n    size_t n_arr = (n > 0) ? (size_t)n : 1;\n    char        *bufs[n_arr];        memset(bufs,       0, sizeof bufs);\n    ua_chunk_t  *buf_chunks[n_arr];  memset(buf_chunks, 0, sizeof buf_chunks);\n    const void  *datas[n_arr];       memset(datas,      0, sizeof datas);\n    int          sizes[n_arr];       memset(sizes,      0, sizeof sizes);\n    int failed = 0;\n    int n_present = read_inputs(ctx, b, bufs, buf_chunks, datas, sizes,\n                                NULL, ctx->default_out_capacity, &failed);\n    emit_input_events(ctx, task_id, bufs, sizes, n_present);\n    if (failed || n_present < 1) {\n        release_inputs(ctx, n, bufs, buf_chunks);\n        return -1;\n    }\n\n    /* The TLS active context is already set by dispatch_action's\n     * prologue, so runtime_create_box finds the graph + slot store\n     * + spec registry it needs. */\n    char id_buf[BOX_ID_GEN_BUF_SIZE];\n    char *err = NULL;\n    int rc = runtime_create_box((const char *)datas[0], sizes[0],\n                                id_buf, sizeof id_buf, &err);\n    release_inputs(ctx, n, bufs, buf_chunks);\n    if (rc != 0) {\n        fprintf(stderr, \"create_box box '%s': %s\\n\",\n                b->id, err ? err : \"(no message)\");\n        free(err);\n        return -1;\n    }\n\n    int written = snprintf(out_buf, (size_t)out_capacity, \"%s\", id_buf);\n    if (written < 0 || written >= out_capacity) return -1;\n    *out_size = written;\n    return 0;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ do_connect_box() — runtime wire-creation box kind\n *\n * Sister to do_create_box_box. The single input port is named\n * `connection` and carries one connection-entry shape (the same\n * JSON object that goes inside a box JSON's `connections[]`\n * array). On success the box emits the literal string \"true\"\n * so downstream consumers can chain off the side effect. */\nstatic int do_connect_box(dispatch_ctx_t *ctx, const box_t *b, int task_id,\n                          char *out_buf, int out_capacity, int *out_size)\n{\n    int n = b->n_inputs;\n    if (n < 0 || n > DISPATCH_MAX_INPUTS_PER_BOX) return -1;\n    size_t n_arr = (n > 0) ? (size_t)n : 1;\n    char        *bufs[n_arr];        memset(bufs,       0, sizeof bufs);\n    ua_chunk_t  *buf_chunks[n_arr];  memset(buf_chunks, 0, sizeof buf_chunks);\n    const void  *datas[n_arr];       memset(datas,      0, sizeof datas);\n    int          sizes[n_arr];       memset(sizes,      0, sizeof sizes);\n    int failed = 0;\n    int n_present = read_inputs(ctx, b, bufs, buf_chunks, datas, sizes,\n                                NULL, ctx->default_out_capacity, &failed);\n    emit_input_events(ctx, task_id, bufs, sizes, n_present);\n    if (failed || n_present < 1) {\n        release_inputs(ctx, n, bufs, buf_chunks);\n        return -1;\n    }\n    char *err = NULL;\n    int rc = runtime_connect((const char *)datas[0], sizes[0], &err);\n    release_inputs(ctx, n, bufs, buf_chunks);\n    if (rc != 0) {\n        fprintf(stderr, \"connect box '%s': %s\\n\",\n                b->id, err ? err : \"(no message)\");\n        free(err);\n        return -1;\n    }\n    if (out_capacity >= 4) {\n        memcpy(out_buf, \"true\", 4);\n        *out_size = 4;\n    } else {\n        *out_size = 0;\n    }\n    return 0;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ dispatch_action() — the pool action body */",
          "file_path":"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech/src/012-dispatch.c"

    "originalFile":"#!/bin/bash\n# scripts/run-tests.sh — phase 3 integration tests.\n#\n# Runs every fixture map under tests/maps/ through `soramech-pool`\n# and asserts that the captured outputs match a hardcoded\n# expectation per map. The point is to catch regressions\n# end-to-end — past the spec interface, past the dispatch action,\n# past JSONL writing — rather than via the in-process unit tests.\n#\n# Per the project convention: scripts run from any directory via a\n# hard-coded ${DIR} path with an override argument; all paths are\n# relative to ${DIR}.\n\nset -u\n\nDIR=\"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech\"\nif [[ $# -ge 1 ]]; then\n    DIR=\"$1\"\nfi\n\ncd \"$DIR\"\n\npass=0\nfail=0\nfailures=()\n\n# {{{ check_map() — run one fixture, verify expected substrings\ncheck_map() {\n    local map=\"$1\"\n    shift\n    local expected=(\"$@\")\n\n    printf \"  %-44s \" \"$map\"\n\n    local output\n    # Per-map env opt-in: a map may set SORAMECH_TEST_WORKERS to\n    # pin worker count for tests that depend on per-worker state\n    # (e.g. issue 318's $lang_opaque, which lives in the producer's\n    # Lua registry and can only be reconstructed by a consumer on\n    # the same worker).\n    local workers_env=\"\"\n    if [[ -f \"$DIR/tests/maps/$map/.test_workers\" ]]; then\n        workers_env=$(cat \"$DIR/tests/maps/$map/.test_workers\")\n    fi\n    if [[ -n \"$workers_env\" ]]; then\n        output=$(SORAMECH_WORKERS=\"$workers_env\" \"$DIR/soramech-pool\" \"$DIR/tests/maps/$map\" 2>&1)\n    else\n        output=$(\"$DIR/soramech-pool\" \"$DIR/tests/maps/$map\" 2>&1)\n    fi\n    local rc=$?\n\n    local missing=\"\"\n    if [[ $rc -ne 0 ]]; then\n        missing=\"exit=$rc\"\n    fi\n    for e in \"${expected[@]}\"; do\n        if [[ \"$output\" != *\"$e\"* ]]; then\n            missing+=\"${missing:+; }missing '$e'\"\n        fi\n    done\n\n    if [[ -z \"$missing\" ]]; then\n        printf \"ok\\n\"\n        pass=$((pass + 1))\n    else\n        printf \"FAIL — %s\\n\" \"$missing\"\n        fail=$((fail + 1))\n        failures+=(\"$map: $missing\")\n    fi\n}\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ pipeline_output_check() — additional: the pipeline writes to disk\npipeline_output_check() {\n    local file=\"/tmp/soramech-pipeline-out.txt\"\n    rm -f \"$file\"\n    \"$DIR/soramech-pool\" \"$DIR/tests/maps/pipeline\" > /dev/null 2>&1\n    printf \"  %-44s \" \"pipeline write output\"\n    if [[ -f \"$file\" ]]; then\n        local content\n        content=$(cat \"$file\")\n        if [[ \"$content\" == \"11!\" ]]; then\n            printf \"ok\\n\"\n            pass=$((pass + 1))\n        else\n            printf \"FAIL — expected '11!', got '%s'\\n\" \"$content\"\n            fail=$((fail + 1))\n            failures+=(\"pipeline file: $content\")\n        fi\n    else\n        printf \"FAIL — output file missing\\n\"\n        fail=$((fail + 1))\n        failures+=(\"pipeline: $file missing\")\n    fi\n}\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ compile_pipeline_check() — soramech-compile produces a portable artifact\n# Verifies issue 309's compile pipeline: bundles all spec.so + sources\n# into compiled/, then runs the artifact from /tmp (i.e. with no\n# dependency on the project's cwd) and verifies it produces the same\n# output as the source map.\ncompile_pipeline_check() {\n    local map=\"$DIR/tests/maps/pipeline\"\n    local compiled=\"$map/compiled\"\n    local file=\"/tmp/soramech-pipeline-out.txt\"\n\n    printf \"  %-44s \" \"compile pipeline (portable run)\"\n\n    rm -rf \"$compiled\"\n    if ! \"$DIR/scripts/soramech-compile.sh\" \"$map\" --dir \"$DIR\" >/dev/null 2>&1; then\n        printf \"FAIL — soramech-compile failed\\n\"\n        fail=$((fail + 1))\n        failures+=(\"compile: script returned non-zero\")\n        return\n    fi\n    if [[ ! -x \"$compiled/pool-runner\" ]]; then\n        printf \"FAIL — compiled/pool-runner missing or not executable\\n\"\n        fail=$((fail + 1))\n        failures+=(\"compile: pool-runner missing\")\n        return\n    fi\n\n    rm -f \"$file\"\n    local output\n    output=$(cd /tmp && \"$compiled/pool-runner\" \"$compiled\" 2>&1)\n\n    local content=\"\"\n    [[ -f \"$file\" ]] && content=$(cat \"$file\")\n\n    if [[ \"$output\" == *\"addone → 11\"* ]] && [[ \"$content\" == \"11!\" ]]; then\n        printf \"ok\\n\"\n        pass=$((pass + 1))\n    else\n        printf \"FAIL — output='%s' file='%s'\\n\" \"$output\" \"$content\"\n        fail=$((fail + 1))\n        failures+=(\"compile: bad output\")\n    fi\n}\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ run all fixtures\necho \"integration tests (fixture maps):\"\n\ncheck_map \"calc\" \\\n    \"add → 42\"\n\ncheck_map \"hello\" \\\n    \"greet → Hello, World!\"\n\ncheck_map \"comparator\" \\\n    \"classify → 8\" \\\n    \"high → HIGH:8\" \\\n    \"low → (no output)\" \\\n    \"mid → (no output)\"\n\ncheck_map \"iter-route\" \\\n    \"iter → hi\" \\\n    \"a → A:hi\" \\\n    \"b → (no output)\" \\\n    \"c → (no output)\"\n\ncheck_map \"pipeline\" \\\n    \"double → 10\" \\\n    \"addone → 11\" \\\n    \"shout → 11!\"\n\ncheck_map \"read-literal\" \\\n    \"echo → hello, world!\"\n\ncheck_map \"319a-many-inputs\" \\\n    \"combine → count=20 sum=210\"\n\ncheck_map \"319d-runtime-create\" \\\n    \"trigger → trigger-fired:auto_\" \\\n    \"auto_\" \\\n    \"echo_dyn-received:trigger-fired:auto_\"\n\ncheck_map \"319e-c-create\" \\\n    \"trigger → c-trigger-fired:auto_\" \\\n    \"c-echo-received:c-trigger-fired:auto_\"\n\ncheck_map \"246-c-shim\" \\\n    \"echo → seen:HELLO-FROM-SEED\"\n\ncheck_map \"246-lua-shim\" \\\n    \"echo → seen:REV-fedcba\"\n\n# Issue 318 — the producer's output proves the emit side works\n# end-to-end (Lua function → $lang_opaque sentinel in JSON). The\n# consumer's reconstruction needs the dual-ring slot to surface\n# \"I was written as JSON\" to the same-language consumer, which is\n# a deeper per-edge classification issue documented in 318's\n# closeout; the emit fixture stands today.\ncheck_map \"318-lang-opaque\" \\\n    '\"$lang_opaque\"' \\\n    '\"lang\":\"lua\"' \\\n    '\"shape\":\"function\"'\n\npipeline_output_check\ncompile_pipeline_check\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ parser_tests() — issue 232: unit tests for langs/<lang>/parser.js\n# Run Node's built-in test runner over each per-language parser test\n# file and fold the result into the surrounding pass/fail counters.\n# Each .mjs file is one logical \"test\" from this script's perspective;\n# Node prints its own subtest breakdown on failure for the diagnostic.\nparser_tests() {\n    if ! command -v node >/dev/null 2>&1; then\n        printf \"  %-44s SKIP — node not installed\\n\" \"parser tests (lua, bash)\"\n        return\n    fi\n    for tf in \"$DIR/tests/232-lua-parser-test.mjs\" \\\n              \"$DIR/tests/233-bash-parser-test.mjs\" \\\n              \"$DIR/tests/234-language-spec-js-test.mjs\"; do\n        local label\n        label=$(basename \"$tf\")\n        printf \"  %-44s \" \"$label\"\n        local out\n        out=$(SORAMECH_DIR=\"$DIR\" node --test \"$tf\" 2>&1)\n        local rc=$?\n        if [[ $rc -eq 0 ]]; then\n            printf \"ok\\n\"\n            pass=$((pass + 1))\n        else\n            printf \"FAIL\\n\"\n            echo \"$out\" | sed 's/^/      /'\n            fail=$((fail + 1))\n            failures+=(\"$label: node --test exit=$rc\")\n        fi\n    done\n}\nparser_tests\n# }}}\n\necho\necho \"  $pass passed, $fail failed\"\n\nif [[ $fail -gt 0 ]]; then\n    echo\n    echo \"  failures:\"\n    for f in \"${failures[@]}\"; do\n        echo \"    - $f\"\n    done\nfi\n\nexit $fail\n",

        "input":{
          "content":"# 319f — `create_box` and `connect` as language-agnostic box kinds\n\n## Status\ncomplete\n\n## Parent issue\nDesign-correction follow-on to 319d/319e. Per parent-issue\nreview feedback, the per-language wrappers added in 319d (Lua\nbinding) and 319e (C binding) are an architectural smell — they\nadd work per implementer rather than per primitive. The right\nshape for these primitives is **box kinds**, the same way `read`\nand `write` are language-agnostic kinds the runtime owns and\nevery language uses by wiring values in and out.\n\n## Current behavior\n\nTwo new box kinds, both language-agnostic, both implemented in\n`src/012-dispatch.c` (sibling to `do_write_box`):\n\n- **`kind: \"create_box\"`** — single input port named `spec`,\n  carrying the JSON box-schema text for the new box. The box's\n  output is the new box's id string. Implementation:\n  `do_create_box_box` reads the input, calls\n  `runtime_create_box` (the same C function the per-language\n  wrappers call), writes the id to the output buffer.\n\n- **`kind: \"connect\"`** — single input port named `connection`,\n  carrying one connection-entry JSON object. The box's output is\n  the literal `\"true\"`. Implementation: `do_connect_box` mirrors\n  `do_create_box_box`'s shape.\n\nThe dispatch's per-task TLS (set by `dispatch_action` in 319d)\nmakes `runtime_create_box` and `runtime_connect` reach the\nactive graph + slot store + spec registry without needing them\nthreaded through the new box-kind `do_*` signatures.\n\n## Why box kinds instead of per-language callbacks\n\nPer the strategem `strategems/contracts-must-fit-every-implementer.md`,\na contract that requires per-language wrappers is one the\nawkward implementer (Bash) can't satisfy without shims. The\nper-language wrappers from 319d/319e:\n\n- worked cleanly for Lua (registered as `soramech.create_box` /\n  `soramech.connect`)\n- worked cleanly for C (header alias macros over the runtime_*\n  symbols)\n- were genuinely hard for Bash (needs line-protocol extension\n  back to the runner — the gap that made 319e defer Bash)\n\nThe box-kind shape collapses all three cases: every language can\nwrite a value to an output wire; every language can consume a\nvalue from an input wire. Routing the value through a special\nbox kind that knows what to do is the universal mechanism. Bash\ngets self-construction for free now — its box function just\nwrites the spec string, no protocol extension needed.\n\n## Compatibility with the per-language wrappers\n\nThe Lua and C wrappers from 319d/319e are not removed. Existing\nmaps that use them continue to work; the box-kind path is the\nnew idiomatic way. Per the strategem `redesigns-change-the-\nsurface-too.md`, the deprecation of the per-language wrappers\nis acknowledged here as the right direction — both paths reach\nthe same `runtime_create_box` / `runtime_connect` C functions,\nso behaviour is identical. The on-ramp for new users and the\ndocumented examples should be the box-kind path; the per-language\nwrappers are grandfathered.\n\n## Validation\n\n- 18 integration tests pass (one new fixture\n  `tests/maps/319-box-kind-create/` exercises the create_box kind\n  end-to-end: a read box emits a spec, a create_box-kind box\n  consumes it, the new box's id `auto_00000000` appears in\n  captured outputs).\n- The slot-store unit suite (23 passing) and the rest of the\n  per-component suites all still pass.\n\n## Relevant files\n\n- `src/010-graph-loader.h` — `BOX_CREATE_BOX`, `BOX_CONNECT`\n  added to `box_kind_t`.\n- `src/010-graph-loader.c` — parse `\"create_box\"` / `\"connect\"`\n  from JSON `kind` field; include these kinds in the\n  \"runs as a task\" filter used by entry-box detection and\n  read-predecessor-list building.\n- `src/012-dispatch.c` — `do_create_box_box` /\n  `do_connect_box` implementations; cases added to\n  `dispatch_action`'s switch.\n- `tests/maps/319-box-kind-create/` — end-to-end fixture.\n- `scripts/run-tests.sh` — invokes the fixture.\n\n## Deferred / follow-on\n\n- The per-language Lua/C wrappers from 319d/319e are still\n  present. A future cleanup could remove them in favour of the\n  box-kind path exclusively. Until then, both work.\n- Bash maps that want to use self-construction can now drop a\n  `create_box` kind box on the canvas; no Bash-spec changes\n  needed.\n",
          "file_path":"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech/issues/completed/319f-create-box-and-connect-as-box-kinds.md"
        },

    "originalFile":"#!/bin/bash\n# scripts/export-llm-transcripts.sh — capture this project's Claude\n# conversation history at every verbosity level.\n#\n# What it does, in CEO terms: every conversation Claude has had about\n# this project is stored as a JSONL file under ~/.claude/projects/.\n# An external tool can render those JSONL files into human-readable\n# markdown at six different levels of detail (terse code-only to raw\n# tool-result firehose). This script invokes that external tool once\n# per verbosity level and parks the rendered markdown under\n# llm-transcripts/ so the project repo carries its own development\n# history alongside the code.\n#\n# Intended use: run as part of the commit ritual — refreshes the\n# tracked transcripts so each commit captures the state of project\n# history at that moment.\n#\n# Per the project convention: scripts run from any directory via a\n# hard-coded ${DIR} path with an override argument; all paths are\n# relative to ${DIR}.\n\nset -u\n\nDIR=\"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech\"\nif [[ $# -ge 1 ]]; then\n    DIR=\"$1\"\nfi\n\n# {{{ External exporter location and verbosity table\nEXPORTER=\"/home/ritz/programming/ai-stuff/scripts/claude-conversation-exporter.sh\"\n\n# Verbosity levels offered by the external tool. Each produces a\n# different lens on the same conversations:\n#   v0 minimal  — code + essentials, useful for \"what was actually written\"\n#   v1 compact  — drops user sentiments\n#   v2 standard — the default, everything readable\n#   v3 verbose  — adds context-file expansions\n#   v4 complete — adds LLM execution detail + vimfolds\n#   v5 raw      — every intermediate step and tool result\ndeclare -A LEVELS=(\n    [0]=\"minimal\"\n    [1]=\"compact\"\n    [2]=\"standard\"\n    [3]=\"verbose\"\n    [4]=\"complete\"\n    [5]=\"raw\"\n)\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ Sanity checks\nif [[ ! -x \"$EXPORTER\" ]]; then\n    echo \"error: external exporter not found at $EXPORTER\" >&2\n    exit 1\nfi\n\nif [[ ! -d \"$DIR\" ]]; then\n    echo \"error: project directory not found: $DIR\" >&2\n    exit 1\nfi\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ Output directory\nOUT_DIR=\"$DIR/llm-transcripts\"\nmkdir -p \"$OUT_DIR\"\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ Run the exporter once per verbosity level\necho \"Exporting LLM transcripts for $DIR\"\necho \"  → $OUT_DIR/\"\n\nfor level in 0 1 2 3 4 5; do\n    name=\"${LEVELS[$level]}\"\n    out_file=\"$OUT_DIR/v${level}-${name}.md\"\n    printf \"  v%d %-10s \" \"$level\" \"$name\"\n\n    if \"$EXPORTER\" \"-v$level\" \"$DIR\" all > \"$out_file\" 2>/dev/null; then\n        size=$(wc -c < \"$out_file\" 2>/dev/null || echo \"?\")\n        printf \"ok (%s bytes)\\n\" \"$size\"\n    else\n        rc=$?\n        printf \"FAIL (exit=%d)\\n\" \"$rc\"\n    fi\ndone\n# }}}\n\necho \"Done.\"\n",

(input.description or input.id or \"?\")\n    end\n    return name .. \" (...)\"\nend\n\nlocal function tool_result_text(item)\n    local c = item.content\n    if type(c) == \"string\" then return c end\n    if type(c) == \"table\" then\n        local out = {}\n        for i = 1, #c do\n            local sub = c[i]\n            if type(sub) == \"table\" and sub.type == \"text\" then\n                out[#out + 1] = sub.text or \"\"\n            end\n        end\n        return table.concat(out, \"\\n\")\n    end\n    return \"\"\nend\n\n-- Pull every fenced code block out of a markdown string.\nlocal function extract_code_blocks(text)\n    if not text or text == \"\" then return {} end\n    local blocks = {}\n    for code in text:gmatch(\"```[%w_-]*\\n(.-)```\") do\n        blocks[#blocks + 1] = code\n    end\n    return blocks\nend\n\n-- Truncate a multi-line string to at most N lines, marking the tail.\nlocal function truncate_lines(text, max_lines)\n    if not text or text == \"\" then return text end\n    local count = 0\n    local cut_at = nil\n    for pos in text:gmatch(\"()\\n\") do\n        count = count + 1\n        if count == max_lines then cut_at = pos break end\n    end\n    if not cut_at then return text end\n    return text:sub(1, cut_at) ..\n           \"... [truncated; \" .. max_lines .. \"-line cap]\"\nend\n-- }}}\n\n-- {{{ render — one conversation at one verbosity level\n-- Returns a string. Each level walks the JSONL entries once and\n-- emits a different subset.\n\nlocal function render_v0_minimal(entries)\n    -- Code blocks from assistant text only. Tool results are omitted.\n    local out = { \"# Compact transcript\\n\" }\n    for _, e in ipairs(entries) do\n        if e.type == \"user\" then\n            local text = get_user_text(e)\n            if text and text:match(\"%S\") then\n                out[#out + 1] = \"## User\\n\\n\" .. text .. \"\\n\"\n            end\n        elseif e.type == \"assistant\" then\n            local text_chunks = item.text or \"\"\n                elseif item.type == \"tool_use\" then\n                    tools[#tools + 1] = summarise_tool_call(item)\n                end\n            end\n            if #text_chunks > 0 or #tools > 0 then\n                out[#out + 1] = \"## Assistant\\n\"\n                if #text_chunks > 0 then\n                    out[#out + 1] = table.concat(text_chunks, \"\\n\") .. \"\\n\"\n                end\n                if #tools > 0 then\n                    out[#out + 1] = \"_Tools:_\\n\"\n                    for _, t in ipairs(tools) do\n                        out[#out + 1] = \"- `\" .. t .. \"`\"\n                    end\n                    out[#out + 1] = \"\"\n                end\n            end\n        end\n    end\n    return table.concat(out, \"\\n\")\nend\n\nlocal function render_with_tool_results(entries, result_max_lines)\n    local out = { \"# Transcript\\n\" }\n    for _, e in ipairs(entries) do\n        if e.type == \"user\" then\n            local m = e.message or {}\n            local c = m.content\n            if type(c) == \"string\" then\n                out[#out + 1] = \"## User\\n\\n\" .. c .. \"\\n\"\n            elseif          out[#out + 1] = \"## User\\n\\n\" ..\n                                    table.concat(text_items, \"\\n\") .. \"\\n\"\n                end\n                for _, tr in ipairs(tool_results) do\n                    local txt = tool_result_text(tr)\n                    if result_max_lines and result_max_lines > 0 then\n                        txt = truncate_lines(txt, result_max_lines)\n                    end\n                    out[#out + 1] = \"### Tool result\\n\\n```\\n\" ..\n                                    (txt or \"\") .. \"\\n```\\n\"\n                end\n            end\n             end\n            end\n        end\n    end\n    return table.concat(out, \"\\n\")\nend\n\nlocal function render_v2_standard(entries) return render_with_tool_results(entries, 200)           "command":"git commit -m \"$(cat <<'EOF'\nscripts: local transcript exporter replaces the broken external one\n\nThe external claude-conversation-exporter was architecturally\nwrong for projects outside /home/ritz/programming/ai-stuff/ —\nit guessed at the source directory and got it wrong, re-rendered\nevery conversation top-to-bottom every run, and prepended global\nCLAUDE.md text into the output. The local replacement reads the\nright project (the path is encoded directly from $DIR into the\n~/.claude/projects/<encoded>/ lookup), supports incremental\nrefresh via mtime comparison, and never includes ambient context.\n\nSix verbosity levels with distinct semantics:\n\n  v0 minimal   code blocks from assistant messages only\n  v1 compact   user prompts + assistant text + tool signatures\n  v2 standard  v1 + truncated tool results (200-line cap)\n  v3 verbose   v2 + full tool results\n  v4 complete  v3 + tool metadata\n  v5 raw       pretty-printed JSONL entries\n\nOutput layout switches from one-bundle-per-level files to\nper-conversation directories — llm-transcripts/v{N}-{name}/<conv-id>.md.\nPer-conversation files let the incremental check work cleanly\n(skip a conversation when every level's output is newer than the\nsource JSONL) and make it easier to grep into a specific\nsession's history.\n\nThe previously-committed bundle files (v0-minimal.md etc. as\nflat files) are removed — they were the broken external tool's\noutput. The May-8 historical artifacts (2029ad16-* and friends)\nstay in place as snapshots of an even older system.\n\nImplementation in Lua (luajit) — matches the project's preferred\nlanguage and uses libs/dkjson for JSONL parsing. The .sh entry\npoint is a thin shape-consistent wrapper that exec's the .lua.\n\nInitial run renders all 15 conversations (~89 MB across all six\nlevels, dominated by v5 raw). Subsequent runs skip unchanged\nconversations.\n\nCo-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>\nEOF\n)\" 2>&1 | tail -5",
