          "old_string":"        /* Incoming edges: for each input port the port is native iff\n         * it has at least one feeder AND every feeder is a call box\n         * sharing this box's language. A mixed-language fan-in\n         * downgrades the port to JSON — the slot can carry only one\n         * format and JSON is the common denominator. */\n        for (int port = 0; port < b->n_inputs; port++) {\n            input_feeders_t f = scan_input_feeders(g, i, port, b->lang);\n            b->input_edge_native[port] = (f.n_feeders > 0 &&\n                                          f.n_native == f.n_feeders) ? 1 : 0;\n        }",
          "replace_all":false,
          "new_string":"        /* Incoming edges: for each input port the port is native iff\n         * EVERY feeder will actually write native bytes to this slot\n         * at run time. Two conditions must both hold for a given\n         * feeder to be \"native-writing\":\n         *   - the feeder is a call box sharing this consumer's lang\n         *     (so its same-language native form is meaningful here);\n         *   - the feeder has no OTHER cross-language sibling\n         *     consumer, because if it does, the producer's per-call\n         *     output_native flag is 0 and it writes JSON to ALL its\n         *     consumers (including this one). The 2026-05 dual-ring\n         *     design (issue 312) writes one format per call, not one\n         *     per edge, and same-language siblings of cross-language\n         *     fan-out eat the JSON cost.\n         *\n         * This is the conservative fix for issue 318's\n         * intra-Lua $lang_opaque round-trip case where the producer\n         * is forced to JSON by a write-box sibling: previously the\n         * consumer's input_edge_native = 1 lied, and the Lua spec's\n         * decode skipped the JSON-parse path. Now the bit\n         * correctly says \"this slot may carry JSON\" and the spec\n         * runs json_to_native, reconstructing the sentinel. */\n        for (int port = 0; port < b->n_inputs; port++) {\n            input_feeders_t f = scan_input_feeders(g, i, port, b->lang);\n            int port_native = (f.n_feeders > 0 &&\n                               f.n_native == f.n_feeders) ? 1 : 0;\n            if (port_native) {\n                /* Walk feeders and check whether any one of them\n                 * has a cross-language sibling that would force it\n                 * to JSON. */\n                for (int p = 0; p < g->n_boxes && port_native; p++) {\n                    const box_t *prod = g->boxes[p];\n                    int feeds_this = 0;\n                    for (int k = 0; k < prod->n_connections; k++) {\n                        const connection_t *c = &prod->connections[k];\n                        if (c->to_box_idx == i && c->to_input_idx == port) {\n                            feeds_this = 1;\n                            break;\n                        }\n                    }\n                    if (!feeds_this) continue;\n                    /* This producer feeds the consumer port; check\n                     * its sibling outputs for cross-language ones. */\n                    for (int k = 0; k < prod->n_connections; k++) {\n                        const connection_t *c = &prod->connections[k];\n                        int dst = c->to_box_idx;\n                        if (dst < 0) continue;\n                        const box_t *sib = g->boxes[dst];\n                        int sib_native = (sib->kind == BOX_CALL && sib->lang\n                                          && prod->lang\n                                          && strcmp(sib->lang, prod->lang) == 0);\n                        if (!sib_native) { port_native = 0; break; }\n                    }\n                }\n            }\n            b->input_edge_native[port] = port_native;\n        }",

    "filePath":"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech/src/010-graph-loader.c",
    "oldString":"        /* Incoming edges: for each input port the port is native iff\n         * it has at least one feeder AND every feeder is a call box\n         * sharing this box's language. A mixed-language fan-in\n         * downgrades the port to JSON — the slot can carry only one\n         * format and JSON is the common denominator. */\n        for (int port = 0; port < b->n_inputs; port++) {\n            input_feeders_t f = scan_input_feeders(g, i, port, b->lang);\n            b->input_edge_native[port] = (f.n_feeders > 0 &&\n                                          f.n_native == f.n_feeders) ? 1 : 0;\n        }",
    "newString":"        /* Incoming edges: for each input port the port is native iff\n         * EVERY feeder will actually write native bytes to this slot\n         * at run time. Two conditions must both hold for a given\n         * feeder to be \"native-writing\":\n         *   - the feeder is a call box sharing this consumer's lang\n         *     (so its same-language native form is meaningful here);\n         *   - the feeder has no OTHER cross-language sibling\n         *     consumer, because if it does, the producer's per-call\n         *     output_native flag is 0 and it writes JSON to ALL its\n         *     consumers (including this one). The 2026-05 dual-ring\n         *     design (issue 312) writes one format per call, not one\n         *     per edge, and same-language siblings of cross-language\n         *     fan-out eat the JSON cost.\n         *\n         * This is the conservative fix for issue 318's\n         * intra-Lua $lang_opaque round-trip case where the producer\n         * is forced to JSON by a write-box sibling: previously the\n         * consumer's input_edge_native = 1 lied, and the Lua spec's\n         * decode skipped the JSON-parse path. Now the bit\n         * correctly says \"this slot may carry JSON\" and the spec\n         * runs json_to_native, reconstructing the sentinel. */\n        for (int port = 0; port < b->n_inputs; port++) {\n            input_feeders_t f = scan_input_feeders(g, i, port, b->lang);\n            int port_native = (f.n_feeders > 0 &&\n                               f.n_native == f.n_feeders) ? 1 : 0;\n            if (port_native) {\n                /* Walk feeders and check whether any one of them\n                 * has a cross-language sibling that would force it\n                 * to JSON. */\n                for (int p = 0; p < g->n_boxes && port_native; p++) {\n                    const box_t *prod = g->boxes[p];\n                    int feeds_this = 0;\n                    for (int k = 0; k < prod->n_connections; k++) {\n                        const connection_t *c = &prod->connections[k];\n                        if (c->to_box_idx == i && c->to_input_idx == port) {\n                            feeds_this = 1;\n                            break;\n                        }\n                    }\n                    if (!feeds_this) continue;\n                    /* This producer feeds the consumer port; check\n                     * its sibling outputs for cross-language ones. */\n                    for (int k = 0; k < prod->n_connections; k++) {\n                        const connection_t *c = &prod->connections[k];\n                        int dst = c->to_box_idx;\n                        if (dst < 0) continue;\n                        const box_t *sib = g->boxes[dst];\n                        int sib_native = (sib->kind == BOX_CALL && sib->lang\n                                          && prod->lang\n                                          && strcmp(sib->lang, prod->lang) == 0);\n                        if (!sib_native) { port_native = 0; break; }\n                    }\n                }\n            }\n            b->input_edge_native[port] = port_native;\n        }"
  },

The 2026-05 dual-ring\n         *     design (issue 312) writes one format per call, not one\n         *     per edge, and same-language siblings of cross-language\n         *     fan-out eat the JSON cost.\n         *\n         * This is the conservative fix for issue 318's\n         * intra-Lua $lang_opaque round-trip case where the producer\n         * is forced to JSON by a write-box sibling: previously the\n         * consumer's input_edge_native = 1 lied, and the Lua spec's\n         * decode skipped the JSON-parse path. 1 : 0;\n            if (port_native) {\n                /* Walk feeders and check whether any one of them\n                 * has a cross-language sibling that would force it\n                 * to JSON. */\n                for (int p = 0; p < g->n_boxes && port_native; p++) {\n                    const box_t *prod = g->boxes[p];\n                    int feeds_this = 0;\n                    for (int k = 0; k < prod->n_connections; k++) {\n                        const connection_t *c = &prod->connections[k];\n                        if (c->to_box_idx == i && c->to_input_idx == port) {\n                            feeds_this = 1;\n                            break;\n                        }\n                    }\n                    if (!feeds_this) continue;\n                    /* This producer feeds the consumer port; check\n                     * its sibling outputs for cross-language ones. */\n                    for (int k = 0; k < prod->n_connections; k++) {\n                        const connection_t *c = &prod->connections[k];\n                        int dst = c->to_box_idx;\n                        if (dst < 0) continue;\n                        const box_t *sib = g->boxes[dst];\n                        int sib_native = (sib->kind == BOX_CALL && sib->lang\n                                          && prod->lang\n                                          && strcmp(sib->lang, prod->lang) == 0);\n                        if (!sib_native) { port_native = 0; break; }\n                    }\n                }\n            }\n            b->input_edge_native[port] = port_native;\n            fprintf(stderr, \"DEBUG: box %s port %d input_edge_native=%d (feeders=%d native=%d)\\n\",\n                    b->id, port, port_native, f.n_feeders, f.n_native);\n        }",

    "filePath":"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech/src/010-graph-loader.c",
    "oldString":"        /* Incoming edges: for each input port the port is native iff\n         * EVERY feeder will actually write native bytes to this slot\n         * at run time. Two conditions must both hold for a given\n         * feeder to be \"native-writing\":\n         *   - the feeder is a call box sharing this consumer's lang\n         *     (so its same-language native form is meaningful here);\n         *   - the feeder has no OTHER cross-language sibling\n         *     consumer, because if it does, the producer's per-call\n         *     output_native flag is 0 and it writes JSON to ALL its\n         *     consumers (including this one). The 2026-05 dual-ring\n         *     design (issue 312) writes one format per call, not one\n         *     per edge, and same-language siblings of cross-language\n         *     fan-out eat the JSON cost.\n         *\n         * This is the conservative fix for issue 318's\n         * intra-Lua $lang_opaque round-trip case where the producer\n         * is forced to JSON by a write-box sibling: previously the\n         * consumer's input_edge_native = 1 lied, and the Lua spec's\n         * decode skipped the JSON-parse path. Now the bit\n         * correctly says \"this slot may carry JSON\" and the spec\n         * runs json_to_native, reconstructing the sentinel. */\n        for (int port = 0; port < b->n_inputs; port++) {\n            input_feeders_t f = scan_input_feeders(g, i, port, b->lang);\n            int port_native = (f.n_feeders > 0 &&\n                               f.n_native == f.n_feeders) ? 1 : 0;\n            if (port_native) {\n                /* Walk feeders and check whether any one of them\n                 * has a cross-language sibling that would force it\n                 * to JSON. */\n                for (int p = 0; p < g->n_boxes && port_native; p++) {\n                    const box_t *prod = g->boxes[p];\n                    int feeds_this = 0;\n                    for (int k = 0; k < prod->n_connections; k++) {\n                        const connection_t *c = &prod->connections[k];\n                        if (c->to_box_idx == i && c->to_input_idx == port) {\n                            feeds_this = 1;\n                            break;\n                        }\n                    }\n                    if (!feeds_this) continue;\n                    /* This producer feeds the consumer port; check\n                     * its sibling outputs for cross-language ones. */\n                    for (int k = 0; k < prod->n_connections; k++) {\n                        const connection_t *c = &prod->connections[k];\n                        int dst = c->to_box_idx;\n                        if (dst < 0) continue;\n                        const box_t *sib = g->boxes[dst];\n                        int sib_native = (sib->kind == BOX_CALL && sib->lang\n                                          && prod->lang\n                                          && strcmp(sib->lang, prod->lang) == 0);\n                        if (!sib_native) { port_native = 0; break; }\n                    }\n                }\n            }\n            b->input_edge_native[port] = port_native;\n            fprintf(stderr, \"DEBUG: box %s port %d input_edge_native=%d (feeders=%d native=%d)\\n\",\n                    b->id, port, port_native, f.n_feeders, f.n_native);\n        }",
    "newString":"        /* Incoming edges: for each input port the port is native iff\n         * it has at least one feeder AND every feeder is a call box\n         * sharing this box's language. A mixed-language fan-in\n         * downgrades the port to JSON — the slot can carry only one\n         * format and JSON is the common denominator.\n         *\n         * NOTE (issue 318 follow-on): this per-edge classification is\n         * the FALLBACK on single-ring slots. For dual-ring slots\n         * (issue 312), the consumer's read path uses the per-cell\n         * which_ring tag returned by slot_pop_ordered instead. The\n         * dual-ring path is what makes intra-Lua $lang_opaque survive\n         * a producer that was forced to JSON by a cross-language\n         * sibling consumer — each cell carries its own format flag,\n         * so the consumer doesn't have to trust a per-edge\n         * approximation that lies when the producer's per-call\n         * output_native is 0. */\n        for (int port = 0; port < b->n_inputs; port++) {\n            input_feeders_t f = scan_input_feeders(g, i, port, b->lang);\n            b->input_edge_native[port] = (f.n_feeders > 0 &&\n                                          f.n_native == f.n_feeders) ? 1 : 0;\n        }"
  },

We must\n     * push to the JSON ring so the consumer's slot_pop_ordered\n     * returns the correct which_ring tag and the consumer's spec\n     * runs json_to_native rather than treating the JSON bytes as\n     * its language's native form. (Issue 318 follow-on: the\n     * per-edge bit alone lies about a per-call decision.)\n     *\n     * When output_native is 1 the producer wrote native bytes\n     * intended for same-language consumers; cross-language\n     * consumers on the same producer get the per-edge bit's\n     * direction (push to JSON ring with a wrapper or fall back —\n     * the wrapper path is captured elsewhere). */\n    if (dst_flags >= 0 && (dst_flags & SLOT_FLAG_DUAL_RING)) {\n        int native_edge = wire_is_native(b, c);\n        int push_native = output_native && native_edge;\n        if (push_native) {\n            rc = slot_push_native(ctx->slots, dst_slot,\n                                  out_bytes, out_size, tag);\n        } else {\n            rc = slot_push_json(ctx->slots, dst_slot,\n                                out_bytes, out_size, tag);\n        }\n    } else {\n        rc = slot_push(ctx->slots, dst_slot, out_bytes, out_size, tag);\n    }"
  },

      "content":"/* {{{ push_branch() — push only to outgoing connections matching `branch` */\n/* `branch` is one of \"lt\" / \"eq\" / \"gt\" / \"out_<n>\". Connections\n * whose from_branch is NULL (plain) are skipped; connections whose\n * from_branch equals `branch` fire. */\nstatic int push_branch(dispatch_ctx_t *ctx, const box_t *b,\n                       const char *branch,\n                       const void *out_bytes, int out_size,\n                       uint32_t tag)\n{\n    int fired = 0;\n    for (int i = 0; i < b->n_connections; i++) {\n        const connection_t *c = &b->connections[i];\n        if (!c->from_branch) continue;\n        if (strcmp(c->from_branch, branch) != 0) continue;\n        if (push_one_connection(ctx, b, c, out_bytes, out_size, tag) != 0)\n            return -1;\n        fired++;\n    }\n    return fired;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ push_to_downstream() — fan output to every outgoing connection */\n/* The push triggers spawn_if_ready on the consumer. Tag = 0 for\n * the plain fan-out case; iterator routing uses push_branch with a\n * non-zero tag. */\nstatic int push_to_downstream(dispatch_ctx_t *ctx, const box_t *b,\n                              const void *out_bytes, int out_size)\n{\n    for (int i = 0; i < b->n_connections; i++) {\n        if (push_one_connection(ctx, b, &b->connections[i],\n                                out_bytes, out_size, 0) != 0) return -1;\n    }\n    return 0;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ parse_double() — parse a NUL-bounded byte run as a double */\nstatic double parse_double(const void *bytes, int size)\n{\n    char tmp[64];\n    int n = size < 63 ? size : 63;\n    if (n > 0) memcpy(tmp, bytes, (size_t)n);\n    tmp[n] = '\\0';\n    return strtod(tmp, NULL);",

Tag = 0 for\n * the plain fan-out case; iterator routing uses push_branch with a\n * non-zero tag. */\nstatic int push_to_downstream(dispatch_ctx_t *ctx, const box_t *b,\n                              const void *out_bytes, int out_size)\n{\n    for (int i = 0; i < b->n_connections; i++) {\n        if (push_one_connection(ctx, b, &b->connections[i],\n                                out_bytes, out_size, 0) != 0) return -1;\n    }\n    return 0;\n}",
    "newString":"static int push_branch(dispatch_ctx_t *ctx, const box_t *b,\n                       const char *branch,\n                       const void *out_bytes, int out_size,\n                       uint32_t tag, int output_native)\n{\n    int fired = 0;\n    for (int i = 0; i < b->n_connections; i++) {\n        const connection_t *c = &b->connections[i];\n        if (!c->from_branch) continue;\n        if (strcmp(c->from_branch, branch) != 0) continue;\n        if (push_one_connection(ctx, b, c, out_bytes, out_size, tag,\n                                output_native) != 0)\n            return -1;\n        fired++;\n    }\n    return fired;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ push_to_downstream() — fan output to every outgoing connection */\n/* The push triggers spawn_if_ready on the consumer. Tag = 0 for\n * the plain fan-out case; iterator routing uses push_branch with a\n * non-zero tag. `output_native` is the per-call format flag from\n * the producer's invoke (issue 312); it threads through so\n * push_one_connection can route to the correct dual-ring side. */\nstatic int push_to_downstream(dispatch_ctx_t *ctx, const box_t *b,\n                              const void *out_bytes, int out_size,\n                              int output_native)\n{\n    for (int i = 0; i < b->n_connections; i++) {\n        if (push_one_connection(ctx, b, &b->connections[i],\n                                out_bytes, out_size, 0, output_native) != 0)\n            return -1;\n    }\n    return 0;\n}"

{
  "uuid":"d6f462f0-2e0c-4cbe-a14a-1e58d8193309",
  "type":"user",
  "timestamp":"2026-05-24T02:40:36.301Z",
  "parentUuid":"c337f201-c2eb-4ed6-9d7a-a0a952cf8de4",
  "toolUseResult":{
    "type":"text",
    "file":{
      "numLines":155,
      "startLine":641,
      "totalLines":1256,
      "content":"/* {{{ push_routed() — branch picker over routing.kind, then push */\nstatic int push_routed(dispatch_ctx_t *ctx, const box_t *b,\n                       const void *out_bytes, int out_size)\n{\n    /* Read and write boxes don't carry a routing kind; their\n     * output fans plain. Same for call boxes with no routing set\n     * (treated as plain). */\n    if (b->kind != BOX_CALL) return push_to_downstream(ctx, b, out_bytes, out_size);\n\n    switch (b->routing.kind) {\n        case ROUTING_PLAIN:\n            return push_to_downstream(ctx, b, out_bytes, out_size);\n\n        case ROUTING_COMPARATOR: {\n            double v = parse_double(out_bytes, out_size);\n            const char *branch =\n                (v < b->routing.comparand) ? \"lt\" :\n                (v > b->routing.comparand) ? \"gt\" : \"eq\";\n            return push_branch(ctx, b, branch, out_bytes, out_size, 0) < 0 ? -1 : 0;\n        }\n\n        case ROUTING_ITERATOR: {\n            if (b->counter_slot_id < 0 || b->routing.n_outputs < 1) {\n                /* No counter slot or zero outputs — fall back to plain. */\n                return push_to_downstream(ctx, b, out_bytes, out_size);\n            }\n            /* The counter is both the branch selector AND the order\n             * tag for the consumer slot (issue 304 cell-tagged\n             * ordering). Tagged consumers serve pops by ascending\n             * tag, so parallel iterator tasks land in invocation\n             * order regardless of which worker finishes first. */\n            uint32_t idx = slot_read_inc(ctx->slots, b->counter_slot_id,\n                                         (uint32_t)b->routing.n_outputs);\n            char branch[MAX_BRANCH_NAME];\n            snprintf(branch, sizeof branch, \"out_%u\", idx);\n            return push_branch(ctx, b, branch, out_bytes, out_size, idx) < 0 ? -1 : 0;\n        }\n\n        case ROUTING_RANDOMIZER: {\n            if (b->counter_slot_id < 0 || b->routing.n_outputs < 1) {\n                return push_to_downstream(ctx, b, out_bytes, out_size);\n            }\n            /* Mix the monotonic counter so consecutive invocations\n             * don't go to consecutive branches. xorshift32-style,\n             * no crypto pretensions. */\n            uint32_t i = slot_read_inc(ctx->slots, b->counter_slot_id, UINT32_MAX);\n            uint32_t h = i;\n            h ^= h >> 16; h *= 0x85ebca6bu;\n            h ^= h >> 13; h *= 0xc2b2ae35u;\n            h ^= h >> 16;\n            uint32_t branch_idx = h % (uint32_t)b->routing.n_outputs;\n            char branch[MAX_BRANCH_NAME];\n            snprintf(branch, sizeof branch, \"out_%u\", branch_idx);\n            /* Randomizer is also multi-spawn-aware; pass i as tag so\n             * any downstream tagged slot still serves in order. */\n            return push_branch(ctx, b, branch, out_bytes, out_size, i) < 0 ? -1 : 0;\n        }\n\n        case ROUTING_WEIGHTED: {\n            if (b->counter_slot_id < 0 || b->routing.n_outputs < 1 ||\n                !b->routing.weights) {\n                return push_to_downstream(ctx, b, out_bytes, out_size);\n            }\n            /* Cumulative-band lookup against a counter scaled to a\n             * fixed precision. ```json
{
  "uuid":"7f40b3cc-d849-480f-9d08-6ca31e907c77",
  "type":"user",
  "timestamp":"2026-05-24T02:43:28.509Z",
  "parentUuid":"edba21b5-b605-496b-b440-5e5e06b5b47c",
  "toolUseResult":{
    "originalFile":"#!/bin/bash\n# scripts/run-tests.sh — phase 3 integration tests.\n#\n# Runs every fixture map under tests/maps/ through `soramech-pool`\n# and asserts that the captured outputs match a hardcoded\n# expectation per map. The point is to catch regressions\n# end-to-end — past the spec interface, past the dispatch action,\n# past JSONL writing — rather than via the in-process unit tests.\n#\n# Per the project convention: scripts run from any directory via a\n# hard-coded ${DIR} path with an override argument; all paths are\n# relative to ${DIR}.\n\nset -u\n\nDIR=\"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech\"\nif [[ $# -ge 1 ]]; then\n    DIR=\"$1\"\nfi\n\ncd \"$DIR\"\n\npass=0\nfail=0\nfailures=()\n\n# {{{ check_map() — run one fixture, verify expected substrings\ncheck_map() {\n    local map=\"$1\"\n    shift\n    local expected=(\"$@\")\n\n    printf \"  %-44s \" \"$map\"\n\n    local output\n    # Per-map env opt-in: a map may set SORAMECH_TEST_WORKERS to\n    # pin worker count for tests that depend on per-worker state\n    # (e.g. issue 318's $lang_opaque, which lives in the producer's\n    # Lua registry and can only be reconstructed by a consumer on\n    # the same worker).\n    local workers_env=\"\"\n    if [[ -f \"$DIR/tests/maps/$map/.test_workers\" ]]; then\n        workers_env=$(cat \"$DIR/tests/maps/$map/.test_workers\")\n    fi\n    if [[ -n \"$workers_env\" ]]; then\n        output=$(SORAMECH_WORKERS=\"$workers_env\" \"$DIR/soramech-pool\" \"$DIR/tests/maps/$map\" 2>&1)\n    else\n        output=$(\"$DIR/soramech-pool\" \"$DIR/tests/maps/$map\" 2>&1)\n    fi\n    local rc=$?\n\n    local missing=\"\"\n    if [[ $rc -ne 0 ]]; then\n        missing=\"exit=$rc\"\n    fi\n    for e in \"${expected[@]}\"; do\n        if [[ \"$output\" != *\"$e\"* ]]; then\n            missing+=\"${missing:+; }missing '$e'\"\n        fi\n    done\n\n    if [[ -z \"$missing\" ]];         "input":{
          "content":"# 318a — per-call output_native threads through to push_one_connection\n\n## Status\ncomplete\n\n## Parent issue\nFollow-on to 318. Issue 318's closeout documented that intra-Lua\n`$lang_opaque` reconstruction failed when the producer was\nforced to JSON output by a cross-language sibling consumer; the\nconsumer's same-language wire's per-edge classification said\n\"native\" but the slot received JSON bytes. This sub-issue fixes\nthe underlying mismatch.\n\n## Current behavior\n\nThe producer's per-call `output_native` flag (1 = native, 0 =\nJSON, computed inside `invoke_box_impl` as\n`all_wires_native(b)`) now threads through to\n`push_one_connection`. On a dual-ring destination slot:\n\n- If `output_native = 1` AND the per-edge bit is 1, push to the\n  native ring (same-language native form).\n- Otherwise, push to the JSON ring. This covers two cases:\n  - per-edge bit = 0 (cross-language wire) — JSON is the right\n    form regardless.\n  - per-call output_native = 0 (producer wrote JSON because of\n    some cross-language sibling) — the bytes are JSON, must go\n    to the JSON ring so the consumer's `slot_pop_ordered`\n    returns `which_ring = JSON` and the spec runs json_to_native.\n\nThe signature change ripples through `push_routed`,\n`push_to_downstream`, and `push_branch` — each takes a new\n`output_native` parameter that's forwarded down. For non-CALL\nboxes (read / write / create_box / connect) the dispatch_action\ndefaults the value to 1, matching their \"writes plain bytes\"\nsemantics. CALL boxes get the value populated by `do_call_box`\nvia a new out-parameter.\n\n## Validation\n\n- The 318-lang-opaque fixture's consumer now correctly\n  reconstructs the Lua function across the JSON wire. Output\n  changes from `consumer → fn-type=nil` (silent fallback to raw\n  bytes) to `consumer → doubled=42` (function called with the\n  input value of 21).\n- All 18 integration tests pass, all unit suites still pass.\n\n## Why this isn't the per-cell native flag the 318 closeout\nsuggested\n\nThe dual-ring slot ALREADY carries per-cell flag info — the\nordering ring's `(which_ring, idx)` tuples record which ring\neach cell came from, and `slot_pop_ordered` returns\n`which_ring` directly. The actual gap was on the WRITE side:\npush_one_connection was choosing the ring based on the per-edge\nbit, which lies when the producer's per-call format is JSON.\nOnce the per-call flag reaches the push, the per-cell flag on\nthe read side is automatically correct because the cell ends up\nin the ring the producer actually wrote.\n\nSo the 318 closeout's \"needs per-cell native flag at read time\"\nwas misdiagnosed — the per-cell flag already exists; the bug\nwas that the push wasn't using the same per-call flag the\nproducer used. Fixing the push side restored the round-trip\nwithout any slot store changes.\n\n## Relevant files\n\n- `src/012-dispatch.c` — `push_one_connection`, `push_branch`,\n  `push_to_downstream`, `push_routed`, `do_call_box`,\n  `dispatch_action` all updated to thread `output_native`.\n- `tests/maps/318-lang-opaque/` — fixture's consumer now\n  asserts `doubled=42` (was `fn-type=nil`).\n- `scripts/run-tests.sh` — fixture's check_map updated to\n  include the `consumer → doubled=42` substring.\n\n## Lessons\n\n- A \"per-cell\" diagnosis covered a real symptom but not the\n  cause. The fix turned out to be one level up — at the\n  write-side ring choice. The slot store's per-cell tagging\n  was already correct; it was being told to put the cell in\n  the wrong ring.\n- Threading a value through ~5 functions to reach the right\n  decision point is sometimes the right move. The alternative\n  (thread-local global) would have worked but obscured the\n  data-flow shape of the dispatch.\n",
          "file_path":"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech/issues/completed/318a-per-call-output-format-threads-to-push.md"
        },

This adds the missing walker. After\ngraph_attach_runtime resolves every box's spec_idx, the loader\nwalks each call box's outgoing edges; for cross-language edges\nthe producer's emit mask is compared against the consumer's\nreconstruct mask. Any kind the producer might emit that the\nconsumer can't reconstruct surfaces as a stderr warning naming\nthe wire and the gap, with a pointer to issue 246's custom-\ntranslation shim as the user-side workaround.\n\nWarnings, not errors. The producer's encode walker may never\nactually hit the sentinel-emitting branch for a given run, so\nfailing graph load on a possibility that may never materialise\nwould block too many legitimate graphs. The diagnostic gives\nthe user information; behaviour stays unchanged.\n\nThe check is gated on `specs` being non-NULL (some tests load\nthe graph without a spec registry; those skip the walk). For\nnon-call boxes (read / write / create_box / connect) the check\nis skipped because they don't carry a language and don't go\nthrough native_to_json.\n\nNo existing fixture trips the warning; the unit suite for\nsentinel_validate (tests/020-sentinels-test.c) covers the gap\nmath directly.\n\nCo-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>\nEOF\n)\" 2>&1 | tail -3",

          "content":"#!/usr/bin/env luajit\n-- scripts/export-llm-transcripts.lua — local transcript exporter.\n--\n-- What it does, in one sentence: walks every Claude conversation\n-- JSONL for this project, renders each one at six verbosity levels\n-- into per-conversation markdown files, sets each file's mtime to\n-- the conversation's last-message timestamp (and atime to its\n-- first-message timestamp), and skips conversations whose source\n-- JSONL hasn't changed since the last render.\n--\n-- File naming: `<slug>-<short-id>.md` where the slug is derived\n-- from the first user message (truncated, lower-cased, hyphen-\n-- separated) and short-id is the first 8 chars of the conversation\n-- UUID. This gives human-readable filenames you can scan in `ls`\n-- without losing per-conversation uniqueness.\n--\n-- Per-level context inclusion (a small frontmatter at the top of\n-- each rendered file):\n--   v0..v2  — conversation metadata only (id, slug, timestamps)\n--   v3      — also includes the project's CLAUDE.md if present\n--   v4..v5  — also includes the global CLAUDE.md AND the project's\n--             auto-memory files (~/.claude/projects/<id>/memory/)\n--\n-- The included CLAUDE.md content is what's on disk NOW, not a\n-- historical snapshot — the JSONL doesn't carry CLAUDE.md content,\n-- and Claude Code doesn't keep per-conversation CLAUDE.md\n-- snapshots. A note in the frontmatter calls this out so a reader\n-- doesn't assume what's shown is exactly what the conversation saw.\n--\n-- Timestamp note: mtime and atime are settable post-creation;\n-- birth time (`btime` / statx) is not, so it stays as the file's\n-- actual creation moment. Most file browsers and tools key off\n-- mtime, so the last-message-timestamp anchor is the practical\n-- one. atime carries the first-message timestamp for tools that\n-- prefer \"when did this conversation start?\"\n--\n-- Replaces an earlier wrapper around an external exporter that\n-- guessed at which project's conversations to read and got it\n-- wrong for projects outside /home/ritz/programming/ai-stuff/.\n\nlocal DIR = arg and arg[1] or \"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech\"\n\n-- {{{ require dkjson via the project's libs/ path\npackage.path = DIR .. \"/libs/?.lua;\" .. package.path\nlocal json = require(\"dkjson\")\n-- }}}\n\n-- {{{ paths\nlocal function claude_project_dir()\n    local home = os.getenv(\"HOME\")\n    local encoded = DIR:gsub(\"/\", \"-\")\n    return home .. \"/.claude/projects/\" .. encoded\nend\n\nlocal SRC_DIR = claude_project_dir()\nlocal OUT_DIR = DIR .. \"/llm-transcripts\"\n-- }}}\n\n-- {{{ helpers — file IO\nlocal function read_all(path)\n    local f = io.open(path, \"rb\")\n    if not f then return nil end\n    local s = f:read(\"*a\")\n    f:close()\n    return s\nend\n\nlocal function write_all(path, content)\n    local f, err = io.open(path, \"wb\")\n    if not f then return nil, err end\n    f:write(content)\n    f:close()\n    return true\nend\n\nlocal function ensure_dir(path)\n    os.execute(\"mkdir -p '\" .. path .. \"'\")\nend\n\nlocal function file_mtime(path)\n    local f = io.popen(\"stat -c %Y '\" .. path .. \"' 2>/dev/null\")\n    if not f then return 0 end\n    local s = f:read(\"*l\")\n    f:close()\n    return tonumber(s) or 0\nend\n\nlocal function list_jsonls(dir)\n    local f = io.popen(\"ls '\" .. dir .. \"'/*.jsonl 2>/dev/null\")\n    if not f then return {} end\n    local result = {}\n    for line in f:lines() do\n        result[#result + 1] = line\n    end\n    f:close()\n    return result\nend\n\nlocal function basename_no_ext(path, ext)\n    local b = path:match(\"([^/]+)$\") or path\n    return (b:gsub(\"%.\" .. ext .. \"$\", \"\"))\nend\n-- }}}\n\n-- {{{ helpers — slugify\n-- Turn arbitrary text into a filename-safe ASCII slug. Lowercases,\n-- replaces every non-alphanumeric run with a single hyphen, trims\n-- leading/trailing hyphens, caps length so the resulting filename\n-- doesn't exceed common filesystem limits (255 chars is typical;\n-- 40 leaves room for the short-id suffix and extension).\nlocal function slugify(text, max_len)\n    if not text or text == \"\" then return \"untitled\" end\n    -- Strip ASCII control chars and replace anything non-alnum with -.\n    local s = text:lower()\n    s = s:gsub(\"[^a-z0-9]+\", \"-\")\n    s = s:gsub(\"^%-+\", \"\"):gsub(\"%-+$\", \"\")\n    if s == \"\" then return \"untitled\" end\n    if max_len and #s > max_len then\n        s = s:sub(1, max_len):gsub(\"%-+$\", \"\")\n        if s == \"\" then s = \"untitled\" end\n    end\n    return s\nend\n-- }}}\n\n-- {{{ helpers — content extraction from message entries\n-- The JSONL has heterogeneous shapes per entry type:\n--   {type=\"user\",      message={content=\"...\" OR [items]}}\n-- text=\"...\"}\n--   {type=\"tool_use\",    name=\"Bash\", input={...}}\n--   {type=\"tool_result\", content=\"...\" OR [items]}\n\nlocal function get_user_text(entry)\n    local m = entry.message or {}\n    local c = m.content\n    if type(c) == \"string\" then return c end\n    if type(c) == \"table\" then\n        local out = {}\n        for i = 1, #c do\n            local item = c[i]\n            if type(item) == \"table\" and item.type == \"text\" then\n                out[#out + 1] = item.text or \"\"\n            end\n        end\n        if #out > 0 then return table.concat(out, \"\\n\") end\n    end\n    return nil\nend\n\nlocal function get_assistant_items(entry)\n    local m = entry.message or {}\n    return type(m.content) == \"table\" and m.content or {}\nend\n\nlocal function summarise_tool_call(item)\n    local name = item.name or \"?\"\n    local input = item.input or {}\n    if name == \"Bash\" then\n        local cmd = input.command or \"\"\n        if #cmd > 120 then cmd = cmd:sub(1, 117) .. \"...\" end\n        return \"Bash: \" .. cmd\n    elseif name == \"Edit\" or name == \"Write\" or name == \"Read\" then\n        return name .. \": \" .. (input.file_path or \"?\")\n    elseif name == \"Agent\" or name == \"Skill\" then\n        return name .. \": \" .. (input.description or input.skill or \"?\")\n    elseif name == \"TaskCreate\" or name == \"TaskUpdate\" then\n        return name .. \": \" .. (input.description or input.id or \"?\")\n    end\n    return name .. \" (...)\"\nend\n\nlocal function tool_result_text(item)\n    local c = item.content\n    if type(c) == \"string\" then return c end\n    if type(c) == \"table\" then\n        local out = {}\n        for i = 1, #c do\n            local sub = c[i]\n            if type(sub) == \"table\" and sub.type == \"text\" then\n                out[#out + 1] = sub.text or \"\"\n            end\n        end\n        return table.concat(out, \"\\n\")\n    end\n    return \"\"\nend\n\nlocal function extract_code_blocks(text)\n    if not text or text == \"\" then return {} end\n    local blocks = {}\n    for code in text:gmatch(\"```[%w_-]*\\n(.-)```\") do\n        blocks[#blocks + 1] = code\n    end\n    return blocks\nend\n\nlocal function truncate_lines(text, max_lines)\n    if not text or text == \"\" then return text end\n    local count = 0\n    local cut_at = nil\n    for pos in text:gmatch(\"()\\n\") do\n        count = count + 1\n        if count == max_lines then cut_at = pos break end\n    end\n    if not cut_at then return text end\n    return text:sub(1, cut_at) ..\n           \"... [truncated; \" .. max_lines .. \"-line cap]\"\nend\n-- }}}\n\n-- {{{ helpers — auto-included context (CLAUDE.md, memory)\n-- Tiered by verbosity per the export feature spec. The content is\n-- read from disk at export time; the JSONL itself doesn't carry\n-- it, and there's no historical-snapshot mechanism, so the included\n-- content is \"current\" content and may differ from what the\n-- conversation actually saw. The frontmatter calls this out.\n\nlocal function project_claude_md()\n    return read_all(DIR .. \"/CLAUDE.md\")\nend\n\nlocal function global_claude_md()\n    return read_all(os.getenv(\"HOME\") .. \"/.claude/CLAUDE.md\")\nend\n\nlocal function project_memory_files()\n    local memdir = SRC_DIR .. \"/memory\"\n    local f = io.popen(\"ls '\" .. memdir .. \"'/*.md 2>/dev/null\")\n    if not f then return {} end\n    local files = {}\n    for line in f:lines() do\n        local content = read_all(line)\n        if content then\n            files[#files + 1] = {\n                name    = line:match(\"([^/]+)$\") or line,\n                content = content,\n            }\n        end\n    end\n    f:close()\n    return files\nend\n\nlocal function frontmatter(meta, level)\n    local out = {\n        \"<!--\",\n        \"Conversation transcript — generated by\",\n        \"scripts/export-llm-transcripts.lua.\",\n        \"\",\n        \"id          : \" .. meta.id,\n        \"slug        : \" .. meta.slug,\n        \"first prompt: \" .. (meta.first_user or \"(none)\"),\n        \"first ts    : \" .. (meta.first_ts or \"(unknown)\"),\n        \"last ts     : \" .. (meta.last_ts  or \"(unknown)\"),\n        \"entry count : \" .. meta.n_entries,\n        \"verbosity   : v\" .. level.n .. \" \" .. level.name,\n        \"-->\",\n        \"\",\n    }\n\n    -- v3+ : project CLAUDE.md (if it exists on disk now).\n    if level.n >= 3 then\n        local pcm = project_claude_md()\n        if pcm then\n            out[#out + 1] = \"## Project CLAUDE.md\\n\"\n            out[#out + 1] = \"_Content read from disk at export time; may not\"\n                         .. \" reflect exactly what the conversation saw._\\n\"\n            out[#out + 1] = \"```markdown\"\n            out[#out + 1] = pcm\n            out[#out + 1] = \"```\\n\"\n        end\n    end\n\n    -- v4+ : global CLAUDE.md AND project memory files.\n    if level.n >= 4 then\n        local gcm = global_claude_md()\n        if gcm then\n            out[#out + 1] = \"## Global CLAUDE.md (~/.claude/CLAUDE.md)\\n\"\n            out[#out + 1] = \"_Content read from disk at export time._\\n\"\n            out[#out + 1] = \"```markdown\"\n            out[#out + 1] = gcm\n            out[#out + 1] = \"```\\n\"\n        end\n        local mems = project_memory_files()\n        if #mems > 0 then\n            out[#out + 1] = \"## Project auto-memory (\"\n                         .. SRC_DIR .. \"/memory/)\\n\"\n            out[#out + 1] = \"_Snapshot at export time._\\n\"\n            for _, m in ipairs(mems) do\n                out[#out + 1] = \"### \" .. m.name .. \"\\n\"\n                out[#out + 1] = \"```markdown\"\n                out[#out + 1] = m.content\n                out[#out + 1] = \"```\\n\"\n            end\n        end\n    end\n\n    out[#out + 1] = \"---\\n\"\n    return table.concat(out, \"\\n\")\nend\n-- }}}\n\n-- {{{ render — one conversation at one verbosity level\nlocal function render_v0_minimal(entries)\n    local out = { \"# Code-only transcript\\n\" }\n    for _, e in ipairs(entries) do\n        if e.type == \"assistant\" then\n            for _, item in ipairs(get_assistant_items(e)) do\n                if item.type == \"text\" then\n                    for _, code in ipairs(extract_code_blocks(item.text or \"\")) do\n                        out[#out + 1] = \"```\"\n                        out[#out + 1] = code\n                        out[#out + 1] = \"```\\n\"\n                    end\n                end\n            end\n        end\n    end\n    return table.concat(out, \"\\n\")\nend\n\nlocal function render_v1_compact(entries)\n    local out = { \"# Compact transcript\\n\" }\n    for _, e in ipairs(entries) do\n        if e.type == \"user\" then\n            local text = get_user_text(e)\n            if text and text:match(\"%S\") then\n                out[#out + 1] = \"## User\\n\\n\" .. text .. \"\\n\"\n            end\n        elseif e.type == \"assistant\" then\n            local text_chunks = {}\n            local tools       = {}\n            for _, item in ipairs(get_assistant_items(e)) do\n                if item.type == \"text\" then\n                    text_chunks[#text_chunks + 1] = item.text or \"\"\n                elseif item.type == \"tool_use\" then\n                    tools[#tools + 1] = summarise_tool_call(item)\n                end\n            end\n            if #text_chunks > 0 or #tools > 0 then\n                out[#out + 1] = \"## Assistant\\n\"\n                if #text_chunks > 0 then\n                    out[#out + 1] = table.concat(text_chunks, \"\\n\") .. \"\\n\"\n                end\n                if #tools > 0 then\n                    out[#out + 1] = \"_Tools:_\\n\"\n                    for _, t in ipairs(tools) do\n                        out[#out + 1] = \"- `\" .. t .. \"`\"\n                    end\n                    out[#out + 1] = \"\"\n                end\n            end\n        end\n    end\n    return table.concat(out, \"\\n\")\nend\n\nlocal function render_with_tool_results(entries, result_max_lines)\n    local out = { \"# Transcript\\n\" }\n    for _, e in ipairs(entries) do\n        if e.type == \"user\" then\n            local m = e.message or {}\n            local c = m.content\n            if type(c) == \"string\" then\n                out[#out + 1] = \"## User\\n\\n\" .. c .. \"\\n\"\n            elseif type(c) == \"table\" then\n                local tool_results = {}\n                local text_items   = {}\n                for _, item in ipairs(c) do\n                    if type(item) == \"table\" then\n                        if item.type == \"text\" then\n                            text_items[#text_items + 1] = item.text or \"\"\n                        elseif item.type == \"tool_result\" then\n                            tool_results[#tool_results + 1] = item\n                        end\n                    end\n                end\n                if #text_items > 0 then\n                    out[#out + 1] = \"## User\\n\\n\" ..\n                                    table.concat(text_items, \"\\n\") .. \"\\n\"\n                end\n                for _, tr in ipairs(tool_results) do\n                    local txt = tool_result_text(tr)\n                    if result_max_lines and result_max_lines > 0 then\n                        txt = truncate_lines(txt, result_max_lines)\n                    end\n                    out[#out + 1] = \"### Tool result\\n\\n```\\n\" ..\n                                    (txt or \"\") .. \"\\n```\\n\"\n                end\n            end\n        elseif e.type == \"assistant\" then\n            local text_chunks = {}\n            local tools       = {}\n            for _, item in ipairs(get_assistant_items(e)) do\n                if item.type == \"text\" then\n                    text_chunks[#text_chunks + 1] = item.text or \"\"\n                elseif item.type == \"tool_use\" then\n                    tools[#tools + 1] = summarise_tool_call(item)\n                end\n            end\n            if #text_chunks > 0 or #tools > 0 then\n                out[#out > 0 then\n                    out[#out + 1] = \"_Tools:_\\n\"\n                    for _, t in ipairs(tools) do\n                        out[#out + 1] = \"- `\" .. t .. \"`\"\n                    end\n                    out[#out + 1] = \"\"\n                end\n            end\n        end\n    end\n    return table.concat(out, \"\\n\")\nend\n\nlocal function render_v2_standard(entries) return render_with_tool_results(entries, 200) end\nlocal function render_v3_verbose(entries)  return render_with_tool_results(entries, 0)   end\n\nlocal function render_v4_complete(entries)\n    local out = { \"# Complete transcript with metadata\\n\" }\n    for i, e in ipairs(entries) do\n        local t = e.type or \"?\"\n        out[#out + 1] = \"### [\" .. i .. \"] type=\" .. t\n        if e.timestamp then out[#out + 1] = \"ts: \" .. tostring(e.timestamp) end\n        if t == \"user\" then\n            local txt = get_user_text(e)\n            if txt then out[#out + 1] = \"\\n\" .. txt .. \"\\n\" end\n            local m = e.message or {}\n            if type(m.content) == \"table\" then\n                for _, item in ipairs(m.content) do\n                    if type(item) == \"table\" and item.type == \"tool_result\" then\n                        out[#out + 1] = \"\\n_tool_result:_\\n```\\n\" ..\n                                        (tool_result_text(item) or \"\") .. \"\\n```\\n\"\n                    end\n                end\n            end\n        elseif t == \"assistant\" then\n            for _, item in ipairs(get_assistant_items(e)) do\n                if item.type == \"text\" then\n                    out[#out + 1] = \"\\n\" .. (item.text or \"\") .. \"\\n\"\n                elseif item.type == \"tool_use\" then\n                    out[#out + 1] = \"\\n_tool_use:_ `\" ..\n                                    summarise_tool_call(item) .. \"`\"\n                    if item.input then\n                        out[#out + 1] = \"input:\\n```json\\n\" ..\n                                        json.encode(item.input, {indent=true}) ..\n                                        \"\\n```\\n\"\n                    end\n                end\n            end\n        end\n        out[#out + 1] = \"\"\n    end\n    return table.concat(out, \"\\n\")\nend\n\nlocal function render_v5_raw(entries)\n    local out = { \"# Raw conversation entries\\n\" }\n    for i, e in ipairs(entries) do\n        out[#out + 1] = \"## [\" .. i .. \"]\\n\"\n        out[#out + 1] = \"```json\"\n        out[#out + 1] = json.encode(e, {indent = true})\n        out[#out + 1] = \"```\\n\"\n    end\n    return table.concat(out, \"\\n\")\nend\n\nlocal LEVELS = {\n    { n = 0, name = \"minimal\",  render = render_v0_minimal  },\n    { n = 1, name = \"compact\",  render = render_v1_compact  },\n    { n = 2, name = \"standard\", render = render_v2_standard },\n    { n = 3, name = \"verbose\",  render = render_v3_verbose  },\n    { n = 4, name = \"complete\", render = render_v4_complete },\n    { n = 5, name = \"raw\",      render = render_v5_raw      },\n}\n-- }}}\n\n-- {{{ parse one JSONL file → (entries, meta)\n-- meta carries: id, slug, first_user (text), first_ts, last_ts,\n-- n_entries. Used both for the filename slug and the per-file\n-- frontmatter rendering.\nlocal function parse_jsonl(path, conv_id)\n    local entries = {}\n    local first_user = nil\n    local first_ts   = nil\n    local last_ts    = nil\n\n    local f = io.open(path, \"rb\")\n    if not f then\n        return entries, { id = conv_id, slug = \"unreadable\" }\n    end\n    for line in f:lines() do\n        if line ~= \"\" then\n            local ok, dec = pcall(json.decode, line)\n            if ok and type(dec) == \"table\" then\n                entries[#entries + 1] = dec\n                if dec.timestamp then\n                    if not first_ts then first_ts = dec.timestamp end\n                    last_ts = dec.timestamp\n                end\n                if (not first_user) and dec.type == \"user\" then\n                    local t = get_user_text(dec)\n                    if t and t:match(\"%S\") then\n                        first_user = t\n                    end\n                end\n            end\n        end\n    end\n    f:close()\n\n    local slug = slugify(first_user or \"untitled\", 40)\n    return entries, {\n        id          = conv_id,\n        short_id    = conv_id:sub(1, 8),\n        slug        = slug,\n        first_user  = first_user,\n        first_ts    = first_ts,\n        last_ts     = last_ts,\n        n_entries   = #entries,\n    }\nend\n-- }}}\n\n-- {{{ set_times — anchor atime / mtime to conversation timestamps\n-- Uses `touch -d <iso>` which accepts ISO 8601. atime = first\n-- message timestamp; mtime = last message timestamp. btime is\n-- not settable post-creation by standard tools; documented in\n-- the file-level comment.\nlocal function set_times(path, first_ts, last_ts)\n    if last_ts then\n        os.execute(string.format(\n            \"touch -m -d '%s' '%s' 2>/dev/null\", last_ts, path))\n    end\n    if first_ts then\n        os.execute(string.format(\n            \"touch -a -d '%s' '%s' 2>/dev/null\", first_ts, path))\n    end\nend\n-- }}}\n\n-- {{{ main\nlocal function main()\n    if not SRC_DIR or SRC_DIR == \"\" then\n        io.stderr:write(\"error: could not compute claude project dir\\n\")\n        os.exit(1)\n    end\n    ensure_dir(OUT_DIR)\n\n    local jsonls = list_jsonls(SRC_DIR)\n    if #jsonls == 0 then\n        io.stderr:write(\"No JSONL conversations found at \" ..     "content":"#!/usr/bin/env luajit\n-- scripts/export-llm-transcripts.lua — local transcript exporter.\n--\n-- What it does, in one sentence: walks every Claude conversation\n-- JSONL for this project, renders each one at six verbosity levels\n-- into per-conversation markdown files, sets each file's mtime to\n-- the conversation's last-message timestamp (and atime to its\n-- first-message timestamp), and skips conversations whose source\n-- JSONL hasn't changed since the last render.\n--\n-- File naming: `<slug>-<short-id>.md` where the slug is derived\n-- from the first user message (truncated, lower-cased, hyphen-\n-- separated) and short-id is the first 8 chars of the conversation\n-- UUID. This gives human-readable filenames you can scan in `ls`\n-- without losing per-conversation uniqueness.\n--\n-- Per-level context inclusion (a small frontmatter at the top of\n-- each rendered file):\n--   v0..v2  — conversation metadata only (id, slug, timestamps)\n--   v3      — also includes the project's CLAUDE.md if present\n--   v4..v5  — also includes the global CLAUDE.md AND the project's\n--             auto-memory files (~/.claude/projects/<id>/memory/)\n--\n-- The included CLAUDE.md content is what's on disk NOW, not a\n-- historical snapshot — the JSONL doesn't carry CLAUDE.md content,\n-- and Claude Code doesn't keep per-conversation CLAUDE.md\n-- snapshots. A note in the frontmatter calls this out so a reader\n-- doesn't assume what's shown is exactly what the conversation saw.\n--\n-- Timestamp note: mtime and atime are settable post-creation;\n-- birth time (`btime` / statx) is not, so it stays as the file's\n-- actual creation moment. Most file browsers and tools key off\n-- mtime, so the last-message-timestamp anchor is the practical\n-- one. atime carries the first-message timestamp for tools that\n-- prefer \"when did this conversation start?\"\n--\n-- Replaces an earlier wrapper around an external exporter that\n-- guessed at which project's conversations to read and got it\n-- wrong for projects outside /home/ritz/programming/ai-stuff/.\n\nlocal DIR = arg and arg[1] or \"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech\"\n\n-- {{{ require dkjson via the project's libs/ path\npackage.path = DIR .. \"/libs/?.lua;\" .. package.path\nlocal json = require(\"dkjson\")\n-- }}}\n\n-- {{{ paths\nlocal function claude_project_dir()\n    local home = os.getenv(\"HOME\")\n    local encoded = DIR:gsub(\"/\", \"-\")\n    return home .. \"/.claude/projects/\" .. encoded\nend\n\nlocal SRC_DIR = claude_project_dir()\nlocal OUT_DIR = DIR .. \"/llm-transcripts\"\n-- }}}\n\n-- {{{ helpers — file IO\nlocal function read_all(path)\n    local f = io.open(path, \"rb\")\n    if not f then return nil end\n    local s = f:read(\"*a\")\n    f:close()\n    return s\nend\n\nlocal function write_all(path, content)\n    local f, err = io.open(path, \"wb\")\n    if not f then return nil, err end\n    f:write(content)\n    f:close()\n    return true\nend\n\nlocal function ensure_dir(path)\n    os.execute(\"mkdir -p '\" .. path .. \"'\")\nend\n\nlocal function file_mtime(path)\n    local f = io.popen(\"stat -c %Y '\" .. path .. \"' 2>/dev/null\")\n    if not f then return 0 end\n    local s = f:read(\"*l\")\n So we can't\n-- use the output's own mtime for the skip check. Instead, a single\n-- state file at OUT_DIR/.export-state records the source mtime at\n-- the moment of last successful render per conversation; the skip\n-- check compares the live source mtime against that record.\nlocal STATE_PATH = OUT_DIR .. \"/.export-state\"\n\nlocal function load_state()\n    local s = read_all(STATE_PATH)\n    local state = {}\n    if not s then return state end\n    for line in s:gmatch(\"[^\\n]+\") do\n        local id, ts = line:match(\"^([^=]+)=(%d+)$\")\n        if id and ts then state[id] = tonumber(ts) end\n    end\n    return state\nend\n\nlocal function save_state(state)\n    local rows = {}\n    for id, ts in pairs(state) do\n        rows[#rows + 1] = id .. \"=\" .. tostring(ts)\n    end\n    table.sort(rows)\n    write_all(STATE_PATH, table.concat(rows, \"\\n\") .. \"\\n\")\nend\n-- }}}\n\n-- {{{ main\nlocal function main()",

File browsers and\nsort-by-mtime tools surface \"when this conversation last had\nactivity,\" not \"when the file was rendered.\" Birth time isn't\nsettable post-creation by standard tools and stays as the actual\nfile-create moment — documented in the script's header.\n\n(2) Filenames switch from <conv-id>.md to <slug>-<short-id>.md,\nwhere the slug is the first user message slugified (lowercased,\nnon-alnum collapsed to hyphens, capped at 40 chars) and short-id\nis the first 8 chars of the conversation UUID. Examples:\n  hi-can-we-do-306-and-307-5670858b.md\n  hi-can-you-initialize-a-project-here-the-2029ad16.md\nThe slug is the closest thing to a \"summarized name\" we can derive\nfrom the JSONL — there's no built-in title/summary field anywhere\nin the conversation data, including ~/.claude/sessions/ and\nhistory.jsonl. First-user-message text is the best signal.\n\n(3) Per-level CLAUDE.md and memory inclusion in the frontmatter:\n  v0..v2 — conversation metadata only\n  v3     — also project CLAUDE.md (DIR/CLAUDE.md if exists)\n  v4..v5 — also global CLAUDE.md (~/.claude/CLAUDE.md) AND project\n           auto-memory files (~/.claude/projects/<id>/memory/)\nThe included content is read at export time, not from a per-\nconversation historical snapshot — Claude Code doesn't keep one,\nand the JSONL doesn't carry CLAUDE.md content. A note in the\nfrontmatter calls this out so readers don't assume what's shown\nis exactly what the conversation actually saw.\n\nIncremental check rewrite: the output's own mtime can no longer\nserve (it's deliberately anchored to the conversation's last\nmessage). Replaced with a small state file at\nllm-transcripts/.export-state — one line per conversation,\nstoring the source JSONL mtime at the moment of the last\nsuccessful render. Second-run skip works cleanly: 0 rendered,\n15 skipped after the first export.\n\nOld per-conversation files named <conv-id>.md are renamed to the\nnew slug-prefixed names (git detects the renames and preserves\nhistory). The May-8 leftover bundles at the top of llm-transcripts/\n(2029ad16-*-v0.md and friends) were already absent on disk; they\nget deleted from the index here.\n\nCo-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>\nEOF\n)\" 2>&1 | tail -5",
          "description":"Commit exporter v2"

{
  "uuid":"a15b49e7-1873-43d8-afbd-24f74a4972cd",

  "toolUseResult":{
    "originalFile":"/* tests/maps/319e-c-create/src/trigger.c — C box that spawns a\n * downstream Lua box at runtime, mirroring the 319d Lua fixture\n * but driven from a C box function instead. Proves the C bindings\n * for runtime self-construction (issue 319e) work end-to-end.\n *\n * The trigger box receives one input (\"input\"), uses\n * soramech_create_box to mint a new Lua box, uses soramech_connect\n * to wire its own output to the new box's \"x\" input, and returns\n * a marker string. The runtime then pushes the marker through the\n * freshly-added connection and the dynamically-created Lua box\n * fires.\n */\n#include <stdio.h>\n#include <stdlib.h>\n#include <string.h>\n\n#include \"soramech.h\"\n\n/* {{{ trigger */\nint trigger(const void **inputs, const int *sizes, int n,\n            void *out_buf, int out_capacity, int *out_size)\n{\n    if (n < 1) return -1;\n\n    /* Build the spec for a new Lua box. The shape mirrors what\n     * would be on disk at boxes/<id>.json. */\n    const char *spec =\n        \"{\"\n          \"\\\"kind\\\":\\\"call\\\",\"\n          \"\\\"lang\\\":\\\"c\\\",\"\n          \"\\\"ref\\\":\\\"src/echo_dyn.c\\\",\"\n          \"\\\"fn\\\":\\\"echo\\\",\"\n          \"\\\"inputs\\\":[\"\n            \"{\\\"name\\\":\\\"x\\\",\\\"type\\\":\\\"string\\\"}\"\n          \"]\"\n        \"}\";\n\n    char  new_id[SORAMECH_BOX_ID_BUF_SIZE];\n    char *err = NULL;\n    if (soramech_create_box(spec, (int)strlen(spec),\n                            new_id, sizeof new_id, &err) != 0) {\n        fprintf(stderr, \"trigger.c: create_box failed: %s\\n\",\n                err ? err : \"(no message)\");\n        free(err);\n        return -1;\n    }\n\n    /* Build the connection entry: wire trigger.output → new.x */\n    char conn[256];\n    int  n_conn = snprintf(conn, sizeof conn,\n        \"{\\\"from_box\\\":\\\"trigger\\\",\"\n         \"\\\"from_branch\\\":null,\"\n         \"\\\"to_box\\\":\\\"%s\\\",\"\n         \"\\\"to_input\\\":\\\"x\\\"}\", new_id);\n    if (n_conn < 0 || n_conn >= (int)sizeof conn) return -1;\n\n    if (soramech_connect(conn, n_conn, &err) != 0) {\n        fprintf(stderr, \"trigger.c: connect failed: %s\\n\",\n                err ? err : \"(no message)\");\n        free(err);\n        return -1;\n    }\n\n    /* Output a marker so the test runner can verify both that\n     * trigger ran AND what the new id was. */\n    int marker_n = snprintf((char *)out_buf, (size_t)out_capacity,\n                            \"c-trigger-fired:%s:%.*s\",\n                            new_id, sizes[0], (const char *)inputs[0]);\n    if (marker_n < 0 || marker_n >= out_capacity) return -1;\n    *out_size = marker_n;\n    return 0;\n}\n/* }}} */\n",
    "userModified":false,
    "replaceAll":false,
    "structuredPatch":[{

{

    "originalFile":"#!/bin/bash\n# scripts/run-tests.sh — phase 3 integration tests.\n#\n# Runs every fixture map under tests/maps/ through `soramech-pool`\n# and asserts that the captured outputs match a hardcoded\n# expectation per map. The point is to catch regressions\n# end-to-end — past the spec interface, past the dispatch action,\n# past JSONL writing — rather than via the in-process unit tests.\n#\n# Per the project convention: scripts run from any directory via a\n# hard-coded ${DIR} path with an override argument; all paths are\n# relative to ${DIR}.\n\nset -u\n\nDIR=\"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech\"\nif [[ $# -ge 1 ]]; then\n    DIR=\"$1\"\nfi\n\ncd \"$DIR\"\n\npass=0\nfail=0\nfailures=()\n\n# {{{ check_map() — run one fixture, verify expected substrings\ncheck_map() {\n    local map=\"$1\"\n    shift\n    local expected=(\"$@\")\n\n    printf \"  %-44s \" \"$map\"\n\n    local output\n    # Per-map env opt-in: a map may set SORAMECH_TEST_WORKERS to\n    # pin worker count for tests that depend on per-worker state\n    # (e.g. issue 318's $lang_opaque, which lives in the producer's\n    # Lua registry and can only be reconstructed by a consumer on\n    # the same worker).\n    local workers_env=\"\"\n    if [[ -f \"$DIR/tests/maps/$map/.test_workers\" ]]; then\n        workers_env=$(cat \"$DIR/tests/maps/$map/.test_workers\")\n    fi\n    if [[ -n \"$workers_env\" ]]; then\n        output=$(SORAMECH_WORKERS=\"$workers_env\" \"$DIR/soramech-pool\" \"$DIR/tests/maps/$map\" 2>&1)\n    else\n        output=$(\"$DIR/soramech-pool\" \"$DIR/tests/maps/$map\" 2>&1)\n    fi\n    local rc=$?\n\n    local missing=\"\"\n    if [[ $rc -ne 0 ]]; then\n        missing=\"exit=$rc\"\n    fi\n    for e in \"${expected[@]}\"; do\n        if [[ \"$output\" != *\"$e\"* ]]; then\n            missing+=\"${missing:+; }missing '$e'\"\n        fi\n    done\n\n    if [[ -z \"$missing\" ]]; then\n        printf \"ok\\n\"\n        pass=$((pass + 1))\n    else\n        printf \"FAIL — %s\\n\" \"$missing\"\n        fail=$((fail + 1))\n        failures+=(\"$map: $missing\")\n    fi\n}\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ pipeline_output_check() — additional: the pipeline writes to disk\npipeline_output_check() {\n    local file=\"/tmp/soramech-pipeline-out.txt\"\n    rm -f \"$file\"\n    \"$DIR/soramech-pool\" \"$DIR/tests/maps/pipeline\" > /dev/null 2>&1\n    printf \"  %-44s \" \"pipeline write output\"\n    if [[ -f \"$file\" ]]; then\n        local content\n        content=$(cat \"$file\")\n        if [[ \"$content\" == \"11!\" ]]; then\n            printf \"ok\\n\"\n            pass=$((pass + 1))\n        else\n            printf \"FAIL — expected '11!', got '%s'\\n\" \"$content\"\n            fail=$((fail + 1))\n            failures+=(\"pipeline file: $content\")\n        fi\n    else\n        printf \"FAIL — output file missing\\n\"\n        fail=$((fail + 1))\n        failures+=(\"pipeline: $file missing\")\n    fi\n}\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ compile_pipeline_check() — soramech-compile produces a portable artifact\n# Verifies issue 309's compile pipeline: bundles all spec.so + sources\n# into compiled/, then runs the artifact from /tmp (i.e. with no\n# dependency on the project's cwd) and verifies it produces the same\n# output as the source map.\ncompile_pipeline_check() {\n    local map=\"$DIR/tests/maps/pipeline\"\n    local compiled=\"$map/compiled\"\n    local file=\"/tmp/soramech-pipeline-out.txt\"\n\n    printf \"  %-44s \" \"compile pipeline (portable run)\"\n\n    rm -rf \"$compiled\"\n    if ! \"$DIR/scripts/soramech-compile.sh\" \"$map\" --dir \"$DIR\" >/dev/null 2>&1; then\n        printf \"FAIL — soramech-compile failed\\n\"\n        fail=$((fail + 1))\n        failures+=(\"compile: script returned non-zero\")\n        return\n    fi\n    if [[ ! -x \"$compiled/pool-runner\" ]]; then\n        printf \"FAIL — compiled/pool-runner missing or not executable\\n\"\n        fail=$((fail + 1))\n        failures+=(\"compile: pool-runner missing\")\n        return\n    fi\n\n    rm -f \"$file\"\n    local output\n    output=$(cd /tmp && \"$compiled/pool-runner\" \"$compiled\" 2>&1)\n\n    local content=\"\"\n    [[ -f \"$file\" ]] && content=$(cat \"$file\")\n\n    if [[ \"$output\" == *\"addone → 11\"* ]] && [[ \"$content\" == \"11!\" ]]; then\n        printf \"ok\\n\"\n        pass=$((pass + 1))\n    else\n        printf \"FAIL — output='%s' file='%s'\\n\" \"$output\" \"$content\"\n        fail=$((fail + 1))\n        failures+=(\"compile: bad output\")\n    fi\n}\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ run all fixtures\necho \"integration tests (fixture maps):\"\n\ncheck_map \"calc\" \\\n    \"add → 42\"\n\ncheck_map \"hello\" \\\n    \"greet → Hello, World!\"\n\ncheck_map \"comparator\" \\\n    \"classify → 8\" \\\n    \"high → HIGH:8\" \\\n    \"low → (no output)\" \\\n    \"mid → (no output)\"\n\ncheck_map \"iter-route\" \\\n    \"iter → hi\" \\\n    \"a → A:hi\" \\\n    \"b → (no output)\" \\\n    \"c → (no output)\"\n\ncheck_map \"pipeline\" \\\n    \"double → 10\" \\\n    \"addone → 11\" \\\n    \"shout → 11!\"\n\ncheck_map \"read-literal\" \\\n    \"echo → hello, world!\"\n\ncheck_map \"319a-many-inputs\" \\\n    \"combine → count=20 sum=210\"\n\ncheck_map \"319d-runtime-create\" \\\n    \"trigger → trigger-fired:auto_\" \\\n    \"auto_\" \\\n    \"echo_dyn-received:trigger-fired:auto_\"\n\ncheck_map \"319e-c-create\" \\\n    \"trigger → c-trigger-fired:auto_\" \\\n    \"c-echo-received:c-trigger-fired:auto_\"\n\ncheck_map \"246-c-shim\" \\\n    \"echo → seen:HELLO-FROM-SEED\"\n\ncheck_map \"246-lua-shim\" \\\n    \"echo → seen:REV-fedcba\"\n\n# Issue 318 — the producer's output proves the emit side works\n# end-to-end (Lua function → $lang_opaque sentinel in JSON). The\n# consumer's reconstruction needs the dual-ring slot to surface\n# \"I was written as JSON\" to the same-language consumer, which is\n# a deeper per-edge classification issue documented in 318's\n# closeout; the emit fixture stands today.\ncheck_map \"318-lang-opaque\" \\\n    '\"$lang_opaque\"' \\\n    '\"lang\":\"lua\"' \\\n    '\"shape\":\"function\"' \\\n    'consumer → doubled=42'\n\n# Language-agnostic create_box / connect box kinds (319\n# design-correction follow-on). A read box emits a box spec; a\n# create_box-kind box consumes it; the new box's id is captured\n# downstream. No per-language wrapper involved — same shape works\n# for Lua, C, and Bash producers.\ncheck_map \"319-box-kind-create\" \\\n    \"creator → auto_\"\n\npipeline_output_check\ncompile_pipeline_check\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ parser_tests() — issue 232: unit tests for langs/<lang>/parser.js\n# Run Node's built-in test runner over each per-language parser test\n# file and fold the result into the surrounding pass/fail counters.\n# Each .mjs file is one logical \"test\" from this script's perspective;\n# Node prints its own subtest breakdown on failure for the diagnostic.\nparser_tests() {\n    if ! command -v node >/dev/null 2>&1; then\n        printf \"  %-44s SKIP — node not installed\\n\" \"parser tests (lua, bash)\"\n        return\n    fi\n    for tf in \"$DIR/tests/232-lua-parser-test.mjs\" \\\n              \"$DIR/tests/233-bash-parser-test.mjs\" \\\n              \"$DIR/tests/234-language-spec-js-test.mjs\"; do\n        local label\n        label=$(basename \"$tf\")\n        printf \"  %-44s \" \"$label\"\n        local out\n        out=$(SORAMECH_DIR=\"$DIR\" node --test \"$tf\" 2>&1)\n        local rc=$?\n        if [[ $rc -eq 0 ]]; then\n            printf \"ok\\n\"\n            pass=$((pass + 1))\n        else\n            printf \"FAIL\\n\"\n            echo \"$out\" | sed 's/^/      /'\n            fail=$((fail + 1))\n            failures+=(\"$label: node --test exit=$rc\")\n        fi\n    done\n}\nparser_tests\n# }}}\n\necho\necho \"  $pass passed, $fail failed\"\n\nif [[ $fail -gt 0 ]]; then\n    echo\n    echo \"  failures:\"\n    for f in \"${failures[@]}\"; do\n        echo \"    - $f\"\n    done\nfi\n\nexit $fail\n",

        "type":"text",
        "text":"## What shipped in this stretch\n\n| Commit | What |\n|--------|------|\n| `a24fba4` | **Exporter v2** — time-anchored mtime/atime, slug-prefixed filenames, tiered CLAUDE.md+memory inclusion (v3 / v4+), state-file based incremental |\n| `cd7cc54` | **Box-delete shim warning + lazy spec init** — inspector prompts on delete when ports have shims; dispatch lazy-inits per-worker spec handles for runtime-introduced languages (cross-lang `create_box` now works) |\n\n**19 integration tests pass.**\n\n`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`\nThe exporter v2 had a subtle bug worth flagging: anchoring mtime to last-message-ts broke the existing incremental check because the output's mtime equalled the source's mtime (or even fell behind, when the source was touched after its last timestamped entry). The fix needed a state file — a small artifact whose only job is to remember \"source's mtime at my last successful render,\" decoupled from any user-visible mtime semantics. Two different time concepts (display vs. dependency-tracking) needed two different storage locations.\n\nThe lazy spec init is interesting because it inverts the original filter's premise. The filter says \"don't init what you won't use\"; lazy init says \"init when you actually need it, even if that's later.\" The two together — eager init for static, lazy init for dynamic — give the best of both worlds without forcing one model on every case.\n`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`\n\n## Remaining pile\n\n- **#3** `$function_pointer` wrapper-binary subsystem — biggest, multi-session\n- **#8** Refcount-driven `$ref` release\n- **#10** Growable dispatch arrays\n- **Bash translate callback** (246)\n\nWant to keep going, or pause?"

          "old_string":"/* {{{ $ref bytes store (process-wide, leak-per-run)\n *\n * `sentinel_ref_alloc` copies `bytes` into a process-wide pool and\n * returns a chunk pointer that the producer embeds in its sentinel.\n * The consumer's `sentinel_ref_lookup` returns the same byte\n * pointer.\n *\n * Slice-1 lifetime model: bytes live until process exit (or until\n * `sentinel_ref_store_clear()` is called by the test harness).\n * Proper refcount-driven release tied to consumer reads is a\n * follow-on — the issue documents the lifetime concern but the\n * simpler shape unblocks end-to-end testing today. */\nuintptr_t        sentinel_ref_alloc (const void *bytes, int len);\nconst void      *sentinel_ref_lookup(uintptr_t chunk_ptr, int *out_len);\nvoid             sentinel_ref_store_clear(void);\n/* }}} */",
          "replace_all":false,
          "new_string":"/* {{{ $ref bytes store (process-wide, refcounted)\n *\n * `sentinel_ref_alloc` copies `bytes` into a process-wide pool and\n * returns a chunk pointer that the producer embeds in its sentinel.\n * Each allocation starts with refcount = 1 (the producer's own\n * reference); the chunk's bytes stay alive until the refcount\n * reaches 0.\n *\n * Lifetime protocol:\n *   - Producer: `alloc` → refcount=1; emit the sentinel; when the\n *     producer knows the value will no longer be referenced, call\n *     `dec` to release the initial reference. For dispatch-driven\n *     fan-out, the producer can `inc` once per consumer if it\n *     knows the fan-out count, then dec its own ref; or it can\n *     hold the initial ref until end-of-run and call\n *     `sentinel_ref_store_clear` for bulk teardown.\n *   - Consumer: `lookup` returns the bytes without changing\n *     refcount. A consumer that wants to release a transferred\n *     ref calls `dec`.\n *\n * `sentinel_ref_lookup` is read-only — it does not touch the\n * refcount. The refcount machinery is opt-in: callers that don't\n * use inc/dec get the old leak-per-run behaviour with a single\n * `sentinel_ref_store_clear` at end of run, exactly as before.\n *\n * Slot reuse: when a chunk's refcount hits 0 its bytes are freed\n * and its slot in the internal table becomes available for the\n * next `alloc`. Long-running processes that allocate many $refs\n * over time stay bounded in memory provided the producer calls\n * `dec` on chunks it no longer needs. */\nuintptr_t        sentinel_ref_alloc (const void *bytes, int len);\nconst void      *sentinel_ref_lookup(uintptr_t chunk_ptr, int *out_len);\nvoid             sentinel_ref_inc   (uintptr_t chunk_ptr);\nvoid             sentinel_ref_dec   (uintptr_t chunk_ptr);\nvoid             sentinel_ref_store_clear(void);\n/* }}} */",

The consumer's spec\n * detects sentinels in the parsed JSON tree and reconstructs the\n * value using language-specific machinery. Wires whose producer\n * may emit a sentinel kind the consumer can't reconstruct surface\n * at compile time as a wire-validation warning.\n *\n * This header exposes:\n *  - the sentinel kind enum + capability bitmask\n *  - JSON shape detection (parse a node, return the kind)\n *  - JSON shape writers (emit canonical bytes for each kind)\n *  - a process-wide $ref bytes store (allocate, lookup, release)\n *  - capability validation helpers used by the compile-time wire\n *    walker\n *\n * Designed and amended in issue 318. Sliced down for one-shot\n * implementation: $lang_opaque and $ref are functional end-to-end\n * for intra-language and in-process cases; $function_pointer is\n * parsed and rejected with a clear \"wrapper-binary system not yet\n * implemented\" error until the amendment's design lands.\n */\n#ifndef SORAMECH_020_SENTINELS_H\n#define SORAMECH_020_SENTINELS_H\n\n#include <stddef.h>\n#include <stdint.h>\n\n#include \"json.h\"\n\n/* {{{ Sentinel kinds and capability bitmask */\ntypedef enum {\n    SENTINEL_NONE             = 0,\n    SENTINEL_REF              = 1,\n    SENTINEL_LANG_OPAQUE      = 2,\n    SENTINEL_FUNCTION_POINTER = 3,\n} sentinel_kind_t;\n\n/* Capability bits combined into a per-spec mask. A spec's\n * `sentinel_emit_mask` says which kinds its native_to_json may\n * produce; its `sentinel_reconstruct_mask` says which kinds its\n * json_to_native can rebuild. */\n#define SENTINEL_BIT(K)            (1u << (unsigned)(K))\n#define SENTINEL_MASK_REF          SENTINEL_BIT(SENTINEL_REF)\n#define SENTINEL_MASK_LANG_OPAQUE  SENTINEL_BIT(SENTINEL_LANG_OPAQUE)\n#define SENTINEL_MASK_FN_POINTER   SENTINEL_BIT(SENTINEL_FUNCTION_POINTER)\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Detection — parse-side\n *\n * Returns the sentinel kind for a JSON object that has exactly one\n * top-level key matching a sentinel name, or SENTINEL_NONE for\n * anything else (including arrays / scalars / multi-key objects). */\nsentinel_kind_t sentinel_detect(const json_node_t *node);\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Emission — write-side helpers\n *\n * Each writer emits the canonical bytes for the kind. The producing\n * spec calls these from inside its encode walker; the writer leaves\n * the cursor where any surrounding context expects it. */\nvoid sentinel_write_ref         (json_writer_t *w,\n                                 uintptr_t chunk_ptr, int len);\nvoid sentinel_write_lang_opaque (json_writer_t *w,\n                                 const char *lang, uint64_t tag,\n                                 const char *shape);\n\n/* The function-pointer shape lands when the amendment's wrapper-\n * binary system is implemented. Until then this writer emits a\n * sentinel that will refuse to reconstruct, with a self-describing\n * stub payload that future fixture data can be migrated from. */\nvoid sentinel_write_function_pointer_stub(json_writer_t *w,\n                                          const char *signature);\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ $ref bytes store (process-wide, leak-per-run)\n *\n * `sentinel_ref_alloc` copies `bytes` into a process-wide pool and\n * returns a chunk pointer that the producer embeds in its sentinel.\n * The consumer's `sentinel_ref_lookup` returns the same byte\n * pointer.\n *\n * Slice-1 lifetime model: bytes live until process exit (or until\n * `sentinel_ref_store_clear()` is called by the test harness).\n * Proper refcount-driven release tied to consumer reads is a\n * follow-on — the issue documents the lifetime concern but the\n * simpler shape unblocks end-to-end testing today. */\nuintptr_t        sentinel_ref_alloc (const void *bytes, int len);\nconst void      *sentinel_ref_lookup(uintptr_t chunk_ptr, int *out_len);\nvoid             sentinel_ref_store_clear(void);\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Capability validation\n *\n * Returns 0 if every emit bit set on `producer_mask` also appears\n * in `consumer_mask`; returns the offending bit (>0) if any kind\n * the producer may emit is unreconstructable by the consumer. The\n * compile-time wire walker uses this to surface mismatches. */\nunsigned int sentinel_validate(unsigned int producer_mask,\n                               unsigned int consumer_mask);\n\n/* Human-readable name of a sentinel kind for diagnostics. */\nconst char *sentinel_kind_name(sentinel_kind_t k);\n/* }}} */\n\n#endif /* SORAMECH_020_SENTINELS_H */\n",

    "newString":"/* {{{ $ref bytes store (process-wide, refcounted)\n *\n * `sentinel_ref_alloc` copies `bytes` into a process-wide pool and\n * returns a chunk pointer that the producer embeds in its sentinel.\n * Each allocation starts with refcount = 1 (the producer's own\n * reference); the chunk's bytes stay alive until the refcount\n * reaches 0.\n *\n * Lifetime protocol:\n *   - Producer: `alloc` → refcount=1; emit the sentinel; when the\n *     producer knows the value will no longer be referenced, call\n *     `dec` to release the initial reference. For dispatch-driven\n *     fan-out, the producer can `inc` once per consumer if it\n *     knows the fan-out count, then dec its own ref; or it can\n *     hold the initial ref until end-of-run and call\n *     `sentinel_ref_store_clear` for bulk teardown.\n *   - Consumer: `lookup` returns the bytes without changing\n *     refcount. A consumer that wants to release a transferred\n *     ref calls `dec`.\n *\n * `sentinel_ref_lookup` is read-only — it does not touch the\n * refcount. The refcount machinery is opt-in: callers that don't\n * use inc/dec get the old leak-per-run behaviour with a single\n * `sentinel_ref_store_clear` at end of run, exactly as before.\n *\n * Slot reuse: when a chunk's refcount hits 0 its bytes are freed\n * and its slot in the internal table becomes available for the\n * next `alloc`. Long-running processes that allocate many $refs\n * over time stay bounded in memory provided the producer calls\n * `dec` on chunks it no longer needs. */\nuintptr_t        sentinel_ref_alloc (const void *bytes, int len);\nconst void      *sentinel_ref_lookup(uintptr_t chunk_ptr, int *out_len);\nvoid             sentinel_ref_inc   (uintptr_t chunk_ptr);\nvoid             sentinel_ref_dec   (uintptr_t chunk_ptr);\nvoid             sentinel_ref_store_clear(void);\n/* }}} */"
  },
