          "old_string":"/* {{{ $ref bytes store\n *\n * Process-wide hash-less append-only table. We don't need fast\n * lookup; producers and consumers reference chunks by raw pointer,\n * which IS the lookup key. Keeping a table at all lets us\n * (a) own the lifetime explicitly and (b) bulk-free at run end\n * via sentinel_ref_store_clear so memory doesn't leak across\n * fresh invocations of the runner in long-lived tests.\n *\n * Concurrency: single mutex guards both append and clear. The\n * lookup path returns a stable pointer (the chunks themselves\n * never move) so reads outside the mutex are safe. */\ntypedef struct ref_entry {\n    void  *bytes;\n    int    len;\n} ref_entry_t;\n\nstatic ref_entry_t  *ref_table;\nstatic int           ref_count;\nstatic int           ref_capacity;\nstatic pthread_mutex_t ref_mu = PTHREAD_MUTEX_INITIALIZER;\n\nuintptr_t sentinel_ref_alloc(const void *bytes, int len)\n{\n    if (len < 0) return 0;\n    void *copy = malloc((size_t)len);\n    if (!copy && len > 0) return 0;\n    if (len > 0) memcpy(copy, bytes, (size_t)len);\n\n    pthread_mutex_lock(&ref_mu);\n    if (ref_count == ref_capacity) {\n        int new_cap = ref_capacity == 0 ? 16 : ref_capacity * 2;\n        ref_entry_t *grown = realloc(ref_table,\n                                     (size_t)new_cap * sizeof *ref_table);\n        if (!grown) { pthread_mutex_unlock(&ref_mu); free(copy); return 0; }\n        ref_table    = grown;\n        ref_capacity = new_cap;\n    }\n    ref_table[ref_count].bytes = copy;\n    ref_table[ref_count].len   = len;\n    ref_count++;\n    pthread_mutex_unlock(&ref_mu);\n    return (uintptr_t)copy;\n}\n\nconst void *sentinel_ref_lookup(uintptr_t chunk_ptr, int *out_len)\n{\n    pthread_mutex_lock(&ref_mu);\n    for (int i = 0; i < ref_count; i++) {\n        if ((uintptr_t)ref_table[i].bytes == chunk_ptr) {\n            if (out_len) *out_len = ref_table[i].len;\n            pthread_mutex_unlock(&ref_mu);\n            return ref_table[i].bytes;\n        }\n    }\n    pthread_mutex_unlock(&ref_mu);\n    if (out_len) *out_len = 0;\n    return NULL;\n}\n\nvoid sentinel_ref_store_clear(void)\n{\n    pthread_mutex_lock(&ref_mu);\n    for (int i = 0; i < ref_count; i++) free(ref_table[i].bytes);\n    free(ref_table);\n    ref_table    = NULL;\n    ref_count    = 0;\n    ref_capacity = 0;\n    pthread_mutex_unlock(&ref_mu);\n}\n/* }}} */",
          "replace_all":false,
          "new_string":"/* {{{ $ref bytes store\n *\n * Process-wide table of malloc'd byte chunks, each with an atomic\n * refcount. `alloc` starts a chunk at refcount=1; `inc`/`dec` bump\n * the count; when `dec` brings it to 0 the bytes are freed and\n * the table slot is marked reusable (bytes = NULL). Subsequent\n * `alloc` scans for a free slot before extending the table, so a\n * long-running process that allocates many $refs over time stays\n * bounded in memory (provided callers `dec` chunks they no longer\n * need).\n *\n * Concurrency: a single mutex guards table mutation (alloc / dec\n * / clear); the refcount itself is atomic so `inc` can run\n * lock-free in the common case. `lookup` takes the mutex briefly\n * to find the matching entry; the returned byte pointer is stable\n * (the bytes themselves never move) so reads outside the mutex\n * are safe. */\ntypedef struct ref_entry {\n    void          *bytes;     /* malloc'd; NULL when slot is free */\n    int            len;\n    _Atomic int    refcount;  /* 0 means free */\n} ref_entry_t;\n\nstatic ref_entry_t    *ref_table;\nstatic int             ref_count;\nstatic int             ref_capacity;\nstatic pthread_mutex_t ref_mu = PTHREAD_MUTEX_INITIALIZER;\n\nuintptr_t sentinel_ref_alloc(const void *bytes, int len)\n{\n    if (len < 0) return 0;\n    void *copy = malloc((size_t)len);\n    if (!copy && len > 0) return 0;\n    if (len > 0) memcpy(copy, bytes, (size_t)len);\n\n    pthread_mutex_lock(&ref_mu);\n\n    /* Scan for a reusable slot first — a chunk that was previously\n     * freed by sentinel_ref_dec leaves bytes=NULL but the slot\n     * itself stays in the table. Reusing keeps the table bounded\n     * under churn. */\n    int idx = -1;\n    for (int i = 0; i < ref_count; i++) {\n        if (ref_table[i].bytes == NULL) { idx = i; break; }\n    }\n\n    if (idx < 0) {\n        if (ref_count == ref_capacity) {\n            int new_cap = ref_capacity == 0 ? 16 : ref_capacity * 2;\n            ref_entry_t *grown = realloc(ref_table,\n                                         (size_t)new_cap * sizeof *ref_table);\n            if (!grown) { pthread_mutex_unlock(&ref_mu); free(copy); return 0; }\n            ref_table    = grown;\n            ref_capacity = new_cap;\n        }\n        idx = ref_count++;\n    }\n\n    ref_table[idx].bytes = copy;\n    ref_table[idx].len   = len;\n    atomic_init(&ref_table[idx].refcount, 1);\n\n    pthread_mutex_unlock(&ref_mu);\n    return (uintptr_t)copy;\n}\n\nconst void *sentinel_ref_lookup(uintptr_t chunk_ptr, int *out_len)\n{\n    pthread_mutex_lock(&ref_mu);\n    for (int i = 0; i < ref_count; i++) {\n        if (ref_table[i].bytes &&\n            (uintptr_t)ref_table[i].bytes == chunk_ptr) {\n            if (out_len) *out_len = ref_table[i].len;\n            void *b = ref_table[i].bytes;\n            pthread_mutex_unlock(&ref_mu);\n            return b;\n        }\n    }\n    pthread_mutex_unlock(&ref_mu);\n    if (out_len) *out_len = 0;\n    return NULL;\n}\n\nvoid sentinel_ref_inc(uintptr_t chunk_ptr)\n{\n    pthread_mutex_lock(&ref_mu);\n    for (int i = 0; i < ref_count; i++) {\n        if (ref_table[i].bytes &&\n            (uintptr_t)ref_table[i].bytes == chunk_ptr) {\n            atomic_fetch_add_explicit(&ref_table[i].refcount, 1,\n                                      memory_order_relaxed);\n            break;\n        }\n    }\n    pthread_mutex_unlock(&ref_mu);\n}\n\nvoid sentinel_ref_dec(uintptr_t chunk_ptr)\n{\n    pthread_mutex_lock(&ref_mu);\n    for (int i = 0; i < ref_count; i++) {\n        if (ref_table[i].bytes &&\n            (uintptr_t)ref_table[i].bytes == chunk_ptr) {\n            int prev = atomic_fetch_sub_explicit(&ref_table[i].refcount, 1,\n                                                 memory_order_acq_rel);\n            if (prev <= 1) {\n                free(ref_table[i].bytes);\n                ref_table[i].bytes = NULL;\n                ref_table[i].len   = 0;\n                /* refcount stays at 0; next alloc reuses this slot. */\n            }\n            break;\n        }\n    }\n    pthread_mutex_unlock(&ref_mu);\n}\n\nvoid sentinel_ref_store_clear(void)\n{\n    pthread_mutex_lock(&ref_mu);\n    for (int i = 0; i < ref_count; i++) {\n        if (ref_table[i].bytes) free(ref_table[i].bytes);\n    }\n    free(ref_table);\n    ref_table    = NULL;\n    ref_count    = 0;\n    ref_capacity = 0;\n    pthread_mutex_unlock(&ref_mu);\n}\n/* }}} */",

    "originalFile":"/* src/020-sentinels.c — sentinel primitives implementation.\n *\n * Three sentinel kinds, three responsibilities each (detect, emit,\n * for two of them also reconstruct via the per-spec json_to_native\n * path). This file is the spec-independent machinery; per-spec\n * emission and reconstruction lives in each language's spec.c.\n *\n * Slice-1 scope (issue 318): $lang_opaque and $ref are end-to-end\n * for intra-language and in-process cases respectively;\n * $function_pointer is parsed and rejected pending the amendment's\n * wrapper-binary subsystem.\n */\n#include \"020-sentinels.h\"\n#include \"json.h\"\n\n#include <pthread.h>\n#include <stdio.h>\n#include <stdlib.h>\n#include <string.h>\n\n/* {{{ sentinel_detect()\n *\n * Single-key match against the three reserved key names. We accept\n * any value type for the sentinel's payload — checking the inner\n * shape is the reconstructor's job, not the detector's. */\nsentinel_kind_t sentinel_detect(const json_node_t *node)\n{\n    if (!node) return SENTINEL_NONE;\n    json_node_t *n = (json_node_t *)node;\n    if (json_kind(n) != JSON_OBJECT) return SENTINEL_NONE;\n    if (json_object_size(n) != 1) return SENTINEL_NONE;\n    const char *key = json_object_key(n, 0);\n    if (!key) return SENTINEL_NONE;\n    if (strcmp(key, \"$ref\") == 0)              return SENTINEL_REF;\n    if (strcmp(key, \"$lang_opaque\") == 0)      return SENTINEL_LANG_OPAQUE;\n    if (strcmp(key, \"$function_pointer\") == 0) return SENTINEL_FUNCTION_POINTER;\n    return SENTINEL_NONE;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Emission writers */\nvoid sentinel_write_ref(json_writer_t *w, uintptr_t chunk_ptr, int len)\n{\n    /* The pointer is rendered as hex inside a JSON string so it\n     * survives JSON-string-canonicalisation regardless of platform\n     * pointer width. Decoders parse via strtoull. */\n    char ptr_buf[32];\n    snprintf(ptr_buf, sizeof ptr_buf, \"0x%lx\", (unsigned long)chunk_ptr);\n    json_writer_object(w);\n      json_writer_key(w, \"$ref\");\n      json_writer_object(w);\n        json_writer_key   (w, \"chunk_ptr\"); json_writer_string(w, ptr_buf);\n        json_writer_key   (w, \"len\");       json_writer_int   (w, len);\n      json_writer_end(w);\n    json_writer_end(w);\n}\n\nvoid sentinel_write_lang_opaque(json_writer_t *w,\n                                const char *lang, uint64_t tag,\n                                const char *shape)\n{\n    json_writer_object(w);\n      json_writer_key(w, \"$lang_opaque\");\n      json_writer_object(w);\n        json_writer_key (w, \"lang\"); json_writer_string(w, lang ? lang : \"\");\n        json_writer_key (w, \"tag\");  json_writer_int   (w, (long long)tag);\n        if (shape && *shape) {\n            json_writer_key(w, \"shape\"); json_writer_string(w, shape);\n        }\n      json_writer_end(w);\n    json_writer_end(w);\n}\n\nvoid sentinel_write_function_pointer_stub(json_writer_t *w,\n                                          const char *signature)\n{\n    /* Per the amendment: the wrapper-binary subsystem hasn't landed,\n     * so this writer emits a self-describing stub that the\n     * consumer's json_to_native is expected to reject with a clear\n     * \"not yet implemented\" message. Keeping the shape stable lets\n     * future wrapper-binary work migrate fixture data without\n     * rewriting the producer side. */\n    json_writer_object(w);\n      json_writer_key(w, \"$function_pointer\");\n      json_writer_object(w);\n        json_writer_key(w, \"signature\");\n        json_writer_string(w, signature ? signature : \"void(void)\");\n        json_writer_key(w, \"status\");\n        json_writer_string(w, \"wrapper-binary system not yet implemented\");\n      json_writer_end(w);\n    json_writer_end(w);\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ $ref bytes store\n *\n * Process-wide hash-less append-only table. We don't need fast\n * lookup; producers and consumers reference chunks by raw pointer,\n * which IS the lookup key. Keeping a table at all lets us\n * (a) own the lifetime explicitly and (b) bulk-free at run end\n * via sentinel_ref_store_clear so memory doesn't leak across\n * fresh invocations of the runner in long-lived tests.\n *\n * Concurrency: single mutex guards both append and clear. The\n * lookup path returns a stable pointer (the chunks themselves\n * never move) so reads outside the mutex are safe. */\ntypedef struct ref_entry {\n    void  *bytes;\n    int    len;\n} ref_entry_t;\n\nstatic ref_entry_t  *ref_table;\nstatic int           ref_count;\nstatic int           ref_capacity;\nstatic pthread_mutex_t ref_mu = PTHREAD_MUTEX_INITIALIZER;\n\nuintptr_t sentinel_ref_alloc(const void *bytes, int len)\n{\n    if (len < 0) return 0;\n    void *copy = malloc((size_t)len);\n    if (!copy && len > 0) return 0;\n    if (len > 0) memcpy(copy, bytes, (size_t)len);\n\n    pthread_mutex_lock(&ref_mu);\n    if (ref_count == ref_capacity) {\n        int new_cap = ref_capacity == 0 ? 16 : ref_capacity * 2;\n        ref_entry_t *grown = realloc(ref_table,\n                                     (size_t)new_cap * sizeof *ref_table);\n        if (!grown) { pthread_mutex_unlock(&ref_mu); free(copy); return 0; }\n        ref_table    = grown;\n        ref_capacity = new_cap;\n    }\n    ref_table[ref_count].bytes = copy;\n    ref_table[ref_count].len   = len;\n    ref_count++;\n    pthread_mutex_unlock(&ref_mu);\n    return (uintptr_t)copy;\n}\n\nconst void *sentinel_ref_lookup(uintptr_t chunk_ptr, int *out_len)\n{\n    pthread_mutex_lock(&ref_mu);\n    for (int i = 0; i < ref_count; i++) {\n        if ((uintptr_t)ref_table[i].bytes == chunk_ptr) {\n            if (out_len) *out_len = ref_table[i].len;\n            pthread_mutex_unlock(&ref_mu);\n            return ref_table[i].bytes;\n        }\n    }\n    pthread_mutex_unlock(&ref_mu);\n    if (out_len) *out_len = 0;\n    return NULL;\n}\n\nvoid sentinel_ref_store_clear(void)\n{\n    pthread_mutex_lock(&ref_mu);\n    for (int i = 0; i < ref_count; i++) free(ref_table[i].bytes);\n    free(ref_table);\n    ref_table    = NULL;\n    ref_count    = 0;\n    ref_capacity = 0;\n    pthread_mutex_unlock(&ref_mu);\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Capability validation */\nunsigned int sentinel_validate(unsigned int producer_mask,\n                               unsigned int consumer_mask)\n{\n    unsigned int gap = producer_mask & ~consumer_mask;\n    if (gap == 0) return 0;\n    /* Return the lowest-numbered offending bit so callers can name\n     * one specific kind in their diagnostic. */\n    for (unsigned int b = 1; b != 0; b <<= 1) {\n        if (gap & b) return b;\n    }\n    return gap;   /* unreachable in practice */\n}\n\nconst char *sentinel_kind_name(sentinel_kind_t k)\n{\n    switch (k) {\n        case SENTINEL_NONE:             return \"(none)\";\n        case SENTINEL_REF:              return \"$ref\";\n        case SENTINEL_LANG_OPAQUE:      return \"$lang_opaque\";\n        case SENTINEL_FUNCTION_POINTER: return \"$function_pointer\";\n        default:                        return \"(unknown)\";\n    }\n}\n/* }}} */\n",

    "oldString":"/* {{{ $ref bytes store\n *\n * Process-wide hash-less append-only table. We don't need fast\n * lookup; producers and consumers reference chunks by raw pointer,\n * which IS the lookup key. Keeping a table at all lets us\n * (a) own the lifetime explicitly and (b) bulk-free at run end\n * via sentinel_ref_store_clear so memory doesn't leak across\n * fresh invocations of the runner in long-lived tests.\n *\n * Concurrency: single mutex guards both append and clear. The\n * lookup path returns a stable pointer (the chunks themselves\n * never move) so reads outside the mutex are safe. */\ntypedef struct ref_entry {\n    void  *bytes;\n    int    len;\n} ref_entry_t;\n\nstatic ref_entry_t  *ref_table;\nstatic int           ref_count;\nstatic int           ref_capacity;\nstatic pthread_mutex_t ref_mu = PTHREAD_MUTEX_INITIALIZER;\n\nuintptr_t sentinel_ref_alloc(const void *bytes, int len)\n{\n    if (len < 0) return 0;\n    void *copy = malloc((size_t)len);\n    if (!copy && len > 0) return 0;\n    if (len > 0) memcpy(copy, bytes, (size_t)len);\n\n    pthread_mutex_lock(&ref_mu);\n    if (ref_count == ref_capacity) {\n        int new_cap = ref_capacity == 0 ? 16 : ref_capacity * 2;\n        ref_entry_t *grown = realloc(ref_table,\n                                     (size_t)new_cap * sizeof *ref_table);\n        if (!grown) { pthread_mutex_unlock(&ref_mu); free(copy); return 0; }\n        ref_table    = grown;\n        ref_capacity = new_cap;\n    }\n    ref_table[ref_count].bytes = copy;\n    ref_table[ref_count].len   = len;\n    ref_count++;\n    pthread_mutex_unlock(&ref_mu);\n    return (uintptr_t)copy;\n}\n\nconst void *sentinel_ref_lookup(uintptr_t chunk_ptr, int *out_len)\n{\n    pthread_mutex_lock(&ref_mu);\n    for (int i = 0; i < ref_count; i++) {\n        if ((uintptr_t)ref_table[i].bytes == chunk_ptr) {\n            if (out_len) *out_len = ref_table[i].len;\n            pthread_mutex_unlock(&ref_mu);\n            return ref_table[i].bytes;\n        }\n    }\n    pthread_mutex_unlock(&ref_mu);\n    if (out_len) *out_len = 0;\n    return NULL;\n}\n\nvoid sentinel_ref_store_clear(void)\n{\n    pthread_mutex_lock(&ref_mu);\n    for (int i = 0; i < ref_count; i++) free(ref_table[i].bytes);\n    free(ref_table);\n    ref_table    = NULL;\n    ref_count    = 0;\n    ref_capacity = 0;\n    pthread_mutex_unlock(&ref_mu);\n}\n/* }}} */",
    "newString":"/* {{{ $ref bytes store\n *\n * Process-wide table of malloc'd byte chunks, each with an atomic\n * refcount. `alloc` starts a chunk at refcount=1; `inc`/`dec` bump\n * the count; when `dec` brings it to 0 the bytes are freed and\n * the table slot is marked reusable (bytes = NULL). Subsequent\n * `alloc` scans for a free slot before extending the table, so a\n * long-running process that allocates many $refs over time stays\n * bounded in memory (provided callers `dec` chunks they no longer\n * need).\n *\n * Concurrency: a single mutex guards table mutation (alloc / dec\n * / clear); the refcount itself is atomic so `inc` can run\n * lock-free in the common case. `lookup` takes the mutex briefly\n * to find the matching entry; the returned byte pointer is stable\n * (the bytes themselves never move) so reads outside the mutex\n * are safe. */\ntypedef struct ref_entry {\n    void          *bytes;     /* malloc'd; NULL when slot is free */\n    int            len;\n    _Atomic int    refcount;  /* 0 means free */\n} ref_entry_t;\n\nstatic ref_entry_t    *ref_table;\nstatic int             ref_count;\nstatic int             ref_capacity;\nstatic pthread_mutex_t ref_mu = PTHREAD_MUTEX_INITIALIZER;\n\nuintptr_t sentinel_ref_alloc(const void *bytes, int len)\n{\n    if (len < 0) return 0;\n    void *copy = malloc((size_t)len);\n    if (!copy && len > 0) return 0;\n    if (len > 0) memcpy(copy, bytes, (size_t)len);\n\n    pthread_mutex_lock(&ref_mu);\n\n    /* Scan for a reusable slot first — a chunk that was previously\n     * freed by sentinel_ref_dec leaves bytes=NULL but the slot\n     * itself stays in the table. Reusing keeps the table bounded\n     * under churn. */\n    int idx = -1;\n    for (int i = 0; i < ref_count; i++) {\n        if (ref_table[i].bytes == NULL) { idx = i; break; }\n    }\n\n    if (idx < 0) {\n        if (ref_count == ref_capacity) {\n            int new_cap = ref_capacity == 0 ? 16 : ref_capacity * 2;\n            ref_entry_t *grown = realloc(ref_table,\n                                         (size_t)new_cap * sizeof *ref_table);\n            if (!grown) { pthread_mutex_unlock(&ref_mu); free(copy); return 0; }\n            ref_table    = grown;\n            ref_capacity = new_cap;\n        }\n        idx = ref_count++;\n    }\n\n    ref_table[idx].bytes = copy;\n    ref_table[idx].len   = len;\n    atomic_init(&ref_table[idx].refcount, 1);\n\n    pthread_mutex_unlock(&ref_mu);\n    return (uintptr_t)copy;\n}\n\nconst void *sentinel_ref_lookup(uintptr_t chunk_ptr, int *out_len)\n{\n    pthread_mutex_lock(&ref_mu);\n    for (int i = 0; i < ref_count; i++) {\n        if (ref_table[i].bytes &&\n            (uintptr_t)ref_table[i].bytes == chunk_ptr) {\n            if (out_len) *out_len = ref_table[i].len;\n            void *b = ref_table[i].bytes;\n            pthread_mutex_unlock(&ref_mu);\n            return b;\n        }\n    }\n    pthread_mutex_unlock(&ref_mu);\n    if (out_len) *out_len = 0;\n    return NULL;\n}\n\nvoid sentinel_ref_inc(uintptr_t chunk_ptr)\n{\n    pthread_mutex_lock(&ref_mu);\n    for (int i = 0; i < ref_count; i++) {\n        if (ref_table[i].bytes &&\n            (uintptr_t)ref_table[i].bytes == chunk_ptr) {\n            atomic_fetch_add_explicit(&ref_table[i].refcount, 1,\n                                      memory_order_relaxed);\n            break;\n        }\n    }\n    pthread_mutex_unlock(&ref_mu);\n}\n\nvoid sentinel_ref_dec(uintptr_t chunk_ptr)\n{\n    pthread_mutex_lock(&ref_mu);\n    for (int i = 0; i < ref_count; i++) {\n        if (ref_table[i].bytes &&\n            (uintptr_t)ref_table[i].bytes == chunk_ptr) {\n            int prev = atomic_fetch_sub_explicit(&ref_table[i].refcount, 1,\n                                                 memory_order_acq_rel);\n            if (prev <= 1) {\n                free(ref_table[i].bytes);\n                ref_table[i].bytes = NULL;\n                ref_table[i].len   = 0;\n                /* refcount stays at 0; next alloc reuses this slot. */\n            }\n            break;\n        }\n    }\n    pthread_mutex_unlock(&ref_mu);\n}\n\nvoid sentinel_ref_store_clear(void)\n{\n    pthread_mutex_lock(&ref_mu);\n    for (int i = 0; i < ref_count; i++) {\n        if (ref_table[i].bytes) free(ref_table[i].bytes);\n    }\n    free(ref_table);\n    ref_table    = NULL;\n    ref_count    = 0;\n    ref_capacity = 0;\n    pthread_mutex_unlock(&ref_mu);\n}\n/* }}} */"

    "newString":"/* {{{ $ref store round-trip */\nstatic int test_ref_store(void)\n{\n    sentinel_ref_store_clear();\n    const char *payload = \"0123456789ABCDEF\";\n    int len = (int)strlen(payload);\n    uintptr_t p = sentinel_ref_alloc(payload, len);\n    ASSERT(p != 0);\n    int got_len = 0;\n    const void *got = sentinel_ref_lookup(p, &got_len);\n    ASSERT(got != NULL);\n    ASSERT(got_len == len);\n    ASSERT(memcmp(got, payload, (size_t)len) == 0);\n\n    /* Lookup with a wrong pointer returns NULL. */\n    int dummy = 0;\n    ASSERT(sentinel_ref_lookup(p + 1, &dummy) == NULL);\n\n    sentinel_ref_store_clear();\n    /* After clear, the pointer is no longer valid (and may be freed\n     * memory — we only assert lookup miss, not dereferencing). */\n    ASSERT(sentinel_ref_lookup(p, &dummy) == NULL);\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ $ref refcount: dec to zero frees the chunk */\nstatic int test_ref_refcount_dec(void)\n{\n    sentinel_ref_store_clear();\n    uintptr_t p = sentinel_ref_alloc(\"hello\", 5);\n    ASSERT(p != 0);\n    int len = 0;\n    ASSERT(sentinel_ref_lookup(p, &len) != NULL);\n    ASSERT(len == 5);\n\n    /* Initial refcount is 1. Two decs leaves it at 1; chunk\n     * still present. Third dec brings it to 0; chunk freed. */\n    sentinel_ref_inc(p);\n    sentinel_ref_inc(p);\n    sentinel_ref_dec(p);\n    sentinel_ref_dec(p);\n    int len = 0;\n    ASSERT(sentinel_ref_lookup(p, &len) != NULL);\n    ASSERT(len == 8);\n\n    sentinel_ref_dec(p);\n    ASSERT(sentinel_ref_lookup(p, &len) == NULL);\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ $ref slot reuse — a freed slot is reused by the next alloc */\nstatic int test_ref_slot_reuse(void)\n{\n    sentinel_ref_store_clear();\n    uintptr_t p1 = sentinel_ref_alloc(\"aaa\", 3);\n    uintptr_t p2 = sentinel_ref_alloc(\"bbb\", 3);\n    ASSERT(p1 != 0 && p2 != 0 && p1 != p2);\n\n    /* Free p1.     "originalFile":"/* tests/020-sentinels-test.c — unit tests for src/020-sentinels.\n *\n * Covers the spec-independent sentinel machinery:\n *  - kind detection on parsed JSON\n *  - emit writers produce parseable JSON whose round-trip detects\n *    as the expected kind\n *  - $ref store: alloc / lookup / clear\n *  - capability validation: gap detection across emit / reconstruct\n *    masks\n */\n#include \"020-sentinels.h\"\n#include \"json.h\"\n\n#include <stdio.h>\n#include <stdlib.h>\n#include <string.h>\n\n/* {{{ Tiny test harness */\n#define ASSERT(cond) do { \\\n    if (!(cond)) { \\\n        printf(\"FAIL %s:%d  %s\\n\", __FILE__, __LINE__, #cond); \\\n        return 0; \\\n    } \\\n} while (0)\n\nstatic int tests_run = 0, tests_passed = 0;\n#define RUN(name) do { \\\n    tests_run++; \\\n    printf(\"  %-44s \", #name); \\\n    fflush(stdout); \\\n    if (test_##name()) { \\\n        printf(\"ok\\n\"); \\\n        tests_passed++; \\\n    } \\\n} while (0)\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ detect_round_trip — emit then re-detect */\nstatic int test_detect_round_trip_ref(void)\n{\n    char buf[256];\n    json_writer_t w;\n    json_writer_init(&w, buf, sizeof buf);\n    sentinel_write_ref(&w, 0xCAFEBABE, 1024);\n    int n = json_writer_finish(&w);\n    ASSERT(n > 0);\n\n    json_arena_t *a = json_arena_create();\n    int eo;    ASSERT(p3 != 0);\n    ASSERT(sentinel_ref_lookup(p3, &len) != NULL);\n    ASSERT(len == 3);\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Capability validation */\nstatic int test_validate(void)\n{\n    /* No emission → no gap. */\n    ASSERT(sentinel_validate(0, 0) == 0);\n\n    /* Identical capabilities → no gap. */\n    ASSERT(sentinel_validate(\n        SENTINEL_MASK_REF | SENTINEL_MASK_LANG_OPAQUE,\n        SENTINEL_MASK_REF | SENTINEL_MASK_LANG_OPAQUE) == 0);\n\n    /* Consumer covers producer's emit set → no gap. */\n    ASSERT(sentinel_validate(\n test_kind_names(void)\n{\n    ASSERT(strcmp(sentinel_kind_name(SENTINEL_NONE),             \"(none)\") == 0);\n    ASSERT(strcmp(sentinel_kind_name(SENTINEL_REF),              \"$ref\") == 0);\n    ASSERT(strcmp(sentinel_kind_name(SENTINEL_LANG_OPAQUE),      \"$lang_opaque\") == 0);\n    ASSERT(strcmp(sentinel_kind_name(SENTINEL_FUNCTION_POINTER), \"$function_pointer\") == 0);\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\nint main(void)\n{\n    printf(\"020-sentinels-test:\\n\");\n    RUN(detect_round_trip_ref);\n    RUN(detect_round_trip_lang_opaque);\n     "originalFile":"/* src/020-sentinels.c — sentinel primitives implementation.\n *\n * Three sentinel kinds, three responsibilities each (detect, emit,\n * for two of them also reconstruct via the per-spec json_to_native\n * path). This file is the spec-independent machinery; per-spec\n * emission and reconstruction lives in each language's spec.c.\n *\n * Slice-1 scope (issue 318): $lang_opaque and $ref are end-to-end\n * for intra-language and in-process cases respectively;\n * $function_pointer is parsed and rejected pending the amendment's\n * wrapper-binary subsystem.\n */\n#include \"020-sentinels.h\"\n#include \"json.h\"\n\n#include <pthread.h>\n#include <stdio.h>\n#include <stdlib.h>\n#include <string.h>\n\n/* {{{ sentinel_detect()\n *\n * Single-key match against the three reserved key names. We accept\n * any value type for the sentinel's payload — checking the inner\n * shape is the reconstructor's job, not the detector's. */\nsentinel_kind_t sentinel_detect(const json_node_t *node)\n{\n    if (!node) return SENTINEL_NONE;\n    json_node_t *n = (json_node_t *)node;\n    if (json_kind(n) != JSON_OBJECT) return SENTINEL_NONE;\n    if (json_object_size(n) != 1) return SENTINEL_NONE;\n    const char *key = json_object_key(n, 0);\n    if (!key) return SENTINEL_NONE;\n    if (strcmp(key, \"$ref\") == 0)              return SENTINEL_REF;\n    if (strcmp(key, \"$lang_opaque\") == 0)      return SENTINEL_LANG_OPAQUE;\n    if (strcmp(key, \"$function_pointer\") == 0) return SENTINEL_FUNCTION_POINTER;\n    return SENTINEL_NONE;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Emission writers */\nvoid sentinel_write_ref(json_writer_t *w, uintptr_t chunk_ptr, int len)\n{\n    /* The pointer is rendered as hex inside a JSON string so it\n     * survives JSON-string-canonicalisation regardless of platform\n     * pointer width. Decoders parse via strtoull. */\n    char ptr_buf[32];\n    snprintf(ptr_buf, sizeof ptr_buf, \"0x%lx\", (unsigned long)chunk_ptr);\n    json_writer_object(w);\n      json_writer_key(w, \"$ref\");\n      json_writer_object(w);\n        json_writer_key   (w, \"chunk_ptr\"); json_writer_string(w, ptr_buf);\n        json_writer_key   (w, \"len\");       json_writer_int   (w, len);\n      json_writer_end(w);\n    json_writer_end(w);\n}\n\nvoid sentinel_write_lang_opaque(json_writer_t *w,\n                                const char *lang, uint64_t tag,\n                                const char *shape)\n{\n    json_writer_object(w);\n      json_writer_key(w, \"$lang_opaque\");\n      json_writer_object(w);\n        json_writer_key (w, \"lang\"); json_writer_string(w, lang ? lang : \"\");\n        json_writer_key (w, \"tag\");  json_writer_int   (w, (long long)tag);\n        if (shape && *shape) {\n            json_writer_key(w, \"shape\"); json_writer_string(w, shape);\n        }\n      json_writer_end(w);\n    json_writer_end(w);\n}\n\nvoid sentinel_write_function_pointer_stub(json_writer_t *w,\n                                          const char *signature)\n{\n    /* Per the amendment: the wrapper-binary subsystem hasn't landed,\n     * so this writer emits a self-describing stub that the\n     * consumer's json_to_native is expected to reject with a clear\n     * \"not yet implemented\" message. Keeping the shape stable lets\n     * future wrapper-binary work migrate fixture data without\n     * rewriting the producer side. */\n    json_writer_object(w);\n      json_writer_key(w, \"$function_pointer\");\n      json_writer_object(w);\n        json_writer_key(w, \"signature\");\n        json_writer_string(w, signature ? signature : \"void(void)\");\n        json_writer_key(w, \"status\");\n        json_writer_string(w, \"wrapper-binary system not yet implemented\");\n      json_writer_end(w);\n    json_writer_end(w);\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ $ref bytes store\n *\n * Process-wide table of malloc'd byte chunks, each with an atomic\n * refcount. `alloc` starts a chunk at refcount=1; `inc`/`dec` bump\n * the count; when `dec` brings it to 0 the bytes are freed and\n * the table slot is marked reusable (bytes = NULL). Subsequent\n * `alloc` scans for a free slot before extending the table, so a\n * long-running process that allocates many $refs over time stays\n * bounded in memory (provided callers `dec` chunks they no longer\n * need).\n *\n * Concurrency: a single mutex guards table mutation (alloc / dec\n * / clear); the refcount itself is atomic so `inc` can run\n * lock-free in the common case. `lookup` takes the mutex briefly\n * to find the matching entry; the returned byte pointer is stable\n * (the bytes themselves never move) so reads outside the mutex\n * are safe. */\ntypedef struct ref_entry {\n    void          *bytes;     /* malloc'd; NULL when slot is free */\n    int            len;\n    _Atomic int    refcount;  /* 0 means free */\n} ref_entry_t;\n\nstatic ref_entry_t    *ref_table;\nstatic int             ref_count;\nstatic int             ref_capacity;\nstatic pthread_mutex_t ref_mu = PTHREAD_MUTEX_INITIALIZER;\n\nuintptr_t sentinel_ref_alloc(const void *bytes, int len)\n{\n    if (len < 0) return 0;\n    void *copy = malloc((size_t)len);\n    if (!copy && len > 0) return 0;\n    if (len > 0) memcpy(copy, bytes, (size_t)len);\n\n    pthread_mutex_lock(&ref_mu);\n\n    /* Scan for a reusable slot first — a chunk that was previously\n     * freed by sentinel_ref_dec leaves bytes=NULL but the slot\n     * itself stays in the table. Reusing keeps the table bounded\n     * under churn. */\n    int idx = -1;\n    for (int i = 0; i < ref_count; i++) {\n        if (ref_table[i].bytes == NULL) { idx = i; break; }\n    }\n\n    if (idx < 0) {\n        if (ref_count == ref_capacity) {\n            int new_cap = ref_capacity == 0 ? 16 : ref_capacity * 2;\n            ref_entry_t *grown = realloc(ref_table,\n                                         (size_t)new_cap * sizeof *ref_table);\n            if (!grown) { pthread_mutex_unlock(&ref_mu); free(copy); return 0; }\n            ref_table    = grown;\n            ref_capacity = new_cap;\n        }\n        idx = ref_count++;\n    }\n\n    ref_table[idx].bytes = copy;\n    ref_table[idx].len   = len;\n    atomic_init(&ref_table[idx].refcount, 1);\n\n    pthread_mutex_unlock(&ref_mu);\n    return (uintptr_t)copy;\n}\n\nconst void *sentinel_ref_lookup(uintptr_t chunk_ptr, int *out_len)\n{\n    pthread_mutex_lock(&ref_mu);\n    for (int i = 0; i < ref_count; i++) {\n        if (ref_table[i].bytes &&\n            (uintptr_t)ref_table[i].bytes == chunk_ptr) {\n            if (out_len) *out_len = ref_table[i].len;\n            void *b = ref_table[i].bytes;\n            pthread_mutex_unlock(&ref_mu);\n            return b;\n        }\n    }\n    pthread_mutex_unlock(&ref_mu);\n    if (out_len) *out_len = 0;\n    return NULL;\n}\n\nvoid sentinel_ref_inc(uintptr_t chunk_ptr)\n{\n    pthread_mutex_lock(&ref_mu);\n    for (int i = 0; i < ref_count; i++) {\n        if (ref_table[i].bytes &&\n            (uintptr_t)ref_table[i].bytes == chunk_ptr) {\n            atomic_fetch_add_explicit(&ref_table[i].refcount, 1,\n                                      memory_order_relaxed);\n            break;\n        }\n    }\n    pthread_mutex_unlock(&ref_mu);\n}\n\nvoid sentinel_ref_dec(uintptr_t chunk_ptr)\n{\n    pthread_mutex_lock(&ref_mu);\n    for (int i = 0; i < ref_count; i++) {\n        if (ref_table[i].bytes &&\n            (uintptr_t)ref_table[i].bytes == chunk_ptr) {\n            int prev = atomic_fetch_sub_explicit(&ref_table[i].refcount, 1,\n                                                 memory_order_acq_rel);\n            if (prev <= 1) {\n                free(ref_table[i].bytes);\n                ref_table[i].bytes = NULL;\n                ref_table[i].len   = 0;\n                /* refcount stays at 0; next alloc reuses this slot. */\n            }\n            break;\n        }\n    }\n    pthread_mutex_unlock(&ref_mu);\n}\n\nvoid sentinel_ref_store_clear(void)\n{\n    pthread_mutex_lock(&ref_mu);\n    for (int i = 0; i < ref_count; i++) {\n        if (ref_table[i].bytes) free(ref_table[i].bytes);\n    }\n    free(ref_table);\n    ref_table    = NULL;\n    ref_count    = 0;\n    ref_capacity = 0;\n    pthread_mutex_unlock(&ref_mu);\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Capability validation */\nunsigned int sentinel_validate(unsigned int producer_mask,\n                               unsigned int consumer_mask)\n{\n    unsigned int gap = producer_mask & ~consumer_mask;\n    if (gap == 0) return 0;\n    /* Return the lowest-numbered offending bit so callers can name\n     * one specific kind in their diagnostic. */\n    for (unsigned int b = 1; b != 0; b <<= 1) {\n        if (gap & b) return b;\n    }\n    return gap;   /* unreachable in practice */\n}\n\nconst char *sentinel_kind_name(sentinel_kind_t k)\n{\n    switch (k) {\n        case SENTINEL_NONE:             return \"(none)\";\n        case SENTINEL_REF:              return \"$ref\";\n        case SENTINEL_LANG_OPAQUE:      return \"$lang_opaque\";\n        case SENTINEL_FUNCTION_POINTER: return \"$function_pointer\";\n        default:                        return \"(unknown)\";\n    }\n}\n/* }}} */\n",

This adds the refcount machinery the closeout\ndocumented as the follow-on:\n\n  sentinel_ref_alloc(bytes, len) → refcount=1, returns chunk_ptr\n  sentinel_ref_inc(chunk_ptr)    → atomic bump\n  sentinel_ref_dec(chunk_ptr)    → atomic decrement; frees + reuses\n                                   the table slot when count hits 0\n  sentinel_ref_lookup(chunk_ptr) → unchanged; read-only, refcount\n                                   not touched\n\nSlot reuse: a freed chunk's table entry is marked bytes=NULL but\nleft in place; the next alloc scans for a free slot before\nextending the table. A long-running process that allocates many\n$refs over time stays bounded provided callers dec what they no\nlonger need. The refcount is opt-in — callers that don't use\ninc/dec get the pre-existing leak-per-run behaviour cleared by\nsentinel_ref_store_clear at end of run.\n\nThe protocol is documented in the header: producer alloc starts\nrefcount=1; producer holds the initial ref through the wire's\nlifetime; consumer lookup is read-only; either side can call dec\nto release a ref it owns. The dispatch's automatic ref/dec around\n$ref-bearing pushes is still future work (would require parsing\noutput bytes for $ref tokens); for now, refcount is the building\nblock that future automated machinery will use.\n\nThree new unit tests cover the lifecycle: alloc+dec frees; inc/dec\nbalance correctly; freed slots are reused by subsequent allocs.\nSentinel suite now at 10 passing, integration suite still at 19.\n\nCo-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>\nEOF\n)\" 2>&1 | tail -3",

    "originalFile":"/* src/012-dispatch.h — task dispatch layer, public API.\n *\n * What it is, in a sentence: the C function the thread pool runs\n * per task; reads inputs from the slot store, invokes the box's\n * language spec, pushes outputs to downstream input slots, and\n * spawns consumer tasks on input readiness.\n *\n * Designed in issue 304. As of this iteration: real input\n * reading, real spec invocation via per-worker handles, real\n * output pushing with FIFO + 1-cell peek slots, real\n * spawn-on-input-ready chaining under a single-spawn-per-box\n * rule. Iterator multi-spawn, the routing kinds beyond plain,\n * and the large-value heap path are still ahead.\n *\n * The `dispatch_ctx_t` bundle is the durable runtime state for\n * the whole run: graph, slot store, spec registry, pool, plus\n * a per-box \"ever spawned\" flag array and (optionally) a\n * per-box output-capture table for testing. Tasks carry a\n * pointer to the context so the action has everything it needs\n * without globals.\n */\n\n#ifndef SORAMECH_DISPATCH_H\n#define SORAMECH_DISPATCH_H\n\n#include <stdatomic.h>\n#include <stdint.h>\n\n#include \"010-graph-loader.h\"\n#include \"011-spec-registry.h\"\n#include \"009-slot-store.h\"\n#include \"014-event-queue.h\"\n#include \"pool.h\"\n\n#ifdef __cplusplus\nextern \"C\" {\n#endif\n\n/* {{{ Types */\ntypedef struct dispatch_ctx {\n    const graph_t        *graph;\n    slot_store_t         *slots;\n    spec_registry_t      *specs;\n    pool_t               *pool;\n\n    /* Diagnostic: incremented each time dispatch_action runs. */\n    _Atomic int           tasks_dispatched;\n\n    /* Per-box spawn guard (n_boxes entries). The 1-cell peek model\n     * spawns each box at most once; this flag is the CAS target\n     * that enforces \"only one push wins the spawn.\" */\n    int                   n_boxes;\n    _Atomic int          *box_ever_spawned;\n\n    /* Per-box output capture (opt-in, for tests). When non-NULL,\n     * dispatch_action copies the box's output bytes here on\n     * completion. n_boxes entries. */\n    char                **last_outputs;\n    int                  *last_output_sizes;\n    int                   capture_outputs;\n\n    /* Optional default output buffer size for invoke calls. If 0,\n     * defaults to 4096. */\n    int                   default_out_capacity;\n\n    /* Optional run-log event queue (issue 311). When non-NULL, the\n     * dispatch action emits task_start + task_end events through\n     * it. NULL turns the per-task logging off; the runner emits\n     * run_start / run_end on its own. */\n    event_queue_t        *events;\n\n    /* Verbose-event gate (issue 311 SORAMECH_LOG_VALUES=1). When\n     * 1 and `events` is non-NULL, dispatch_action also emits\n     * task_input / task_output events with the byte payloads\n     * (truncated to 4 KB per the architecture doc). */\n    int                   log_values;\n\n    /* Monotonic task id counter for run-log correlation. */\n    _Atomic int           next_task_id;\n} dispatch_ctx_t;\n\n/* Task structs are allocated from the unified allocator's slab\n * pool so spawn/free pairs amortise across the run instead of\n * paying per-call malloc bookkeeping. The chunk back-reference\n * lets dispatch_action release the cell via ua_unref without\n * having to look it up by data pointer. */\nstruct ua_chunk;\n\ntypedef struct dispatch_task {\n    int                   box_id;\n    int                   task_id;   /* assigned at dispatch_spawn time */\n    const dispatch_ctx_t *ctx;\n\n    /* 304 placeholder — live count of outgoing wires that still\n     * carry an unconsumed value pushed by this task. The box-\n     * retirement consumer that reads this lands with the\n     * lifetime-tracking slice; for now the field is set to 0 on\n     * spawn and otherwise unread. Keeping it in the layout\n     * documents the intent and lets a future slice flip the\n     * read-it-and-act-on-it switch without changing the struct\n     * shape callers depend on. */\n    uint32_t              live_wire_count;\n\n    struct ua_chunk      *chunk;     /* set by dispatch_spawn; freed by dispatch_action */\n} dispatch_task_t;\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Lifecycle */\n/* Initialize the per-box runtime state owned by the context. The\n * graph + slots + specs + pool fields are caller-owned and just\n * referenced. Call after `graph_attach_runtime` so the per-box\n * runtime data is in place.\n *\n * `enable_output_capture` allocates `last_outputs` and\n * `last_output_sizes` so tests can inspect what each box wrote\n * after `pool_wait_quiescent`. */\nint  dispatch_ctx_init   (dispatch_ctx_t *ctx,\n                          const graph_t *g, slot_store_t *s,\n                          spec_registry_t *r, pool_t *p,\n                          int enable_output_capture, char **err);\n\n/* Free per-box runtime arrays; does not touch the externally-owned\n * graph / slots / specs / pool fields. */\nvoid dispatch_ctx_destroy(dispatch_ctx_t *ctx);\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Startup helpers */\n/* Walk every box and push any input-port literal values into the\n * corresponding input slot. After this call, boxes whose inputs\n * are entirely literals are \"ready\" — spawn them with\n * `dispatch_spawn_if_ready` to start the run. */\nint  dispatch_push_literals(dispatch_ctx_t *ctx, char **err);\n\n/* If `box_id` has all required inputs available and hasn't been\n * spawned yet, allocate a task and submit it to the pool. */\nvoid dispatch_spawn_if_ready(dispatch_ctx_t *ctx, int box_id, int priority);\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Task submission / action */\n/* Submit a task explicitly, bypassing the spawn-if-ready check.\n * The dispatch_action will still consume inputs from slots and\n * push outputs to downstream slots. */\nvoid dispatch_spawn(const dispatch_ctx_t *ctx, int box_id, int priority);\n\n/* The pool action. Cast `arg` back to `dispatch_task_t *` inside.\n * Frees the task at the end of the action. */\nvoid dispatch_action(void *arg);\n/* }}} */\n\n#ifdef __cplusplus\n}\n#endif\n\n#endif /* SORAMECH_DISPATCH_H */\n",

{
  "uuid":"f1eaea4b-416c-4a3e-b49f-3f2a0435b82a",

  "toolUseResult":{
    "originalFile":"/* src/012-dispatch.h — task dispatch layer, public API.\n *\n * What it is, in a sentence: the C function the thread pool runs\n * per task; reads inputs from the slot store, invokes the box's\n * language spec, pushes outputs to downstream input slots, and\n * spawns consumer tasks on input readiness.\n *\n * Designed in issue 304. As of this iteration: real input\n * reading, real spec invocation via per-worker handles, real\n * output pushing with FIFO + 1-cell peek slots, real\n * spawn-on-input-ready chaining under a single-spawn-per-box\n * rule. Iterator multi-spawn, the routing kinds beyond plain,\n * and the large-value heap path are still ahead.\n *\n * The `dispatch_ctx_t` bundle is the durable runtime state for\n * the whole run: graph, slot store, spec registry, pool, plus\n * a per-box \"ever spawned\" flag array and (optionally) a\n * per-box output-capture table for testing. Tasks carry a\n * pointer to the context so the action has everything it needs\n * without globals.\n */\n\n#ifndef SORAMECH_DISPATCH_H\n#define SORAMECH_DISPATCH_H\n\n#include <stdatomic.h>\n#include <stdint.h>\n\n#include \"010-graph-loader.h\"\n#include \"011-spec-registry.h\"\n#include \"009-slot-store.h\"\n#include \"014-event-queue.h\"\n#include \"pool.h\"\n\n#ifdef __cplusplus\nextern \"C\" {\n#endif\n\n/* {{{ Types */\ntypedef struct dispatch_ctx {\n    const graph_t        *graph;\n    slot_store_t         *slots;\n    spec_registry_t      *specs;\n    pool_t               *pool;\n\n    /* Diagnostic: incremented each time dispatch_action runs. */\n    _Atomic int           tasks_dispatched;\n\n    /* Per-box runtime state (spawn guard + optional output capture)\n     * lives in chunked-append chunks (see ctx_box_chunk_t in\n     * dispatch.c). The old flat-arrays-with-headroom model imposed\n     * a 4096-box runtime cap that issue 319's create_box could\n     * exceed; chunks remove the cap by growing on demand.\n     *\n     * Access goes through the private ctx_box_slot helper in\n     * dispatch.c; callers don't touch these directly. */\n    void                 *box_chunks_opaque;   /* ctx_box_chunk_t**, hidden type */\n    _Atomic unsigned int  n_box_chunks;\n    pthread_mutex_t       box_chunks_mu;\n    int                   capture_outputs;\n\n    /* Optional default output buffer size for invoke calls. If 0,\n     * defaults to 4096. */\n    int                   default_out_capacity;\n\n    /* Optional run-log event queue (issue 311). When non-NULL, the\n     * dispatch action emits task_start + task_end events through\n     * it. NULL turns the per-task logging off; the runner emits\n     * run_start / run_end on its own. */\n    event_queue_t        *events;\n\n    /* Verbose-event gate (issue 311 SORAMECH_LOG_VALUES=1). When\n     * 1 and `events` is non-NULL, dispatch_action also emits\n     * task_input / task_output events with the byte payloads\n     * (truncated to 4 KB per the architecture doc). */\n    int                   log_values;\n\n    /* Monotonic task id counter for run-log correlation. */\n    _Atomic int           next_task_id;\n} dispatch_ctx_t;\n\n/* Task structs are allocated from the unified allocator's slab\n * pool so spawn/free pairs amortise across the run instead of\n * paying per-call malloc bookkeeping. The chunk back-reference\n * lets dispatch_action release the cell via ua_unref without\n * having to look it up by data pointer. */\nstruct ua_chunk;\n\ntypedef struct dispatch_task {\n    int                   box_id;\n    int                   task_id;   /* assigned at dispatch_spawn time */\n    const dispatch_ctx_t *ctx;\n\n    /* 304 placeholder — live count of outgoing wires that still\n     * carry an unconsumed value pushed by this task. The box-\n     * retirement consumer that reads this lands with the\n     * lifetime-tracking slice; for now the field is set to 0 on\n     * spawn and otherwise unread. Keeping it in the layout\n     * documents the intent and lets a future slice flip the\n     * read-it-and-act-on-it switch without changing the struct\n     * shape callers depend on. */\n    uint32_t              live_wire_count;\n\n    struct ua_chunk      *chunk;     /* set by dispatch_spawn; freed by dispatch_action */\n} dispatch_task_t;\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Lifecycle */\n/* Initialize the per-box runtime state owned by the context. The\n * graph + slots + specs + pool fields are caller-owned and just\n * referenced. Call after `graph_attach_runtime` so the per-box\n * runtime data is in place.\n *\n * `enable_output_capture` allocates `last_outputs` and\n * `last_output_sizes` so tests can inspect what each box wrote\n * after `pool_wait_quiescent`. */\nint  dispatch_ctx_init   (dispatch_ctx_t *ctx,\n                          const graph_t *g, slot_store_t *s,\n                          spec_registry_t *r, pool_t *p,\n                          int enable_output_capture, char **err);\n\n/* Free per-box runtime arrays; does not touch the externally-owned\n * graph / slots / specs / pool fields. */\nvoid dispatch_ctx_destroy(dispatch_ctx_t *ctx);\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Startup helpers */\n/* Walk every box and push any input-port literal values into the\n * corresponding input slot. After this call, boxes whose inputs\n * are entirely literals are \"ready\" — spawn them with\n * `dispatch_spawn_if_ready` to start the run. */\nint  dispatch_push_literals(dispatch_ctx_t *ctx, char **err);\n\n/* If `box_id` has all required inputs available and hasn't been\n * spawned yet, allocate a task and submit it to the pool. */\nvoid dispatch_spawn_if_ready(dispatch_ctx_t *ctx, int box_id, int priority);\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Task submission / action */\n/* Submit a task explicitly, bypassing the spawn-if-ready check.\n * The dispatch_action will still consume inputs from slots and\n * push outputs to downstream slots. */\nvoid dispatch_spawn(const dispatch_ctx_t *ctx, int box_id, int priority);\n\n/* The pool action. Cast `arg` back to `dispatch_task_t *` inside.\n * Frees the task at the end of the action. */\nvoid dispatch_action(void *arg);\n/* }}} */\n\n#ifdef __cplusplus\n}\n#endif\n\n#endif /* SORAMECH_DISPATCH_H */\n",

    "newString":"/* {{{ Per-box ctx chunks — issue 319 follow-on to lift the\n * RUNTIME_BOX_HEADROOM cap. The dispatch carries per-box state\n * (spawn guard + optional output capture) in chunked-append\n * chunks: each chunk holds CTX_CHUNK_SIZE slots, and the\n * top-level array of chunk pointers grows as new boxes appear\n * (graph load + runtime create_box). Slots never move once\n * allocated; the array of chunk pointers can grow via realloc\n * because callers reach individual slots through pointer\n * indirection. */\n#define CTX_CHUNK_SIZE 64\n\ntypedef struct ctx_box_chunk {\n    _Atomic int spawned   [CTX_CHUNK_SIZE];\n    char       *outputs   [CTX_CHUNK_SIZE];\n    int         out_sizes [CTX_CHUNK_SIZE];\n} ctx_box_chunk_t;\n\n/* Return the slot info for box_id, growing the chunk array as\n * needed if create_if_missing is set. Returns the chunk pointer;\n * callers index by `box_id % CTX_CHUNK_SIZE`. Returns NULL when\n * create_if_missing is 0 and the chunk hasn't been allocated. */\nstatic ctx_box_chunk_t *ctx_box_chunk(dispatch_ctx_t *ctx, unsigned int box_id,\n                                      int create_if_missing)\n{\n    unsigned int ci = box_id / CTX_CHUNK_SIZE;\n    unsigned int n  = atomic_load_explicit(&ctx->n_box_chunks,\n                                           memory_order_acquire);\n    ctx_box_chunk_t **chunks = ctx->box_chunks_opaque;\n    if (ci < n && chunks && chunks[ci]) return chunks[ci];\n    if (!create_if_missing) return NULL;\n\n    pthread_mutex_lock(&ctx->box_chunks_mu);\n    n      = atomic_load_explicit(&ctx->n_box_chunks, memory_order_relaxed);\n    chunks = ctx->box_chunks_opaque;\n    if (ci >= n) {\n        /* Grow the top-level array to cover ci+1 chunks. The array\n         * is realloc'd; callers don't hold pointers into it (they\n         * reach individual slots through the chunk pointers, which\n         * stay stable once published). */\n        unsigned int new_n = n == 0 ? 8 : n;\n        while (new_n <= ci) new_n *= 2;\n        ctx_box_chunk_t **grown = realloc(chunks,\n                                          (size_t)new_n * sizeof *grown);\n        if (!grown) { pthread_mutex_unlock(&ctx->box_chunks_mu); return NULL; }\n        for (unsigned int k = n; k < new_n; k++) grown[k] = NULL;\n        ctx->box_chunks_opaque = grown;\n        atomic_store_explicit(&ctx->n_box_chunks, new_n, memory_order_release);\n        chunks = grown;\n    }\n    if (!chunks[ci]) {\n        ctx_box_chunk_t *fresh = calloc(1, sizeof *fresh);\n        if (!fresh) { pthread_mutex_unlock(&ctx->box_chunks_mu); return NULL; }\n        for (int i = 0; i < CTX_CHUNK_SIZE; i++) {\n            atomic_init(&fresh->spawned[i], 0);\n        }\n        chunks[ci] = fresh;\n    }\n    ctx_box_chunk_t *result = chunks[ci];\n    pthread_mutex_unlock(&ctx->box_chunks_mu);\n    return result;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* Sanity ceiling on per-box input count."
  },

    "originalFile":"/* src/012-dispatch.h — task dispatch layer, public API.\n *\n * What it is, in a sentence: the C function the thread pool runs\n * per task; reads inputs from the slot store, invokes the box's\n * language spec, pushes outputs to downstream input slots, and\n * spawns consumer tasks on input readiness.\n *\n * Designed in issue 304. As of this iteration: real input\n * reading, real spec invocation via per-worker handles, real\n * output pushing with FIFO + 1-cell peek slots, real\n * spawn-on-input-ready chaining under a single-spawn-per-box\n * rule. Iterator multi-spawn, the routing kinds beyond plain,\n * and the large-value heap path are still ahead.\n *\n * The `dispatch_ctx_t` bundle is the durable runtime state for\n * the whole run: graph, slot store, spec registry, pool, plus\n * a per-box \"ever spawned\" flag array and (optionally) a\n * per-box output-capture table for testing. Tasks carry a\n * pointer to the context so the action has everything it needs\n * without globals.\n */\n\n#ifndef SORAMECH_DISPATCH_H\n#define SORAMECH_DISPATCH_H\n\n#include <stdatomic.h>\n#include <stdint.h>\n#include <pthread.h>\n\n#include \"010-graph-loader.h\"\n#include \"011-spec-registry.h\"\n#include \"009-slot-store.h\"\n#include \"014-event-queue.h\"\n#include \"pool.h\"\n\n#ifdef __cplusplus\nextern \"C\" {\n#endif\n\n/* {{{ Types */\ntypedef struct dispatch_ctx {\n    const graph_t        *graph;\n    slot_store_t         *slots;\n    spec_registry_t      *specs;\n    pool_t               *pool;\n\n    /* Diagnostic: incremented each time dispatch_action runs. */\n    _Atomic int           tasks_dispatched;\n\n    /* Per-box runtime state (spawn guard + optional output capture)\n     * lives in chunked-append chunks (see ctx_box_chunk_t in\n     * dispatch.c). The old flat-arrays-with-headroom model imposed\n     * a 4096-box runtime cap that issue 319's create_box could\n     * exceed; chunks remove the cap by growing on demand.\n     *\n     * Access goes through the private ctx_box_slot helper in\n     * dispatch.c; callers don't touch these directly. */\n    void                 *box_chunks_opaque;   /* ctx_box_chunk_t**, hidden type */\n    _Atomic unsigned int  n_box_chunks;\n    pthread_mutex_t       box_chunks_mu;\n    int                   capture_outputs;\n\n    /* Optional default output buffer size for invoke calls. If 0,\n     * defaults to 4096. */\n    int                   default_out_capacity;\n\n    /* Optional run-log event queue (issue 311). When non-NULL, the\n     * dispatch action emits task_start + task_end events through\n     * it. NULL turns the per-task logging off; the runner emits\n     * run_start / run_end on its own. */\n    event_queue_t        *events;\n\n    /* Verbose-event gate (issue 311 SORAMECH_LOG_VALUES=1). When\n     * 1 and `events` is non-NULL, dispatch_action also emits\n     * task_input / task_output events with the byte payloads\n     * (truncated to 4 KB per the architecture doc). */\n    int                   log_values;\n\n    /* Monotonic task id counter for run-log correlation. */\n    _Atomic int           next_task_id;\n} dispatch_ctx_t;\n\n/* Task structs are allocated from the unified allocator's slab\n * pool so spawn/free pairs amortise across the run instead of\n * paying per-call malloc bookkeeping. The chunk back-reference\n * lets dispatch_action release the cell via ua_unref without\n * having to look it up by data pointer. */\nstruct ua_chunk;\n\ntypedef struct dispatch_task {\n    int                   box_id;\n    int                   task_id;   /* assigned at dispatch_spawn time */\n    const dispatch_ctx_t *ctx;\n\n    /* 304 placeholder — live count of outgoing wires that still\n     * carry an unconsumed value pushed by this task. The box-\n     * retirement consumer that reads this lands with the\n     * lifetime-tracking slice; for now the field is set to 0 on\n     * spawn and otherwise unread. Keeping it in the layout\n     * documents the intent and lets a future slice flip the\n     * read-it-and-act-on-it switch without changing the struct\n     * shape callers depend on. */\n    uint32_t              live_wire_count;\n\n    struct ua_chunk      *chunk;     /* set by dispatch_spawn; freed by dispatch_action */\n} dispatch_task_t;\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Lifecycle */\n/* Initialize the per-box runtime state owned by the context. The\n * graph + slots + specs + pool fields are caller-owned and just\n * referenced. Call after `graph_attach_runtime` so the per-box\n * runtime data is in place.\n *\n * `enable_output_capture` allocates `last_outputs` and\n * `last_output_sizes` so tests can inspect what each box wrote\n * after `pool_wait_quiescent`. */\nint  dispatch_ctx_init   (dispatch_ctx_t *ctx,\n                          const graph_t *g, slot_store_t *s,\n                          spec_registry_t *r, pool_t *p,\n                          int enable_output_capture, char **err);\n\n/* Free per-box runtime arrays; does not touch the externally-owned\n * graph / slots / specs / pool fields. */\nvoid dispatch_ctx_destroy(dispatch_ctx_t *ctx);\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Startup helpers */\n/* Walk every box and push any input-port literal values into the\n * corresponding input slot. After this call, boxes whose inputs\n * are entirely literals are \"ready\" — spawn them with\n * `dispatch_spawn_if_ready` to start the run. */\nint  dispatch_push_literals(dispatch_ctx_t *ctx, char **err);\n\n/* If `box_id` has all required inputs available and hasn't been\n * spawned yet, allocate a task and submit it to the pool. */\nvoid dispatch_spawn_if_ready(dispatch_ctx_t *ctx, int box_id, int priority);\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Task submission / action */\n/* Submit a task explicitly, bypassing the spawn-if-ready check.\n * The dispatch_action will still consume inputs from slots and\n * push outputs to downstream slots. */\nvoid dispatch_spawn(const dispatch_ctx_t *ctx, int box_id, int priority);\n\n/* The pool action. Cast `arg` back to `dispatch_task_t *` inside.\n * Frees the task at the end of the action. */\nvoid dispatch_action(void *arg);\n/* }}} */\n\n#ifdef __cplusplus\n}\n#endif\n\n#endif /* SORAMECH_DISPATCH_H */\n",

    "stdout":"# 313 — Research: whole-program same-language compilation\n\n## Status\nin progress — Lua slice landed 2026-05-21 (compile-time\nconcatenation in `soramech-compile.sh`, runtime detection in the\nLua spec, end-to-end test). C and Bash merges are follow-ons.\n\n## Concept\n\nInstead of one box = one function call going through the dispatch\nlayer + slot store + spec invocation, **merge all same-language\nboxes at compile time into a single translation unit** for that\nlanguage. Box-to-box transitions within a language region become\nordinary function calls — the optimizer can inline across them, the\nlanguage runtime stays warm, and the slot store and dispatch layer\ndon't run for those transitions at all. Only cross-language wires\nretain the slot machinery.\n\nFor C: every C box becomes a function in one big `.c` file, with\nthe build emitting one `.so`. Wire endpoints become direct calls;\nthe optimizer inlines based on its usual heuristics.\n\nFor Lua: every Lua function gets pre-compiled into one bytecode\nchunk loaded into one shared `lua_State` per worker. Wire\nendpoints become direct `lua_pcall`s into that chunk — no JSON\nencode/decode, no slot push/pop, no spec re-entry per call.\n\nFor Bash: probably no benefit — Bash is already process-per-call;\nfusing scripts doesn't help much. Skip.\n\n## Relationship to 312 — what stays, what thins\n\n312 defines the **wire format**: dual-ring slots (native ring,\nJSON ring, ordering ring) per input port, per-edge classification\nat graph load, JSON-only-at-borders, native-otherwise. Every\nvalue movement between boxes goes through this machinery.\n\nThis issue's merge thins the **spec invocation overhead** — the\ndlsym + bridge + lua_pcall (or equivalent) that happens once\nper box invocation. For boxes in the merged region, the dispatch\nholds a direct pointer to the function inside the merged module\nand calls it without going through the spec interface.\n\nThe slot machinery stays alive in the merged region. Why:\n**boxes still run as separate thread-pool tasks**. A producer\non worker 0 and a consumer on worker 1 still need slots to hand\noff the value across threads. The thread pool's parallelism\ndepends on tasks being scheduled independently; collapsing\nsame-language hops to synchronous function calls would defeat\nthe pool entirely. The merge wins on the per-call indirection\ncost, not on the wire format.\n\nSo a box invocation inside the merged region looks like:\n\n1. Worker picks up the task.\n2. Dispatch reads inputs from the box's slots (same as 312 —\n   dual-ring native side).\n3. Dispatch jumps to the merged function directly (this is\n   what 313 wins).\n4. Function runs, returns a value.\n...\nrunner produces — the merge is transparent.\n\nDeferred to follow-on slices:\n\n- **C merge.** Concatenating C source needs care with static\n  vs. non-static functions, file-scoped declarations, and header\n  inclusion. Plausible approach: wrap each box's source in an\n  anonymous namespace-equivalent (C doesn't have namespaces, but\n  static-by-default at file scope + unique mangled exposure of\n  the box's entry function would do it). Real work; not done.\n- **Bash merge.** Bash already runs one persistent subprocess\n  per worker (issue 308's UDS-server model); the \"merge\" would\n  source every box's `.sh` file into the same subprocess\n  environment at server startup. Smaller surface than C; sized\n  somewhere in between.\n- **Inline-into-dispatch optimization.** This slice loads the\n  merged module per worker but still goes through the spec's\n  `lua_pcall` for every box invocation. The big optimization the\n  issue body talks about — turning box-to-box transitions into\n  direct function calls inside the merged module — needs\n  dispatch-layer work that hasn't started. The current slice is\n  the foundation: load-once-per-worker. The direct-call\n  optimization rides on top.\n\n## Open questions (for the research, not for now)\n\n- Cross-language wires inside the merged region: the merged region\n  still has cross-language outputs that exit to other regions. The\n  spec interface still applies at those boundaries, so the merge is\n  region-internal optimization, not a global rearchitecture.\n- C ABI for inlined wrappers: with whole-program optimization the\n  wrapper-per-box generation might collapse to nothing. If the\n  optimizer can prove a wire endpoint is always called from the\n  merged region with known types, it can skip the wrapper.\n- Iterators-with-side-effects: an iterator self-rescheduling its\n  own task is normally dispatch-layer machinery. Inside a merged\n  region, it could become a `while` loop. Whether that's safe\n  depends on whether other tasks are blocked on the iterator's\n  output slots — which they shouldn't be in a same-language region,\n  but the analysis has to confirm.",

      "content":"# {{{ pre-compile C boxes into compiled/bin/\n# The runner already lazy-compiles .c → .so on first invoke, so this\n# step is purely informational: it surfaces compile errors at compile\n# time rather than at run time, and produces artifacts the user can\n# inspect or distribute alongside the source.\nn_c_compiled=0\nn_c_failed=0\nfor box in \"$COMPILED\"/boxes/*.json; do\n    box_lang=$(box_field \"$box\" lang)\n    if [[ \"$box_lang\" != \"c\" ]]; then continue; fi\n    ref=$(box_field \"$box\" ref)\n    if [[ -z \"$ref\" ]]; then continue; fi\n    src_path=\"$COMPILED/$ref\"\n    if [[ ! -f \"$src_path\" ]]; then\n        echo \"soramech-compile: C box source missing: $ref\" >&2\n        n_c_failed=$((n_c_failed + 1))\n        continue\n    fi\n    base=$(basename \"$ref\" .c)\n    out=\"$COMPILED/bin/$base.so\"\n    if ! gcc -shared -fPIC -O2 -Wall -o \"$out\" \"$src_path\" 2>/tmp/soramech-compile-cc.log; then\n        echo \"soramech-compile: gcc failed for $ref:\" >&2\n        cat /tmp/soramech-compile-cc.log >&2\n        n_c_failed=$((n_c_failed + 1))\n        continue\n    fi\n    n_c_compiled=$((n_c_compiled + 1))\ndone\n\nif [[ $n_c_failed -gt 0 ]]; then\n    echo \"soramech-compile: $n_c_failed C box(es) failed to compile\" >&2\n    exit 1\nfi\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ copy the pool runner into the compiled directory\n# A real copy (not a symlink) is intentional: the runner discovers\n# its sibling langs/ via /proc/self/exe, which follows symlinks to\n# their canonical target.     "oldString":"/* {{{ maybe_lazy_compile() — if file_path is a .c source, compile it\n * to a /tmp .so and return that path; otherwise return file_path\n * unchanged.     "newString":"/* {{{ maybe_lazy_compile() — if file_path is a .c source, compile it\n * to a /tmp .so and return that path; otherwise return file_path\n * unchanged. The output buffer is the caller-supplied so_buf.\n *\n * Issue 313 follow-on (C eager-precompile): if the compile\n * pipeline (scripts/soramech-compile.sh) ran for this map, it\n * already produced a per-box .so in <map_dir>/bin/<basename>.so.\n * Prefer that artifact over re-running gcc at dispatch time.\n * Falls through to lazy compile when running from a source tree\n * the compile pipeline hasn't touched (i.e. the live `maps/`\n * editor flow). */\nstatic const char *maybe_lazy_compile(const char *file_path,\n                                      char *so_buf, size_t so_cap)\n{\n    if (!ends_in_dot_c(file_path)) return file_path;\n\n    /* Try compiled artifact first. (int)(ext - fname) : (int)strlen(fname);\n        int n = snprintf(precompiled, sizeof precompiled,\n                         \"%.*s/bin/%.*s.so\",\n                         prefix_len, file_path, name_len, fname);\n        if (n > 0 && (size_t)n < sizeof precompiled) {\n            struct stat st;\n            if (stat(precompiled, &st) == 0) {\n                int copy_n = snprintf(so_buf, so_cap, \"%s\", precompiled);\n                if (copy_n > 0 && (size_t)copy_n < so_cap) return so_buf;\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    /* Hash the source path so repeat opens of the same source file\n     * pick up the same .so. Concurrent invokes will race on gcc but\n     * the inputs are identical, so the output converges. */\n    unsigned long h = hash_path(file_path);\n    int n = snprintf(so_buf, so_cap, \"/tmp/soramech-c-%lx.so\", h);\n    if (n < 0 || (size_t)n >= so_cap) return NULL;\n    /* No box context on this internal lazy-compile path; the caller\n     * passed us a raw `.c` ref and we just need a default build. */\n    if (c_compile(file_path, so_buf, NULL) != 0) return NULL;\n    return so_buf;\n}"

          "old_string":"    /* 3. Pool. */\n    pool = pool_create(0);   /* default n_workers */",
          "replace_all":false,
          "new_string":"    /* Issue 313 follow-on (Bash merge): collect every distinct\n     * bash box's ref into a colon-separated list and publish it\n     * via SORAMECH_BASH_PRESOURCE_FILES. bash-server.sh reads the\n     * env var at startup and sources each file before entering\n     * the request loop. Replaces the per-call lazy `source` cost\n     * with a single startup cost per worker. Function-name\n     * collisions across boxes are last-write-wins as before;\n     * sourcing eagerly doesn't change those semantics. */\n    {\n        char  presource[8192]; presource[0] = '\\0';\n        int   total_len = 0;\n        int   first = 1;\n        int   n_boxes = graph_n_boxes(g);\n        const char *mdir = graph_map_dir(g);\n        for (int i = 0; i < n_boxes; i++) {\n            const box_t *b = graph_box(g, i);\n            if (!b || b->kind != BOX_CALL) continue;\n            if (!b->lang || strcmp(b->lang, \"bash\") != 0) continue;\n            if (!b->ref) continue;\n            /* Compose absolute path. */\n            char abspath[4096];\n            int an;\n            if (b->ref[0] == '/' || !mdir) {\n                an = snprintf(abspath, sizeof abspath, \"%s\", b->ref);\n            } else {\n                an = snprintf(abspath, sizeof abspath, \"%s/%s\", mdir, b->ref);\n            }\n            if (an < 0 || an >= (int)sizeof abspath) continue;\n            /* Dedup against what's already in presource. */\n            if (strstr(presource, abspath)) continue;\n            int add = snprintf(presource + total_len,\n                               sizeof presource - (size_t)total_len,\n                               \"%s%s\", first ? \"\" : \":\", abspath);\n            if (add < 0 || total_len + add >= (int)sizeof presource) break;\n            total_len += add;\n            first = 0;\n        }\n        if (total_len > 0) setenv(\"SORAMECH_BASH_PRESOURCE_FILES\", presource, 1);\n    }\n\n    /* 3. Pool. */\n    pool = pool_create(0);   /* default n_workers */",
          "file_path":"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech/src/008-pool-runner.c"
        },

Replaces the per-call lazy `source` cost\n     * with a single startup cost per worker. Function-name\n     * collisions across boxes are last-write-wins as before;\n     * sourcing eagerly doesn't change those semantics. */\n    {\n        char  presource[8192]; presource[0] = '\\0';\n        int   total_len = 0;\n        int   first = 1;\n        int   n_boxes = graph_n_boxes(g);\n        const char *mdir = graph_map_dir(g);\n        for (int i = 0; i < n_boxes; i++) {\n            const box_t *b = graph_box(g, i);\n            if (!b || b->kind != BOX_CALL) continue;\n            if (!b->lang || strcmp(b->lang, \"bash\") != 0) continue;\n            if (!b->ref) continue;\n            /* Compose absolute path. */\n            char abspath[4096];\n            int an;\n            if (b->ref[0] == '/' || !mdir) {\n                an = snprintf(abspath, sizeof abspath, \"%s\", b->ref);\n            } else {\n                an = snprintf(abspath, sizeof abspath, \"%s/%s\", mdir, b->ref);\n            }\n            if (an < 0 || an >= (int)sizeof abspath) continue;\n            /* Dedup against what's already in presource. */\n            if (strstr(presource, abspath)) continue;\n            int add = snprintf(presource + total_len,\n                               sizeof presource - (size_t)total_len,\n                               \"%s%s\", first ? \"\" : \":\", abspath);\n            if (add < 0 || total_len + add >= (int)sizeof presource) break;\n            total_len += add;\n            first = 0;\n        }\n        if (total_len > 0) setenv(\"SORAMECH_BASH_PRESOURCE_FILES\", presource, 1);\n    }\n\n    /* 3. Pool. */\n    pool = pool_create(0);   /* default n_workers */"

Box functions use `printf '%s' \"$x\"` to avoid them.\n#\n# Caching: each box file is sourced on first use and remembered in\n# the `sourced` associative array; subsequent invocations skip the\n# `source` and reuse the loaded functions. Per-worker, no locking.\n\nset -u\n\ndeclare -A sourced\n\nwhile IFS= read -r n_args; do\n    [[ \"$n_args\" == \"QUIT\" ]] && break\n\n    IFS= read -r file_path\n    IFS= read -r fn_name\n\n    args=()\n    for ((i = 0; i < n_args; i++)); do\n        IFS= read -r a\n        args+=(\"$a\")\n    done\n\n    if [[ ! -f \"$file_path\" ]]; then\n        printf '127\\n0\\n'\n        continue\n    fi\n\n    if [[ -z \"${sourced[$file_path]:-}\" ]]; then\n        # shellcheck disable=SC1090\n        if ! source \"$file_path\" 2>/dev/null; then\n            printf '126\\n0\\n'\n            continue\n        fi\n        sourced[$file_path]=1\n    fi\n\n    # Capture function output and exit status. The function name\n    # itself failing (not a callable) surfaces as exit 127.\n    if ! declare -F \"$fn_name\" >/dev/null 2>&1; then\n        printf '127\\n0\\n'\n        continue\n    fi\n\n    out=$(\"$fn_name\" \"${args[@]}\" 2>/dev/null)\n    status=$?\n    n=${#out}\n    printf '%d\\n%d\\n' \"$status\" \"$n\"\n    printf '%s' \"$out\"\ndone\n",

          "new_string":"# 313 — Research: whole-program same-language compilation\n\n## Status\ncomplete (the three landable slices). The bigger research item\n— inline-into-dispatch direct calls — stays open as research.\n\n## Current behavior\n\nThree same-language thinning slices have landed:\n\n- **Lua merge** (2026-05-21). `scripts/soramech-compile.sh` walks\n  every `.lua` source in the map and concatenates each into a\n  shared `__merged__.lua` file. Each per-file module wraps in\n  its own closure and exports under the source file's basename,\n  so two files can both define a local `M` without colliding.\n  The Lua spec's `lua_invoke` detects the merged file at first\n  use, loads it once into the worker's `lua_State`, and looks\n  up each box's module by basename. Subsequent invocations skip\n  the per-file `luaL_loadfile` and use the cached merged module.\n\n- **C eager-precompile preference** (2026-05-23). When the source path\n  is `<map>/src/<base>.c` and `<map>/bin/<base>.so` exists, the\n  precompiled `.so` is dlopen'd directly — no gcc invocation\n  on the runtime hot path. Live `maps/` editor runs (which the\n  compile pipeline hasn't touched) fall through to the existing\n  lazy compile.\n\n- **Bash merge — pre-source at server startup** (2026-05-23).\n  The pool runner walks the graph at startup, collects every\n  distinct bash box's absolute source path, and publishes the\n  list via `SORAMECH_BASH_PRESOURCE_FILES`. The persistent\n  bash subprocess (issue 308's UDS server) reads the env var\n  before entering its request loop and sources each file. The\n  per-call `source`+cache machinery stays in place for boxes\n  the precondition didn't cover (runtime-created bash boxes\n  from 319f's box-kind path, or any file outside the static\n  graph). Function-name collisions across files remain last-\n  write-wins; sourcing eagerly doesn't change those semantics.",

The Lua merge was a real merge — one file per language per map. The C and Bash \"merges\" are really \"move the cost out of the hot path\" — C precompiles to many `.so` files (not one), Bash pre-sources (but each file stays its own source). The original 313 design wanted true source-level fusion; the practical answer is \"you don't need fusion if you've already removed the per-call init cost.\"\n\nThis is the recurring pattern from earlier in the session: **a per-X symptom doesn't always mean a per-X structural fix**. 313 wanted to merge to eliminate spec invocation overhead; turns out eliminating *compile-time* and *source-time* overhead got most of the win without needing source-level merge at all.\n`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`\n\n## Phase 3 progress\n\nPhase 3 is effectively at the closeout boundary — every numbered issue is either complete or moved to completed/, with the remaining items being deliberate open research (313's inline-into-dispatch, 318's `$function_pointer` wrapper-binary subsystem, 246's bash translate callback).     "stdout":"# 248 — Encapsulated map as box\n\n## Status\nopen\n\n## Concept\n\nA map directory is normally opened via the map-select UI as the\ntop-level graph being edited. **This issue adds a second way to\nopen a map:** through the file browser, as an *encapsulated box*\non the currently-edited parent map. The opened map becomes a\nsingle box on the parent's canvas. Its inputs come from `data`\nboxes inside the sub-map that have been marked\n**externally-supplied**; its outputs come from `write` boxes\ninside the sub-map that have been marked **externally-consumed**.\nThe two markings are symmetric: one redirects an input from \"file\non disk\" to \"wire from parent,\" the other redirects an output\nfrom \"file on disk\" to \"wire to parent.\"\n\nEncapsulation is a function-like abstraction over a sub-graph.\nThe parent doesn't see the sub-map's internals; it sees one box\nwith declared input ports, declared output ports, and known\nsemantics. The sub-map can be edited independently, reused across\nparent maps, and packaged once for distribution.\n\n**Encapsulated boxes are the documented exception to issue 218's\n\"single output per box\" rule.** Every other box kind has exactly\none output (with fan-out via multiple wires leaving that one\noutput). An encapsulated map has *N* distinct output ports, one\nper `write` box marked externally-consumed. *N* may be zero (the\nmap is a pure side-effect sink), one (matches the common case),\nor many. The exception exists because an encapsulated map's\noutputs are independent values produced by independent\n`write` boxes — packing them into a single blob (the earlier\ndesign in this issue) would have repurposed file-writing\nmachinery to emit strings into wires, which is the wrong shape:\n`write` boxes should keep their semantics (\"terminate a value\")\nand the destination kind (\"file vs. parent wire\") should be a\nmode toggle, not a substitution.\n\n## Marked input ports inside the sub-map\n\nA **data** box inside the sub-map (kind: `data`, the existing\nlanguage-agnostic file-IO source) can be marked as\n**externally-supplied** via a small toggle on the box's\ninspector. Toggling declares: \"this data box's value comes from\nthe encapsulating context, not from its `path` or `value`\nfield.\"\n\nThe toggle is intentionally scoped to `data` boxes — those are\nthe natural entry points for external values into a map. Call\nboxes / read boxes / write boxes don't carry the toggle, which\nkeeps the inspector uncluttered for the common cases. Each\nexternal input becomes a small shared-memory chunk seeded by\nthe encapsulating call's invoke; the marked data box reads from\nthat chunk on each fire, treating it identically to a value\nloaded from disk.\n\nThe toggle records the port's binding kind on the box JSON:\n\n```json\n{\n    \"id\": \"sum_input\",\n    \"kind\": \"data\",\n    \"external\": {\n        \"kind\": \"named\",            // or \"positional\" / \"numbered\"\n        \"name\": \"count\",            // for named\n        \"index\": 0                  // for positional / numbered\n    },\n    \"...\": \"...\"\n}\n```\n\nThree binding kinds capture how the encapsulating box's input\nmaps to this internal port:\n\n- **`positional`** — bound by argument order. The encapsulating\n  box has N input ports; the *k*th port's value flows to the\n  internal box whose `external.index` is *k*. Conceptually\n  matches positional function arguments.\n- **`numbered`** — bound by an explicit integer index. Same shape\n  as positional but the user picks the number (so they can leave\n  gaps, reorder freely, etc.).\n- **`named`** — bound by a string name. The encapsulating box's\n  input port has a label; the matching internal box's\n  `external.name` is the same string.\n\nA single sub-map can mix kinds across its marked boxes — some\npositional, some named — and the parent map's encapsulated box\nexposes the union as its input ports.\n\n## Marked output ports inside the sub-map\n\nA **write** box inside the sub-map (kind: `write`, issue 229's\nfile-write kind) can be marked as **externally-consumed** via a\nsmall toggle on the box's inspector — the mirror of the\nexternally-supplied toggle on data boxes. Toggling declares:\n\"this write box's value goes to the encapsulating context, not\nto its `path` field.\"\n\nThe toggle is intentionally scoped to `write` boxes — those are\nthe natural exit points for values out of a map. Each\nexternally-consumed write box surfaces as one **distinct output\nport** on the encapsulating box. The port carries that one\nvalue, on its own wire, to whichever downstream box(es) the\nparent wires it to.\n\nThe toggle records the port's binding kind on the box JSON, in\nthe same shape as the input-side toggle:\n\n```json\n{\n    \"id\": \"result_value\",\n    \"kind\": \"write\",\n    \"external\": {\n        \"kind\": \"named\",            // or \"positional\" / \"numbered\"\n        \"name\": \"result\",           // for named\n        \"index\": 0                  // for positional / numbered\n    },\n    \"...\": \"...\"",
