Present on `read` boxes inside a sub-map that should\n * source their value from the encapsulating map's input, and on\n * `write` boxes that should surface their value back to the\n * encapsulating map's output. Absent → external.kind = EXTERNAL_NONE\n * (the box behaves as a normal local read/write).\n *\n * Shape (any of the three is valid):\n *\n *   { \"kind\": \"positional\", \"index\": 0 }\n *   { \"kind\": \"numbered\",   \"index\": 7 }\n *   { \"kind\": \"named\",      \"name\":  \"count\" }\n */\nstatic int parse_external_binding(json_node_t *ext_n, box_t *box,\n                                  const char *box_id, char **err)\n{\n    box->external.kind  = EXTERNAL_NONE;\n    box->external.index = -1;\n    box->external.name  = NULL;\n\n    if (!ext_n) return 0;\n    if (json_kind(ext_n) != JSON_OBJECT) {\n        *err = err_fmt(\"box '%s': 'external' is not an object\", box_id);\n        return -1;\n    }\n    json_node_t *kn = json_object_get(ext_n, \"kind\");\n    if (!kn || json_kind(kn) != JSON_STRING) {\n        *err = err_fmt(\"box '%s': external.kind missing or not a string\", box_id);\n        return -1;\n    }\n    const char *ks = json_string_value(kn);\n    if (strcmp(ks, \"positional\") == 0) box->external.kind = EXTERNAL_POSITIONAL;\n    else if (strcmp(ks, \"numbered\") == 0) box->external.kind = EXTERNAL_NUMBERED;\n    else if (strcmp(ks, \"named\")    == 0) box->external.kind = EXTERNAL_NAMED;\n    else {\n        *err = err_fmt(\"box '%s': external.kind '%s' not recognized \"\n                       \"(positional | numbered | named)\", box_id, ks);\n        return -1;\n    }\n    if (box->external.kind == EXTERNAL_NAMED) {\n        json_node_t *nn = json_object_get(ext_n, \"name\");\n        if (!nn || json_kind(nn) != JSON_STRING) {\n            *err = err_fmt(\"box '%s': external.kind=named requires 'name' string\",\n                           box_id);\n            return -1;\n        }\n        box->external.name = json_string_value(nn);\n    } else {\n        json_node_t *in = json_object_get(ext_n, \"index\");\n        if (!in || json_kind(in) != JSON_NUMBER) {\n            *err = err_fmt(\"box '%s': external.kind=%s requires 'index' number\",\n                           box_id, ks);\n            return -1;\n        }\n        box->external.index = (int)json_number_value(in);\n        if (box->external.index < 0) {\n            *err = err_fmt(\"box '%s': external.index must be >= 0\", box_id);\n            return -1;\n        }\n    }\n    return 0;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ parse_box_file() — read one boxes/<id>.json into a box_t */",
          "file_path":"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech/src/010-graph-loader.c"

Absent → external.kind = EXTERNAL_NONE\n * (the box behaves as a normal local read/write).\n *\n * Shape (any of the three is valid):\n *\n *   { \"kind\": \"positional\", \"index\": 0 }\n *   { \"kind\": \"numbered\",   \"index\": 7 }\n *   { \"kind\": \"named\",      \"name\":  \"count\" }\n */\nstatic int parse_external_binding(json_node_t *ext_n, box_t *box,\n                                  const char *box_id, char **err)\n{\n    box->external.kind  = EXTERNAL_NONE;\n    box->external.index = -1;\n    box->external.name  = NULL;\n\n    if (!ext_n) return 0;\n    if (json_kind(ext_n) != JSON_OBJECT) {\n        *err = err_fmt(\"box '%s': 'external' is not an object\", box_id);\n        return -1;\n    }\n    json_node_t *kn = json_object_get(ext_n, \"kind\");\n    if (!kn || json_kind(kn) != JSON_STRING) {\n        *err = err_fmt(\"box '%s': external.kind missing or not a string\", box_id);\n        return -1;\n    }\n    const char *ks = json_string_value(kn);\n    if (strcmp(ks, \"positional\") == 0) box->external.kind = EXTERNAL_POSITIONAL;\n    else if (strcmp(ks, \"numbered\") == 0) box->external.kind = EXTERNAL_NUMBERED;\n    else if (strcmp(ks, \"named\")    == 0) box->external.kind = EXTERNAL_NAMED;\n    else {\n        *err = err_fmt(\"box '%s': external.kind '%s' not recognized \"\n                       \"(positional | numbered | named)\", box_id, ks);\n        return -1;\n    }\n    if (box->external.kind == EXTERNAL_NAMED) {\n        json_node_t *nn = json_object_get(ext_n, \"name\");\n        if (!nn || json_kind(nn) != JSON_STRING) {\n            *err = err_fmt(\"box '%s': external.kind=named requires 'name' string\",\n                           box_id);\n            return -1;\n        }\n        box->external.name = json_string_value(nn);\n    } else {\n        json_node_t *in = json_object_get(ext_n, \"index\");\n        if (!in || json_kind(in) != JSON_NUMBER) {\n            *err = err_fmt(\"box '%s': external.kind=%s requires 'index' number\",\n                           box_id, ks);\n            return -1;\n        }\n        box->external.index = (int)json_number_value(in);\n        if (box->external.index < 0) {\n            *err = err_fmt(\"box '%s': external.index must be >= 0\", box_id);\n            return -1;\n        }\n    }\n    return 0;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ parse_box_file() — read one boxes/<id>.json into a box_t */"
  },

When neither is set, the box may still be valid if\n         * its `path` arrives at runtime via the input wire — that's\n         * checked in dispatch, not here. */\n        json_node_t *val_n  = json_object_get(n, \"value\");\n        json_node_t *path_n = json_object_get(n, \"path\");\n        if (val_n && json_kind(val_n) == JSON_STRING) {\n            box->value = json_string_value(val_n);\n        }\n        if (path_n && json_kind(path_n) == JSON_STRING) {\n            box->path = json_string_value(path_n);\n        }\n    }\n    /* write boxes: nothing additional beyond inputs. */\n\n    if (parse_inputs(json_object_get(n, \"inputs\"),\n                     box, box->id, err) != 0) return -1;\n    if (parse_connections(json_object_get(n, \"connections\"),\n                          box, box->id, err) != 0) return -1;\n\n    return 0;\n}",

    "newString":"/* {{{ track_owned_str() — remember a heap string to free at destroy */\nstatic int track_owned_str(graph_t *g, char *s)\n{\n    struct owned_str *o = malloc(sizeof *o);\n    if (!o) return -1;\n    o->str  = s;\n    o->next = g->owned_strs;\n    g->owned_strs = o;\n    return 0;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ find_input_port_index() — look up a named input port on a box */\nstatic int find_input_port_index(const box_t *b, const char *port_name)\n{\n    for (int i = 0; i < b->n_inputs; i++) {\n        if (strcmp(b->inputs[i].name, port_name) == 0) return i;\n    }\n    return -1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ find_ext_supplied_for_port() — locate the sub-map's data box\n *\n * Given the encapsulating BOX_MAP and one of its input port indices,\n * scan the sub-map's boxes for the externally-supplied read box that\n * binds to it. Matching rules (issue 248):\n *\n *   positional / numbered — D.external.index == port_idx\n *   named                 — D.external.name  == encap.inputs[port_idx].name\n *\n * The two index-based kinds collapse to the same lookup here; the\n * editor preserves the user-meaningful distinction even though the\n * loader doesn't need it. */\nstatic box_t *find_ext_supplied_for_port(box_t **sub_boxes, int sub_n,\n                                         const box_t *encap, int port_idx)\n{\n    const char *port_name = encap->inputs[port_idx].name;\n    for (int i = 0; i < sub_n; i++) {\n        box_t *d = sub_boxes[i];\n        if (d->kind != BOX_READ) continue;\n        if (d->external.kind == EXTERNAL_NONE) continue;\n        if (d->external.kind == EXTERNAL_NAMED) {\n            if (d->external.name && port_name &&\n                strcmp(d->external.name, port_name) == 0) return d;\n        } else {\n            if (d->external.index == port_idx) return d;\n        }\n    }\n    return NULL;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ load_sub_map_boxes() — parse all boxes/*.json under sub_dir\n *\n * Just the box layer — no meta.json, no topology resolution. Boxes go\n * into a fresh malloc'd array which the caller takes ownership of\n * (and either splices into the parent or frees on error). Strings are\n * arena-allocated in g->arena, same as the parent. */\nstatic int load_sub_map_boxes(graph_t *g, const char *sub_dir,\n                              box_t ***out_boxes, int *out_n, char **err)\n{\n    char boxes_dir[4096];\n    int w = snprintf(boxes_dir, sizeof boxes_dir, \"%s/boxes\", sub_dir);\n    if (w < 0 || w >= (int)sizeof boxes_dir) {\n        *err = err_fmt(\"sub-map boxes path too long\");\n        return -1;\n    }\n\n    int n = count_json_files_in_dir(boxes_dir, err);\n    if (n < 0) return -1;\n    if (n == 0) { *out_boxes = NULL; *out_n = 0; return 0; }\n\n    box_t **arr = calloc((size_t)n, sizeof(box_t *));\n    if (!arr) { *err = err_fmt(\"out of memory\"); return -1; }\n    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {\n        arr[i] = calloc(1, sizeof(box_t));\n        if (!arr[i]) {\n            for (int k = 0; k < i; k++) free(arr[k]);\n            free(arr);\n            *err = err_fmt(\"out of memory\");\n            return -1;\n        }\n    }\n\n    DIR *d = opendir(boxes_dir);\n    if (!d) {\n        for (int k = 0; k < n; k++) free(arr[k]);\n        free(arr);\n        *err = err_fmt(\"cannot open directory '%s'\", boxes_dir);\n        return -1;\n    }\n    int i = 0;\n    struct dirent *e;\n    while ((e = readdir(d))) {\n        if (e->d_name[0] == '.')            continue;\n        if (!ends_with(e->d_name, \".json\")) continue;\n        char path[4096];\n        int wp = snprintf(path, sizeof path, \"%s/%s\", boxes_dir, e->d_name);\n        if (wp < 0 || wp >= (int)sizeof path) {\n            closedir(d);\n            for (int k = 0; k < n; k++) free(arr[k]);\n            free(arr);\n            *err = err_fmt(\"sub-map box path too long\");\n            return -1;\n        }\n        if (parse_box_file(g, arr[i], path, err) != 0) {\n            closedir(d);\n            for (int k = 0; k < n; k++) free(arr[k]);\n            free(arr);\n            return -1;\n        }\n        i++;\n    }\n    closedir(d);\n    *out_boxes = arr;\n    *out_n     = n;\n    return 0;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ inline_one_encapsulation()\n *\n * Splice the sub-map at encap->ref into the parent graph, replacing the\n * BOX_MAP at encap_idx with its sub-map boxes. Input-side rewiring\n * only this slice: each parent wire targeting encap.port_a is replaced\n * with copies pointing to the downstream consumers of the matching\n * externally-supplied data box, preserving from_branch tags.\n *\n * Steps:\n *   1. Resolve sub_dir relative to parent's map_dir.\n *   2. Load sub-map's boxes into a temporary array (separate parse).\n *   3. Prefix-rename every sub-box id with `<encap_id>__<sub_id>`,\n *      then rewrite each sub-box's connections.to_box strings that\n *      reference sibling sub-boxes to the renamed form.\n *   4. For each parent producer, walk its connections; any that target\n *      encap_id get replaced (1→N) by the corresponding ext-supplied\n *      data box's downstream targets.\n *   5. Append sub-boxes to parent's box array (grow capacity if needed).\n *   6. Orphan the encap box (clear its connections; kind stays BOX_MAP\n *      so dispatch's no-op case never confuses it for a live producer).\n *\n * Output-side (externally-consumed write boxes) is deferred to the\n * next slice. Wires originally leaving encap.port_x are dropped.\n */\nstatic int inline_one_encapsulation(graph_t *g, int encap_idx, char **err)\n{\n    box_t **boxes = atomic_load_explicit(&g->boxes, memory_order_relaxed);\n    box_t  *encap = boxes[encap_idx];\n\n    if (!encap->ref) {\n        *err = err_fmt(\"box '%s': BOX_MAP missing 'ref'\", encap->id);\n        return -1;\n    }\n\n    char sub_dir[4096];\n    if (encap->ref[0] == '/') {\n        int w = snprintf(sub_dir, sizeof sub_dir, \"%s\", encap->ref);\n        if (w < 0 || w >= (int)sizeof sub_dir) {\n            *err = err_fmt(\"encap '%s': sub-map path too long\", encap->id);\n            return -1;\n        }\n    } else {\n        int w = snprintf(sub_dir, sizeof sub_dir, \"%s/%s\",\n                         g->map_dir, encap->ref);\n        if (w < 0 || w >= (int)sizeof sub_dir) {\n            *err = err_fmt(\"encap '%s': sub-map path too long\", encap->id);\n            return -1;\n        }\n    }\n\n    box_t **sub_boxes = NULL;\n    int     sub_n     = 0;\n    if (load_sub_map_boxes(g, sub_dir, &sub_boxes, &sub_n, err) != 0) {\n        return -1;\n    }\n\n    /* Save the pre-rename ids so we can rewrite intra-sub-map\n     * connection refs before clobbering the ids on the box records. */\n    const char **old_ids = calloc((size_t)sub_n, sizeof(const char *));\n    char       **new_ids = calloc((size_t)sub_n, sizeof(char *));\n    if ((sub_n > 0 && !old_ids) || (sub_n > 0 && !new_ids)) {\n        free(old_ids); free(new_ids);\n        for (int k = 0; k < sub_n; k++) free(sub_boxes[k]);\n        free(sub_boxes);\n        *err = err_fmt(\"out of memory\");\n        return -1;\n    }\n\n    const char *prefix = encap->id;\n    size_t      plen   = strlen(prefix);\n    for (int i = 0; i < sub_n; i++) {\n        old_ids[i] = sub_boxes[i]->id;\n        size_t need = plen + 2 + strlen(old_ids[i]) + 1;\n        char *nid = malloc(need);\n        if (!nid) {\n            for (int k = 0; k < i; k++) free(new_ids[k]);\n            free(old_ids); free(new_ids);\n            for (int k = 0; k < sub_n; k++) free(sub_boxes[k]);\n            free(sub_boxes);\n            *err = err_fmt(\"out of memory\");\n            return -1;\n        }\n        snprintf(nid, need, \"%s__%s\", prefix, old_ids[i]);\n        new_ids[i] = nid;\n    }\n\n    /* Rewrite intra-sub-map connection refs to use the renamed ids.\n     * Connections that already target an outside-the-sub-map id (which\n     * shouldn't happen at this layer, but guard anyway) are left alone. */\n    for (int i = 0; i < sub_n; i++) {\n        int n_c = atomic_load_explicit(&sub_boxes[i]->n_connections,\n                                       memory_order_relaxed);\n        connection_t *cs =\n            atomic_load_explicit(&sub_boxes[i]->connections,\n                                 memory_order_relaxed);\n        for (int k = 0; k < n_c; k++) {\n            for (int j = 0; j < sub_n; j++) {\n                if (strcmp(cs[k].to_box, old_ids[j]) == 0) {\n                    cs[k].to_box = new_ids[j];\n                    break;\n                }\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    /* Adopt the renamed ids onto the sub-box records. From this point\n     * on, the sub-boxes look like normal parent boxes with namespaced\n     * ids. The malloc'd new_ids strings move into the graph's\n     * owned-strings list. */\n    for (int i = 0; i < sub_n; i++) {\n        sub_boxes[i]->id = new_ids[i];\n        if (track_owned_str(g, new_ids[i]) != 0) {\n            /* Leak the rest of new_ids on this rare failure; we're\n             * about to error out anyway. */\n            free(old_ids); free(new_ids);\n            *err = err_fmt(\"out of memory\");\n            return -1;\n        }\n    }\n    free(new_ids);    /* the strings live on; only the temp array goes */\n\n    /* INPUT-side rewiring. Each parent producer's connection that\n     * targets (encap_id, port) becomes one-or-more new connections\n     * targeting the matching ext-supplied data box's downstreams. */\n    uint32_t cur_n = atomic_load_explicit(&g->n_boxes, memory_order_relaxed);\n    for (uint32_t p = 0; p < cur_n; p++) {\n        box_t *prod = g->boxes[p];\n        if (prod == encap) continue;\n\n        int n_c = atomic_load_explicit(&prod->n_connections,\n                                       memory_order_relaxed);\n        if (n_c == 0) continue;\n        connection_t *cs =\n            atomic_load_explicit(&prod->connections, memory_order_relaxed);\n\n        /* First pass: compute the new array's size. Each connection\n         * to encap explodes to N entries where N = matched data box's\n         * out-degree (potentially 0; that prunes the wire). */\n        int new_cap = 0;\n        int touches_encap = 0;\n        for (int k = 0; k < n_c; k++) {\n            if (strcmp(cs[k].to_box, encap->id) != 0) {\n                new_cap += 1;\n                continue;\n            }\n            touches_encap = 1;\n            int port_idx = find_input_port_index(encap, cs[k].to_input);\n            if (port_idx < 0) {\n                *err = err_fmt(\"encap '%s': producer '%s' wires to unknown \"\n                               \"port '%s'\",\n                               encap->id, prod->id, cs[k].to_input);\n                free(old_ids);\n                return -1;\n            }\n            box_t *D = find_ext_supplied_for_port(sub_boxes, sub_n,\n                                                  encap, port_idx);\n            if (!D) {\n                *err = err_fmt(\"encap '%s': port '%s' has no matching \"\n                               \"externally-supplied data box in sub-map\",\n                               encap->id, cs[k].to_input);\n                free(old_ids);\n                return -1;\n            }\n            new_cap += atomic_load_explicit(&D->n_connections,\n                                            memory_order_relaxed);\n        }\n        if (!touches_encap) continue;\n\n        /* Second pass: build the new array. */\n        connection_t *new_cs =\n            (new_cap > 0) ? calloc((size_t)new_cap, sizeof(connection_t)) : NULL;\n        if (new_cap > 0 && !new_cs) {\n            free(old_ids);\n            *err = err_fmt(\"out of memory\");\n            return -1;\n        }\n        int new_n = 0;\n        for (int k = 0; k < n_c; k++) {\n            if (strcmp(cs[k].to_box, encap->id) != 0) {\n                new_cs[new_n] = cs[k];\n                new_cs[new_n].to_box_idx   = -1;\n                new_cs[new_n].to_input_idx = -1;\n                new_n++;\n                continue;\n            }\n            int port_idx = find_input_port_index(encap, cs[k].to_input);\n            box_t *D = find_ext_supplied_for_port(sub_boxes, sub_n,\n                                                  encap, port_idx);\n            int dn = atomic_load_explicit(&D->n_connections,\n                                          memory_order_relaxed);\n            connection_t *dc =\n                atomic_load_explicit(&D->connections, memory_order_relaxed);\n            for (int j = 0; j < dn; j++) {\n                new_cs[new_n].to_box      = dc[j].to_box;\n                new_cs[new_n].to_input    = dc[j].to_input;\n                new_cs[new_n].from_branch = cs[k].from_branch;\n                new_cs[new_n].to_box_idx   = -1;\n                new_cs[new_n].to_input_idx = -1;\n                new_n++;\n            }\n        }\n\n        free(cs);\n        atomic_store_explicit(&prod->connections, new_cs,\n                              memory_order_release);\n        atomic_store_explicit(&prod->n_connections, new_n,\n                              memory_order_release);\n    }\n    free(old_ids);\n\n    /* Grow the parent's box pointer array if needed and append the\n     * sub-boxes. No atomic publish ordering needed at load time\n     * (single-threaded), but we keep the same shape as graph_add_box\n     * for consistency. */\n    uint32_t cap = atomic_load_explicit(&g->box_capacity,\n                                        memory_order_relaxed);\n    uint32_t want = cur_n + (uint32_t)sub_n;\n    if (want > cap) {\n        uint32_t new_cap = cap ? cap : 16u;\n        while (new_cap < want) new_cap *= 2u;\n        box_t **new_arr = calloc((size_t)new_cap, sizeof(box_t *));\n        if (!new_arr) {\n            for (int k = 0; k < sub_n; k++) free(sub_boxes[k]);\n            free(sub_boxes);\n            *err = err_fmt(\"out of memory\");\n            return -1;\n        }\n        box_t **old_arr =\n            atomic_load_explicit(&g->boxes, memory_order_relaxed);\n        if (old_arr) {\n            memcpy(new_arr, old_arr, cur_n * sizeof(box_t *));\n            struct stale_arr *st = malloc(sizeof *st);\n            if (st) { st->ptr = old_arr; st->next = g->stale_box_arrs;\n                      g->stale_box_arrs = st; }\n        }\n        atomic_store_explicit(&g->boxes, new_arr, memory_order_release);\n        atomic_store_explicit(&g->box_capacity, new_cap,\n                              memory_order_release);\n    }\n    box_t **arr = atomic_load_explicit(&g->boxes, memory_order_relaxed);\n    for (int i = 0; i < sub_n; i++) {\n        arr[cur_n + (uint32_t)i] = sub_boxes[i];\n    }\n    atomic_store_explicit(&g->n_boxes, cur_n + (uint32_t)sub_n,\n                          memory_order_release);\n    free(sub_boxes);\n\n    /* Orphan the encap box. Its outgoing connections (if any) were\n     * the output-side wiring path which this slice doesn't implement\n     * yet; dropping them means any wires the user drew from encap's\n     * output ports won't fire. The box itself stays in the index\n     * (so its slot id remains valid for any unfixed references) but\n     * becomes inert — BOX_MAP has a no-op dispatch case. */\n    int n_old_out = atomic_load_explicit(&encap->n_connections,\n                                         memory_order_relaxed);\n    connection_t *old_out =\n        atomic_load_explicit(&encap->connections, memory_order_relaxed);\n    (void)n_old_out;\n    if (old_out) {\n        free(old_out);\n        atomic_store_explicit(&encap->connections, NULL,\n                              memory_order_release);\n        atomic_store_explicit(&encap->n_connections, 0,\n                              memory_order_release);\n    }\n\n    return 0;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ inline_encapsulations() — splice every BOX_MAP into the graph\n *\n * Iterates until no BOX_MAP remains. Sub-maps that themselves contain\n * a BOX_MAP get picked up on the next iteration once their boxes are\n * in the parent list. A high iteration bound guards against\n * pathological recursion (which would also imply a cycle, caught\n * later by detect_cycles in the flat form). */\nstatic int inline_encapsulations(graph_t *g, char **err)\n{\n    for (int iter = 0; iter < 1024; iter++) {\n        uint32_t n = atomic_load_explicit(&g->n_boxes,\n                                          memory_order_relaxed);\n        box_t **boxes =\n            atomic_load_explicit(&g->boxes, memory_order_relaxed);\n        int found = -1;\n        for (uint32_t i = 0; i < n; i++) {\n            if (boxes[i]->kind == BOX_MAP) { found = (int)i; break; }\n        }\n        if (found < 0) return 0;\n        if (inline_one_encapsulation(g, found, err) != 0) return -1;\n    }\n    *err = err_fmt(\"inline_encapsulations: exceeded recursion limit (1024) \"\n                   \"— likely a sub-map cycle\");\n    return -1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ graph_load() */"

      "content":"/* {{{ cache_read_box_values() — issue 244\n *\n * Every BOX_READ's downstream value lives on its box record from\n * graph_load onward. Inline `value` literals are strdup'd; `path`\n * fields trigger a one-time file read whose bytes become the cache.\n * Once cached the read box never re-reads — its value is the run's\n * source of truth. */\nstatic int cache_read_box_values(graph_t *g, char **err)\n{\n    for (int i = 0; i < g->n_boxes; i++) {\n        box_t *b = g->boxes[i];\n        if (b->kind != BOX_READ) continue;\n\n        if (b->value) {\n            int n = (int)strlen(b->value);\n            b->cached_value = malloc((size_t)n + 1);\n            if (!b->cached_value) { *err = err_fmt(\"oom\"); return -1; }\n            memcpy(b->cached_value, b->value, (size_t)n);\n            b->cached_value[n] = '\\0';\n            b->cached_size = n;\n            continue;\n        }\n        if (!b->path) {\n            /* No value, no path — error surfaces only if a consumer\n             * actually tries to pull from this box, but flagging at\n             * load is louder. Future iterations may allow `path`\n             * inputs that arrive at run time; for now an unconfigured\n             * read box is a load failure. */\n            *err = err_fmt(\"read box '%s' has neither 'value' nor 'path'\", b->id);\n            return -1;\n        }\n\n        /* Resolve `path` relative to the map directory and slurp the\n         * file. The graph holds onto these bytes for the life of\n         * the run. */\n        const char *base = g->map_dir;\n        size_t blen = base ? strlen(base) : 0;\n        size_t plen = strlen(b->path);\n        char *full = malloc(blen + 1 + plen + 1);\n        if (!full) { *err = err_fmt(\"oom\"); return -1; }\n        if (b->path[0] == '/') {\n            memcpy(full, b->path, plen + 1);\n        } else if (blen > 0) {\n            memcpy(full, base, blen);\n            full[blen] = '/';\n            memcpy(full + blen + 1, b->path, plen + 1);\n        } else {\n            memcpy(full, b->path, plen + 1);\n        }\n\n        FILE *fp = fopen(full, \"rb\");\n        if (!fp) {\n            *err = err_fmt(\"read box '%s': cannot open '%s'\", b->id, full);\n            free(full);\n            return -1;\n        }\n        free(full);\n        fseek(fp, 0, SEEK_END);\n        long len = ftell(fp);\n        fseek(fp, 0, SEEK_SET);\n        if (len < 0) {\n            *err = err_fmt(\"read box '%s': ftell failed\", b->id);\n            fclose(fp);\n            return -1;\n        }\n        b->cached_value = malloc((size_t)len + 1);\n        if (!b->cached_value) {\n            *err = err_fmt(\"oom\");\n            fclose(fp);\n            return -1;\n        }\n        size_t got = fread(b->cached_value, 1, (size_t)len, fp);\n        fclose(fp);\n        b->cached_value[got] = '\\0';\n        b->cached_size = (int)got;",

      "content":"/* {{{ build_read_predecessor_lists() — issue 244\n *\n * For every call / write box, walk each input port and collect the\n * indices of any BOX_READ producers feeding it. The list lives on\n * the consumer's box record so dispatch can pull on demand without\n * a full graph scan. Reuses scan_input_feeders only indirectly —\n * we need the producer indices, not just counts, and the existing\n * helper doesn't expose them. The walk is small enough that an\n * inline loop is clearer than threading a callback through. */\nstatic int build_read_predecessor_lists(graph_t *g, char **err)\n{\n    for (int i = 0; i < g->n_boxes; i++) {\n        box_t *b = g->boxes[i];\n        /* The kinds that run as tasks. BOX_CREATE_BOX and BOX_CONNECT\n         * join the list with the box-kind path for runtime self-\n         * construction (319 design-correction). BOX_READ never runs\n         * as a task (it's pull-on-demand per issue 244). */\n        if (b->kind != BOX_CALL && b->kind != BOX_WRITE &&\n            b->kind != BOX_CREATE_BOX && b->kind != BOX_CONNECT) continue;\n        if (b->n_inputs <= 0) continue;\n\n        b->n_read_predecessors    = calloc((size_t)b->n_inputs, sizeof(int));\n        b->read_predecessor_ids   = calloc((size_t)b->n_inputs, sizeof(int *));\n        b->read_pred_counter_slot = malloc((size_t)b->n_inputs * sizeof(int));\n        if (!b->n_read_predecessors || !b->read_predecessor_ids ||\n            !b->read_pred_counter_slot) {\n            *err = err_fmt(\"oom\");\n            return -1;\n        }\n        for (int p = 0; p < b->n_inputs; p++) b->read_pred_counter_slot[p] = -1;\n\n        for (int port = 0; port < b->n_inputs; port++) {\n            /* First pass: count. */\n            int n = 0;\n            for (int p = 0; p < g->n_boxes; p++) {\n                const box_t *prod = g->boxes[p];\n                if (prod->kind != BOX_READ) continue;\n                for (int k = 0; k < prod->n_connections; k++) {\n                    const connection_t *c = &prod->connections[k];\n                    if (c->to_box_idx == i && c->to_input_idx == port) n++;\n                }\n            }\n            if (n == 0) continue;\n\n            int *ids = malloc((size_t)n * sizeof(int));\n            if (!ids) { *err = err_fmt(\"oom\"); return -1; }\n\n            /* Second pass: fill. */\n            int idx = 0;\n            for (int p = 0; p < g->n_boxes; p++) {\n                const box_t *prod = g->boxes[p];\n                if (prod->kind != BOX_READ) continue;\n                for (int k = 0; k < prod->n_connections; k++) {\n                    const connection_t *c = &prod->connections[k];\n                    if (c->to_box_idx == i && c->to_input_idx == port) {\n                        ids[idx++] = p;\n                    }\n                }\n            }\n            b->n_read_predecessors[port]  = n;",

    "stdout":"#!/bin/bash\n# scripts/run-tests.sh — phase 3 integration tests.\n#\n# Runs every fixture map under tests/maps/ through `soramech-pool`\n# and asserts that the captured outputs match a hardcoded\n# expectation per map. The point is to catch regressions\n# end-to-end — past the spec interface, past the dispatch action,\n# past JSONL writing — rather than via the in-process unit tests.\n#\n# Per the project convention: scripts run from any directory via a\n# hard-coded ${DIR} path with an override argument; all paths are\n# relative to ${DIR}.\n\nset -u\n\nDIR=\"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech\"\nif [[ $# -ge 1 ]]; then\n    DIR=\"$1\"\nfi\n\ncd \"$DIR\"\n\npass=0\nfail=0\nfailures=()\n\n# {{{ check_map() — run one fixture, verify expected substrings\ncheck_map() {\n    local map=\"$1\"\n    shift\n    local expected=(\"$@\")\n\n    printf \"  %-44s \" \"$map\"\n\n    local output\n    # Per-map env opt-in: a map may set SORAMECH_TEST_WORKERS to\n    # pin worker count for tests that depend on per-worker state\n    # (e.g. issue 318's $lang_opaque, which lives in the producer's\n    # Lua registry and can only be reconstructed by a consumer on\n    # the same worker).\n    local workers_env=\"\"\n    if [[ -f \"$DIR/tests/maps/$map/.test_workers\" ]]; then\n        workers_env=$(cat \"$DIR/tests/maps/$map/.test_workers\")\n    fi\n    if [[ -n \"$workers_env\" ]]; then\n        output=$(SORAMECH_WORKERS=\"$workers_env\" \"$DIR/soramech-pool\" \"$DIR/tests/maps/$map\" 2>&1)\n    else\n        output=$(\"$DIR/soramech-pool\" \"$DIR/tests/maps/$map\" 2>&1)\n    fi\n    local rc=$?\n\n    local missing=\"\"\n    if [[ $rc -ne 0 ]]; then\n        missing=\"exit=$rc\"\n    fi\n    for e in \"${expected[@]}\"; do\n        if [[ \"$output\" != *\"$e\"* ]]; then\n            missing+=\"${missing:+; }missing '$e'\"\n        fi\n    done\n\n    if [[ -z \"$missing\" ]]; then\n        printf \"ok\\n\"\n        pass=$((pass + 1))\n    else\n        printf \"FAIL — %s\\n\" \"$missing\"\n        fail=$((fail + 1))\n        failures+=(\"$map: $missing\")\n    fi\n}\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ pipeline_output_check() — additional: the pipeline writes to disk\npipeline_output_check() {\n    local file=\"/tmp/soramech-pipeline-out.txt\"\n    rm -f \"$file\"\n    \"$DIR/soramech-pool\" \"$DIR/tests/maps/pipeline\" > /dev/null 2>&1\n    printf \"  %-44s \" \"pipeline write output\"\n    if [[ -f \"$file\" ]]; then\n        local content\n        content=$(cat \"$file\")\n        if [[ \"$content\" == \"11!\" ]]; then\n            printf \"ok\\n\"\n            pass=$((pass + 1))\n        else\n            printf \"FAIL — expected '11!', got '%s'\\n\" \"$content\"\n            fail=$((fail + 1))\n            failures+=(\"pipeline file: $content\")\n        fi\n    else\n        printf \"FAIL — output file missing\\n\"\n        fail=$((fail + 1))\n        failures+=(\"pipeline: $file missing\")\n    fi\n}\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ compile_pipeline_check() — soramech-compile produces a portable artifact\n# Verifies issue 309's compile pipeline: bundles all spec.so + sources\n# into compiled/, then runs the artifact from /tmp (i.e. with no\n# dependency on the project's cwd) and verifies it produces the same\n# output as the source map.\ncompile_pipeline_check() {\n    local map=\"$DIR/tests/maps/pipeline\"\n    local compiled=\"$map/compiled\"\n    local file=\"/tmp/soramech-pipeline-out.txt\"\n\n    printf \"  %-44s \" \"compile pipeline (portable run)\"\n\n    rm -rf \"$compiled\"\n    if ! \"$DIR/scripts/soramech-compile.sh\" \"$map\" --dir \"$DIR\" >/dev/null 2>&1; then\n        printf \"FAIL — soramech-compile failed\\n\"\n        fail=$((fail + 1))\n        failures+=(\"compile: script returned non-zero\")\n        return\n    fi\n    if [[ ! -x \"$compiled/pool-runner\" ]]; then\n        printf \"FAIL — compiled/pool-runner missing or not executable\\n\"\n        fail=$((fail + 1))\n        failures+=(\"compile: pool-runner missing\")\n        return\n    fi\n\n    rm -f \"$file\"\n    local output\n    output=$(cd /tmp && \"$compiled/pool-runner\" \"$compiled\" 2>&1)\n\n    local content=\"\"\n    [[ -f \"$file\" ]] && content=$(cat \"$file\")\n\n    if [[ \"$output\" == *\"addone → 11\"* ]] && [[ \"$content\" == \"11!\" ]]; then\n        printf \"ok\\n\"\n        pass=$((pass + 1))\n    else\n        printf \"FAIL — output='%s' file='%s'\\n\" \"$output\" \"$content\"\n        fail=$((fail + 1))\n        failures+=(\"compile: bad output\")\n    fi\n}\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ run all fixtures\necho \"integration tests (fixture maps):\"\n\ncheck_map \"calc\" \\\n    \"add → 42\"\n\ncheck_map \"hello\" \\\n    \"greet → Hello, World!\"\n\ncheck_map \"comparator\" \\\n    \"classify → 8\" \\\n    \"high → HIGH:8\" \\\n    \"low → (no output)\" \\\n    \"mid → (no output)\"\n\ncheck_map \"iter-route\" \\\n    \"iter → hi\" \\\n    \"a → A:hi\" \\\n    \"b → (no output)\" \\\n    \"c → (no output)\"\n\ncheck_map \"pipeline\" \\\n    \"double → 10\" \\\n    \"addone → 11\" \\\n    \"shout → 11!\"\n\ncheck_map \"read-literal\" \\\n    \"echo → hello, world!\"\n\ncheck_map \"319a-many-inputs\" \\\n    \"combine → count=20 sum=210\"\n\ncheck_map \"319d-runtime-create\" \\\n    \"trigger → trigger-fired:auto_\" \\\n    \"auto_\" \\\n    \"echo_dyn-received:trigger-fired:auto_\"\n\ncheck_map \"319e-c-create\" \\\n    \"trigger → c-trigger-fired:auto_\" \\\n    \"c-echo-received:c-trigger-fired:auto_\"\n\ncheck_map \"246-c-shim\" \\\n    \"echo → seen:HELLO-FROM-SEED\"\n\ncheck_map \"246-lua-shim\" \\\n    \"echo → seen:REV-fedcba\"\n\n# Issue 318 — the producer's output proves the emit side works\n# end-to-end (Lua function → $lang_opaque sentinel in JSON). The\n# consumer's reconstruction needs the dual-ring slot to surface\n# \"I was written as JSON\" to the same-language consumer, which is\n# a deeper per-edge classification issue documented in 318's\n# closeout; the emit fixture stands today.\ncheck_map \"318-lang-opaque\" \\\n    '\"$lang_opaque\"' \\\n    '\"lang\":\"lua\"' \\\n    '\"shape\":\"function\"' \\\n    'consumer → doubled=42'\n\n# Language-agnostic create_box / connect box kinds (319\n# design-correction follow-on). A read box emits a box spec; a\n# create_box-kind box consumes it; the new box's id is captured\n# downstream. No per-language wrapper involved — same shape works\n# for Lua, C, and Bash producers.\ncheck_map \"319-box-kind-create\" \\\n    \"creator → auto_\"\n\n# 319 auto-init follow-on: a C trigger creates a Lua box at\n# runtime; the Lua spec wasn't in the static graph's language set,\n# so the worker's Lua handle was NULL at pool startup. The\n# dispatch's lazy-init populates the handle on demand and the new\n# box fires.\ncheck_map \"319-cross-lang-create\" \\\n    \"trigger → c-trigger-fired:auto_\" \\\n    \"lua-echo-from-runtime-init:c-trigger-fired:auto_\"\n\npipeline_output_check\ncompile_pipeline_check\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ parser_tests() — issue 232: unit tests for langs/<lang>/parser.js\n# Run Node's built-in test runner over each per-language parser test\n# file and fold the result into the surrounding pass/fail counters.\n# Each .mjs file is one logical \"test\" from this script's perspective;\n# Node prints its own subtest breakdown on failure for the diagnostic.\nparser_tests() {\n    if ! command -v node >/dev/null 2>&1; then\n        printf \"  %-44s SKIP — node not installed\\n\" \"parser tests (lua, bash)\"\n        return\n    fi\n    for tf in \"$DIR/tests/232-lua-parser-test.mjs\" \\\n              \"$DIR/tests/233-bash-parser-test.mjs\" \\\n              \"$DIR/tests/234-language-spec-js-test.mjs\"; do\n        local label\n        label=$(basename \"$tf\")\n        printf \"  %-44s \" \"$label\"\n        local out\n        out=$(SORAMECH_DIR=\"$DIR\" node --test \"$tf\" 2>&1)\n        local rc=$?\n        if [[ $rc -eq 0 ]]; then\n            printf \"ok\\n\"\n            pass=$((pass + 1))\n        else\n            printf \"FAIL\\n\"\n            echo \"$out\" | sed 's/^/      /'\n            fail=$((fail + 1))\n            failures+=(\"$label: node --test exit=$rc\")\n        fi\n    done\n}\nparser_tests\n# }}}\n\necho\necho \"  $pass passed, $fail failed\"\n\nif [[ $fail -gt 0 ]]; then\n    echo\n    echo \"  failures:\"\n    for f in \"${failures[@]}\"; do\n        echo \"    - $f\"\n    done\nfi\n\nexit $fail",

    "originalFile":"#!/bin/bash\n# scripts/run-tests.sh — phase 3 integration tests.\n#\n# Runs every fixture map under tests/maps/ through `soramech-pool`\n# and asserts that the captured outputs match a hardcoded\n# expectation per map. The point is to catch regressions\n# end-to-end — past the spec interface, past the dispatch action,\n# past JSONL writing — rather than via the in-process unit tests.\n#\n# Per the project convention: scripts run from any directory via a\n# hard-coded ${DIR} path with an override argument; all paths are\n# relative to ${DIR}.\n\nset -u\n\nDIR=\"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech\"\nif [[ $# -ge 1 ]]; then\n    DIR=\"$1\"\nfi\n\ncd \"$DIR\"\n\npass=0\nfail=0\nfailures=()\n\n# {{{ check_map() — run one fixture, verify expected substrings\ncheck_map() {\n    local map=\"$1\"\n    shift\n    local expected=(\"$@\")\n\n    printf \"  %-44s \" \"$map\"\n\n    local output\n    # Per-map env opt-in: a map may set SORAMECH_TEST_WORKERS to\n    # pin worker count for tests that depend on per-worker state\n    # (e.g. issue 318's $lang_opaque, which lives in the producer's\n    # Lua registry and can only be reconstructed by a consumer on\n    # the same worker).\n    local workers_env=\"\"\n    if [[ -f \"$DIR/tests/maps/$map/.test_workers\" ]]; then\n        workers_env=$(cat \"$DIR/tests/maps/$map/.test_workers\")\n    fi\n    if [[ -n \"$workers_env\" ]]; then\n        output=$(SORAMECH_WORKERS=\"$workers_env\" \"$DIR/soramech-pool\" \"$DIR/tests/maps/$map\" 2>&1)\n    else\n        output=$(\"$DIR/soramech-pool\" \"$DIR/tests/maps/$map\" 2>&1)\n    fi\n    local rc=$?\n\n    local missing=\"\"\n    if [[ $rc -ne 0 ]]; then\n        missing=\"exit=$rc\"\n    fi\n    for e in \"${expected[@]}\"; do\n        if [[ \"$output\" != *\"$e\"* ]]; then\n            missing+=\"${missing:+; }missing '$e'\"\n        fi\n    done\n\n    if [[ -z \"$missing\" ]]; then\n        printf \"ok\\n\"\n        pass=$((pass + 1))\n    else\n        printf \"FAIL — %s\\n\" \"$missing\"\n        fail=$((fail + 1))\n        failures+=(\"$map: $missing\")\n    fi\n}\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ pipeline_output_check() — additional: the pipeline writes to disk\npipeline_output_check() {\n    local file=\"/tmp/soramech-pipeline-out.txt\"\n    rm -f \"$file\"\n    \"$DIR/soramech-pool\" \"$DIR/tests/maps/pipeline\" > /dev/null 2>&1\n    printf \"  %-44s \" \"pipeline write output\"\n    if [[ -f \"$file\" ]]; then\n        local content\n        content=$(cat \"$file\")\n        if [[ \"$content\" == \"11!\" ]]; then\n            printf \"ok\\n\"\n            pass=$((pass + 1))\n        else\n            printf \"FAIL — expected '11!', got '%s'\\n\" \"$content\"\n            fail=$((fail + 1))\n            failures+=(\"pipeline file: $content\")\n        fi\n    else\n        printf \"FAIL — output file missing\\n\"\n        fail=$((fail + 1))\n        failures+=(\"pipeline: $file missing\")\n    fi\n}\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ compile_pipeline_check() — soramech-compile produces a portable artifact\n# Verifies issue 309's compile pipeline: bundles all spec.so + sources\n# into compiled/, then runs the artifact from /tmp (i.e. with no\n# dependency on the project's cwd) and verifies it produces the same\n# output as the source map.\ncompile_pipeline_check() {\n    local map=\"$DIR/tests/maps/pipeline\"\n    local compiled=\"$map/compiled\"\n    local file=\"/tmp/soramech-pipeline-out.txt\"\n\n    printf \"  %-44s \" \"compile pipeline (portable run)\"\n\n    rm -rf \"$compiled\"\n    if ! \"$DIR/scripts/soramech-compile.sh\" \"$map\" --dir \"$DIR\" >/dev/null 2>&1; then\n        printf \"FAIL — soramech-compile failed\\n\"\n        fail=$((fail + 1))\n        failures+=(\"compile: script returned non-zero\")\n        return\n    fi\n    if [[ ! -x \"$compiled/pool-runner\" ]]; then\n        printf \"FAIL — compiled/pool-runner missing or not executable\\n\"\n        fail=$((fail + 1))\n        failures+=(\"compile: pool-runner missing\")\n        return\n    fi\n\n    rm -f \"$file\"\n    local output\n    output=$(cd /tmp && \"$compiled/pool-runner\" \"$compiled\" 2>&1)\n\n    local content=\"\"\n    [[ -f \"$file\" ]] && content=$(cat \"$file\")\n\n    if [[ \"$output\" == *\"addone → 11\"* ]] && [[ \"$content\" == \"11!\" ]]; then\n        printf \"ok\\n\"\n        pass=$((pass + 1))\n    else\n        printf \"FAIL — output='%s' file='%s'\\n\" \"$output\" \"$content\"\n        fail=$((fail + 1))\n        failures+=(\"compile: bad output\")\n    fi\n}\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ run all fixtures\necho \"integration tests (fixture maps):\"\n\ncheck_map \"calc\" \\\n    \"add → 42\"\n\ncheck_map \"hello\" \\\n    \"greet → Hello, World!\"\n\ncheck_map \"comparator\" \\\n    \"classify → 8\" \\\n    \"high → HIGH:8\" \\\n    \"low → (no output)\" \\\n    \"mid → (no output)\"\n\ncheck_map \"iter-route\" \\\n    \"iter → hi\" \\\n    \"a → A:hi\" \\\n    \"b → (no output)\" \\\n    \"c → (no output)\"\n\ncheck_map \"pipeline\" \\\n    \"double → 10\" \\\n    \"addone → 11\" \\\n    \"shout → 11!\"\n\ncheck_map \"read-literal\" \\\n    \"echo → hello, world!\"\n\ncheck_map \"319a-many-inputs\" \\\n    \"combine → count=20 sum=210\"\n\ncheck_map \"319d-runtime-create\" \\\n    \"trigger → trigger-fired:auto_\" \\\n    \"auto_\" \\\n    \"echo_dyn-received:trigger-fired:auto_\"\n\ncheck_map \"319e-c-create\" \\\n    \"trigger → c-trigger-fired:auto_\" \\\n    \"c-echo-received:c-trigger-fired:auto_\"\n\ncheck_map \"246-c-shim\" \\\n    \"echo → seen:HELLO-FROM-SEED\"\n\ncheck_map \"246-lua-shim\" \\\n    \"echo → seen:REV-fedcba\"\n\n# Issue 318 — the producer's output proves the emit side works\n# end-to-end (Lua function → $lang_opaque sentinel in JSON). The\n# consumer's reconstruction needs the dual-ring slot to surface\n# \"I was written as JSON\" to the same-language consumer, which is\n# a deeper per-edge classification issue documented in 318's\n# closeout; the emit fixture stands today.\ncheck_map \"318-lang-opaque\" \\\n    '\"$lang_opaque\"' \\\n    '\"lang\":\"lua\"' \\\n    '\"shape\":\"function\"' \\\n    'consumer → doubled=42'\n\n# Language-agnostic create_box / connect box kinds (319\n# design-correction follow-on). A read box emits a box spec; a\n# create_box-kind box consumes it; the new box's id is captured\n# downstream. No per-language wrapper involved — same shape works\n# for Lua, C, and Bash producers.\ncheck_map \"319-box-kind-create\" \\\n    \"creator → auto_\"\n\n# 319 auto-init follow-on: a C trigger creates a Lua box at\n# runtime; the Lua spec wasn't in the static graph's language set,\n# so the worker's Lua handle was NULL at pool startup. The\n# dispatch's lazy-init populates the handle on demand and the new\n# box fires.\ncheck_map \"319-cross-lang-create\" \\\n    \"trigger → c-trigger-fired:auto_\" \\\n    \"lua-echo-from-runtime-init:c-trigger-fired:auto_\"\n\npipeline_output_check\ncompile_pipeline_check\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ parser_tests() — issue 232: unit tests for langs/<lang>/parser.js\n# Run Node's built-in test runner over each per-language parser test\n# file and fold the result into the surrounding pass/fail counters.\n# Each .mjs file is one logical \"test\" from this script's perspective;\n# Node prints its own subtest breakdown on failure for the diagnostic.\nparser_tests() {\n    if ! command -v node >/dev/null 2>&1; then\n        printf \"  %-44s SKIP — node not installed\\n\" \"parser tests (lua, bash)\"\n        return\n    fi\n    for tf in \"$DIR/tests/232-lua-parser-test.mjs\" \\\n              \"$DIR/tests/233-bash-parser-test.mjs\" \\\n              \"$DIR/tests/234-language-spec-js-test.mjs\"; do\n        local label\n        label=$(basename \"$tf\")\n        printf \"  %-44s \" \"$label\"\n        local out\n        out=$(SORAMECH_DIR=\"$DIR\" node --test \"$tf\" 2>&1)\n        local rc=$?\n        if [[ $rc -eq 0 ]]; then\n            printf \"ok\\n\"\n            pass=$((pass + 1))\n        else\n            printf \"FAIL\\n\"\n            echo \"$out\" | sed 's/^/      /'\n            fail=$((fail + 1))\n            failures+=(\"$label: node --test exit=$rc\")\n        fi\n    done\n}\nparser_tests\n# }}}\n\necho\necho \"  $pass passed, $fail failed\"\n\nif [[ $fail -gt 0 ]]; then\n    echo\n    echo \"  failures:\"\n    for f in \"${failures[@]}\"; do\n        echo \"    - $f\"\n    done\nfi\n\nexit $fail\n",

          "old_string":"# 248 — Encapsulated map as box\n\n## Status\nopen\n\n## Concept",
          "replace_all":false,
          "new_string":"# 248 — Encapsulated map as box\n\n## Status\nin progress · input-side load-time inlining shipped; output-side\n(ext-consumed write boxes), editor UI, and recursion across mixed\next-consumed wires deferred\n\n## Current behavior\n\nInput-side encapsulation runs at graph load. The loader recognizes\n`kind: \"map\"` with a `ref` to a sub-map directory. A new pass between\n`load_boxes` and `resolve_topology` walks every BOX_MAP record,\nloads the sub-map's boxes into the parent's arena, prefix-renames\ntheir ids with `<encap_id>__<sub_id>`, splices them into the parent's\nflat box list, then rewires each parent producer's connection that\ntargeted the encapsulating box. The rewire splices THROUGH the\nexternally-supplied data box: each parent wire to `encap.port` is\nreplaced with copies pointing to the matching data box's\ndownstreams, preserving each from_branch tag. Externally-supplied\ndata boxes are matched to the encapsulating box's input ports by\nthe issue's three binding kinds (positional / numbered by index,\nnamed by string).\n\nAfter inlining, the encap box stays in the index but is inert\n(connections cleared, `ref` stripped — the loader skips it on\nsubsequent passes, dispatch's BOX_MAP case is a logged no-op). The\next-supplied data box is also orphaned (its outgoing connections\nwere absorbed into the parent producer; the cache pass skips it so\nthe \"neither value nor path\" check doesn't reject the value-less\nshape).\n\nThe end-to-end fixture `tests/maps/248-encap-input-only/` proves\nthe splice reaches disk: a parent read box wires\n`\"encapsulated-greeting\"` to a BOX_MAP whose sub-map has one\nexternally-supplied data box feeding a write box; the parent's\nbytes land in `/tmp/soramech-248-encap-out.txt`.\n\nOutput-side encapsulation (externally-consumed write boxes\nsurfacing as the encap's output ports) is not yet wired. Wires\nthe user drew from `encap.port_x` to a parent consumer don't fire\nin this slice. The editor toggles, file-browser Encapsulate\naction, and the multi-output exception to issue 218 also remain\nahead.\n\n## Concept",
          "file_path":"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech/issues/248-encapsulated-map-as-box.md"
        },
        "caller":{
          "type":"direct"
        },

        "type":"tool_use"
      }],

A new pass between\n`load_boxes` and `resolve_topology` walks every BOX_MAP record,\nloads the sub-map's boxes into the parent's arena, prefix-renames\ntheir ids with `<encap_id>__<sub_id>`, splices them into the parent's\nflat box list, then rewires each parent producer's connection that\ntargeted the encapsulating box. The rewire splices THROUGH the\nexternally-supplied data box: each parent wire to `encap.port` is\nreplaced with copies pointing to the matching data box's\ndownstreams, preserving each from_branch tag. Externally-supplied\ndata boxes are matched to the encapsulating box's input ports by\nthe issue's three binding kinds (positional / numbered by index,\nnamed by string).\n\nAfter inlining, the encap box stays in the index but is inert\n(connections cleared, `ref` stripped — the loader skips it on\nsubsequent passes, dispatch's BOX_MAP case is a logged no-op). The\next-supplied data box is also orphaned (its outgoing connections\nwere absorbed into the parent producer; the cache pass skips it so\nthe \"neither value nor path\" check doesn't reject the value-less\nshape).\n\nThe end-to-end fixture `tests/maps/248-encap-input-only/` proves\nthe splice reaches disk: a parent read box wires\n`\"encapsulated-greeting\"` to a BOX_MAP whose sub-map has one\nexternally-supplied data box feeding a write box; the parent's\nbytes land in `/tmp/soramech-248-encap-out.txt`.\n\nOutput-side encapsulation (externally-consumed write boxes\nsurfacing as the encap's output ports) is not yet wired. Wires\nthe user drew from `encap.port_x` to a parent consumer don't fire\nin this slice. The editor toggles, file-browser Encapsulate\naction, and the multi-output exception to issue 218 also remain\nahead.\n\n## Concept"
  },

Output-side\n(externally-consumed write boxes surfacing as the encap's output\nports) and editor UI are tracked as deferred on the issue.\n\nCo-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>\nEOF\n)\"",

The orphaned BOX_MAP record stays in the index (cheap) and a stripped `ref` signals \"already handled\" to the loop — invariant-by-discriminator-erasure is a quieter pattern than a parallel \"inlined\" flag.\n`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`\n\nWhat shipped:\n- Loader recognizes `kind: \"map\"` + the `external` block (positional / numbered / named) on data and write boxes (`src/010-graph-loader.{c,h}`).\n- New pass `inline_encapsulations` splices each sub-map into the parent's flat list with `<encap>__<sub>` ids, rewires parent producers' wires through the matching ext-supplied data box, preserves routing branch tags, and orphans both the encap record and the data box.\n- Dispatch has a no-op BOX_MAP case so a stray reach can't crash.\n- End-to-end fixture (`tests/maps/248-encap-input-only/` + `248-encap-sub-input/`) plus a disk-file check in `run-tests.sh` proves the parent's bytes reach the sub-map's write box.\n\nDeferred (still on the issue): output-side (externally-consumed write boxes), editor toggles + file-browser Encapsulate action, multi-output exception to issue 218. ## [3868]

```json
{
  "slug":"optimized-skipping-umbrella",
  "uuid":"cd4261c8-f343-4b11-a9a1-7c85dc0d5549",
  "type":"user",
  "timestamp":"2026-05-24T04:36:58.714Z",
  "parentUuid":"c754fcb8-c251-4670-8270-1c268af5c29b",
  "toolUseResult":{
    "type":"text",
    "file":{
      "numLines":272,
      "startLine":1,
      "totalLines":272,
      "content":"# 315 — Reference-counted compiled-map artifacts\n\n## Status\nopen\n\n## Current behavior\n\n`scripts/soramech-compile.sh` from issue 309 is destructive at the\ntop:\n\n```bash\nrm -rf \"$COMPILED\"\nmkdir -p \"$COMPILED\" \"$COMPILED/boxes\" \"$COMPILED/src\" ...\n```\n\nWhatever lived in `<map>/compiled/` before the rebuild is gone. If\nanother process — a long-running runner, a different shell, a\nsibling tool that opened the artifact yesterday — had pinned to\nthat exact compiled layout (a particular `pool-runner` binary, a\nparticular `spec.so` ABI, a particular set of pre-compiled C\nboxes), the rebuild yanks the rug. The holder either crashes,\nsilently retains stale `dlopen` handles, or starts reading new\nfiles mid-flight.\n\nThis is fine in single-user development. It stops being fine the\nmoment a SoraMech artifact is the kind of thing other programs\nhold onto across time.\n\n## Intended behavior\n\nA compiled artifact carries its own reference count. Other\nprograms that depend on a particular build of a map are expected\nto *acquire* a reference on startup and *release* it on shutdown.\nWhen `soramech-compile` is asked to rebuild a map that has any\nlive references, it does NOT clobber the existing directory.\nInstead it builds a sibling directory next door, leaving the\nreferenced one untouched until its holders are done with it.\n\nThe reference count is **expected to be unreliable**. A crashing\nholder doesn't get the chance to release; an SSH session that\ndrops doesn't either. The design accepts that staleness is the\ncommon case, not the exception — every reference entry carries\nenough metadata to be independently validated and (eventually)\nreaped. The reference count is a hint and a courtesy, not a\nguarantee.\n\nThis is conceptually a copy-on-write filesystem for compiled\nartifacts: writes (rebuilds) fork the universe when readers\nexist; readers can keep reading the version they pinned to;\ngenerations get garbage-collected when nothing observable still\npoints at them.\n\n## Concept\n\nA compiled directory contains a `.refs` file (hidden, dot-prefixed\nso it doesn't clutter directory listings). It's append-only by\ndesign — concurrent acquires never need to take a lock; concurrent\nreleases write a separate marker without rewriting the file.\n\nEach reference has three parts:\n\n1. **A date.** When the reference was acquired. Lets a janitor\n   prune references older than some threshold even if their back\n   pointer can't be validated.\n2. **A back-pointer.** The identity of the holder — enough\n   information that an outside observer can ask \"is this holder\n   still alive, and does it still want this reference?\" without\n   trusting the count alone. Concrete candidates:\n   - process PID + start time (PID alone is not enough; PIDs\n     recycle)\n   - a path to a marker file the holder maintains (presence of\n     the marker = the holder is still live and aware of the\n     ref)\n   - some combination (PID + a marker path)\n3. **An opaque ref id.** A short string the holder can use later\n   to identify *its* reference when it wants to release, so it\n   doesn't accidentally release someone else's.\n\nA release writes an entry referencing the original acquire id.\nNet live refs = acquires whose id isn't in the release set.\n\n## Reference file format\n\nA line-oriented log. Each line is one of two record types:\n\n```\nacquire <id> <iso8601-date> <pid> <pid-start-time-ticks> <marker-path>\nrelease <id> <iso8601-date>\n```\n\nAppend-only. Holders open with `O_APPEND` and write a single line\nper operation. Atomic on POSIX as long as the line fits in\n`PIPE_BUF` (4 KB on Linux) — well within budget for these short\nrecords.\n\nReading: tail through the file, build a set of acquire ids,\nsubtract release ids; remaining ids are nominally live. Then\nvalidate each survivor's back pointer.\n\nA `.refs.lock` file is used only for compaction (rewriting the\nlog to drop matched acquire/release pairs) and for the\nfork-to-sibling decision during compile. Steady-state reads /\nwrites don't lock.\n\n## Acquire / release API\n\nA small helper utility, probably a shell script for portability\nsince holders are written in many languages:\n\n```\nscripts/soramech-ref.sh acquire <compiled-dir> [--id <id>] [--marker <path>]\nscripts/soramech-ref.sh release <compiled-dir> --id <id>\nscripts/soramech-ref.sh list    <compiled-dir>          # JSON, including staleness verdicts\nscripts/soramech-ref.sh reap    <compiled-dir>          # compact + drop dead refs\n```\n\n`acquire` prints the assigned id to stdout; the holder is\nresponsible for plumbing it to wherever it'll need to call\nrelease. If no `--id` was supplied, the script generates one\n(timestamp + random suffix).\n\n`list` walks the log and prints a JSON array of `{id, date,\nholder, valid}` entries. Validation reads the back pointer's\nliveness signal (PID exists & start-time matches, or marker file\nexists).\n\n`reap` is destructive — it rewrites the log to remove entries\nwhose holders failed validation. Run periodically; never\nautomatically as part of compile (compile must not destroy state\nits caller might care about).\n\n## Compile-time fork logic\n\n`soramech-compile.sh` consults `<map>/compiled/.refs` (and any\nsibling generation directories' `.refs` files) before deciding\nwhere to write:\n\n1. If `<map>/compiled/` doesn't exist → build there, fresh.\n2. If it exists but has zero live references → build there, after\n   `rm -rf`. Same destructive behavior as today.\n3. If it exists with one or more live references → pick a sibling\n   directory name (see below) and build there. The original\n   `compiled/` stays intact.\n\nAfter a fork-build, the caller has a new directory; `manifest.json`\nin the new directory records the fork relationship (`forked_from`\nfield pointing at the previous generation's path).\n\n### Sibling directory naming\n\nTwo reasonable schemes; pick whichever the implementer prefers:\n\n- **Generation index:** `compiled.0`, `compiled.1`, `compiled.2`...\n  Always pick `compiled.N` where N is one more than the highest\n  existing generation. Easy to grep for; index order = build\n  order.\n- **Timestamp suffix:** `compiled.2026-05-19T2347` (ISO 8601\n  compact). Order-preserving lexicographically; the name itself\n  tells the operator when it was built.\n\nWhichever wins, the script should also leave a `compiled` symlink\npointing at the newest generation, so callers who want \"the\nlatest\" don't have to enumerate.\n\n## Stale reference handling\n\nA reference is stale if any of the following hold:\n\n- The PID no longer exists on the system.\n- The PID exists but its start time (`/proc/<pid>/stat` field 22)\n  doesn't match the recorded value — different process, recycled\n  PID.\n- The marker file path was supplied at acquire and is now\n  missing.\n\nStale refs are *tolerated*: compile-time fork still triggers if\nANY ref exists, stale or otherwise — the caller can run\n`soramech-ref.sh reap` first if they want to consolidate. The\nphilosophy is: the artifact directory belongs to its readers\nuntil proven otherwise, and the cost of an extra build dir is\ntrivial compared to the cost of a use-after-rebuild crash.\n\n## Gitignore considerations\n\nEvery generation (`compiled/`, `compiled.0/`, `compiled.1/`,\n`compiled.2026-05-19T2347/`, the `compiled` symlink) is a derived\nartifact and should never be tracked. The existing\n`.gitignore` line `tests/maps/*/compiled/` covers the canonical\nname; add a sibling pattern to cover generations:\n\n```\ntests/maps/*/compiled/\ntests/maps/*/compiled.*/\n```\n\nThe `.refs` file itself lives *inside* the compiled directory,\nso it inherits the same gitignore.\n\n## Suggested implementation steps\n\n1. Pick the back-pointer format. Recommend PID + start time +\n   optional marker path. Document the choice with a comment at\n   the top of the ref helper.\n2. Write `scripts/soramech-ref.sh` with `acquire`, `release`,\n   `list`, `reap`. Append-only writes for the first two, log\n   rewrite under `.refs.lock` for the last.\n3. Add a small `tests/315-refs-test.sh` that exercises:\n   acquire → list (1 entry, valid) → release → list (0 valid) →\n   acquire → kill the holder process → list (1 entry, stale) →\n   reap → list (0).\n4. Teach `soramech-compile.sh` to read `.refs` and pick the\n   target directory. Implement the sibling-naming scheme.\n   `compiled` becomes a symlink to the newest generation.\n5. Add a `forked_from` field to `manifest.json` when forking.\n6. Update `.gitignore` for the new generation pattern.\n7. Integration check in `scripts/run-tests.sh`: compile the\n   pipeline fixture twice — second time with a live `acquire` —\n   assert a sibling generation was created and the original\n   pinned generation still runs unchanged.\n\n## Open questions\n\n- Should the runner (`soramech-pool`) itself acquire a reference\n  when it opens a compiled directory? On the one hand, yes —\n  it's the canonical case the system protects against. On the\n  other, soramech-pool runs are usually short-lived and the\n  acquire/release overhead per run is unwelcome. If `compiled.5` is built while\n  `compiled.4` had live refs but `compiled.4`'s refs are now all\n  stale (caller never released, then died), do we ever prune\n  `compiled.4`? Probably yes, via `soramech-ref.sh reap-all\n  <map>` which walks every generation and drops the ones whose\n  refs all validate as dead.\n- Is the `.refs` log itself something that should be versioned\n  (`.refs.v1`)? If we ever change the line format, in-flight\n  holders won't know how to read it. Versioning the filename\n  avoids the problem.\n- Does the editor (`maps/<x>/` user-facing) want the same\n  mechanism? Probably yes eventually, but out of scope for this\n  issue — start with `compiled/` artifacts only.\n\n## Relevant files\n\n- `scripts/soramech-compile.sh` — issue 309's compile pipeline,\n  modified here to fork on live references\n- `scripts/soramech-ref.sh` — new helper for acquire / release /\n  list / reap\n- `tests/315-refs-test.sh` — new\n- `.gitignore` — extended pattern for generation directories\n- `scripts/run-tests.sh` — new integration check\n- `issues/309-build-system.md` — parent issue; references this\n  one's fork behavior\n\n## Notes (philosophy)\n\nThe unreliability is a feature, not a bug. A reliable reference\ncount would require a kernel-level mechanism (file locks held\nfor the lifetime of the holder), and that's a tower of\noperational complexity for marginal value.       "content":"            if [[ -z \"$MAP\" ]]; then\n                MAP=\"$1\"\n            else\n                echo \"soramech-compile: unexpected argument '$1'\" >&2\n                exit 2\n            fi\n            shift\n            ;;\n    esac\ndone\n\nif [[ -z \"$MAP\" ]]; then\n    echo \"usage: soramech-compile <map-dir> [--dir <project-root>]\" >&2\n    exit 2\nfi\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ resolve paths & sanity-check\nif [[ ! -d \"$MAP\" ]]; then\n    echo \"soramech-compile: not a directory: $MAP\" >&2\n    exit 1\nfi\nMAP=$(cd \"$MAP\" && pwd)\nif [[ ! -f \"$MAP/meta.json\" ]]; then\n    echo \"soramech-compile: missing meta.json in $MAP\" >&2\n    exit 1\nfi\nif [[ ! -d \"$MAP/boxes\" ]]; then\n    echo \"soramech-compile: missing boxes/ in $MAP\" >&2\n    exit 1\nfi\nif [[ ! -x \"$DIR/soramech-pool\" ]]; then\n    echo \"soramech-compile: pool runner not built at $DIR/soramech-pool\" >&2\n    echo \"  run 'make' in $DIR first\" >&2\n    exit 1\nfi\n\nCOMPILED=\"$MAP/compiled\"\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ box_field — pull a top-level string field from a box JSON file\n# Tolerant of whitespace; returns empty string if the field is missing.\n# We don't have jq in-tree, so a regex over the small box files is\n# fine. Box JSON is hand-written and shallow.\nbox_field() {\n    local file=\"$1\"\n    local field=\"$2\"\n    grep -o \"\\\"$field\\\"[[:space:]]*:[[:space:]]*\\\"[^\\\"]*\\\"\" \"$file\" \\\n        | head -n1 \\\n        | sed 's/.*\"\\([^\"]*\\)\"$/\\1/'\n}\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ wipe & lay out the compiled directory\nrm -rf \"$COMPILED\"\nmkdir -p \"$COMPILED\" \"$COMPILED/boxes\" \"$COMPILED/src\" \"$COMPILED/bin\" \"$COMPILED/langs\"\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ copy verbatim assets (meta, boxes, src, data, *.txt)\ncp \"$MAP/meta.json\" \"$COMPILED/meta.json\"\ncp -r \"$MAP/boxes/.\" \"$COMPILED/boxes/\"\n\nif [[ -d \"$MAP/src\" ]]; then\n    cp -r \"$MAP/src/.\" \"$COMPILED/src/\"\nfi\n\nif [[ -d \"$MAP/data\" ]]; then\n    mkdir -p \"$COMPILED/data\"\n    cp -r \"$MAP/data/.\" \"$COMPILED/data/\"\nfi\n\n# Issue 246 — per-port custom translation shims. Box JSONs reference\n# them by relative path under translations/; the runtime resolves\n# the path relative to the compiled map dir at dispatch time.\nif [[ -d \"$MAP/translations\" ]]; then\n    mkdir -p \"$COMPILED/translations\"\n    cp -r \"$MAP/translations/.\" \"$COMPILED/translations/\"\nfi\n\n# Top-level data files (input.txt, names.txt, etc) — the runner\n# resolves file_write/data refs relative to the map root.\nshopt -s nullglob\nfor f in \"$MAP\"/*.txt; do\n    cp \"$f\" \"$COMPILED/\"\ndone\nshopt -u nullglob\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ enumerate the set of languages the map actually uses\n# A box file is in compiled/boxes/. We read `lang` from each.\nLANGS=()\nfor box in \"$COMPILED\"/boxes/*.json; do\n    lang=$(box_field \"$box\" lang)\n    if [[ -z \"$lang\" ]]; then continue; fi\n    seen=0\n    for known in \"${LANGS[@]+\"${LANGS[@]}\"}\"; do\n        if [[ \"$known\" == \"$lang\" ]]; then seen=1; break; fi\n    done\n    if [[ $seen -eq 0 ]]; then\n        LANGS+=(\"$lang\")",

We read `lang` from each.\n140\tLANGS=()\n141\tfor box in \"$COMPILED\"/boxes/*.json; do\n142\t    lang=$(box_field \"$box\" lang)\n143\t    if [[ -z \"$lang\" ]]; then continue; fi\n144\t    seen=0\n145\t    for known in \"${LANGS[@]+\"${LANGS[@]}\"}\"; do\n146\t        if [[ \"$known\" == \"$lang\" ]]; then seen=1; break; fi\n147\t    done\n148\t    if [[ $seen -eq 0 ]]; then\n149\t        LANGS+=(\"$lang\")"
